item.name: Codex of the Last Archivist
entries: This silver-bound black spellbook has an eye-shaped clasp. Silver writing appears on its blank pages at its attuned keeper's touch; its origin is unknown.

entries.name: Arcane Supremacy
entries: While holding the codex, you gain a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and to the saving throw DCs of your spells. The codex can be used as a Spellcasting Focus.

entries.name: Endless Archive
entries: The codex holds any number of Wizard spells and halves the time and gold needed to copy them. When you finish a Long Rest, choose one Wizard spell recorded in it. Until your next Long Rest, that spell is always prepared and doesn't count against your prepared spells.

entries.name: Forbidden Index
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks concerning spells, magical writing, curses, artifacts, or lost magic. {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} are always prepared for you while you are attuned to the codex, and they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare. You can also cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} and {@spell Identify|XPHB} from the codex without expending a spell slot.

entries.name: Archive the Unwritten
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a level 1–9 spell, you can take a Reaction to archive its echo in the codex. Before your next Long Rest, you can cast that Archived Spell once using your spellcasting ability, without a spell slot or any Material components, including costly or consumed ones. After successfully archiving a spell, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Perfect Recollection
entries: When you cast a spell recorded in the codex using a spell slot, choose one of the following benefits:

items: You have Advantage on one spell attack roll made as part of the spell.
One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.
The spell ignores Resistance to one damage type it deals.

entries: You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Unbroken Formula
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saves to maintain Concentration. Once per Long Rest, you can turn a failed Constitution save to maintain Concentration into a success.

entries.name: Final Annotation
entries: Once per dawn, you can turn a failed saving throw against a spell or magical effect into a success.

entries.name: Unblemished Archive
entries: Ordinary means can't permanently damage or destroy the codex: its pages, writing, and binding restore themselves. If destroyed, it reforms at the next dawn with all contents intact, beside its Soul-Bound keeper or, if it has none, where it was destroyed.

entries.name: Curse: The Endless Archive
entries: The codex bears a 9th-level curse. Attuning to it binds the keeper to the Archive.

entries.name: Soul Bound
entries: You can't willingly end Attunement, relinquish the codex, or remain separated from it. It can't be permanently taken by force; once separation can no longer be maintained, it reappears on your person. No other creature can attune to it while your Soul Bound connection remains.

entries.name: Archivist's Claim
entries: While Soul Bound to the codex, you can't willingly attune to another cursed magic item. You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist an effect that would forcibly bind you to, possess you through, or establish magical ownership over you.

entries.name: Curse Suppression
entries: While you possess the codex, curses of 9th level or lower can't affect you, and curses from Legendary or lower-rarity magic items are suppressed. Existing curses are suppressed, not removed. Artifacts, deities, and comparable powers can bypass this protection at the GM's discretion.

entries.name: Archive Remembers
entries: Arcane writing recorded in the codex can't be permanently erased, removed, or destroyed. Lost arcane writing returns the next time the codex is opened.

entries.name: Breaking the Curse
entries: {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} suppresses the Soul Bound curse and its restrictions for 24 hours but doesn't permanently end it. {@spell Wish|XPHB} or magic of comparable power can permanently break the curse.

item.name: Ascendant Script Tattoo
entries: Arcane symbols inked into your skin rearrange themselves whenever you cast a spell.

entries.name: Ascendant Casting
entries: When you cast a level 1–8 spell using a spell slot, you can spend up to 2 charges. Treat the spell's slot level as one higher per charge, to a maximum of 9.

entries.name: Overflowing Spell
entries: When you use Ascendant Casting, you can expend 1 additional charge and choose one of the following effects:

items: {@b Empowered.} Reroll a number of the spell's damage dice up to your Proficiency Bonus. You must use the new rolls.
{@b Extended.} If the spell has a duration of at least 1 minute and isn't Instantaneous, double its duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.
{@b Far-Reaching.} If the spell has a range of at least 10 feet, double its range. If its range is Touch, its range becomes 30 feet.
{@b Overwhelming.} One creature affected by the spell has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against the spell.

entries.name: Restored Script
entries: The tattoo regains {@dice 1d4 + 1} expended charges daily at dawn.

item.name: Mantle of the Unbroken Spell
entries: Arcane notation drifts across this dark mantle like ink beneath water. No maker's mark has ever been found on it.

entries.name: Unbroken Concentration
entries: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.

entries.name: Spell Refuses to Break
entries: When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can succeed instead. You can use this property twice, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Stability
entries: When you take damage while concentrating on a spell, you can reduce the DC of the resulting Constitution saving throw by 5, to a minimum DC of 10. You can use this property a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Persistent Spell
entries: If you become Incapacitated while concentrating, your Concentration ends at the end of your next turn unless the condition ends first. Death still ends Concentration normally.

item.name: Earring of the Silent Word
entries: This single black earring bears one arcane glyph that has resisted every attempt at translation. Its origin is unknown.

entries.name: Silent Casting
entries: While wearing the earring, you can omit any spell's Verbal component. Somatic and Material components remain required.

entries.name: Unspoken Word
entries: An omitted Verbal component produces no incantation or sound, preventing detection solely through speech. This property doesn't conceal other components, visible manifestations, or sounds produced by the spell.

item.name: Coin of the Open Rite
entries: This old silver coin bears an incomplete magical circle resembling an open doorway. No known mint claims its design.

entries.name: Open Rite
entries: You can cast a prepared level 1–3 spell with a normal casting time of 1 minute or less as a Ritual, even without the Ritual tag. Add 10 minutes to its casting time and expend no spell slot. Components, range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Greater Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The circle engraved on this silver coin is nearly complete, except for a narrow break at its center.

entries.name: Greater Open Rite
entries: You can cast a level 1–5 spell with a normal casting time of 1 minute or less as a Ritual, even without the Ritual tag. It must be known, prepared, or recorded in an available spellbook or similar spellcasting source; recorded spells needn't be prepared. Add 10 minutes to its casting time and expend no spell slot.
You must still provide the spell's normal components, and its range, duration, Concentration, and other effects are unchanged.

item.name: Grand Coin of the Open Rite
entries: The engraved circle on this coin appears complete until viewed closely, when a hairline opening becomes visible along its edge.

entries.name: Grand Open Rite
entries: You can cast a level 1–7 spell with a normal casting time of 1 minute or less as a Ritual, even without the Ritual tag. It must be known, prepared, or recorded in an available spellbook or similar spellcasting source, and you must be capable of casting spells of its level. Add 10 minutes to its casting time and expend no spell slot.

entries.name: Open Beyond Preparation
entries: You can cast an eligible spell directly from a spellbook or similar spellcasting source available to you even if the spell isn't prepared.

entries.name: Patient Invocation
entries: You can increase the added casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour to omit non-consumed Material components worth 1,000 GP or less. Consumed components and non-consumed components worth more than 1,000 GP remain required.

item.name: Final Coin of the Open Rite
entries: No visible break exists in the circle engraved upon this coin, yet its design still gives the unmistakable impression of an open door.

entries.name: Final Open Rite
entries: You can cast a level 1–9 spell with a normal casting time of 1 minute or less as a Ritual, even without the Ritual tag. It must be known, prepared, or recorded in an available spellbook or similar spellcasting source, and you must be capable of casting spells of its level. Add 10 minutes to its casting time and expend no spell slot.

entries.name: Ninth Door
entries: An eligible spell recorded in a spellbook or similar spellcasting source can be cast through the coin even if the spell isn't on your class's spell list. You use your own spellcasting ability for the spell.

entries.name: Perfect Invocation
entries: You can increase the added casting time from 10 minutes to 1 hour to omit costly Material components that aren't consumed. Consumed components remain required.

entries.name: Sacrifice of Time
entries: Instead of the normal added casting time, perform the rite over 8 hours to replace consumed Material components worth up to 10,000 GP combined. Replaced components count as consumed.

entries.name: Unbroken Rite
entries: An interrupted ritual retains its progress for 1 hour; resuming the same ritual within that time continues from the interruption. The coin preserves only one unfinished ritual at a time.

item.name: Mantle of the Second Shape
entries: This cloak shifts its weight, texture, and cut to meet approaching hardship. When you finish a Short or Long Rest, choose one benefit below; it lasts until you choose again.

items: You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Your walking speed increases by 10 feet.
You gain Advantage on Strength and Dexterity saving throws made to resist being moved, knocked Prone, or Restrained.
You gain Darkvision out to 60 feet. If you already have Darkvision, its range increases by 60 feet instead.
You gain Resistance to one damage type chosen from Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder.

entries: Once per Long Rest, you can use a Bonus Action to change the benefit before your next rest.

item.name: Ring of the Last Refusal
entries: The inside of this black iron ring is engraved with a single sentence: {@i Not yet.} When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but aren't killed outright, you can remain conscious.
Until the end of your next turn:

items: Being at 0 Hit Points doesn't make you Unconscious.
You can move, take Actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions normally.
Taking damage doesn't cause you to fail Death Saving Throws.
You don't make Death Saving Throws.
Gaining Hit Points works normally and immediately ends this effect.

entries: At the end of your next turn, if you still have 0 Hit Points, you fall Unconscious and begin making Death Saving Throws normally. while this effect is active, if you would be killed outright by damage because the remaining damage equals or exceeds your Hit Point maximum, you can prevent that death. You remain at 0 Hit Points instead. Once the ring prevents you from falling Unconscious this way, it can't do so again until the next dawn.

item.name: Afterimage Rune
entries: This rune appears a moment behind the present. During a Short or Long Rest, affix it to one weapon you touch. It remains until you remove it during another Short or Long Rest or attach it to another weapon.
If the weapon already requires Attunement, that Attunement also satisfies the rune, using no additional slot. Otherwise, you must attune to the rune normally.
While the rune is attached:

items: The weapon is magical.
The weapon has a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls, regardless of any lower bonus it normally possesses.
Any other magical properties of the weapon continue to function normally.

entries: Each hit against a creature with the rune-bearing weapon leaves a delayed attack. At the start of your next turn, each repeats against its original target if still within the weapon's normal reach or range.

items: Roll a new attack roll using the same attack bonus as the original attack.
The repeated attack requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
On a hit, it deals the weapon's normal damage plus 2d8 Force damage.
It otherwise counts as an attack made with that weapon.
A repeated ranged attack doesn't expend ammunition.
A repeated attack can't create another delayed attack.
If the original target is invalid, you can redirect the repeated attack to a creature within 5 feet of its last position that is within the weapon's normal reach or range.

entries: There is no limit to the number of delayed attacks you can have at one time.

item.name: Wraps of Unarmed Prowess
entries: These reinforced combat wraps are treated as a simple melee weapon while worn.
{@b Fist.} Attacks made with this weapon are treated as Unarmed Strikes.

While wearing the wraps, you can make Unarmed Strikes with them, using your normal Unarmed Strike damage if its die exceeds {@damage 1d6}. Each strike counts as both an Unarmed Strike and an attack with this weapon for features, enhancements, infusions, enchantments, and other weapon effects.
Strikes with any body part count as attacks with these wraps.

item.name: Wraps of Unarmed Prowess +1
entries: These reinforced combat wraps are treated as a simple melee weapon while worn.
{@b Fist.} Attacks made with this weapon are treated as Unarmed Strikes.

While wearing the wraps, you can make Unarmed Strikes with them, using your normal Unarmed Strike damage if its die exceeds {@damage 1d8}. Attacks with them gain +1 to attack and damage rolls. Each strike counts as both an Unarmed Strike and an attack with this weapon for features, enhancements, infusions, enchantments, and other weapon effects.
Strikes with any body part count as attacks with these wraps.

item.name: Wraps of Unarmed Prowess +2
entries: These reinforced combat wraps are treated as a simple melee weapon while worn.
{@b Fist.} Attacks made with this weapon are treated as Unarmed Strikes.

While wearing the wraps, you can make Unarmed Strikes with them, using your normal Unarmed Strike damage if its die exceeds {@damage 1d10}. Attacks with them gain +2 to attack and damage rolls. Each strike counts as both an Unarmed Strike and an attack with this weapon for features, enhancements, infusions, enchantments, and other weapon effects.
Strikes with any body part count as attacks with these wraps.

item.name: Wraps of Unarmed Prowess +3
entries: These reinforced combat wraps are treated as a simple melee weapon while worn.
{@b Fist.} Attacks made with this weapon are treated as Unarmed Strikes.

While wearing the wraps, you can make Unarmed Strikes with them, using your normal Unarmed Strike damage if its die exceeds {@damage 1d12}. Attacks with them gain +3 to attack and damage rolls. Each strike counts as both an Unarmed Strike and an attack with this weapon for features, enhancements, infusions, enchantments, and other weapon effects.
Strikes with any body part count as attacks with these wraps.

item.name: Bracers of Heavy Impact
entries: These bracers become crushingly heavy on impact. While worn, your Unarmed Strikes deal an extra 1d6 Force damage on a hit. Each hit can also push the target up to 10 feet directly away if it is no more than one Size larger than you.

If you score a Critical Hit with an Unarmed Strike, the extra Force damage becomes 2d6, and the creature is also knocked Prone if it is Large or smaller. The benefits apply to every Unarmed Strike you make, regardless of which part of your body you use.

item.name: Gauntlets of the Extended Blow
entries: These gauntlets carry each blow through a ripple in the air. While worn, your Unarmed Strike reach increases by 5 feet. Hits beyond your normal reach deal an extra 1d6 Force damage.
Your Unarmed Strikes can interact with creatures and objects within the extended reach as though your body reached them, regardless of which body part you use.

item.name: Grasping Wraps
entries: These wraps tighten into a crushing grip. While worn, each Unarmed Strike hit lets you immediately attempt to Grapple the target as part of that attack, if it is eligible. A creature Grappled by you takes 1d6 Bludgeoning damage at the start of each of its turns.

Whenever you hit a creature you are currently Grappling with an Unarmed Strike, the attack deals an extra 1d8 Bludgeoning damage. If you are Grappling a creature and successfully move it at least 10 feet on your turn, you can knock it Prone at the end of that movement. The benefits apply regardless of which part of your body you use to make the Unarmed Strike.

item.name: Pendant of Lingering Magic
entries: This pendant glows with lingering spelllight. Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher that forces saving throws, each creature that succeeds is marked by its remnant until the start of your next turn.

At the start of your next turn, marked creatures repeat that save against your spell save DC. Failure applies the original save's failure effects, using the spell's original level and your statistics when you cast it.

items: This requires no Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or additional spell slot.
Damage is rolled again normally.
Repeat only effects that can reasonably apply directly to that creature; don't repeat areas, summons, object movement, or other effects that can't.
A spell that requires Concentration doesn't create a second instance of the spell.
A creature that originally failed its saving throw doesn't repeat it.
The repeated saving throw can't cause this effect to occur again.

item.name: Gloves of Mutable Weight
entries: These gray gloves unsettle an object's weight. As a Bonus Action, touch an object not worn or carried by an unwilling creature and make it one-tenth or ten times its normal weight. Its other properties are unchanged. This lasts until you touch it to end the effect or use the gloves to select the other weight.

The object can be any size you can physically touch but must initially weigh no more than 10,000 pounds. Gravity still applies normally. Its altered weight affects lifting, carrying, pushing, pulling, throwing, transport, and anything it weighs down normally.
If an affected object becomes worn or carried by another creature, its altered weight remains until the effect ends. You can have any number of objects affected simultaneously.

item.name: Chalk of the Open Wall
entries: This chalk draws doorways through solid matter. As an Action, begin drawing on a solid surface you can reach. After 1 minute, the completed outline, up to 5 feet wide and 10 feet tall, opens a passage through up to 20 feet of nonmagical solid material.

items: The passage follows a straight line through the material.
It doesn't damage or destroy the surrounding structure.
Creatures and objects can move through it normally.
The passage remains open for 10 minutes.
When it closes, any creature or object still inside is harmlessly pushed to the nearest open space.
It can't create a passage through a creature, magical barrier, or material created or sustained by a spell.

entries: The chalk isn't consumed when used. You can have only one passage created by the chalk open at a time. Creating another immediately closes the previous one.

item.name: Ring of Spellbinding
entries: A thin silver ring etched with a single continuous line. When its magic takes hold, the line glows without ever breaking. While wearing the ring, you have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration on a spell.

entries.name: Refuse to Break
entries: When you fail a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can succeed instead. Once this property is used, it can't be used again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Anchored Casting
entries: If you would become Incapacitated without being reduced to 0 Hit Points, your Concentration doesn't automatically end. You still lose Concentration if another rule or effect specifically ends the spell.

item.name: Boots of the Unfinished Journey
entries: These weathered boots are always dusted with soil from somewhere you have not yet been. While wearing the boots, your Speed increases by 10 feet.

entries.name: Keep Moving
entries: Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement.

entries.name: Never Quite There
entries: At the end of your turn, if you moved at least 20 feet, you can move an additional 10 feet without an action. This extra movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

item.name: Gloves of the Far Hand
entries: Translucent hands echo these gloves' movements. While wearing them, you can manipulate unattended objects within 30 feet as though within reach whenever you could normally interact with an object, including opening doors, drawing or stowing items, picking things up, pulling levers, turning keys, and pouring containers.

entries.name: Extended Use
entries: You can also perform actions involving an object at this distance, such as:

items: Administer a potion to a willing or Incapacitated creature.
Use a set of tools.
Place or retrieve an object from another creature that is willing.
Light, extinguish, load, unload, or otherwise operate an object.

entries: The gloves don't increase your ability to lift or carry weight; the distant hands use your normal Strength and carrying limits. The hands can't make attacks, Grapple, Shove, or directly manipulate an unwilling creature.

item.name: Cape of the Uncaught
entries: This gray cape slips around approaching blows. While wearing it, your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Slip Aside
entries: When a creature misses you with a melee attack, you can move up to 10 feet immediately after the attack, without using your Reaction. You can use Slip Aside only once per turn.

entries.name: Through the Crowd
entries: You can move through the spaces of hostile creatures that are your size or larger. Those spaces count as Difficult Terrain for you, and you can't end your turn in another creature's space.

item.name: Scabbard of the Ready Blade
entries: This dark scabbard holds a weapon ready for your hand. It can hold any one weapon that can reasonably be sheathed or holstered within it.

entries.name: Always at Hand
entries: While the weapon is inside the scabbard, you can draw it without using an object interaction, including during another action or immediately before making an attack with it.

entries.name: Recall Weapon
entries: If the weapon is within 120 feet of you and isn't being worn or carried by another creature, you can cause it to instantly return to the scabbard, no action required.

entries.name: Instant Exchange
entries: Once on each of your turns when you draw the stored weapon, you can simultaneously stow one weapon you are currently holding into the scabbard.

entries.name: Ready Before Thought
entries: When Initiative is rolled, you can immediately draw the stored weapon before the first turn begins.

race.name: Runeblood
entries: Living inscriptions mark Runeblood bodies, appearing beneath skin, across eyes and limbs, or only when magic stirs. Their origin is unknown; identical symbols occur among unrelated Runeblood centuries apart.

entries.name: Arcane Sight
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast it using any spell slots you have.

entries.name: Living Rune
entries: Choose one of the following runes when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Rune.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce that damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Force Rune.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d8} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Passage Rune.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Insight Rune.} When you fail an ability check, you can roll {@dice 1d6} and add it to the check, potentially turning the failure into a success.

entries: You can activate your Living Rune a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Runic Magic
entries: You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.

entries.name: Read the Script
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to understand magical runes, glyphs, inscriptions, or written magical effects.

entries.name: Runic Memory
entries: You gain proficiency in {@skill Arcana}. If already proficient, choose {@skill History}, {@skill Investigation}, or {@skill Religion} instead.

entries.name: Inscribed Focus
entries: You can use the runes on your body as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

race.name: Fragmentborn
entries: Fragmentborn carry an unexplained fragment in body, mind, or soul. It may appear as crystal, a scar, an eye-symbol, a distortion, or nothing visible. Its origin and even its physical existence resist reliable identification.

entries.name: Fragment Sense
entries: You can cast {@spell Detect Magic|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. Once you cast it with this trait, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Nature
entries: Choose one of the following manifestations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Fragment.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Fragment.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Echo Fragment.} When you fail an ability check or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success.
{@b Rift Fragment.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Void Fragment.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.

entries: If your Fragment Nature has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Fragment Stability
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would alter your form against your will.

entries.name: Uncertain Presence
entries: Divination of your nature, origin, or supernatural identity can detect an unusual magical presence but doesn't automatically identify your fragment or its origin.

entries.name: Fragment Resonance
entries: You have Advantage on Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}) checks made to identify portals, teleportation effects, magical anomalies, or effects that alter space or reality.

entries.name: Anchored Form
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws and ability checks made to resist being teleported or moved against your will by a magical effect.

race.name: Spellforged
entries: Spellforged are living Constructs built around a magical Spellcore, with bodies of metal, stone, crystal, porcelain, wood, or stranger materials. Their creators are unknown; unrelated discoveries sometimes share identical internal components.

entries.name: Constructed Existence
entries: You need no food, drink, breath, or sleep, and magic can't put you to sleep. To gain a Long Rest's benefits, spend at least 6 hours inactive but conscious, seeing and hearing normally.

entries.name: Arcane Chassis
entries: While you aren't wearing armor, your base Armor Class is 13 + your Dexterity modifier. You can use a Shield and still gain this benefit.

entries.name: Integrated Spell Focus
entries: Your body can serve as a Spellcasting Focus whenever a spell you cast permits one.

entries.name: Arcane Maintenance
entries: When {@spell Mending|XPHB} is cast on you, you can spend and roll one Hit Point Die, regaining the result + your Constitution modifier in Hit Points. After recovering Hit Points this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Spellcore Configuration
entries: Choose one of the following configurations when you select this species. Your choice is permanent.

items: {@b Aegis Core.} When you take damage, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Arcane Core.} Choose one cantrip from the Wizard spell list. You know that cantrip. Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for it.
{@b Assault Core.} Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with an attack or spell, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force damage to one creature damaged by it.
{@b Mobility Core.} As a Bonus Action, you teleport up to 20 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.
{@b Restoration Core.} As a Bonus Action, you or one creature you touch regains {@dice 1d6} + your Proficiency Bonus Hit Points.

entries: If your Spellcore Configuration has an activated effect, you can use that effect a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Construct Resilience
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition. You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Integrated Compartment
entries: Your body has a concealed compartment holding up to 5 pounds; each object must fit within roughly a 1-foot cube. Finding it closed requires an Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check against DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier. Opening or closing it takes the Utilize action.

race.name: Arcane Aberrant
entries: Magic has permanently altered Arcane Aberrants, from crystalline growths and shifting eyes to changes invisible until their power stirs.

Their bodies continually adapt to this intrinsic magic, whose origin remains uncertain. They mature at roughly the Human rate, but their maximum lifespan is unknown; none has been confirmed to die of old age.

entries.name: Natural Inclination
entries: Increase your Ability Scores by a total of {@b 2 points}. These increases are separate from those granted by your Background.

entries.name: Gradual Development
entries: Choose different Ability Scores as your permanent {@b Primary Ability} and {@b Secondary Ability}. Your Primary Ability increases by {@b 1} at character levels {@b 5, 9, 13, and 17}, and by another {@b 1} for every {@b 2 points} your Secondary Ability exceeds 10.
The Secondary Ability's contribution changes whenever its score crosses a threshold in either direction. These increases are separate from those granted by Backgrounds, Feats, or other features.

entries.name: Mutative Instinct
entries: When you fail an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll {@dice 1d4} and add it to the roll, potentially turning the failure into a success. You can use this trait a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. The die becomes {@dice 1d6} when your Proficiency Bonus becomes +4, {@dice 1d8} when it becomes +5, and {@dice 1d10} when it becomes +6.

entries.name: Aberrant Magic
entries: You know the {@spell Prestidigitation|XPHB} cantrip. Starting at character level 3, you can cast {@spell Chromatic Orb|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot or providing its Material component. Starting at character level 5, you can cast {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} once without expending a spell slot. You regain the ability to cast each of these spells with this trait when you finish a Long Rest. You can also cast them using any spell slots you have of the appropriate level.
Choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as your spellcasting ability for these spells. Your body can serve as a Spellcasting Focus for your spells.

entries.name: Resilient Metabolism
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid or end the Poisoned condition. You also have Resistance to Poison damage.

entries.name: Heightened Senses
entries: You have proficiency in the {@skill Perception} skill. You also have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

race.name: Warborn
entries: Warborn descend from soldiers engineered to survive hostile magic through strength, reflexes, endurance, and an instinctive rejection of spellcraft.

Breeding, alchemy, and exposure to magic made these adaptations hereditary. The wars may be forgotten, but Warborn bodies retain their purpose—and can learn to reproduce what beneficial magic once made possible.

entries.name: Built for War
entries: You gain proficiency with Martial Weapons, Light Armor, Medium Armor, Heavy Armor, and Shields. You also gain proficiency in two skills of your choice from Acrobatics, Athletics, Intimidation, Perception, or Survival. Choose one of those two skills. You gain Expertise in it.

entries.name: Arcane Rejection
entries: You can't cast spells by any means or gain or expend Spell Slots or Pact Magic slots. Classes, Subclasses, Feats, species traits, magic items, and other features can't grant you spellcasting; you can't use an item to cast a spell.
You can still use magic weapons and armor, passive magic-item benefits, and non-spell abilities that don't require casting. Others' spells and magical effects can affect you normally.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries: You have Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.

entries.name: Spellward Flesh
entries: Spell Attack Rolls against you have Disadvantage. You have Resistance to damage dealt by spells and magical effects. Whenever you succeed on a Saving Throw against a spell or magical effect, you take no damage and suffer no other effect from it if you would normally suffer a reduced effect on a successful save.

entries.name: Reject the Arcane
entries: When a spell or magical effect would affect you without an attack roll or saving throw, you can make a Constitution save against its save DC, or {@b 8 + the source's Proficiency Bonus + the ability modifier used for the effect} if it has none. Success negates the effect on you. You can decline the save to accept beneficial magic.

entries.name: Violent Rejection
entries: At the start of each of your turns, you can make a Constitution save against the save DC of a spell or magical effect affecting you with a duration longer than Instantaneous. Success ends it on you, even if it normally allows no further saves.

entries.name: Immutable Warrior
entries: You are immune to magical aging. You have Advantage on Saving Throws against magical effects that would Charm you, Paralyze you, Petrify you, possess you, transform you against your will, or teleport you against your will. Whenever you successfully resist one of these effects, you become immune to that specific named spell, trait, or magical effect until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Superior Physique
entries: You count as one Size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the creatures you can Grapple or Shove. Your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift are doubled. You have Advantage on Strength and Constitution Ability Checks. Your Strength and Constitution scores can exceed 20, to a maximum of {@b 24}.

entries.name: Warrior's Vitality
entries: Your Hit Point maximum increases by {@b 2 for each character level you have}. Whenever you gain a level, your Hit Point maximum increases by an additional 2.

entries.name: Combat Reflexes
entries: You add your Proficiency Bonus to Initiative rolls. You can't be Surprised while you're conscious. When you roll Initiative, you can immediately move up to half your Speed. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Martial Adaptation
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose one weapon with which you are proficient. Until you finish your next Long Rest, you can use Strength or Dexterity for its Attack and Damage Rolls, you can't be disarmed of it while you're conscious, and your attacks with it score a Critical Hit on a roll of {@b 19 or 20}.

entries.name: Born to Kill
entries: Whenever you hit with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, the attack deals additional damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Relentless Advance
entries: Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement. Standing from Prone costs you only 5 feet of movement. Your Speed can't be reduced below {@b 15 feet} unless you're Incapacitated. You have Advantage on Saving Throws against effects that would move you against your will. Being Grappled reduces your Speed to {@b 10 feet} instead of 0. If you're Grappling a creature while moving this way, you move it with you normally.

entries.name: Refuse to Die
entries: When you're reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you use this trait, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest. Starting at character level {@b 11}, you can use this trait twice between Long Rests.

entries.name: Imitated Perfection
entries: From 1st level, you can permanently imitate beneficial spells that personally affected you. Begin with {@b two Imitated Enhancements}, each from an eligible spell experienced before your adventuring career. Spell level imposes no restriction.

entries.name: Learning an Enhancement
entries: A spell is eligible for imitation if all of the following are true:

items: The spell personally affected you.
It granted you a beneficial effect.
It directly affected your body, senses, movement, reflexes, physical capabilities, or another inherent capability.
The benefit can reasonably exist as an inherent property of your body.

entries: After experiencing an eligible spell, you can internalize its benefit when you finish a Long Rest if you have an available Imitated Enhancement. You needn't know, identify, or understand the spell.
You can have no more Imitated Enhancements than shown for your character level.

entries.name: Permanent Imitation
entries: An Imitated Enhancement permanently reproduces the chosen spell's beneficial effects on you alone. It is nonmagical, has no duration, requires no Concentration, Spell Slot, components, or spellcasting ability, and can't be countered, dispelled, suppressed by Antimagic, or transferred. It doesn't let you cast the spell.
If the spell has a drawback that occurs specifically because its Duration ends, the spell ends, or Concentration is lost, that drawback doesn't occur.

entries.name: Selective Imitation
entries: Imitation reproduces only inherent enhancements to you. It excludes spellcasting, summoned or created creatures, independent objects or effects away from your body, direct control of others, independent damage to others, and Instantaneous healing. A spell containing both eligible and excluded effects grants only its eligible enhancement.

entries.name: Choices Within a Spell
entries: Imitate the choices you personally experienced: {@spell Protection from Energy|XPHB} granting Fire Resistance permits that version. Experiencing a different choice makes that version separately eligible.

entries.name: Inherent Expression
entries: Imitation reproduces magic's result through individual physical adaptation, not retained magic.

Examples include accelerated nerves and muscles for {@spell Haste|XPHB}, gripping structures for {@spell Spider Climb|XPHB}, and extraordinary senses for {@spell True Seeing|XPHB}. Bodily benefits of {@spell Enhance Ability|XPHB}, {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB}, and {@spell Foresight|XPHB} can likewise be imitated.
The physical manifestation doesn't need to visually resemble the original spell.

entries.name: Replacing an Enhancement
entries: Whenever you gain a character level, you can replace any number of Imitated Enhancements with eligible effects you previously experienced, within your maximum. Replaced adaptations disappear as your body restructures.

race.name: Ascendant
entries: Ascendants are exceptional individuals born among any ancestry, not a separate people. No blessing, curse, transformation, or creator grants their nature.
Their stable bodies recover persistently and remain capable of improvement beyond ordinary limits.
That potential can develop as strength, speed, endurance, intellect, awareness, discipline, or presence; no single path is predetermined.

Ascendants mature as their ancestry does, then cease natural aging at physical maturity. Their natural lifespan has no known limit, but injury, starvation, disease, poison, and other causes can still kill them.

Ascendance preserves ancestry, appearance, culture, language, family, and identity. It isn't ordinarily inherited: even two Ascendant parents normally have ordinary children of their ancestry, though another Ascendant may arise among later descendants.
Ascendant is a lineage, not a separate species. Injury and recovery cultivate its extraordinary physical potential.

entries.name: Ancestral Legacy
entries: When replacing a species with this lineage, you can retain its Skill Proficiencies and any Climb, Fly, or Swim Speed. If you retain none, or choose this lineage at character creation, gain proficiency in two skills of your choice. Your ancestry remains unchanged.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

entries.name: Survivor's Resilience
entries: With at least 1 Hit Point, you regain Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus every 1 minute. In combat, this instead occurs at the start of each of your turns and restores twice your Proficiency Bonus, provided you still have at least 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Potential Points
entries: Gain 1 Potential Point each separate time a hostile creature damages you in combat, with no per-turn or per-combat limit. Also gain Potential Points equal to Hit Points actually restored by Survivor's Resilience; overhealing grants none.
Potential Points remain until spent and have no pool maximum. Permanently increasing an Ability Score by 1 costs 10 times its new score in Potential Points.
You can increase Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, with no maximum imposed by this trait. Spent points normally can't be recovered or reassigned.

entries.name: Restful Vigil
entries: You can complete a Long Rest conscious and without sleep, performing light activity throughout. Strenuous activity, combat, spellcasting, and similar exertion interrupt the rest normally.

entries.name: Superior Physiology
entries: Increase one Ability Score of your choice by 2. Your Speed increases by 5 feet. Your Hit Point Maximum increases by 1 for each character level you have. Whenever you gain a level, your Hit Point Maximum increases by an additional 1. You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift. You also count as one size larger when determining the creatures you can Grapple or Shove.
When you move a creature Grappled by you that is your size or smaller, moving that creature costs you no additional movement.

feat.name: Spell Thief
entries: You have learned to seize the lingering structure of another creature's magic before it fades.

entries.name: Steal Spell
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of level 1 or higher, no higher than your Proficiency Bonus or 5th level, you can take a Reaction and make a spellcasting ability check against DC 10 + the spell's level. Success stores its echo, replacing any previously stolen spell.

entries.name: Stolen Casting
entries: You can cast the stolen spell once at its stolen level without a spell slot, using your spellcasting ability for attacks and save DC. It counts as your spell while held and requires its normal Material components, including costly or consumed ones. It disappears after casting or when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Arcane Larceny
entries: Once you successfully steal a spell, you can't successfully steal another spell until you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: You have developed an instinctive response to creatures using magic around you.

entries.name: Arcane Reflex
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can use your Reaction to move up to half your Speed.
Immediately after this movement, you can do one of the following against that creature:

items: Make one attack with a weapon.
Cast a cantrip that has a casting time of an Action and makes an attack roll.

entries: This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Spell Resistance
entries: When you succeed on a saving throw against a spell, you take no damage and suffer no other effect from that spell that would normally occur on a successful save.

feat.name: Spellcrafting
entries: You dismantle spells into their constituent parts and rebuild them into new formulae.

entries.name: Create a Spellcraft Formula
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose three spells you can cast to create a {@b Spellcraft Formula}: one {@b Base Spell} and two {@b Secondary Spells}. Replace up to two parts of the Base Spell, taking at most one from each Secondary Spell.

entries.name: What Can Be Replaced?
entries: You can replace any major part of the Base Spell with the same kind of part from a Secondary Spell.

items: Casting Time
Range
Targeting
Area of Effect
Attack Roll or Saving Throw
Damage
Damage Type
Healing
Duration
Concentration
Conditions
Movement
Teleportation
Summoning
Transformation
Terrain effects
Defensive effects
Another complete magical effect

entries: A replacement includes any rules it needs to function, such as repeated saves to end an imposed condition.

entries.name: Replacing an Effect
entries: You can replace complete magical effects, not just numbers. The Formula remains one spell, not simultaneous castings of its sources.

entries.name: Concentration
entries: You can replace the Concentration requirement independently of Duration. A Secondary Spell without Concentration can remove that requirement from the Base Spell; one requiring it can add it.

entries.name: Replacement, Not Addition
entries: Replacements normally substitute effects rather than adding them: replaced damage or conditions aren't also retained.

entries.name: Spell Level
entries: The Formula's level is the highest among its source spells. Casting requires a slot of at least that level, with no additional slot cost.

entries.name: Casting the Formula
entries: The Formula is available to you as a spell. It uses the Base Spell's spellcasting ability and the casting time, range, components, duration, Concentration, targets, effects, and other rules resulting from your replacements.

entries.name: Costly Components
entries: Any costly or consumed Material component required by an adopted Secondary Spell effect remains required; Spellcrafting can't remove that cost.

entries.name: Formula Limit
entries: You can retain up to your Proficiency Bonus in Spellcraft Formulas. When you finish a Long Rest, create, replace, or change any of them; each remains until replaced or forgotten.
Formula construction requires no combat action; it occurs when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Simple Example
entries: Example: use {@spell Fireball|XPHB} as the Base Spell, replacing parts with the Frightened effect of {@spell Fear|XPHB} and the Cold damage of {@spell Cone of Cold|XPHB}. The Formula retains Fireball's remaining structure and is 5th level, matching its highest-level source.

feat.name: Instinctive Adaptation
entries: You turn unfamiliar skills into instinct when the moment demands them.

entries.name: Rapid Familiarity
entries: When you finish a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one Skill, one Tool, or one Simple or Martial Weapon. You gain proficiency with the chosen option until you use this feature again.

entries.name: Learn by Doing
entries: When you fail an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you aren't proficient, you can immediately gain proficiency with that Skill or Tool and reroll the check. You must use the new roll. The proficiency lasts until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Borrowed Technique
entries: When a creature you see within 60 feet succeeds on a Skill or Tool check, use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to gain that proficiency until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, or Expertise if already proficient. Borrowed Technique grants only one proficiency or Expertise at a time.

entries.name: Quick Hands
entries: When you make an ability check using a Tool with which you are proficient, you can use Intelligence, Wisdom, or Dexterity for the check, regardless of the ability normally associated with that Tool. Choose the ability each time you make the check.

feat.name: Relentless Reserve
entries: When your reserves run dry, you force one final measure of strength from them.

entries.name: Hold Something Back
entries: When you expend a use of a feature that has a limited number of uses and regains those uses on a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 6, that use isn't expended. This benefit can't preserve spell slots, Hit Dice, or magic item charges. It can preserve limited-use features from your class, species, feats, or other personal abilities.

entries.name: Last Reserve
entries: You can use an exhausted limited-use feature once more, choosing it when you activate Last Reserve. You can't use Last Reserve again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Refuse Exhaustion
entries: When you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one limited-use feature that normally regains all of its uses on a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. If that feature currently has no uses remaining, you regain one use of it. Once you regain a use this way, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Deep Reserves
entries: Whenever another feature causes you to regain one or more uses of a limited-use ability, you can regain one additional use, up to that ability's normal maximum. You can benefit from Deep Reserves only once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Iterative Mastery
entries: Each failure refines your next attempt.

entries.name: Learn from Failure
entries: Failing an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw grants one {@dice d4} Adaptation Die for that specific kind of roll, such as a Longsword attack, Dexterity (Stealth) check, or Wisdom save. You can hold only one die per specific kind of roll.

entries.name: Refined Attempt
entries: The next time you make the associated roll before finishing a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, roll the Adaptation Die and add it to the {@dice d20} roll. You can roll the Adaptation Die after rolling the {@dice d20} but before you know whether the roll succeeds or fails. The Adaptation Die is then lost.

entries.name: Persistent Improvement
entries: If the roll still fails after adding your Adaptation Die, the die isn't lost. Instead, it increases by one size: {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, and {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}. It can't increase beyond a {@dice d12}. Once the associated roll succeeds, its Adaptation Die disappears.

entries.name: Never the Same Mistake Twice
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you fail a roll for which you already have a {@dice d12} Adaptation Die, you can treat the {@dice d20} roll as a 20 instead. The Adaptation Die then disappears.

feat.name: Flow State
entries: One success carries you into the next, turning practiced motion into instinct.

entries.name: Build Momentum
entries: Whenever you succeed on an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can enter a Flow State and gain a Momentum Die, which starts as a {@dice d4}. You can have only one Momentum Die at a time.

entries.name: Carry the Flow
entries: When you make another attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can roll your Momentum Die and add it to the {@dice d20} roll. You can decide to use the die after rolling the {@dice d20} but before you know whether the roll succeeds or fails. If the roll succeeds after using the Momentum Die, your Flow continues and the die increases by one size: {@dice d4} to {@dice d6}, {@dice d6} to {@dice d8}, {@dice d8} to {@dice d10}, and {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}. The die can't increase beyond a {@dice d12}.
If the roll fails, your Flow State ends and you lose the Momentum Die.

entries.name: Keep Moving
entries: Success preserves the Momentum Die. You can't apply it to consecutive rolls of exactly the same kind: between assisted Longsword attacks, for example, it must assist a different weapon attack, check, or save.

entries.name: Perfect Rhythm
entries: When your Momentum Die is a {@dice d12} and you succeed on a roll after adding it, you can enter Perfect Rhythm until the end of your next turn. While in Perfect Rhythm, you keep your {@dice d12} Momentum Die, and the first time you use it on each turn, you roll it twice and use the higher result. While in Perfect Rhythm, moving doesn't provoke {@variantrule {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}|XPHB|{@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}s}, standing from {@condition Prone|XPHB} costs you no movement, and drawing or stowing objects requires no action.
Once Perfect Rhythm ends, your Momentum Die returns to a {@dice d4} rather than disappearing. Once you enter Perfect Rhythm, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Defiant Pulse
entries: You hold pain, fear, and failure at bay through sheer refusal.

entries.name: Refuse the Moment
entries: When you fail a save, you can delay its consequences until the end of your next turn, treating it as a success meanwhile. Then repeat the save at the same DC: success cancels those consequences; failure applies them, with their duration beginning then. You can't use Refuse the Moment again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Keep Moving
entries: When an effect would reduce your Speed to 0, knock you {@condition Prone|XPHB}, or move you against your will, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to resist it. Until the end of the current turn, your Speed can't be reduced below 10 feet, you can't be knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB} against your will, and you can't be moved against your will. Once you use Keep Moving, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Fight Through It
entries: While you have half your Hit Points or fewer, you have Advantage on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, and {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} conditions. If you already have Advantage on such a saving throw, you can instead add your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} to the roll.

entries.name: One More Step
entries: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points but not killed outright, you can immediately move up to half your Speed before falling {@condition Unconscious|XPHB}. This movement doesn't provoke {@variantrule {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}|XPHB|{@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}s}. Once you use One More Step, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Unbound Movement
entries: Walls and gaps offer you new paths rather than obstacles.

entries.name: Natural Traverse
entries: You gain a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Speed. climbing, swimming, crawling, and moving through Difficult Terrain don't cost you extra movement.

entries.name: Running Start
entries: You don't need a running start to make a Long Jump or High Jump. Whenever you jump, the distance you can cover is doubled, though each foot of the jump still costs 1 foot of movement.

entries.name: Flow Through
entries: You can move through the space of any creature that is one Size larger or smaller than you, though you can't willingly end your movement there. Moving through another creature's space this way doesn't cost extra movement. The first time on a turn that you leave a creature's reach after moving through its space, you don't provoke an {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB} from that creature.

entries.name: Catch Yourself
entries: When you fall, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the effective distance of the fall by a number of feet equal to 10 × your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. If this reduces the effective distance to 0 feet, you take no falling damage and land on your feet.

entries.name: Keep the Momentum
entries: Once on each of your turns, immediately after you jump, climb at least 10 feet, swim at least 10 feet, or move through another creature's space, you can move an additional 10 feet without spending movement. This movement can itself include climbing, swimming, or jumping, but it can't trigger Keep the Momentum again that turn.

feat.name: Improvised Genius
entries: You turn scraps and unfamiliar devices into the tools the moment requires.

entries.name: Make Do
entries: For a Tool check with which you are proficient, a reasonably suitable improvised object counts as the required Tool. You can also use an improvised object as a Spellcasting Focus for any spell.

entries.name: Improvised Weaponry
entries: You are proficient with Improvised Weapons. When you attack with an Improvised Weapon, you can choose for it to deal {@dice 1d6} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as appropriate to the object. You can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls. Immediately before each attack, you can give the weapon one of the following properties until that attack ends: Finesse, Light, Thrown (20/60), or Versatile ({@dice 1d8}).

entries.name: Field Modification
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, choose one nonmagical object you are holding or touching that is no larger than Large. Until the end of your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can designate it as one of the following: a Tool with which you are proficient, a Shield, a Spellcasting Focus, or a Simple Weapon of your choice. The object retains its normal form, but functions mechanically as the chosen equipment while you use it. You can have a number of modified objects equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} at one time.

entries.name: Emergency Solution
entries: When you fail an ability check involving an object, mechanism, Tool, vehicle, trap, lock, or piece of equipment, you can immediately reroll the check using Intelligence, Wisdom, or Dexterity. You are treated as proficient with the relevant Tool for that reroll. You must use the new roll. Once you use Emergency Solution, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

feat.name: Practiced Certainty
entries: Long practice makes familiar tasks less dependent on luck.

entries.name: Reliable Practice
entries: Whenever you make an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient, you can treat a {@dice d20} roll of 4 or lower as a 5.

entries.name: Steady Hand
entries: Whenever you make an attack roll with a weapon with which you are proficient, a {@dice d20} roll of 2 is treated as a 3. This benefit doesn't change a natural 1.

entries.name: Familiar Task
entries: When you make an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient and you aren't under an immediate harmful consequence for failure, you can take 10 instead of rolling the {@dice d20}. You must choose before rolling. The DM can determine that a task is too uncertain or chaotic for Familiar Task to apply.

entries.name: Absolute Routine
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you make an ability check using a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient, you can treat the {@dice d20} roll as a 15 instead of rolling. You must choose before rolling.

feat.name: Rooted Stance
entries: Your settled stance redirects force rather than yielding to it.

entries.name: Grounded
entries: You have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws you make to resist being Grappled, Shoved, knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}, moved against your will, or disarmed.

entries.name: Absorb the Impact
entries: When you take Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage from an attack, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to reduce the damage by {@dice 1d6} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. If this reduces the damage to 0, you can immediately move 5 feet without provoking {@variantrule {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}|XPHB|{@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB}s}.
You can use Absorb the Impact a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Braced Position
entries: If you end your turn having moved no more than 10 feet since the start of that turn, you become Braced until the start of your next turn. While Braced, you can't be moved against your will unless you are {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, standing from {@condition Prone|XPHB} costs only 5 feet of movement, and you count as one Size larger when determining what you can Grapple or Shove.

entries.name: Turn the Force
entries: Once per turn, when a creature within your reach fails to Grapple, Shove, move, or knock you {@condition Prone|XPHB}, you can immediately move that creature 5 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, provided it is no more than one Size larger than you. This movement doesn't require an action or {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB}.

feat.name: Reactive Adaptation
entries: Your body remembers danger and adapts to meet it.

entries.name: Learn the Damage
entries: When you take damage, you can use your {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to choose one damage type dealt by that instance of damage. You gain Resistance to the chosen damage type until the start of your next turn. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Retained Adaptation
entries: If you take the chosen damage type again while Learn the Damage is active, you can extend that Resistance until the end of your next turn without expending another use. You can extend the same adaptation only once.

entries.name: Hardened Response
entries: Whenever your Resistance from this feat reduces damage, you gain {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} after the damage is resolved.

entries.name: Familiar Threat
entries: After you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one damage type that dealt damage to you since your previous {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. The first time you take that damage type before your next Short or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. This reduction applies before you decide whether to use Learn the Damage.

entries.name: Refuse the Same Wound
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you take damage of a type to which you currently have Resistance from this feat, you can cause that instance of damage to deal no damage to you instead. Any other effects of the triggering attack or effect still occur normally.

feat.name: Invocation Initiate
entries: You discover enduring supernatural truths and engrave them into yourself as Invocations.

entries.name: First Invocation
entries: Gain one Invocation and all its benefits. Ignore class-membership prerequisites when choosing through this feat, but meet every other requirement, including level, Pact, and required features.

entries.name: Growing Doctrine
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain one additional Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites. Invocations gained from this feat are permanent unless replaced by Rewritten Doctrine.

entries.name: Rewritten Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace one Invocation gained from this feat with another Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites. If replacing an Invocation causes you to stop meeting the prerequisite of another Invocation you possess, you must also replace any Invocation that depends on it.

entries.name: Invocation Beyond Training
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, choose one Invocation for which you meet every prerequisite except its level requirement. Your level can be up to 2 levels lower than that Invocation's requirement. You temporarily gain that Invocation until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. This temporary Invocation doesn't count against the number of Invocations you gain from this feat.

entries.name: Independent Invocation
entries: Invocations gained from this feat are their own source of power. They don't require spellcasting, spell slots, a particular spell list, or membership in another class unless the Invocation itself explicitly requires one of those things.

feat.name: Invocation Prodigy
entries: You absorb new Invocations with unnatural speed.

entries.name: Accelerated Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain two additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Unending Study
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain one additional Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites. This Invocation is gained in addition to the Invocation granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Refined Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace any number of Invocations gained through this feat with other Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.

feat.name: Invocation Adept
entries: Practice lets you exchange one supernatural doctrine for another.

entries.name: Deepened Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain two additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Living Doctrine
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one Invocation you possess from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, or this feat with another Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites. The new Invocation remains until you replace it again.

entries.name: Practiced Revelation
entries: Choose one Invocation you possess that has a limited number of uses which are restored when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You gain one additional use of that Invocation. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can choose a different eligible Invocation for this benefit. If an Invocation has several separately limited abilities, choose which one receives the additional use when you select it.

entries.name: Expanding Doctrine
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain one additional Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites. This Invocation is gained in addition to the Invocations granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome} and Unending Study from {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}.

feat.name: Invocation Paragon
entries: As your power grows, entire collections of Invocations unfold within you.

entries.name: Greater Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain three additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Cascading Insight
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain two additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations are gained in addition to any Invocations granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome} and Unending Study from {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Perfected Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace any number of Invocations you possess from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, or this feat with other Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites.

entries.name: Endless Revelation
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one Invocation for which you meet the prerequisites that you don't already possess. You gain that Invocation until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. This temporary Invocation doesn't count against the number of Invocations granted by your feats.

feat.name: Invocation Sovereign
entries: Your Invocations answer as one supernatural authority shaped by your will.

entries.name: Sovereign Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain four additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Accelerated Ascension
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain three additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations are gained in addition to those granted by Growing Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, Unending Study from {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, Expanding Doctrine from {@feat Invocation Adept|FftForbiddenTome}, and Cascading Insight from {@feat Invocation Paragon|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Sovereign Selection
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose two Invocations you don't possess for which you meet the prerequisites. You gain both Invocations until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. These temporary Invocations don't count against the number of Invocations granted by your feats.

entries.name: Absolute Doctrine
entries: Whenever you gain a level, you can replace any number of Invocations you possess from {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Prodigy|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Adept|FftForbiddenTome}, {@feat Invocation Paragon|FftForbiddenTome}, or this feat with other Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. You can make these replacements separately; you don't have to replace all of them at once.

entries.name: Perfect Invocation
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose one Invocation you possess that has a limited number of uses restored when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. Until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, the number of uses of that Invocation is doubled. If the Invocation contains multiple separately limited abilities, choose one of those abilities to double.

feat.name: Boon of Infinite Doctrine
entries: An endless lattice of Invocations becomes part of your existence.

entries.name: Infinite Doctrine
entries: You immediately gain ten additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations follow the same rules as Invocations gained through {@feat Invocation Initiate|FftForbiddenTome}.

entries.name: Endless Ascension
entries: Whenever your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} increases, you gain ten additional Invocations for which you meet the prerequisites. These Invocations are gained in addition to every Invocation granted by the earlier feats in this chain.

entries.name: Living Archive
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, choose up to ten Invocations you don't possess. You temporarily gain all chosen Invocations until you finish your next {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. For these choices, you can ignore class prerequisites, Pact prerequisites, required spells, required features, required Invocations, and level prerequisites. You must still possess anything the Invocation actually requires to function.

entries.name: Perfect Doctrine
entries: Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace any number of permanent Invocations you possess from this feat chain with other Invocations. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can replace up to three such Invocations. You must meet the prerequisites of the new Invocations unless another feature allows you to ignore them.

entries.name: Unbound Invocation
entries: Every Invocation you possess that has a limited number of uses has three times its normal number of uses. This applies to uses restored on a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, uses per turn, uses per round, uses tied to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, and any other explicitly limited use count. If an Invocation contains multiple separate use pools, each pool is tripled.

entries.name: Inexhaustible Doctrine
entries: Whenever you expend a use of an Invocation, roll a {@dice d6}. On a 3-6, that use isn't expended. If this causes the Invocation to remain at its maximum number of uses, you can still benefit from this feature.

entries.name: Doctrine Without Limit
entries: Invocations can apply simultaneously whenever their conditions are met, even when modifying the same attack, spell, action, movement, roll, target, or effect. Identically named effects still don't stack unless expressly allowed.

entries.name: Transcendent Invocation
entries: You can substitute your character level for an Invocation's class, Warlock, Pact, or other progression value, and any chosen ability score for its referenced score or modifier. Replace a fixed DC with 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + a chosen ability modifier if higher.

entries.name: Supreme Revelation
entries: You no longer need to meet the prerequisites of Invocations you gain from Living Archive. In addition, once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can permanently gain one Invocation whose prerequisites you don't meet. That Invocation remains permanent even if you later lose whatever would normally qualify you for it.

entries.name: Eternal Revelation
entries: Whenever you gain a character level, choose two temporary Invocations you currently possess through Living Archive. Both become permanent and no longer count against your temporary selections.

entries.name: Absolute Invocation
entries: Once per turn, when you use an Invocation, you can make that use Absolute. For that use, no limited use is expended, no spell slot is expended, and no Material component is required unless it is consumed or has a listed cost. Attack Rolls made as part of that use have Advantage, and Saving Throws made against it have Disadvantage. Damage caused by that use ignores Resistance, and Immunity to that damage is treated as Resistance.

Any dice rolled for damage, healing, Temporary Hit Points, movement increase, or another numerical benefit use their maximum possible result instead of being rolled. If the Invocation has a range other than Self, double that range. If it has a duration longer than Instantaneous, double that duration, to a maximum of 24 hours.

entries.name: Overwhelming Doctrine
entries: Once per {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can activate up to five Invocations simultaneously as part of the same action, Bonus Action, Reaction, attack, spell, or other qualifying event, provided each Invocation could legally apply to that event. If multiple Invocations require the same trigger, they all resolve from that single trigger.

entries.name: Infinite Revelation
entries: At the start of each of your turns, choose one Invocation you don't possess. You gain it until the start of your next turn and can ignore all prerequisites for it. You can choose a different Invocation each turn. This temporary Invocation doesn't count against any other Invocation limit.

entries.name: Doctrine Incarnate
entries: Your Invocations can't be forcibly lost, replaced, suppressed, or disabled without your consent. Antimagic, nullification, dispelling, and similar effects don't suppress them unless an Invocation explicitly says otherwise; they are inherent to you.

feat.name: Counterfighter
entries: You fight best when the enemy commits first. Whenever a creature within your reach misses you with an attack, you can immediately make one melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} against that creature. This attack requires no Reaction and can't trigger Counterfighter again. The attack has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} if the missed attack was a Critical Miss. On a hit, the target can't make Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of its next turn.

feat.name: Flowing Combat
entries: Every attack carries you into the next position. Whenever you make a weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can move up to 5 feet immediately before or after the attack. This movement costs no additional movement, doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the target of that attack, can occur even if your Speed is currently 0 provided you aren't {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB}, and can be used on every attack you make, not just once per turn. You can't use this movement to pass through or enter a space you couldn't normally enter.

feat.name: Deflecting Guard
entries: You don't need to stop an attack completely. A slight change in angle is enough. While you are wielding a melee weapon or are capable of making an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, whenever an attack hits you, you can attempt to deflect the blow. Roll either the normal damage dice of one melee weapon you are wielding or the normal damage dice of your Unarmed Strike. If your Unarmed Strike doesn't normally use damage dice, use a d4 instead.

Reduce the damage you take from the triggering attack by the total rolled + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. This reduction requires no Reaction and can be used against every attack that hits you.
