The reduction applies separately to each attack and can be used against melee attacks, ranged attacks, and spell attacks, provided you can perceive the attack. If you are wielding more than one eligible melee weapon, you choose which weapon's normal damage dice to roll each time you use this Fighting Style.
If your Unarmed Strike can use more than one possible set of damage dice, use the damage dice you would normally use for that Unarmed Strike at the time the attack hits you.

entries.name: Perfect Deflection
entries: If Deflecting Guard reduces the triggering attack's damage to 0, you perfectly deflect the attack.
When this happens, you gain all of the following benefits:

items: You can immediately move up to 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
The attacker can't make Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of its next turn.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the next melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike you make against that attacker before the end of your next turn.

entries: These benefits require no Reaction. The movement granted by Perfect Deflection doesn't count against your Speed.
Deflecting Guard can't reduce damage from an effect that doesn't involve an attack roll.

entries.name: Examples
entries: Use only the weapon's or Unarmed Strike's normal base damage dice. Exclude ability modifiers, magic-item bonuses, and additional dice from other features.

feat.name: Freehand Combat
entries: An empty hand is not an unused hand.
While you are wielding a melee weapon in one hand and holding nothing in the other, you gain the following benefits:

items: You gain a +1 bonus to AC.
Whenever you hit a creature with the weapon, you can immediately attempt to Grapple or Shove that creature as part of the same attack.
Making the Grapple or Shove this way requires no Action or Bonus Action.
A creature Grappled by you doesn't prevent you from continuing to attack with your one-handed weapon.

Whenever a creature you are Grappling misses you with an attack, you can immediately move it 5 feet to another unoccupied space within your reach, provided it is no more than one size larger than you.

entries: The Grapple or Shove is available on every hit; an already-Grappled creature needn't be Grappled again.

feat.name: Threatening Reach
entries: Once something enters your range, leaving it untouched is a choice you rarely make. While wielding a melee weapon or capable of making an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, whenever a hostile creature enters your reach, moves from one space to another while remaining within your reach, or willingly moves 5 feet or more while within your reach, you can immediately make one melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike against that creature.

This attack requires no Reaction, occurs immediately after the triggering movement, doesn't count as an Opportunity Attack, and can be made even if the creature hasn't left your reach. A creature can trigger this Fighting Style multiple times during its turn if its movement creates multiple separate qualifying triggers. If one of these attacks hits, the creature's Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the end of that turn. This reduction is cumulative for multiple hits.

feat.name: Brutal Impact
entries: When you commit to a strike, you make sure the target feels all of it. Whenever you hit with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can make that hit a Brutal Impact. When you do, roll the attack's normal damage dice one additional time and add them to the damage.

Your ability modifier and other flat bonuses are added only once as normal. If the attack is a Critical Hit, the additional damage dice granted by this Fighting Style are also doubled normally. You can use Brutal Impact once on each of your turns. At the end of your turn, if you used Brutal Impact and the attack hit a creature no more than one size larger than you, you can also choose to Push it 5 feet or knock it Prone.

feat.name: Escalating Force
entries: The first hit breaks the guard. The next one breaks everything behind it. Whenever you hit the same creature more than once during a turn with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, each hit after the first deals additional damage equal to one of the attack's normal damage dice.
The bonus increases with each consecutive hit against that creature during the same turn:

items: Second hit: 1 additional normal damage die.
Third hit: 2 additional normal damage dice.
Fourth hit: 3 additional normal damage dice.
Each later hit adds one more normal damage die than the previous hit.

entries: For a weapon whose normal damage is 2d6, each additional normal damage die is 1d6, not 2d6. If you attack a different creature, the count for the original creature ends. The count also ends when your turn ends. If one of these attacks is a Critical Hit, the additional damage dice from this Fighting Style are doubled normally.

feat.name: Crushing Power
entries: Even your weakest strike carries enough force to break something. Whenever you deal damage with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, each of the attack's normal damage dice that rolls below half of that die's maximum value is treated as half of its maximum value instead, rounded up.

This applies to every qualifying attack you make. This Fighting Style applies to all damage dice rolled as part of the attack, including damage dice from the weapon or Unarmed Strike, class features, feats, spells, magic items, and other effects. Whenever every normal damage die of an attack rolls its maximum value, the attack also deals one additional normal damage die.

feat.name: Overwhelming Blow
entries: When you decide that one hit is enough, you make it true. Whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can turn that hit into an Overwhelming Blow. When you do, roll the attack's normal damage dice one additional time and add them to the damage. The attack ignores Resistance to its damage. If the target has Immunity to that damage, treat that Immunity as Resistance instead. Any damage reduction that would reduce the damage of that attack is only half as effective.

After the damage is dealt, if the target is no more than one size larger than you, choose one of the following effects: push it up to 10 feet, knock it Prone, or cause it to drop one object it is holding. You can use Overwhelming Blow once per turn. If the attack is a Critical Hit, the additional damage dice granted by this feat are doubled normally as part of the Critical Hit.

feat.name: Titan Grip
entries: What others need two hands to control, you wield with one. You can wield a melee weapon with the Two-Handed property in one hand.

items: The weapon retains its normal damage dice and all of its other properties.
The Two-Handed property doesn't require a second hand for you to attack with the weapon.
The weapon's Heavy property has no effect on you.
For features, feats, spells, and other effects, you can treat the weapon as being wielded with one hand or with two hands, whichever is more beneficial to you.
Your other hand remains free for weapons, a Shield, Grappling, or object manipulation.
You can draw or stow such a weapon as easily as a one-handed weapon.

Whenever you hit with a melee weapon you are wielding in one hand through this Fighting Style, you can Push the target 5 feet if it is no more than one size larger than you. This requires no additional action or saving throw.
Once on each of your turns when you hit with such a weapon, roll one of the weapon's normal damage dice one additional time and add it to the damage.

feat.name: Charging Force
entries: Momentum turns every step into part of the strike.
Whenever you move at least 10 feet toward a creature immediately before hitting it with a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, the attack gains the following benefits:

items: Roll the attack's normal damage dice one additional time and add them to the damage.
You can Push the target 10 feet directly away from you.
If the target collides with a solid surface or another creature before moving the full distance, it takes additional Bludgeoning damage equal to one of the attack's normal damage dice.
The movement toward the target doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from that target.

entries: Each qualifying attack can benefit, provided you move the required 10 feet before it; sufficient movement permits repeated triggers in one turn.

feat.name: Armor Breaker
entries: Each blow leaves a crack in the guard. Each melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} hit against a creature reduces its AC by 1, cumulatively to a minimum of 10. This lasts 1 minute after your latest qualifying hit; further hits refresh it.

On a hit against an affected creature, you can also damage one defense: worn armor, a Shield, magical armor, Natural Armor, or an ongoing magical effect granting AC, Resistance, Immunity, or damage reduction.

The hit damages both the creature and the chosen defense without reducing its normal damage. If the defense completely blocks the attack from reaching the creature, damage the defense first; the creature takes damage only once the attack can pass through.
Each time you target a defense that provides AC, you permanently reduce the AC it provides by 1. This reduction doesn't disappear when the 1-minute duration ends.

items: Armor or a Shield whose AC contribution is reduced to 0 provides no AC until repaired.
Magical armor or a magical Shield can be physically broken in the same way; being magical doesn't prevent this Fighting Style from damaging it.
Natural Armor can be cracked, shattered, torn, or otherwise breached, preventing the creature from benefiting from the destroyed portion until it is healed, regenerated, or restored.
An ongoing magical defense that is broken is ended, even if it would normally be unable to be damaged by weapon attacks.

entries: A magical defense without a numerical AC bonus breaks after hits equal to its effect level + 1, or 3 hits if unlevelled. Hits remain accumulated across turns and encounters until the defense is repaired, restored, renewed, or replaced.

While a creature has been hit at least 2 times by you while the 1-minute reduction remains active, your attacks against it ignore its damage reduction. While it has been hit at least 3 times, your attacks against it ignore Resistance. While it has been hit at least 5 times, you treat its Immunity as Resistance. While it has been hit at least 7 times, your attacks ignore that Resistance as well.

feat.name: Beyond Your Limits
entries: You push past failure. After an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw fails, you can roll 1d6 and add it to the result, potentially succeeding.

entries.name: Push Further
entries: If the roll still fails after adding the d6, you can roll another d6 and add it as well. You can continue doing this until the roll succeeds or you choose to stop. For every d6 you roll beyond the first, you take 1d12 Force damage after the roll is resolved. This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way, doesn't interrupt the roll you're attempting, and can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Breakthrough
entries: Success after rolling 3 or more d6s grants Advantage on your next d20 Test of the same type—Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw—before the end of your next turn.

feat.name: Strength Above All
entries: Raw strength substitutes for other talents. You can use Strength for any Ability Check, including any Skill or Tool check.

entries.name: Physical Supremacy
entries: You can also use your Strength modifier in place of the normal ability modifier for Initiative, Saving Throws, determining the DC of a feature or ability you use, and Attack Rolls and Damage Rolls with weapons or Unarmed Strikes. If a feature already uses Strength, this provides no additional benefit.

entries.name: Refuse to Falter
entries: Whenever you make a Saving Throw using Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma, you can use your Strength modifier instead. whenever an effect would reduce one of your Ability Scores, you can choose for it to reduce your Strength score instead.

feat.name: Perfect Execution
entries: Once you prove that you can do something, chance has less and less authority over the result. Whenever you succeed on an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw, record the unmodified d20 result of that roll for that type of test. Whenever you later make the same type of test and roll lower than the recorded result, you can expend 1 use of this feat to treat the d20 roll as the recorded result instead. You can use this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Raise the Standard
entries: If you later succeed with a higher unmodified d20 result for the same type of test, the recorded result increases to that number. Recording or increasing a result doesn't expend a use.

feat.name: Absolute Focus
entries: You impose certainty on an attempt. After rolling a d20 for an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw but before resolving it, you can replace the result with 20. It counts as the actual d20 result, including a Critical Hit when a 20 would normally cause one.
You can use this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

feat.name: Act Before the Moment
entries: You act before others can respond. Immediately after a creature you can see starts its turn, interrupt it with a special turn: move up to your Speed, take one Action, and take one Bonus Action. It then resumes where interrupted. Your normal turn and Initiative are unchanged.

Regain your Reaction at the special turn's start; afterward, restore your pre-turn number of Reactions. You can use this feat a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all uses on a Long Rest.

feat.name: Refuse the Outcome
entries: You refuse failure. After an Ability Check, Attack Roll, or Saving Throw fails, you can reroll the d20 instead of resolving failure, using the new result. Repeat failed rerolls until you succeed or choose to stop.

entries.name: The Cost of Insistence
entries: The first reroll is free. For every reroll after the first, you take 1d12 Force damage after that reroll is resolved. This damage can't be reduced or prevented, doesn't interrupt the roll, and can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Uses
entries: You have uses equal to your Proficiency Bonus and regain all on a Long Rest. One use covers every reroll of that test until you succeed or stop.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your forbidden studies open the Archive, granting the features below.

subclassFeature.name: Archive Keeper
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you gain Pact of the Tome without meeting its prerequisites. It doesn't count against Forbidden Invocations, and its Book of Shadows becomes your Archive and Wizard spellbook.

entries.name: Endless Pages
entries: The Archive has effectively endless pages for Wizard spells, Pact magic, and any written or illustrated information. It counts as your spellbook and Book of Shadows. Pact of the Tome spell and cantrip choices can come from any list and use Intelligence.

entries.name: Living Chronicle
entries: The Archive automatically records what you personally see, including detailed portraits and each appearance in which you encounter someone. It reveals no unperceived information. When first gained, it can also record previously encountered people using only details you genuinely remember.
While holding the Archive, request recorded information as a Bonus Action to open its searchable index to the relevant entries. Its records survive the loss of your own memories.

entries.name: The Archive Remembers
entries: Ordinary damage can't permanently erase accepted information. Recreate a lost or destroyed Archive with a 1-hour ritual, restoring all spells, Pact magic, and recorded information; any previous copy disappears on completion.

subclassFeature.name: Forbidden Invocations
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you gain two Eldritch Invocations of your choice from the Warlock class. You ignore every prerequisite for Invocations gained through this feature. If one refers to a prerequisite you lack, you are treated as having it only to use that Invocation; this grants no prerequisite and qualifies you for nothing else. If such an Invocation uses a spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, or spell save DC, you can use your Intelligence and Wizard spellcasting statistics.
Whenever you gain a Wizard level, you can replace one Invocation gained through this feature with another, ignoring its prerequisites.
Pact of the Tome granted by The Archive doesn't count toward this number.

subclassFeature.name: Archive Spells
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you reach a Wizard level shown in the Archive Spells table, the listed spells are added to your Archive if absent, requiring no gold, time, or materials. They aren't automatically prepared unless another feature says otherwise.

subclassFeature.name: Tome Convergence
entries: Starting at 6th level, the Archive can merge with written vessels of magic without destroying them.

entries.name: Merge Spellbook
entries: While touching your Archive and an eligible spellbook, grimoire, codex, tome, or similar written vessel of spells or magical research, perform a 10-minute ritual to merge it. It becomes part of your Archive, Book of Shadows, and Wizard spellbook, with its properties usable through the Archive. Charges, limitations, activation requirements, Attunement, and other rules remain unchanged.
You can merge multiple eligible spellbooks. Merging creates no additional Attunement or Attunement slot, though you must still be attuned to a merged spellbook that requires Attunement at this level.

entries.name: Perfect Copy
entries: Merging copies all written and illustrated contents without gold, special ink, or additional time. Copied Wizard spells remain permanently, including spells above your current casting level; these can't be prepared or cast before normally allowed.

entries.name: Separate Tome
entries: While touching the Archive, perform a 1-minute ritual to separate a merged spellbook intact with its Charges and magical properties. The Archive retains independent copies of its contents; merging again copies new or changed information.

entries.name: Hovering Archive
entries: Without an action from you, the Archive can hover, follow at your normal pace, remain nearby, or enter your reaching hand.

subclassFeature.name: Open the Index
entries: Starting at 10th level, as a Bonus Action, you open the Archive's Living Index for 1 minute. Once used, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest unless you expend a spell slot of 4th level or higher to activate it again.

entries.name: Every Page at Hand
entries: While Open the Index is active, every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is prepared for you without counting against your prepared spells; you still expend spell slots normally. For an Intelligence check concerning a creature, location, object, symbol, event, spell, or other subject previously recorded by the Archive, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

After casting a Wizard spell that wasn't prepared before Open the Index began, you take {@damage 1d4} Psychic damage per spell level. Cantrips cause no damage. If this reduces you to 0 Hit Points, Open the Index ends.

entries.name: Second Mind
entries: When you cast a Wizard spell that requires Concentration, you can have the Archive maintain Concentration instead, requiring no action. You can then concentrate on another spell normally, and the Archive can maintain only one spell at a time. The Archive makes no Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration; damage, effects that would force such a save, and you becoming {@condition Incapacitated} don't end it.

Its Concentration ends only if you die, the Archive is destroyed, you and it are more than 1 mile apart, you end the spell, the spell ends normally, or the Archive begins concentrating on another spell.

subclassFeature.name: The Archive Awakens
entries: Starting at 14th level, the Archive awakens as a living magical entity.

entries.name: Living Archive
entries: The living Archive can independently write, illustrate, rearrange pages, present information, fly, follow, avoid obvious danger, and return to your hand. Ordinary movement and harmless behavior cost you no action. It communicates through writing, illustrations, speech, or telepathy; you can communicate telepathically within 1 mile. It understands your languages and sufficiently documented ones, without teaching them to you.

On the same plane, you always know its direction and approximate distance. Within 30 feet, call it into an empty hand without an action. It recognizes you as Keeper despite changes of appearance, age, disguise, transformation, form, or body.

entries.name: The Archive Acts
entries: Once on each of your turns, the Archive can cast one Wizard cantrip recorded within it without requiring your Action or Bonus Action. It uses your Wizard spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC. The spell originates from the Archive, requires no Verbal or Somatic components from you, and must have a casting time of 1 Action or less. The Archive makes the spell's choices, though you can mentally direct them while within 1 mile. The spell still counts as your Wizard spell for your class and Archive features.

entries.name: Beyond Attunement
entries: The Archive can satisfy merged magic spellbooks' Attunement requirements, granting their properties without your Attunement or slots. You can end existing Attunement while retaining these properties during the merge. Separation ends this benefit; the Archive never permanently copies those properties.

subclassFeature.name: This Is Only the Beginning
entries: Starting at 17th level, the Archive carries your magic beyond conventional limits.

entries.name: Magic Without Permission
entries: Antimagic and similar suppression can't prevent or disable your Wizard spells and class features, Archive features, the Archive itself, merged spellbooks' properties, or spells maintained through Second Mind. Your Wizard spells function normally within, through, and from {@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, dead-magic zones, and similar nullifying effects.

If you create an antimagic or magic-suppressing effect, you can leave your own magic and the Archive unaffected while it suppresses other magic normally. This doesn't make you immune to hostile magic.

entries.name: Beyond the Ninth
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can cast one 9th-level Wizard spell recorded in your Archive without expending a spell slot, following its normal casting time, components, material costs, and consumed components. When you cast a Wizard spell of 6th level or higher, a lower-level spell or magical effect can't counter, dispel, suppress, or end it solely by suppressing magic. Effects of the same or higher level can interact with it normally unless another feature says otherwise.
A 9th-level spell ceiling doesn't restrict Archive features' interaction with those spells. This grants no 10th-level spells or slots.

subclassFeature.name: The Last Archivist
entries: Starting at 20th level, you and the Archive become inseparable.

entries.name: The Archive Within
entries: Every Wizard spell recorded in your Archive is always prepared for you without counting against your prepared spells, and you can cast it with your Wizard spell slots even without the physical Archive. You no longer suffer Knowledge Overload. Anything permanently contained within the Archive remains available through your bond with it.

A lost, sealed, suppressed, or destroyed Archive doesn't remove your recorded Wizard spells or Archive features. Features can access stored spells, formulae, and information regardless of the book's location.

entries.name: The Final Keeper
entries: The Archive can no longer be permanently separated from you. If destroyed, you can use a Bonus Action to recreate it in an empty hand or an unoccupied space within 5 feet, retaining every recorded spell and other preserved record. Tome Convergence doesn't duplicate an external magic item; a merged spellbook remains the same original item. Once you recreate the Archive this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Physiology
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, choose one Manifestation until the start of your next turn:

items: {@b Flow.} Immediately move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
{@b Density.} Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Sorcerer level.
{@b Refraction.} Until the manifestation ends, you have Half Cover.
{@b Surge.} Add your Charisma modifier to one damage or healing roll of the spell.

subclassFeature.name: Spellform
entries: Starting at 3rd level, as a Bonus Action, you can spend 2 Sorcery Points to enter Spellform for 1 minute.
While in Spellform:

items: You can move through creatures but not objects.
You can move through a creature's space without treating it as Difficult Terrain.
You have Advantage on checks and saving throws made to escape a Grapple or the Restrained condition.
You can provide Somatic components even if your hands are occupied.
Your body visibly changes into an arcane form of your choice—living flame, flowing runes, fractured light, black mist, geometric energy, or another magical manifestation.

entries: Spellform doesn't make you incorporeal or let you end your movement inside another creature.

subclassFeature.name: Rewrite the Formula
entries: Starting at 6th level, whenever you cast a Sorcerer spell, you can spend 1 Sorcery Point to alter one of the following properties for that casting:

items: {@b Shape.} If the spell creates a Cone, Cube, Cylinder, Line, or Sphere, you can change it into another of those shapes while preserving approximately the same affected size.
{@b Vector.} Change the direction from which the spell's force or visible effect appears to strike a target.
{@b Signature.} Change one damage type dealt by the spell to Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Psychic, Radiant, or Thunder.
{@b Origin.} Cause the spell to originate from an unoccupied point you can see within 30 feet rather than from yourself, provided doing so doesn't increase its maximum range.

entries: This isn't Metamagic and can be combined with Metamagic normally.

subclassFeature.name: No Longer Entirely Physical
entries: Starting at 14th level, your Spellform gains the following benefits:

items: You gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover.
You can move through solid objects and creatures as though they were Difficult Terrain.
If you end your turn inside a solid object, you are moved to the nearest unoccupied space and take {@damage 1d10} Force damage.
You can't be Grappled or Restrained by purely physical means.
Squeezing never costs you additional movement.

entries: Spellform now costs 1 Sorcery Point.

subclassFeature.name: I Am the Casting
entries: Starting at 18th level, once on each of your turns when you cast a Sorcerer spell of 1st level or higher, you can become part of it until it finishes resolving.
During that casting:

items: You can choose any point occupied by or affected by the spell as your position.
You can move between points within the spell's area or path without spending movement.
Attacks and effects can't target you until the spell finishes resolving unless they can also affect the spell itself.

entries: When the spell finishes resolving, you appear in an unoccupied space the spell affected or passed through. While in Spellform, the first Metamagic option you apply to a spell on each of your turns costs 1 fewer Sorcery Point, to a minimum of 0.

subclassFeature.name: Break the Impossible
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your weapon attacks and Unarmed Strikes count as magical for overcoming Resistance and Immunity. You can physically attack magical effects with a tangible boundary or occupied area, such as barriers, walls, restraints, and summoned bindings. Such an effect has AC 10 + its spell level, or AC 15 if it has no spell level.

On a hit, you damage it as an object. It has Hit Points equal to 5 × its spell level, or 20 Hit Points if it has no spell level. At 0 Hit Points, the struck portion is destroyed, or the entire effect ends if it can't meaningfully exist in separate portions. Instantaneous effects can't be attacked this way. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you can break its stance, preventing it from making Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Nothing Holds Forever
entries: Starting at 7th level, you have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to escape the Grappled, Restrained, or Paralyzed condition. When you fail such a saving throw, you can expend one use of Second Wind to succeed instead. As an Action, you can strike a magical condition affecting yourself or a creature within your reach. Make one weapon attack or Unarmed Strike against AC 10 + the effect's level, or AC 15 if it wasn't created by a leveled spell.
On a hit, end one of these conditions caused by that effect on the target: Charmed, Frightened, Grappled, Paralyzed, Restrained, or Stunned.

subclassFeature.name: Strike Through Magic
entries: Starting at 10th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you can force one magical effect affecting it to make a Constitution saving throw against DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the Strength or Dexterity modifier used for the attack.
On a failed save, choose one:

items: Suppress that magical effect until the start of your next turn.
End one spell of 3rd level or lower affecting the creature.
Prevent the creature from teleporting until the start of your next turn.

entries: At Fighter level 15, the maximum spell level you can end becomes 5th level. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses after a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: There Is No Safe Distance
entries: Starting at 15th level, when a creature you can see within 60 feet attempts to teleport, magically move to another space, or move to another plane, you can use your Reaction to make one weapon attack against it; your weapon's reach or range extends far enough for this attack. On a hit, the creature takes damage normally and must make a Constitution saving throw against your Strike Through Magic DC. On a failure, the movement fails, but any Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell slot, or other resource spent on it is still expended.

subclassFeature.name: Everything Can Break
entries: Starting at 18th level, your attacks can interact with Force effects, incorporeal or ethereal creatures, magical barriers, and similar effects as though they were physically present.
When you hit a creature, object, or magical effect, you can declare a Perfect Break. The attack:

items: Ignores Resistance to its damage.
Treats Immunity to its damage as Resistance instead.
Ignores magical bonuses to AC.
Ignores Half Cover, Three-Quarters Cover, and magical cover.
Can damage magical effects even if they normally state that they can't be damaged.

entries: Against a spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower, you can destroy or end it immediately instead of dealing damage. You can use Perfect Break a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can cast spells from the Wizard spell list as martial techniques through your weapons.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: At 3rd level, you know four Wizard cantrips of your choice. You learn more as shown in the Cantrips column of the Spellblade Spellcasting table. Whenever you gain a Fighter level, you can replace one Spellblade cantrip you know with another Wizard cantrip.

entries.name: Prepared Spells
entries: You prepare Wizard spells, with the number prepared shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Spellblade Spellcasting table. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace any prepared Spellblade spells with other Wizard spells for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Spellblade Spellcasting table shows your spell slots, which you regain when you finish a Long Rest. You reach 5th-level Spellblade spells at Fighter level 11 and never progress beyond 5th-level Spellblade spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: When casting a Spellblade spell through a weapon focus, use the Strength or Dexterity you would use for its attack roll, choosing if both qualify. Spell save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + that modifier; spell attack modifier = your Proficiency Bonus + that modifier.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: Any proficient weapon can focus your Spellblade spells, with Somatic components performed through weapon handling or fighting motions.

subclassFeature.name: Spellwoven Combat
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack with a Spellblade cantrip that normally has a casting time of an Action. If it requires a weapon attack as part of its casting, that attack counts as the attack you replaced. Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can change that attack's damage type to Force, Psychic, or a damage type dealt by one of your prepared Spellblade spells. Choose the type when the attack hits.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Rhythm
entries: Starting at 5th level, once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can immediately cast one Spellblade cantrip with a casting time of an Action.
Casting it this way:

items: Requires no Action or Bonus Action.
Is considered part of the same Attack action.
Can originate from you or from the weapon that triggered this feature.
Doesn't prevent you from making any remaining attacks granted by Extra Attack.

entries: You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. At Fighter level 11, the first use on each of your turns expends no use; a second use that turn expends one.

subclassFeature.name: Blade and Spell as One
entries: Starting at 7th level, when you cast a Spellblade spell of 1st level or higher with a casting time of an Action, you can make one weapon attack as part of the same Action.

Alternatively, when you take the Attack action, you can replace one attack with a Spellblade spell of 1st level or higher that normally has a casting time of an Action. You can do so a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest, and you can't cast more than one leveled Spellblade spell as part of the same Attack action this way.
You can deliver Spellblade spells requiring a melee weapon or melee weapon attack through a proficient ranged weapon, including bows, crossbows, thrown weapons, or firearms if present.

Replace a required melee weapon attack with a ranged weapon attack. Range or reach requirements serving only that melee attack become the ranged weapon's normal range. The spell otherwise resolves normally through the projectile or thrown weapon.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Impact
entries: Starting at 10th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, its next saving throw against one of your Spellblade spells before the end of your next turn is made with Disadvantage. If the next Spellblade spell you use against it instead requires an attack roll, you have Advantage on the first spell attack roll you make against it before the end of your next turn.
Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature with a Spellblade spell, you can prevent it from making Opportunity Attacks until the start of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Pursuit
entries: Starting at 15th level, immediately after you cast a Spellblade spell or make a weapon attack as part of your Attack action, you can teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, once on each of your turns. If you appear within the reach of a weapon you wield, your next weapon attack against a creature within that reach before the end of the turn has Advantage. When you use Action Surge, you can teleport once before or after each Action you take that turn without counting those teleports against this feature's normal once-per-turn limit.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Spellwarfare
entries: Starting at 18th level, when you take the Attack action, you can replace any number of attacks with different Spellblade cantrips that normally have a casting time of an Action; you can't cast the same cantrip more than once during that Attack action this way. Once on each of your turns when you cast a Spellblade spell of 1st level or higher, you can immediately make one weapon attack without using an Action or Bonus Action.

When you use Action Surge, one Spellblade spell of 5th level or lower you cast that turn can be cast without expending a spell slot. Once you do so, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclassFeature.name: Spellcasting
entries: Starting at 3rd level, you can cast spells from the Wizard spell list through physical combat techniques.

entries.name: Cantrips
entries: At 3rd level, you know four Wizard cantrips of your choice. You learn more as shown in the Cantrips column of the Spellfist Spellcasting table. Whenever you gain a Pugilist level, you can replace one Spellfist cantrip you know with another Wizard cantrip.

entries.name: Prepared Spells
entries: You prepare Wizard spells, with the number prepared shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Spellfist Spellcasting table. Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace any prepared Spellfist spells with other Wizard spells for which you have spell slots.

entries.name: Spell Slots
entries: The Spellfist Spellcasting table shows your spell slots, which you regain when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You gain 1st-level spells at Pugilist level 3, 2nd at level 5, 3rd at level 7, 4th at level 9, and 5th at level 11. Your Spellfist spellcasting never progresses beyond 5th-level spells.

entries.name: Spellcasting Ability
entries: Strength is your Spellcasting Ability for your Spellfist spells. Your spell save DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier, and your spell attack modifier equals your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier.

entries.name: Spellcasting Focus
entries: Your body is a Spellcasting Focus for Spellfist spells; fighting motions and breathing can supply Somatic components.

subclassFeature.name: Fists and Formulae
entries: Starting at 3rd level, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one attack with a Spellfist cantrip that normally has a casting time of an Action, then make any remaining attacks normally.

For your Spellfist spells, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} count as proficient melee weapons and can satisfy requirements to wield, use, or attack with a melee weapon. For a Material component or other requirement specifying a melee weapon with a monetary value, an Unarmed Strike counts as a melee weapon worth 1 GP only for casting that spell. If the spell makes an attack with the weapon used in its casting, you can make an Unarmed Strike for that attack.

Whenever you make a spell attack, you can treat it as an Unarmed Strike for Pugilist features that trigger when you make or hit with an Unarmed Strike. It remains a spell attack and deals the spell's normal damage unless another feature says otherwise.

subclassFeature.name: Arcane Follow-Through
entries: Starting at 5th level, once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend 1 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Point} to immediately cast a Spellfist cantrip with a casting time of an Action. The casting requires no Action or Bonus Action, counts as part of the same Attack action, doesn't prevent remaining Extra Attack attacks, and can target the creature you hit or another legal target.

If it targets the creature you hit, you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on the first attack roll of the cantrip, or that creature has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its first saving throw against the cantrip. You can use this feature only once on each of your turns.

subclassFeature.name: Moxie Casting
entries: Starting at 6th level, when you cast a Spellfist spell of 1st level or higher, you can expend Moxie Points equal to the spell's casting level instead of a spell slot. The spell otherwise functions normally, and you can't cast it above the highest Spellfist spell level you can normally cast. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one attack with a Spellfist spell of 1st level or higher that normally has a casting time of an Action, once on each of your turns, then make any remaining attacks normally.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Hits Back
entries: Starting at 11th level, once on each of your turns when you damage one or more creatures with a Spellfist spell, you can immediately make one {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} without using an Action or Bonus Action. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can immediately cast one Spellfist cantrip with a casting time of an Action without using an Action or Bonus Action. You can benefit from each of these effects during the same turn.

When a Spellfist spell requires a spell attack against a creature within your Unarmed Strike's reach, you can instead make an Unarmed Strike attack roll. On a hit, the spell hits and the target suffers both the spell's normal effects and your Unarmed Strike's normal damage; the attack counts as both a spell attack hit and an Unarmed Strike hit.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Arcane Violence
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace any number of attacks with different Spellfist cantrips that normally have a casting time of an Action; you can't cast the same cantrip more than once during that Attack action this way. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can expend Moxie Points equal to the level of a prepared Spellfist spell to cast it immediately without using an Action or Bonus Action.

The spell must normally have a casting time of an Action and must be able to target the creature you hit or have an area that can legally originate from its space. An area spell can include that creature. The spell counts as part of the triggering attack but otherwise follows its normal rules. Whenever you cast a 5th-level Spellfist spell using 5 Moxie Points, roll your Fisticuffs die after it resolves. On a 5 or higher, regain 1 Moxie Point.

subclassFeature.name: Beyond Ordinary Flesh
entries: Starting at 3rd level, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} count as magical for overcoming Resistance and Immunity to nonmagical attacks and damage. For carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, Grappling, and Shoving, you count as one size larger than you are. When you hit with an Unarmed Strike, you can roll twice the normal number of Fisticuffs dice for its normal damage. Only those dice are doubled; your ability modifier and additional damage aren't unless another feature says otherwise. This costs no Moxie Point.

If the hit causes a Strength check or Strength saving throw, the target makes it with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. When you fail a Strength check, Strength saving throw, or Constitution saving throw, you can add one roll of your Fisticuffs die, potentially turning it into a success. You can do so a number of times equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}, regaining all uses on a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

If this turns a failed saving throw into a success, that effect can't knock you {@condition Prone|XPHB}, push, pull, forcibly move you, or reduce your Speed. Your Unarmed Strikes deal double damage to objects and structures and ignore a Damage Threshold equal to or lower than your Pugilist level + your Strength score.

subclassFeature.name: Force of Will
entries: Starting at 5th level, impossible physical prowess reproduces effects others achieve with magic.

entries.name: Impossible Techniques
entries: Choose four cantrips from the Cleric, Druid, Sorcerer, Warlock, or Wizard list as Conquerer Techniques. Use their rules, but the techniques are neither spells nor magical effects, and using them isn't spellcasting.

This grants no Spellcasting or Spell Slots. Techniques can't be {@spell Counterspell|XPHB|Counterspelled}, dispelled, or suppressed by Antimagic or similar effects. Ignore Verbal components; perform Somatic components as physical motions, and provide Material components only if costly or consumed.

entries.name: Strength Is Your Power
entries: Strength is the ability you use whenever a Conquerer Technique refers to your spellcasting ability. Your Technique Save DC equals 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier, and your Technique Attack Modifier equals your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier. If a cantrip uses your spellcasting ability modifier for damage, healing, distance, or another numerical effect, use your Strength modifier instead.

entries.name: Technique Attack
entries: During the Attack action, you can replace one attack with a Conquerer Technique whose normal casting time is an Action. This isn't spellcasting; its attack rolls count as attacks for Pugilist and Conquerer features.

entries.name: Cast Through Violence
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, immediately after the attack's damage, you can use one Action-casting-time Conquerer Technique without an additional Action. It must target or include that creature, or have an area that can legally originate from its space. This isn't spellcasting and is separate from Technique Attack.

entries.name: Growing Force
entries: You learn one additional Conquerer Technique when you reach Pugilist levels 8, 11, 14, and 17.

entries.name: Weaponized Body
entries: Your Unarmed Strikes count as proficient melee weapons worth 1 gp for Conquerer Techniques. Techniques affecting weapons can affect your body, which you count as holding and wielding whenever required.
While such an effect affects your body, every Unarmed Strike, regardless of body part, counts as an attack with that affected weapon for all its benefits and triggers.

subclassFeature.name: Too Tough to Matter
entries: Starting at 6th level, whenever you take damage, reduce it by one roll of your Fisticuffs die + your Constitution modifier + your Pugilist level. This requires no action or Moxie, has no usage limit, and applies every time you take damage. The number of Fisticuffs dice rolled for this reduction increases to two at Pugilist level 11, three at level 17, and four at level 20.

Apply this reduction after every other damage modifier, including Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, multiplication, and other reductions. It is the final reduction before you lose Hit Points, and the damage source can't reduce, ignore, bypass, or prevent it. If the damage remaining after this reduction is equal to or less than your Constitution modifier, you take 0 damage. If this feature reduces damage to 0, any additional effect that would occur solely because that damage was dealt also fails to affect you.

Against an effect that normally deals half damage on a successful save, you take no damage on a success and half on a failure; then apply Too Tough to Matter to any remaining damage. You also have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against being {@condition Frightened|XPHB} or magically put to sleep.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Gives Way
entries: Starting at 8th level, your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} can physically interact with ongoing magical effects that have tangible form or occupy physical space, such as walls, barriers, restraints, conjured objects, Force constructs, cages, chains, and shields. You need no special weapon, damage type, or property to strike them. If such an effect has AC and Hit Points, you can attack and damage it normally. If it normally can't be attacked, make an Unarmed Strike against AC 10 + its spell level, or AC 15 if it has no spell level.

Hitting such an effect deals normal Unarmed Strike damage and lets you suppress a contiguous section up to a 20-foot cube until the start of your next turn. Instead, permanently destroy that section if the effect's level is at most half your Pugilist level, rounded down.

If the entire effect fits, you can destroy it completely. At Pugilist level 17, the spell-level limit disappears. Abstract magic—charms, curses, divinations, teleportation, and resolved spells without physical manifestations—remains ineligible.

subclassFeature.name: Nothing Keeps You Down
entries: Starting at 11th level, at the start of each of your turns, you can end one of these conditions on yourself without an action or Moxie: {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Restrained|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB}. Difficult Terrain costs you no extra movement, standing from {@condition Prone|XPHB} costs only 5 feet, and while conscious your Speed can't be reduced below half its normal value.

You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against being unwillingly transformed, teleported, banished, or transported to another plane. When an effect would move you against your will, you choose how much of that movement occurs, from 0 feet to the full distance.

During your turn, you can move through a hostile creature's space regardless of size, but can't willingly end there. A larger creature's space counts as Difficult Terrain for this movement, and Opportunity Attacks triggered by moving through a hostile creature's space are made with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Magic Cannot Hold
entries: Starting at 14th level, your Unarmed Strikes can interact with ongoing magical effects attached to a creature or object even if the effect has no separate physical form. When you hit a creature or object with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, once on each of your turns you can choose one spell or magical effect affecting it. The effect makes a Constitution saving throw against DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier.

If a spell created the effect, use its caster's spellcasting ability modifier for the save. If it has no identifiable caster, use a modifier equal to the effect's level, or +5 if it has no level. On a failed save, choose one: suppress the effect until the start of your next turn; end it if its spell level is no greater than half your Pugilist level, rounded down; or remove one magical restraint, barrier, transformation, or defensive benefit affecting the target. This costs no Moxie.

On a successful save, you can expend 1 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Point} to force another save with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. If that save fails, treat the effect as 2 spell levels lower when determining whether you can end it.

Against a creature, you can specifically target one magical benefit, such as magical Resistance or Immunity, an AC bonus, regeneration, flight, Invisibility, transformation, temporary form, or protection from forced movement or Prone. On a failed save, that benefit is suppressed until the end of your next turn even if the underlying effect remains active.

subclassFeature.name: The Strongest Thing in the Room
entries: Starting at 17th level, for carrying, lifting, pushing, dragging, Grappling, and Shoving, you count as Gargantuan if smaller. You can Grapple or Shove creatures regardless of size, and your Speed isn't reduced by Grappling, dragging, carrying, or forcibly moving them. A creature you Grapple can't use size alone or a feature that merely says it can't be moved to stop you from moving it. This doesn't overcome something genuinely impossible to move because it has no meaningful movable body or is an immovable part of the environment.

Your Unarmed Strikes ignore Resistance, Immunity, Damage Thresholds, damage reduction, and per-attack damage caps. They can damage physical objects and structures regardless of material, magical reinforcement, or rules describing them as indestructible or immune to ordinary weapon damage. This doesn't let you strike active spells, abstract magical phenomena, or other nonphysical effects.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, the attack deals extra damage equal to three Fisticuffs dice, or four if you already hit that creature with an Unarmed Strike earlier that turn. This costs no Moxie and can apply to the same strike as Beyond Ordinary Flesh and Overwhelming Force.

Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, you can force a Strength saving throw against DC 8 + your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus} + your Strength modifier. A Gargantuan or smaller creature makes it with {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}. On a failure, choose three: push it up to 30 feet; knock it {@condition Prone|XPHB}; Grapple it; make it drop one held object; or prevent it from taking Reactions until the start of your next turn. Its size doesn't prevent these effects.

You can expend 1 {@classFeature Moxie|Pugilist|Pugilist2024|2|Pugilist2024|Moxie Point} when using this feature to make the target automatically fail and apply all five physically applicable effects. Whenever you roll a Fisticuffs die for a Pugilist or Conquerer feature, treat a result below two-thirds of the die's maximum, rounded down, as that value (d8: 5; d10: 6; d12: 8).

subclassFeature.name: The World Yields
entries: Starting at 20th level, whenever you make a Strength check or Strength saving throw, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.

You can attempt otherwise impossible strength feats caused solely by weight, size, structural strength, or scale, using a difficulty-based Strength check instead of automatic failure. This includes moving structures or enormous loads, supporting collapses, forcing gates, tearing magically reinforced structures, redirecting massive moving objects, and resisting automatic forced movement.

entries.name: Unmatched Force
entries: Whenever you hit with an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, use the maximum value of every Fisticuffs die forming the attack's normal Unarmed Strike damage instead of rolling them, including dice added to that normal damage by Beyond Ordinary Flesh. Additional Fisticuffs dice from other Pugilist or Conquerer features are still rolled normally, subject to your level 17 minimum-roll feature.

entries.name: There Is No Immovable Object
entries: When you hit a creature with an Unarmed Strike, ignore any effect preventing it from being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, Grappled, moved while Grappled, or forced to drop an object if that prevention is based on its size, physical strength, weight, stability, anatomy, or magical bodily reinforcement. If an effect would make it completely immovable, it instead has Advantage on the relevant Strength saving throw or ability check against you. A Conquerer feature that makes it automatically fail still overrides this Advantage.

entries.name: The Blow That Moves Everything
entries: Once on each of your turns when you hit with an Unarmed Strike, choose a 30-foot cone originating from the target or a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on it. Each other creature of your choice in the area makes a Strength saving throw against DC 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Strength modifier. On a failure, it takes Bludgeoning damage equal to four Fisticuffs dice and is pushed up to 30 feet in a direction you choose; on a success, it takes half damage and isn't pushed.
Unattended physical objects and structures in the area automatically take the damage. This costs no Moxie.

entries.name: Conquer
entries: Once per {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, when you hit a creature, object, structure, or ongoing magical effect you can physically interact with through your Conquerer features, you can declare that it gives way without Moxie or an additional action. For that strike, ignore all Resistance, Immunity, damage reduction, Damage Thresholds, and damage caps, and maximize the attack's normal Fisticuffs damage and all additional Fisticuffs damage dice from your Pugilist and Conquerer features.

If a non-creature target survives, you can still create a physically meaningful breach large enough for a Gargantuan creature to pass through. If a creature survives, it automatically suffers every physically applicable push, Prone, Grapple, disarm, and no-Reactions effect from The Strongest Thing in the Room.

spell.name: Private Audience

components.m: a folded scrap of paper bearing two written names

entries: Your conversation becomes indistinct beyond an unseen boundary, leaving visible lips and gestures unreadable.

entries.name: Private Conversation
entries: Choose a visible point within range. For the duration, a 10-foot-radius sphere there muffles deliberate conversation. When casting, designate any creatures you can see to hear and understand speech from inside normally. Other creatures outside hear only murmurs and can't read its speakers' lips.

Ordinary recording devices and unattended magical sensors outside the sphere record only indistinct murmurs from speech inside. The spell doesn't conceal creatures, block other sounds, or restrict entry. While inside, you can use a Bonus Action to move its center to a visible point within 30 feet of you.

spell.name: Borrowed Mastery
entries: You borrow the practiced shape of another's experience without diminishing their knowledge.

entries.name: Borrowed Proficiency
entries: Touch a willing creature and choose one of its skill, tool, weapon, or language proficiencies. You gain it for the duration; the donor retains it. If already proficient in the chosen skill or tool, instead add {@dice 1d4} to its ability checks. You gain no Expertise, class features, weapon properties, or associated supernatural abilities.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of level 2 or higher, you can borrow one additional proficiency from the same target for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Arcane Familiarity

components.m: a short length of thread tied around a written word

entries: You trace a temporary path through unfamiliar knowledge, making strange words and tasks feel instinctively familiar.

entries.name: Familiar Knowledge
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one skill proficiency, tool proficiency, or language. The target gains that proficiency for the duration. If the target is already proficient in the chosen skill or tool, it instead adds {@dice 1d4} to ability checks it makes using that proficiency for the duration. If it already knows the chosen language, choose a different option.

spell.name: Arcane Poise

components.m: a polished glass bead

entries: Breath steadies and hesitation fades, lending calm without altering thought or personality.

entries.name: Composed Bearing
entries: Touch one willing creature. For the duration, whenever the target makes a Charisma ability check and rolls a 7 or lower on the d20, it can treat the d20 roll as an 8. The target also has Advantage on ability checks made specifically to maintain composure, conceal nervousness, or speak convincingly under pressure.

spell.name: Perfect Recollection

components.m: a blank card or page

entries: Memories return with their original clarity, revealing nothing beyond what you once perceived.

entries.name: Exact Recall
entries: For the duration, perfectly recall sensory details perceived in the previous 24 hours, reproducing words, images, sounds, sequences, and positions as accurately as originally perceived. You have Advantage on Intelligence checks solely to recall or analyze them. This reveals no unperceived information, corrects no false perceptions, restores no magically removed memories, and identifies nothing previously unrecognized.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The period of memory you can access increases to 7 days with a 2nd-level slot, 30 days with a 3rd-level slot, 1 year with a 4th-level slot, and any memory you still possess with a 5th-level or higher slot.

spell.name: Arcane Edge

components.m: an iron filing wrapped in parchment

entries: A mathematical shimmer traces the weapon, aligning each blow with a second edge of force.

entries.name: Spell-Sharpened Weapon
entries: Touch one weapon. For the duration, the weapon is magical, and attacks made with it can use your spellcasting ability modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for the attack and damage rolls. On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Force damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The extra Force damage increases by {@scaledamage 1d6|1-9|1d6} for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Mystic Aegis

time.condition: which you take when you or a creature you can see within 30 feet is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw

entries: A lattice of force tightens around an imminent threat, then lingers as a faint protective geometry.

entries.name: Reactive Aegis
entries: Choose the triggering creature. If the trigger was an attack, the target gains a +3 bonus to AC against that attack, potentially causing it to miss. If the trigger was a failed saving throw, the target adds {@dice 1d4} to that saving throw, potentially turning it into a success. Until the start of the target's next turn, it also gains a +1 bonus to AC and saving throws.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a slot of level 2 or higher, the lingering bonus to AC and saving throws increases by 1 for every two slot levels above 1, to a maximum of +4.

spell.name: Vortex

components.m: a small spiral shell

entries: Space twists into a violent inward spiral, then snaps shut.

entries.name: Collapsing Spiral
entries: A 10-foot-radius sphere of force forms at a visible point within range. Each creature inside makes a Strength save, which it can choose to fail. Failure deals {@damage 2d10} Force damage and pulls it up to 15 feet toward the center; success deals half damage without pulling.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@scaledamage 2d10|1-9|1d10} for each slot level above 1.

spell.name: Equivalent Exchange

components.m: a pair of balanced scales

entries: Anything may have a price. Matter, years, memories, and souls can purchase what gold alone cannot.

Designate one or more creatures, objects, substances, properties, magical effects, or other things as an Offering and declare the desired result. The spell determines its Equivalent Price. A sufficient Offering is consumed, transferred, altered, surrendered, or otherwise lost as appropriate, and the result is obtained.
If insufficient, the Offering remains untouched and you learn the price isn't met. Nothing is taken unless you choose to complete the exchange.

entries.name: Equivalent Price
entries: Equivalent Price reflects the reasonable cost of obtaining, producing, performing, transferring, or enabling the result under current circumstances, not just monetary or material value.

items: Material value.
Rarity.
Quality.
Complexity.
Magical power.
Permanence.
Availability.
Difficulty of acquisition.
Required expertise.
Labor and time.
Risk to whoever would normally perform the task.
Scarcity of creatures capable of producing the result.
Transportation or access.
Personal or metaphysical significance.
Whether the requested result currently exists at all.
How severely the result violates what would normally be possible.

entries: Simple material exchanges may be nearly equal in market value; scarce expertise can cost far more than raw materials.

entries.name: Price of Access
entries: Material cost alone doesn't bypass scarcity. Equivalent Price includes finding, persuading, and compensating a capable provider, supplying resources, and accepting associated risks.
Rare spellcasters, preparation, danger, inconvenience, and consequences can raise a magical service's price far above its Material component cost.
If no capable provider can reasonably be found, compensating for that absence can raise the price further.

entries.name: Magical Effects
entries: The desired result can be the effect of a spell or another form of magic. You don't need to know or be capable of casting the spell yourself.
Instead, you can request the result you want, such as:

items: Healing that could normally be produced by a spell.
Removal of a curse.
Restoration of a destroyed body.
Teleportation to a distant location.
Transformation into another form.
Creation of a magical structure.
Resurrection.
A specific spell effect.
Another magical phenomenon that can meaningfully be defined.

entries: Price reflects the full difficulty of obtaining the effect. The spell can use any sufficiently equivalent method unless you demand a particular one; specifying an exact spell, caster, power source, or method can raise the price.

entries.name: Magic Items
entries: Magic Items can be offered or requested. Their price reflects current acquisition difficulty, not necessarily market value; readily available items may cost near normal value.
The same item could cost considerably more if:

items: No seller nearby possesses one.
Its method of creation is lost.
The necessary materials are exceptionally rare.
Only a few known artificers can produce it.
Creating it requires dangerous expeditions or unusual magic.
The item is illegal, controlled, sacred, or otherwise difficult to acquire.
Demand greatly exceeds supply.

entries: Unique or irreplaceable items may far exceed ordinary valuations.

entries.name: What Can Be Offered
entries: An Offering isn't limited to physical objects or money.
Anything that can meaningfully be surrendered may possess value for the exchange, including such things as:

items: Objects, coins, precious materials, or Magic Items.
Hit Points or vitality.
Years of a creature's remaining life.
Memories.
Knowledge.
Ability Scores.
Skills or proficiencies.
Spell Slots or magical power.
Conditions, curses, diseases, or injuries.
Physical traits or senses.
A creature's voice, name, appearance, or other personal qualities.
Souls or fragments of souls.
Magical effects.
Services or obligations that can genuinely be surrendered.
Promises, bonds, or other metaphysical things if they possess genuine weight within the world.

entries: An Offering must possess what is surrendered. You must own, possess, control, or have the right to give it unless its owner willingly participates. Willing creatures can contribute, and multiple Offerings can meet one price.

entries.name: Spell Slots as an Offering
entries: Willing creatures can contribute Spell Slots, expended normally and not recoverable by ending or reversing the exchange. Higher-level slots are disproportionately valuable, not merely sums of lower-level slots.

Recovery difficulty and scarcity affect a slot's value; easily restored power may be worth less than permanently lost or scarce power. Slots can purchase nonmagical results when their value meets the price.
You can request Spell Slots. Their price accounts for number, level, normal recovery time, magical capability, and the difficulty of obtaining equivalent power.

Received slots function as recovered expended slots of their level. Receiving a level the creature can't normally possess also requires purchasing the fundamental capacity to contain and use it, at vastly greater cost.

entries.name: Magical Services
entries: A spell effect's price includes the expended slot, caster's scarcity and capability, labor, risk, preparation, components, and other service costs.
Providing your own suitable Spell Slot can substantially reduce the remaining price.
Provided Material components also count toward payment; supplying both power and materials can greatly reduce the remaining cost.

entries.name: Exchange Rather Than Creation
entries: Where possible, the spell obtains an existing result rather than creating from nothing: an available object may be acquired, or an available magical service accounted for.
Obtaining an existing soul may require retrieval, release, persuasion, or ransom; existing knowledge may transfer from an appropriate source. You needn't see or understand the process.

entries.name: The Price of the Impossible
entries: If the requested original no longer exists, is unreachable, or can't otherwise be obtained by exchange, the spell can create or reconstruct the closest equivalent at a dramatically higher price.

A reconstructed, previously destroyed soul is new. Original identity, continuity, memories, relationships, and metaphysical history aren't included unless separately restored or reproduced by the exchange.
Destroyed unique items and magic without a surviving source can likewise be reproduced as equivalents. The further the request departs from obtaining an existing result, the greater its price.

entries.name: Degrees of Equivalence
entries: Offerings need equivalent worth, not similar substance. Money, matter, vitality, knowledge, lifespan, memories, and magic can purchase one another according to their total personal or metaphysical value.

entries.name: Living Creatures
entries: An unwilling creature's intrinsic qualities—including Hit Points, memories, lifespan, soul, abilities, and identity—can't be offered. Receiving a result requires consent only if that result's nature requires it.

entries.name: Understanding the Price
entries: Before committing, you instinctively learn the price's general magnitude: an exact price for straightforward exchanges, or an explanation of extraordinary requirements.
The spell never deliberately deceives you about whether an Offering is sufficient.

entries.name: Examples of Exchange
entries: No request is rejected solely for its magnitude, though its price may be functionally impossible to pay.

spell.name: Shared Concentration
entries: You place a spell's unbroken structure into another willing mind, freeing your own thoughts.

entries.name: Transfer Concentration
entries: Transfer Concentration on a spell you are maintaining to a willing creature you can see within range. All the spell's original statistics, choices, targets, and remaining duration remain unchanged. The target needn't know or be able to cast it.

The target now follows the normal rules for maintaining Concentration on that spell, and your Concentration on it ends without ending the spell. You can immediately concentrate on another spell normally.

spell.name: Arcane Reversal

time.condition: which you take when you succeed on a saving throw against a spell that targets only you, or when a spell attack misses you

entries: You catch a failed spell's momentum and turn it toward a new target without recasting it.

entries.name: Redirect Spell
entries: Redirect the triggering spell to another creature you can see that would be a valid target if it originated from your space. Keep the original caster's statistics and spell level; no recasting, slot, or components are required. Spells with multiple creature targets, areas, object targets, or Self range are ineligible.

spell.name: Arcane Backlash
entries: A quiet resonance waits within the target, turning each act of spellcasting violently against its source.

entries.name: Backlash Mark
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range. It must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failed save, it is marked for the duration. Whenever the marked creature casts a spell of level 1 or higher, it takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage plus Force damage equal to twice the level of the spell it cast. If this damage causes the creature to make a saving throw to maintain Concentration, it has Disadvantage on that saving throw.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Force damage increases by {@scaledamage 1d8|2-9|1d8} for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Borrowed Moment

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet starts its turn

entries: You steal an unspent fragment of another's turn and carry it into your own immediate future.

entries.name: Steal a Moment
entries: The triggering creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, choose one of the following resources: its Action, its Bonus Action, or an amount of its movement equal to its Speed. The creature loses the chosen resource for the current turn. Before the end of your next turn, you gain the corresponding resource once: one additional Action, one additional Bonus Action, or additional movement equal to the amount stolen.
An Action gained from this spell can be used normally, including to cast a spell of level 1 or higher. Any unused stolen resource disappears at the end of your next turn.

spell.name: Borrowed Tomorrow
entries: Your shadow moves ahead as you borrow moments from your own future. Until the end of this turn, borrow actions, movement, reactions, and other opportunities from future turns within Temporal Reach. Each borrowed resource is already spent when its turn arrives.

entries.name: Borrowing from Tomorrow
entries: Each time you borrow something, choose a future turn within your Temporal Reach and take one of the following from it:

items: {@b Action.} You immediately take one additional Action.
{@b Bonus Action.} You immediately take one additional Bonus Action.
{@b Reaction.} You gain one additional Reaction. You can use this Reaction whenever its normal trigger occurs before the beginning of the future turn from which you borrowed it.
{@b Movement.} You immediately gain movement up to your Speed without spending the movement available during your current turn.
{@b Once-per-Turn Use.} You can immediately use a feature or effect that you have already used this turn and that is normally limited to once per turn.
{@b Once-per-Round Use.} You can immediately use a feature or effect that you have already used this round and that is normally limited to once per round.

entries: You must still meet every other requirement of whatever you use. Borrowing something doesn't restore Spell Slots, charges, Hit Dice, limited uses, or any other expendable resource.

entries.name: Escalating Temporal Strain
entries: The first time you borrow something after casting this spell, you take {@damage 1d10} Force damage. Each subsequent borrowing increases this damage by {@damage 1d10}: the second deals {@damage 2d10}, the third deals {@damage 3d10}, and so on. This damage occurs immediately after the borrowed resource is used. If you borrow a Reaction, the damage occurs immediately after you use that Reaction rather than when you borrow it. This damage can't be reduced, prevented, redirected, transferred, or absorbed in any way.

entries.name: The Missing Future
entries: When a turn from which you borrowed something begins, everything taken from that turn is already spent. If you borrowed its:

items: {@b Action,} you can't take an Action during that turn.
{@b Bonus Action,} you can't take a Bonus Action during that turn.
{@b Movement,} the corresponding amount is deducted from the movement available to you during that turn.
{@b Reaction,} you don't regain your Reaction at the start of that turn.
{@b Once-per-Turn use,} that feature is considered already used during that turn.
{@b Once-per-Round use,} that feature is considered already used during that round.

entries: You can borrow multiple different things from the same future turn. You can also borrow the same type of resource from different future turns.

entries.name: Borrowed Spellcasting
entries: Borrowed Actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions belong to their source future turns for spellcasting restrictions, allowing castings your current turn's prior castings would otherwise prevent. A borrowed Reaction can cast a Reaction spell despite your normal Reaction already being spent, but requires its usual trigger.

For once-per-turn and once-per-round spellcasting restrictions, each borrowed resource occurs in its source turn's interval. Slots, components, triggers, and other requirements remain necessary; no Spell Slots are created.

entries.name: Borrowed Movement
entries: Borrow any movement amount up to that normally available on the chosen future turn. Gain it immediately and deduct it when that turn arrives.

entries.name: No Future to Borrow
entries: You can't borrow unavailable resources or the same individual resource twice from one future turn. Later-granted resources function normally but don't refund the borrowed one.

entries.name: Temporal Reach
entries: When cast using a level 3 spell slot, your Temporal Reach includes your next two turns.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: Your Temporal Reach increases by one turn for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Deferred Wound

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 30 feet takes damage

entries: Wounds wait outside the body until borrowed time expires and every injury comes due.

entries.name: Deferred Damage
entries: Reduce the triggering creature's damage to 0 and record its amount and type. Do the same for all damage it would take until the end of its next turn, then apply all recorded damage at once with its original amounts and types. Intervening healing doesn't reduce this total.
Resistance, Immunity, Vulnerability, and other damage modifications are applied when each instance of damage is originally deferred and aren't applied a second time when the recorded damage is taken.

spell.name: Gravity Tilt
entries: You persuade gravity that another direction is down, turning open air into a fall.

entries.name: Personal Down
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range and one direction. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, that direction becomes down for the target for the duration. At the start of each of the target's turns, it falls up to 20 feet in that direction unless something stops the fall. A collision can cause falling damage as normal, treating the distance traveled before the collision as the fall distance. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the saving throw, ending the spell on itself on a success.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The maximum distance the target falls at the start of each turn increases by 10 feet for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Forgotten Presence
