components.m: ash from a burned name or portrait

entries: Memories and records loosen their hold on a person's identity without changing the events they witnessed.

entries.name: Fading Identity
entries: Touch one willing creature. For the duration, creatures other than you have Disadvantage on ability checks made solely to remember, identify, or connect the target to a past encounter unless they are currently observing the target. Ordinary notes, labels, and records that identify the target remain present, but a creature searching them has Disadvantage on ability checks made to locate or connect those records to the target.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell gains the following cumulative effects when cast with higher-level slots:

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: Casual memories of the target's name and appearance become vague unless deliberately refreshed by observing the target or an identifying record.
Ordinary written references, portraits, photographs, and similar identifying records become blurred, incomplete, or contextless for the duration; the underlying objects aren't destroyed.
Ordinary recordings and stored identifying data are affected in the same way, and creatures can't gain Advantage on checks to identify the target from such evidence.
Divination spells of 5th level or lower that are used solely to identify or locate the target from its identity fail to gain useful identifying information.
Memories that directly identify the target become inaccessible while the spell lasts, though a creature still remembers the events themselves with the target's identity indistinct.
Magical and ordinary identifying records of the target are suppressed for the duration unless protected by an Artifact, deity, or magic of comparable power.
All preceding effects apply, and the spell lasts Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Trait Exchange
entries: You transfer a willing creature's physical adaptation into another body, reshaping the recipient to carry it.

entries.name: Exchange Physical Capability
entries: Choose two willing creatures you can see within range. Choose one eligible physical capability possessed by one creature, the donor. The donor loses that capability for the duration, and the other creature, the recipient, gains it.

Eligible capabilities include a Climb, Swim, Burrow, or Fly Speed; Darkvision; Blindsight out to no more than 30 feet; the ability to breathe underwater or in a specific natural environment; a natural adaptation that lets the donor survive ordinary extreme heat or cold; a natural weapon; or a natural body feature used for movement.

The recipient develops temporary anatomy appropriate to the borrowed trait. If the trait is a natural weapon, the recipient uses its own Strength or Dexterity, as appropriate, for the attack and damage rolls and uses the weapon's original damage die, damage type, reach, and physical form. Special riders aren't transferred unless they are inseparable from the physical structure of the weapon. Either participant can take a Bonus Action to end the exchange for itself, returning the trait to the donor and ending that transferred capability.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can transfer one additional eligible capability between the same two creatures for each slot level above 2.

spell.name: Borrowed Shelter
entries: Your shelter shifts between defenses, answering danger with the protection the moment requires.

entries.name: Choose a Shelter
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range and choose one of the following shelters:

items: {@b Bulwark.} The target gains a +2 bonus to AC.
{@b Endurance.} Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Radiant, or Thunder. The target gains Resistance to the chosen damage type.
{@b Steady Mind.} The target has Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.
{@b Sure Body.} The target has Advantage on Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution saving throws.
{@b Covering Veil.} The target has Half Cover against ranged attacks and effects that originate more than 10 feet away from it.

entries.name: Reweave
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can change the shelter affecting one target of the spell to another option.

entries.name: Emergency Shift
entries: When a target of the spell is hit by an attack or fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to change that target's shelter before the triggering attack or saving throw is resolved. The new shelter applies to the triggering event if relevant.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional willing creature for each slot level above 2. Each target can have a different shelter. Reweave and Emergency Shift affect only one target at a time.

spell.name: Spell Graft
entries: A borrowed spell takes temporary root in another willing mind.

entries.name: Graft a Spell
entries: Touch one willing creature and choose one cantrip or level 1 spell that you know or have prepared. The target knows that spell for the duration, even if it has no Spellcasting feature or the spell isn't on any of its spell lists. The target uses your spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC for the grafted spell and follows the spell's normal casting rules and components.

The target can cast the grafted spell once without expending a spell slot. A free casting waives Material components that have no listed cost, but Material components with a listed cost are still required and are consumed normally if the spell says so. After the free casting is used, the target can cast a grafted spell of level 1 or higher only by expending one of its own spell slots of an appropriate level. A grafted cantrip can be cast any number of times while the spell lasts.

You retain the chosen spell. You can maintain only one Spell Graft at a time. Either you or the target can end the graft at any time without using an action; casting this spell again also ends your previous graft.

spell.name: Affliction Relay
entries: You move an affliction's bond from one creature to another, transferring the original burden rather than imitating it.

entries.name: Choose an Affliction
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range that is affected by one instance of the Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Grappled, Poisoned, or Restrained condition. Choose one of the following options.

entries.name: Transfer
entries: A second creature within 30 feet of the first makes a Charisma save. Failure transfers the condition from the first creature to it, retaining source, remaining duration, DC, repeat saves, ending conditions, and other rules. An untransferable physical connection becomes an equivalent spectral restraint or connection.

entries.name: Take
entries: You can choose yourself as the second creature. If you do, no saving throw is required; the chosen condition ends on the original creature and affects you instead.

entries.name: Sever
entries: Instead of transferring the condition, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the level of the spell or magical effect causing the condition. If the effect has no level, the GM assigns it a level from 1 to 9 based on its power. On a success, the chosen condition ends.

entries.name: Borrowed Origin
entries: A transferred affliction remains the same effect for the purpose of immunity, suppression, removal, and interactions with its original source.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a 3rd-level slot, you can also relay the Incapacitated condition; with a 4th-level slot, Paralyzed; with a 5th-level slot, Stunned; and with a 6th-level or higher slot, Petrified.

spell.name: Mirror Wound

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet takes damage

entries: You catch a wound as it forms and divide its burden between bodies.

entries.name: Mirror the Damage
entries: Choose the creature that took the triggering damage and one other creature you can see within range.

entries.name: Share
entries: If both creatures are willing, divide the triggering damage between them in any proportion. The total amount and the original damage types remain unchanged.

entries.name: Take
entries: If you are the second creature, you can take any amount of the triggering damage without making a saving throw, reducing the original creature's damage by the same amount.

entries.name: Reflect
entries: If the second creature is unwilling, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you can transfer up to half the triggering damage, rounded up, from the original creature to the second creature. On a successful save, no damage is transferred.

entries.name: Separate Defenses
entries: Resistance, Immunity, and Vulnerability apply separately to each creature when that creature takes its portion of the damage.

entries.name: No Recursion
entries: Damage created or transferred by Mirror Wound can't trigger another casting of Mirror Wound.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell with a slot of level 3 or higher, the maximum amount you can transfer using Reflect increases by 10 damage for each slot level above 2 and can exceed half the triggering damage. When cast with a 5th-level or higher slot, you can divide transferred damage among up to two secondary creatures. Each unwilling secondary creature makes its own Constitution saving throw.

spell.name: Sealed Agreement

components.m: a written agreement bearing the mark or signature of every participant

entries: Magic seals a willing agreement, ensuring a deliberate breach carries its accepted consequence.

entries.name: Participants and Terms
entries: Choose any number of willing creatures within range that can understand the agreement. Every participant must knowingly and willingly accept the same written terms throughout the casting. If any participant withdraws consent before the casting ends, that creature isn't bound.

The agreement can contain any number of ordinary clauses, but you designate up to three of them as Sealed Clauses. A creature breaches a Sealed Clause only when it knowingly performs an act that clearly violates that clause. Ambiguous, impossible, or involuntary conduct doesn't count as a breach.

entries.name: Breach Consequence
entries: For each Sealed Clause, choose one of the following consequences when you cast the spell. When a bound creature knowingly breaches that clause, the chosen consequence affects that creature for the remaining duration of the agreement unless the consequence says otherwise:

items: {@b Sealed Movement.} All of the breaching creature's Speeds are halved.

{@b Restless Torment.} Whenever the breaching creature attempts to finish a Short Rest or Long Rest, it must make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, magical torment prevents it from gaining any benefits from that rest. It makes this saving throw separately for each rest it attempts.

{@b Withering Judgment.} When the creature breaches the clause, and again at each dawn while this consequence remains, it takes {@damage 6d10} Necrotic damage. This damage ignores Resistance and Immunity to Necrotic damage. Each time the creature takes this damage, its Hit Point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the damage taken. This reduction lasts until this consequence ends.

{@b Arcane Retribution.} Choose Psychic or Force when you create the agreement. When the creature breaches the clause, it takes {@damage 8d6} damage of the chosen type. At each dawn while this consequence remains, the breaching creature and every creature within 10 feet of it take {@damage 2d6} damage of the chosen type.
{@b Arcane Vulnerability.} The breaching creature's saves against spells and magical effects take a penalty equal to Sealed Agreement's slot level minus 1.

entries.name: Spell Clause
entries: Instead of one normal breach consequence, you can designate a Spell Clause. Choose a spell of level 1 or lower that you know or have prepared, has a casting time of an Action or Bonus Action, and can target a single creature. If a participant breaches that clause, the chosen spell is cast on that participant at the next dawn as though you cast it using the same spellcasting ability used for Sealed Agreement. Any costly or consumed Material components required by the chosen spell must be provided during the casting of Sealed Agreement.
A participant can't be affected by more than one Spell Clause from the same Sealed Agreement at a single dawn.

entries.name: Ending the Agreement
entries: The agreement ends early for every participant if every currently bound participant willingly agrees to end it while within 30 feet of one another.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When cast with a 4th-level slot, the duration becomes 1 year. When cast with a 5th-level or higher slot, the duration becomes Until Dispelled.

spell.name: Permanency

m.text: special inks worth 1,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: You replace a spell's ending with a self-sustaining loop that persists until deliberately broken.

entries.name: Make a Spell Permanent
entries: Touch a creature, object, or point affected by your active, non-Instantaneous spell, which must remain active throughout Permanency's casting. Its duration becomes Until Dispelled without Concentration. All other rules remain unchanged, including any option for the caster to end it early.

entries.name: Suppression
entries: An antimagic effect suppresses a spell made permanent by this spell but doesn't end the permanent spell. The spell resumes when the suppression ends unless it was otherwise dispelled or ended.

entries.name: Permanent Limit
entries: You can maintain permanent spells equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier. Before exceeding this limit, end one existing permanent spell of your choice.

spell.name: Void Needle
entries: A hair-thin flaw in space punctures the target, leaving a scar that cuts once more when disturbed.

entries.name: Needle and Scar
entries: Make a ranged spell attack against one creature in range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d12} Force damage. A spatial scar remains in the target's space until the start of your next turn. The first creature other than the original target that enters that space or starts its turn there takes {@damage 1d6} Force damage, and the scar disappears.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The initial damage increases by one {@damage 1d12} at levels 5 (2d12), 11 (3d12), and 17 (4d12). The scar damage increases by one {@damage 1d6} at the same levels (2d6, 3d6, and 4d6).

spell.name: Riftlash
entries: You lash a tear in space across the target, leaving its position dangerously frayed.

entries.name: Spatially Frayed
entries: Make a melee spell attack against one creature within range. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d12} Force damage and becomes Spatially Frayed until the start of your next turn. The first time the frayed target moves 5 feet or more before the effect ends, it takes {@damage 1d8} Force damage. This includes willing movement, forced movement, and teleportation.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The initial damage increases by one {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17. The movement damage increases by one {@damage 1d8} at the same levels.

spell.name: Ready Hand
entries: A fold in space fills your palm with the practical tool the moment demands.

entries.name: Conjured Equipment
entries: Conjure one handheld tool, piece of simple equipment, set of ammunition, or working set of ordinary practical objects of your choice. The conjured matter can weigh up to 10 pounds and must fit within a 3-foot cube. The object functions as a real example of its kind but can't serve as a costly Material component or be sold as genuine permanent goods. As a Bonus Action, you can reform it into another eligible object. It vanishes when the spell ends.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, the weight limit becomes 25 pounds and the space becomes a 5-foot cube. At level 11, the weight limit becomes 100 pounds and you can maintain two conjured objects at once. At level 17, the weight limit becomes 500 pounds, the space becomes a 10-foot cube, and you can maintain three objects at once.

spell.name: Matter Tune
entries: You retune a material's behavior without changing its substance.

entries.name: Tune Matter
entries: Touch one object or continuous portion of material that fits within a 5-foot cube. Choose one mode: Grip, Slip, Harden, Soften, Seal, Float, Insulate, or Conduct.

items: {@b Grip.} The affected surface strongly resists sliding and provides secure handholds and footing.
{@b Slip.} The affected surface becomes extremely slick and difficult to grip.
{@b Harden.} Flexible or fragile material becomes rigid and substantially harder to bend or deform.
{@b Soften.} Rigid material becomes flexible enough to bend, fold, or compress without immediately breaking.
{@b Seal.} Small seams, pores, and ordinary leaks in the affected material close.
{@b Float.} The affected material becomes buoyant enough to float in water unless held under by substantially greater weight.
{@b Insulate.} The material becomes a strong ordinary insulator against heat and electricity.
{@b Conduct.} The material becomes a strong ordinary conductor of heat and electricity.

entries: As a Bonus Action while touching the affected material, you can change its mode.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum affected space increases to a 10-foot cube at level 5, a 20-foot cube at level 11, and a 40-foot cube at level 17.

spell.name: Pinprick Gate
entries: Two pinpricks join distant spaces, admitting light, sound, tools, and careful hands.

entries.name: Linked Gates
entries: Create two linked circular portals in unoccupied spaces you can see within range. Each portal is 1 inch in diameter, and the two portals can be no more than 60 feet apart. A creature adjacent to either portal can see and hear through the other, pass appropriately sized objects through it, reach a body part through it, and treat the opposite portal as the point of origin for a spell or other effect that can physically pass through the opening.
As a Bonus Action, you can move either portal to another unoccupied space you can see, provided both portals remain within the spell's allowed range and separation.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, range becomes 60 feet, maximum separation 120 feet, and diameter 3 inches. At level 11, range becomes 150 feet, separation 300 feet, and diameter 6 inches. At level 17, range becomes 500 feet, separation 1,000 feet, and diameter 1 foot.

spell.name: Skyhook
entries: You fasten an invisible anchor to a position in empty air.

entries.name: Invisible Anchor
entries: Create an invisible fixed anchor at a visible point within range. It supports up to 200 pounds, failing and ending its spell if overloaded. Attach a rope, chain, cord, or similar line; it can catch a falling creature within 5 feet that holds or is attached to the line. You can maintain Skyhooks equal to your Proficiency Bonus; a new one beyond the limit replaces the oldest.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The weight each hook can support increases to 500 pounds at level 5, 1,000 pounds at level 11, and 2,000 pounds at level 17.

spell.name: Counterweight
entries: You alter an object's weight without changing its size or substance.

entries.name: Alter Weight
entries: Touch one object and choose Lighten or Burden. With Lighten, the object weighs one-quarter its normal weight. With Burden, it weighs four times its normal weight. The spell doesn't change the object's size or carrying capacity.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, Lighten reduces weight to one-eighth and Burden multiplies it by 8. At level 11, the values become one-sixteenth and ×16. At level 17, they become one-thirty-second and ×32.

spell.name: Tracefire
entries: Controlled fire traces a precise path for guidance, craft, or harm.

entries.name: Trace a Flame
entries: Trace a line of magical fire up to 30 feet long along a surface or through the air. Choose one mode when you create the line:

items: {@b Guide.} The line provides clear visible guidance along its route.
{@b Signal.} The line flashes or changes intensity in a simple repeating pattern you choose.

{@b Burn.} One creature whose space the line crosses must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 1d12} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a success. A creature can be damaged only once by each casting.
{@b Mark.} The line leaves a harmless visible mark where it touches a surface.
{@b Outline.} The line clings to the outline of an object or opening it crosses.
{@b Fuse.} The line can fuse together a narrow seam in material that ordinary heat could reasonably join.
{@b Rewrite.} As an Action, you can redraw or reposition the existing line within range.

entries: The flame doesn't spread unless the Burn mode directly ignites a readily flammable unattended substance.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Burn damage increases by {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17.

spell.name: Handprint
entries: An invisible handprint records a gesture, ready to repeat it without a hand.

entries.name: Recorded Interaction
entries: Touch an object within a 5-foot cube and perform a simple one-handed interaction requiring no attack roll, save, or check. An invisible Handprint records it. Within 60 feet, use a Bonus Action to repeat it, or choose a simple observable trigger when creating the mark to repeat it automatically.

You can reset a triggered Handprint by touching it. A Handprint can perform its interaction silently if the interaction itself can reasonably be performed without noise. You can maintain a number of Handprints at once equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, the affected object can fit within a 10-foot cube and your remote range becomes 120 feet. At level 11, those values become a 20-foot cube and 300 feet. At level 17, they become a 40-foot cube and 1,000 feet.

spell.name: Palmforge
entries: Matter yields beneath your palm, reshaped by precise intention rather than force.

entries.name: Reshape Material
entries: Touch an object or continuous material within a 1-foot cube and choose Shape, Fit, Join, Separate, Bore, Edge, Texture, or Reform. Make practical changes such as bending, boring, joining compatible pieces, separating seams, sharpening, texturing, or restoring a previously shaped portion. You can't create a complex working mechanism whose internal design you don't understand.
When the spell ends, you can choose for the object's current shape to remain instead of reverting.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The affected size increases to a 3-foot cube at level 5, a 5-foot cube at level 11, and a 10-foot cube at level 17.

spell.name: Forceplate
entries: A translucent plate makes empty air a temporary surface, brace, or barrier.

entries.name: Create Forceplate
entries: Create a flat plane of force up to 2 feet on a side at a point you can see within range. It can support up to 300 pounds and can be oriented in any direction. The plate is solid and can act as a small surface, brace, or barrier. As a Bonus Action, you can move it up to 30 feet to a point you can see and change its orientation. As a Reaction when an unattended object or willing creature within 5 feet of the plate would fall or collide with a surface, you can move the plate up to 5 feet to catch or brace it, provided the weight limit isn't exceeded.
You can dismiss the plate at any time without using an action.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, a plate can be up to 3 feet on a side and support 1,000 pounds. At level 11, a plate can be up to 5 feet on a side and support 5,000 pounds, and you can maintain two Forceplates at once. At level 17, a plate can be up to 10 feet on a side and support 20,000 pounds, and you can maintain three Forceplates at once. If you can maintain more than one plate, each can be moved, oriented, and dismissed independently.

spell.name: Pocket Fold
entries: You crease a pocket into space, leaving its opening within reach.

entries.name: Folded Storage
entries: Create a small extradimensional opening at a point you can see within range. The pocket can contain up to 20 pounds of objects and no more than 1 cubic foot of volume. A creature adjacent to the opening can store or retrieve one object as a Bonus Action. As a Bonus Action, you can move the opening up to 30 feet to another point you can see. If the pocket is overloaded, the excess object falls from the opening and isn't stored. When the spell ends, all stored contents fall harmlessly from the opening's last location.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: At level 5, capacity becomes 50 pounds and 2 cubic feet. At level 11, 200 pounds and 8 cubic feet, and you can maintain a second opening into the same pocket. At level 17, capacity becomes 1,000 pounds and 40 cubic feet, and you can maintain up to three openings.

spell.name: Greenhand

components.m: a seed, leaf, or piece of a living plant

entries: Roots, vines, and leaves grow into useful shapes at your direction.

entries.name: Shape Living Growth
entries: Choose living plant matter within range and create one of the following forms: Vine, Ladder, Brace, Mat, Probe, Filter, Patch, Sprout, or Regrow.

items: {@b Vine.} Grow a flexible plant line that can be used as rope.
{@b Ladder.} Grow climbable stems and grips along a surface.
{@b Brace.} Reinforce or prop a small object or opening with roots and stems.
{@b Mat.} Create a woven surface of roots, moss, or leaves over an area.
{@b Probe.} Extend a thin root or vine into a narrow opening you can reach.
{@b Filter.} Grow a dense layer of plant matter able to strain ordinary debris from air or water.
{@b Patch.} Temporarily close a small tear, hole, or seam with living growth.
{@b Sprout.} Create a healthy young plant from suitable living plant material. This plant remains when the spell ends.
{@b Regrow.} As a Bonus Action, reshape one temporary growth created by this casting into another eligible form.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum useful length or largest dimension of the temporary growth becomes 20 feet at level 5, 40 feet at level 11, and 80 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Mercybrand
entries: A radiant brand promises judgment or mercy, awaiting the moment you spend it.

entries.name: Judgment
entries: Make a ranged spell attack against one creature in range. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d12} Radiant damage and bears your Mercybrand until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Mercy
entries: Instead of attacking, you can place a Mercybrand on one willing creature in range for the duration.

entries.name: Use a Mercybrand
entries: You can use a brand you placed in one of the following ways:

items: {@b Guard.} When the branded creature takes damage, you can take a Reaction to end the brand and reduce the damage by {@dice 1d8} + your spellcasting ability modifier.
{@b Rally.} As a Bonus Action, end the brand. The creature gains {@dice 1d6} Temporary Hit Points.
{@b Beacon.} You always know the direction of a branded creature while it is within 1 mile of you, and you know if it reaches 0 Hit Points.
{@b Signal.} You can cause the brand to glow, dim, or pulse in a simple pattern without using an action.
{@b Transfer.} As a Bonus Action, move the brand to a willing creature within 5 feet of the branded creature.

entries: You can have Mercybrands on multiple creatures, but a creature can bear only one Mercybrand from you at a time.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Judgment damage increases by {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17. Guard's reduction and Rally's Temporary Hit Points each gain one additional die of their listed size at those levels.

spell.name: Warden's Grasp
entries: A hand of condensed force strikes with precision or steadies the world within its grasp.

entries.name: Strike
entries: Make a ranged spell attack against one creature within range. On a hit, it takes {@damage 1d12} Force damage. Immediately after the attack, you can move one unattended object weighing 10 pounds or less that is within 10 feet of the target up to 10 feet.

entries.name: Manifest Hand
entries: Instead of making the attack, manifest a spectral hand at a point within range for the duration. It can support up to 30 pounds. As a Bonus Action, you can move the hand up to 30 feet and have it perform a simple physical task such as handle an object, brace something, carry a light object, hold a rope, or relay an item. As a Reaction, you can command the hand to catch a falling unattended object or willing creature within 5 feet of it, provided its weight limit isn't exceeded.
You can also use the hand to shove or hold fast a light unattended object when physically reasonable. You can reform a destroyed or dismissed hand as a Bonus Action while the spell lasts.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: Strike damage increases by {@damage 1d12} at levels 5, 11, and 17. The hand's weight capacity becomes 100 pounds at level 5, 300 pounds at level 11, and 1,000 pounds at level 17.

spell.name: Voidstride
entries: Your outline skips across a brief absence in space, which closes behind you.

entries.name: Short Teleport
entries: Teleport up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space you can see. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The teleport distance becomes 15 feet at level 5, 20 feet at level 11, and 30 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Death Recall
entries: A corpse recalls its final capabilities for one borrowed turn, without life or undeath.

entries.caption: Death Recall Progression
rows: Last Motion: half Speed, one ordinary attack, one simple object interaction.
Lesser Reconstruction: full movement, ordinary combat Actions, Bonus Actions, one Reaction; temporary bodily repair.
Greater Reconstruction: special actions and reconstructed anatomy; cantrips and spells up to half its former maximum spell level, rounded up.
Perfect Reconstruction: full former capabilities; temporary resources last only for the Stolen Turn.

entries.name: Stolen Turn
entries: Choose one corpse you can see within range. Immediately after your turn ends, the corpse takes one Stolen Turn under your control, using the statistics and capabilities it possessed immediately before it died, subject to the limits below. The corpse isn't revived and doesn't become Undead.

entries.name: Level 1: Last Motion
entries: The corpse can move up to half its Speed, take the Attack action to make one ordinary attack it possessed in life, and perform one simple object interaction. It can use inherent riders that are inseparable from that ordinary attack. It can't use a Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, Multiattack, Recharge action, Legendary Action, or other special action.

entries.name: Level 5: Lesser Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use its full Speed and movement modes, Multiattack or another ordinary combat Action it possessed, Bonus Actions, and one Reaction during the Stolen Turn. The spell temporarily repairs major bodily damage and can restore one missing limb or equivalent structure for the duration of the Stolen Turn.

entries.name: Level 11: Greater Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use special actions, Recharge abilities, breath weapons, supernatural movement, teleportation, and transformations it possessed in life. It can cast its cantrips and spells up to a spell level equal to half the highest spell level it could cast in life, rounded up, using its original spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC. A spell slot required for a spell cast during the Stolen Turn is treated as available for that casting. The spell reconstructs anatomy necessary for those abilities.

entries.name: Level 17: Perfect Reconstruction
entries: The corpse can use its full capabilities from immediately before death, including Actions, Bonus Actions, one Reaction, spells, innate spells, limited-use abilities, and Legendary Actions when their normal timing permits. Temporary resources supplied by this spell exist only for the Stolen Turn.

entries.name: Concentration and Return to Death
entries: If the corpse casts or activates something that requires Concentration, the corpse maintains that Concentration using its original Constitution saving throw modifier. That Concentration ends when Death Recall ends. At the end of the Stolen Turn, every temporary reconstruction and resource created by this spell disappears and the corpse returns to death.

spell.name: Glacier Fang
entries: A ridge of frost along the weapon bites after its edge and steals momentum.

entries.name: Frozen Weapon
entries: Touch one weapon. For the duration, attacks made with it deal an extra {@damage 1d4} Cold damage. Once on each turn when the weapon deals this extra damage to a creature, that creature's Speed is reduced by 5 feet until the start of the attacker's next turn. As a Bonus Action while holding the affected weapon, you can extinguish one ordinary flame no larger than a torch within 5 feet of the weapon or freeze a small amount of exposed water it touches. If you stop holding the weapon, the spell remains on it until the end of your next turn before ending.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The extra damage becomes {@damage 2d4} at level 5, {@damage 3d4} at level 11, and {@damage 4d4} at level 17. The Speed reduction becomes 10 feet at level 11 and 15 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Fatehook

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 30 feet makes an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw

entries: You hook a loose thread of chance and pull an attempt toward success or failure.

entries.name: Boon or Bane
entries: Roll {@dice 1d4}. Choose Boon or Bane. With Boon, add the number rolled to the triggering roll. With Bane, subtract it. If you choose Bane against an unwilling creature, that creature can make a Wisdom saving throw. On a success, Fatehook has no effect on its roll.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The die becomes {@dice 1d6} at level 5, {@dice 1d8} at level 11, and {@dice 1d10} at level 17.

spell.name: Ghostwalk
entries: The target's outline blurs as solid matter yields to its passage.

entries.name: Partial Spectral Form
entries: Choose one willing creature you can see within range. For the duration, the target and everything it is wearing or carrying can move through creatures and solid objects. Moving through such matter costs 1 extra foot of movement for each foot traveled. The target can't move through more than 15 continuous feet of solid matter during a single passage.

entries.name: Ethereal Reach
entries: The target can reach a hand or held object through a solid barrier as part of an interaction, provided the depth of solid matter doesn't exceed the spell's current passage limit.

entries.name: Living Passage
entries: Moving through another creature doesn't damage or displace either creature, and the spaces occupied by creatures are treated as Difficult Terrain for the target.

entries.name: Distort Through Openings
entries: The target can squeeze through openings substantially smaller than its body if its carried equipment can pass with it in spectral form.

entries.name: Look Beyond
entries: By placing part of its face through a barrier within the passage limit, the target can see and hear from the opposite side.

entries.name: Safe Return
entries: If the spell would end while the target is inside a solid object or creature, the target is immediately moved by the shortest route to the nearest unoccupied space it can occupy.

entries.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The maximum continuous depth of solid matter becomes 30 feet at level 5, 60 feet at level 11, and 120 feet at level 17.

spell.name: Rewind

components.m: a small hourglass filled with silver sand

entries: You rewind one creature through its recent moments, restoring its past while leaving every consequence of its actions intact.

entries.name: Rewind
entries: Choose a visible creature within range, or one that died within the rewind period. Restore its exact state at the start of its previous turn or the turn before that, your choice.

This includes the target's location, Hit Points, Temporary Hit Points, conditions, spell slots, expended Hit Dice, expended class features, species features, and other limited-use abilities, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement, magic item charges it expended, ammunition and other expendable resources it used, Material components it consumed, Concentration, physical form, missing or destroyed body parts, and equipment and carried objects it possessed at that moment.
If the target's former space is occupied or otherwise impossible for it to occupy, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space it can safely occupy.

entries.name: The World Remains Changed
entries: The world isn't rewound: the target's damage, deaths, healing, condition changes, altered objects, ongoing spells, summons, revealed information, and others' movement or teleportation remain as they are. Ongoing spells retain their normal remaining durations.
Restored resources return without undoing the effects their expenditure produced.

entries.name: Death Rewound
entries: If the target died after the chosen point and was alive at that point, it returns to life as part of the rewind. The target doesn't need to be willing. If the target was dead at the chosen point, the spell restores it to that dead state instead.

spell.name: Sovereign Edict
entries: A decree moves with you, compelling the surrounding world to contest every violation.

entries.name: Sovereign Aura
entries: A 30-foot Emanation surrounds and moves with you. Choose one Edict when casting. Whenever another creature first enters on a turn or starts its turn there, choose independently whether to subject it to the Edict. You are exempt, and leaving ends its subjection.

entries.name: Defy the Edict
entries: Each attempted violation requires a Charisma save against your spell save DC. Success permits the action or effect. Failure prevents it without spending its Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, slot, charge, or other resources.

entries.name: No Passage
entries: A subject creature can't willingly leave the Emanation. Teleportation, planar travel, or any other effect it willingly uses to move itself outside the Emanation is also prohibited. If you move far enough that a subject creature would fall outside the Emanation, the creature isn't dragged with you; the Edict doesn't prevent you from moving away from it.

entries.name: No Violence
entries: A subject creature can't willingly deal damage to another creature. This includes weapon attacks, spells, features, and other effects whose direct result would deal damage to another creature. It can still attack objects, move, defend itself, heal, or use effects that don't deal damage to another creature.

entries.name: No Restoration
entries: A subject creature can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points. It can still cast or use an effect that restores Hit Points to another creature, provided the subject creature doesn't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points from that effect.

entries.name: No Transformation
entries: A subject creature can't willingly change its form, size, or physical shape through a spell, feature, or magical effect. A transformation already active when the creature becomes subject to the Edict isn't ended.

entries.name: No Spellcasting
entries: A subject creature can't cast spells of 6th level or lower. Spells of 7th level or higher can be cast normally.

spell.name: Severance

components.m: a length of silver thread cut cleanly in two

entries: You draw an unseen edge across the bonds of magic, memory, identity, and ownership.

Choose a creature you can see within range. An unwilling target makes a Charisma save; a willing one can fail willingly. On failure, immediately sever up to three connections below. Multiple instances count separately unless specified otherwise.

entries.name: Concentration
entries: Choose one spell or effect on which the target is concentrating. The target's Concentration on that effect immediately ends.

entries.name: Summoning
entries: Sever the sustaining connection to one creature the target summoned, conjured, or called. It immediately disappears, returning to the state or place appropriate to its summoning effect, or simply ceasing to be present if none exists.
The creature disappears even if it normally survives losing contact with its summoner. Other creatures created by the same effect remain unless their connections are also severed.

entries.name: Control
entries: End one magical control connection between the target and another creature, including Charm, possession, domination, supernatural commands, compulsion, or obedience. Other creatures' connections remain unless severing this one necessarily ends the entire effect.

entries.name: Telepathic Link
entries: End one magical telepathic, sensory, emotional, or communication link involving the target. Neither side can communicate, perceive, share senses, or exchange information through it.

entries.name: Shared Effect
entries: End one ongoing magical link between the target and another creature, including shared damage, Hit Points, senses, conditions, resources, benefits, harm, or other linked states.

entries.name: Planar Bond
entries: Sever one magical bond between the target and a plane, location, creature, or object. This transports neither endpoint, destroys neither, and reverses no past consequences.

entries.name: Remote Effect
entries: Permanently sever the target's remote control over one ongoing spell or magical effect. The effect continues independently if possible; otherwise, it ends.

entries.name: Spell or Curse
entries: Sever one ongoing spell, curse, or magical effect from the target, including magical disease, afflictions, transformations, restraints, seals, wards, buffs, debuffs, Until Dispelled effects, and permanent magic. Other targets and areas remain affected unless the effect depends on this connection.
The casting of Severance must be sufficiently powerful to cut the chosen effect, as described under Severance Power.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: End Attunement to one magic item without altering the item. This can overcome curses or properties preventing voluntary separation if Severance is sufficiently powerful.

Ending Attunement doesn't automatically end unrelated effects that the item already created unless you separately sever those effects. Attunement to an Artifact requires a sufficiently powerful casting of this spell.

entries.name: Memory
entries: Permanently remove one memory or connected group concerning a clearly defined creature, place, event, period, relationship, agreement, experience, or subject. Replace them with plausible false memories, changing surrounding recollections only enough to maintain a natural, continuous, internally consistent past.
Use the smallest plausible reconstruction that conceals what was removed. Reality is unchanged.

Evidence and others' memories remain unchanged. Contradictions can reveal inconsistency but don't restore removed memories. The target can relearn information and form new memories normally. Protected or exceptionally resistant memories may require a higher-level casting.

entries.name: Identity
entries: You sever the target's identity from the memories of every other creature that currently remembers the target as an individual. This counts as one connection, regardless of how many creatures are affected.

Affected creatures permanently forget the target's identity and all personal memories linking it to their experiences, including names, appearance, voice, personality, relationships, conversations, promises, emotions, and roles in events. The target retains its own memories.

entries.name: Reconstructed Identity
entries: Each affected creature receives plausible false memories requiring the fewest changes, leaving no obvious gaps.
Different creatures can receive different replacement histories.
Reconstruction uses only knowledge and possibilities plausible within the creature's experience.

entries.name: Evidence Remains
entries: Reality and surviving physical, written, and magical evidence remain unchanged. Affected creatures can rediscover the target, meet it anew, and form new memories, but can't recognize it through severed recollections.

entries.name: Seamless Reconstruction
entries: Memory and Identity replacements become actual memories, not ongoing illusions. They survive Antimagic Field and dispelling Severance and aren't automatically revealed by Detect Magic. Contradictory evidence remains, and sufficiently powerful memory magic can later alter, remove, or replace them.

entries.name: Violent Severance
entries: After severing connections, choose a clean Severance for no damage, or a violent one dealing {@damage 4d10} Force or Psychic damage, your choice, per severed connection. Only the primary target takes damage, after all severing resolves; Identity's other affected creatures take none.

entries.name: Cut Either Side
entries: A connection's creator or ownership doesn't restrict severing it. Beneficial and harmful links, including those maintained by third parties, are eligible; you can also cut another creature's Concentration.

entries.name: Severance Power
entries: Severance's slot level must meet or exceed the chosen spell effect's level. For unlevelled magic, the DM determines the minimum required level from its power and source.

Ordinary curses, magic item effects, supernatural bonds, memories, Attunement, and similar connections can normally be severed by the spell's base 7th-level casting unless something specifically makes them more powerful.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: Sever up to four connections, including spells and effects of 8th level or lower and those resisting ordinary removal: powerful curses, self-protected effects, protected memories, involuntary Attunement, and Artifact-created or sustained effects, bonds, and Attunement. Artifact properties themselves aren't damaged, suppressed, or removed. Four violent severings deal at most {@damage 16d10}.

Sever up to five connections, including spells and effects of 9th level or lower regardless of protections against removal. Eligible links include permanent magic, Artifact bonds and Attunement, divine curses, blessings, possession or control, deity-created or sustained bonds, comparably protected memories, and similar transcendent sources. The deity itself remains unaffected. Five violent severings deal at most {@damage 20d10}.

spell.name: Final Sanctuary
entries: An unseen boundary denies the protected creature to hostile intent.

Choose one willing creature you can see within range. For the duration, hostile creatures can't directly affect the target unless they first succeed on a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature makes this save each time it attempts to directly affect the protected target. On a failed save, the attempted effect fails against that target.

entries.name: Protected Against
entries: Protection includes attacks, harmful spells, conditions, curses, forced movement, grapples, restraints, possession, Charm, domination, imposed teleportation, and other hostile effects directly targeting or specifically including the creature. Other targets remain affected normally.

entries.name: Area Effects
entries: Before creating an area including the target, a hostile creature makes a Charisma save against your spell save DC. Failure requires placement, aim, or shape that excludes the target, if possible.

If the effect can't be used without including the protected target, the attempted use fails, and any Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell slot, charge, or other resource that would have been spent isn't expended. On a successful save, the effect can include the protected target normally.

entries.name: Indirect Harm
entries: Existing environmental hazards remain: collapses, fire, terrain loss, and objects no longer deliberately or magically directed at the target. Deliberately creating or directing such hazards specifically to harm it still requires the save.

entries.name: The Target Can Still Act
entries: The protected creature can attack, cast spells, move, and otherwise act normally. Doing so doesn't end Final Sanctuary.

entries.name: Absolute Refuge
entries: If a creature succeeds on its saving throw against Final Sanctuary, it can affect the protected creature with that one effect only. It must save again for any later hostile action or effect.

spell.name: Grand Design

m.text: a sculpted figure depicting the intended transformation, worth at least 1,000 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: You persuade flesh and bone to accept another shape as natural, leaving lasting anatomy rather than lingering magic.

Permanently reshape a willing creature you touch, including yourself. It retains its identity, creature type, personality, memories, class features, ability scores, and other statistics except as granted adaptations specify. At 7th level, choose two Major Adaptations and any number of cosmetic changes.

entries.name: Cosmetic Alterations
entries: Permanently change ordinary physical appearance without mechanical benefit, including proportions, coloration, coverings, voice, sex characteristics, decorative anatomy, and apparent age. Apparent age doesn't alter actual age, lifespan, development, or aging effects.

entries.name: Repeated Transformation
entries: Repeated castings are unlimited, permanent, and cumulative, including on yourself. New adaptations leave earlier ones intact unless you choose to remove, replace, reshape, or upgrade them.

The same adaptation doesn't normally stack with itself unless that adaptation specifically says it can be chosen more than once. A later casting using an 8th- or 9th-level spell slot can add Greater or Perfect Adaptations to a creature that was previously altered by a lower-level casting.

entries.name: Major Adaptations
entries: The following adaptations are available when Grand Design is cast using a 7th-level spell slot or higher.

entries.name: Wings
entries: The target permanently grows functional wings and gains a Fly Speed equal to its Speed.

entries.name: Aquatic Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Swim Speed equal to its Speed and can breathe air and water. It also suffers no harmful effects from ordinary underwater pressure.

entries.name: Burrowing Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Burrow Speed equal to half its Speed through earth, sand, clay, and similar natural material. It can't burrow through solid stone or worked structures.

entries.name: Climbing Adaptation
entries: The target gains a Climb Speed equal to its Speed and can move across walls and ceilings without needing to use its hands.

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: The target develops scales, plates, dense hide, crystalline tissue, barklike growth, or similar protection. While the target isn't wearing armor, its base AC is 13 + its Dexterity modifier.

entries.name: Natural Weapon
entries: The target gains a natural weapon of an appropriate physical form: a Simple Melee weapon with which it is proficient. The weapon deals {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, chosen on creation. The target can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls.

entries.name: Enhanced Senses
entries: The target gains Darkvision 120 feet. If it already has Darkvision, its existing range instead increases by 60 feet.

entries.name: Elemental Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison. The target permanently gains Resistance to the chosen damage type. This adaptation can be chosen more than once, choosing a different damage type each time.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: The target counts as one Size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift.

entries.name: Compression
entries: The target can squeeze through spaces as though it were one Size smaller.

entries.name: Additional Limbs
entries: The target grows an additional pair of functional arms, tentacles, or similar appendages for ordinary object handling and interactions. They grant no additional Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, or attacks.

entries.name: Prehensile Tail
entries: The target grows a prehensile tail or similar appendage for simple object interactions. It can't wield weapons, use Shields, or perform Somatic components unless another feature permits it.

entries.name: Leaping Musculature
entries: The target's Long Jump and High Jump distances are tripled. It doesn't need to move 10 feet before making a running jump. The first 20 feet of any fall are ignored when calculating its falling damage.

entries.name: Amphibious Skin
entries: The target can breathe air and water and can comfortably survive ordinary freshwater, saltwater, and deep-water environments. Unlike Aquatic Adaptation, this adaptation doesn't grant a Swim Speed.

entries.name: Environmental Adaptation
entries: Choose extreme heat or extreme cold. The target automatically succeeds on saving throws and ignores ordinary environmental penalties caused solely by the chosen environment. This doesn't grant Resistance to Fire or Cold damage.

entries.name: Keen Senses
entries: Choose sight, hearing, or smell. The target has Advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on the chosen sense. This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different senses.

entries.name: Venom Gland
entries: The target develops organs capable of producing dangerous venom. Once per turn when the target deals Piercing or Slashing damage with a natural weapon created by this spell, it can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Poison damage.

entries.name: Adhesive Limbs
entries: The target can adhere to solid surfaces. It can remain attached to walls and ceilings without using its hands.

entries.name: Dense Frame
entries: The target can permanently increase its weight to as much as four times its normal weight without changing Size. It has Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being pushed, pulled, knocked Prone, or otherwise forcibly moved.

entries.name: Hollow Frame
entries: The target can permanently reduce its weight to as little as one-quarter normal. Falling damage it takes is reduced by an amount equal to five times its Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Extended Reach
entries: Choose one pair of limbs or one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its reach increases by 5 feet.

entries.name: Echolocation
entries: The target gains Blindsight 10 feet while it can hear. This sense doesn't function while the target is Deafened.

entries.name: Photosynthetic Tissue
entries: If the target spends at least 1 hour in bright sunlight during a day, it requires only half as much food that day. This doesn't remove its need for water, air, or rest.

entries.name: Naturalized Form
entries: The alterations created by Grand Design aren't an ongoing spell effect. Once the casting is complete, they become part of the target's actual body. Dispel Magic can't remove them. An Antimagic Field doesn't suppress them. They don't require Concentration, don't disappear when the caster dies, and physical body parts created by the spell can be injured, severed, healed, or restored like natural body parts.

Magic that restores a lost natural body part can restore one created by this spell. The target is not considered transformed by an ongoing spell merely because its body was altered by Grand Design. The spell doesn't automatically cause alterations to become hereditary. Whether descendants can inherit them depends on the creature's biology and the setting.

entries.name: Reversal and Further Modification
entries: Another casting of Grand Design can permanently remove, replace, reshape, or upgrade alterations previously created by the spell. A Wish spell or similarly powerful effect can also restore a creature to an earlier physical form. There is otherwise no automatic expiration to the transformation.

entriesHigherLevel.name: 8th-Level Casting
entries: When you cast Grand Design using an 8th-level spell slot, choose three adaptations rather than two. Each choice can be a Major Adaptation or one of the following Greater Adaptations.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: The target permanently gains Blindsight 60 feet.

entries.name: Greater Wings
entries: The target gains a Fly Speed equal to twice its Speed and can Hover. If it already possesses Wings from this spell, Greater Wings replaces that adaptation.

entries.name: Greater Burrowing
entries: The target gains a Burrow Speed equal to its Speed. It can burrow through natural earth normally and through solid natural stone at half speed. It still can't freely burrow through worked structures.

entries.name: Regenerative Flesh
entries: At the start of each of the target's turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point and no more than half its Hit Points, it regains Hit Points equal to its Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Flexible Anatomy
entries: The target can compress its body enough to pass through an opening as narrow as 6 inches without squeezing. Objects too large to fit through the opening don't compress unless they are physically part of the transformed body.

entries.name: Greater Natural Weapon
entries: Choose one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its damage die becomes {@damage 2d8} instead of {@damage 1d8}.

entries.name: Greater Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. The target permanently gains Resistance to the chosen damage type. This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different damage types.

entries.name: Mighty Frame
entries: The target can become Large, with equipment reshaped to fit but no other Size-based statistic changes. If already Large or larger, it can instead count as one additional Size larger for carrying, pushing, dragging, and lifting.

entries.name: Tremorsense
entries: The target gains Tremorsense 60 feet while it and whatever it is detecting are in contact with the same ground or continuous solid surface.

entries.name: Elastic Anatomy
entries: The target can freely extend or retract elastic anatomy, increasing its reach for unarmed strikes, natural weapons, and object interactions by 10 feet.

entries.name: Chameleon Flesh
entries: The target can alter the color, pattern, and texture of its exterior to match its environment. It has Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks. It can also take the Hide action while only Lightly Obscured by natural terrain or environmental features.

entries.name: Reactive Armor
entries: When the target takes Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Poison damage, it can use its Reaction to gain Resistance to that instance of damage.

entries.name: Venomous Arsenal
entries: Choose one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Once per turn when the target hits with that weapon, it deals an additional {@damage 2d8} Poison damage. When this adaptation is gained, you can choose Acid instead of Poison.

entries.name: Secondary Heart
entries: The target develops redundant circulatory organs. It has Advantage on Constitution saving throws against effects that would cause it to be Paralyzed, Stunned, or Unconscious.

entries.name: Redundant Organs
entries: The target's vital organs are duplicated or distributed through its body. It has Advantage on saving throws against Poison and Disease. Destroying or removing a single ordinary vital organ doesn't by itself kill the target.

entries.name: Amphibious Metabolism
entries: The target can hold its breath for 1 hour. If it can already breathe underwater, it no longer needs to breathe while underwater.

entries.name: Thermal Vision
entries: The target gains Darkvision 180 feet. Within 60 feet, it can also perceive creatures through ordinary smoke, mist, steam, and similar atmospheric concealment by detecting heat differences.

entries.name: Shock-Absorbing Body
entries: The target gains Resistance to falling damage and damage caused specifically by collisions or crushing impacts.

entries.name: Reserve Metabolism
entries: The target can survive for 30 days without food and 7 days without water before suffering the normal effects of deprivation. This doesn't prevent Exhaustion from other sources.

entriesHigherLevel.name: 9th-Level Casting
entries: When you cast Grand Design using a 9th-level spell slot, choose four adaptations. Each choice can be a Major Adaptation, Greater Adaptation, or one of the following Perfect Adaptations.

entries.name: Truesight
entries: The target permanently gains Truesight 60 feet.

entries.name: Perfect Flight
entries: The target gains a Fly Speed equal to twice its Speed and can Hover. It doesn't fall solely because it becomes Incapacitated while airborne. If it possesses Wings or Greater Wings from Grand Design, this adaptation replaces them.

entries.name: Greater Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of the target's turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains {@dice 2d10} Hit Points. This replaces Regenerative Flesh rather than stacking with it.

entries.name: Deathless Organs
entries: The target's vital anatomy becomes extraordinarily redundant. It has Advantage on Death Saving Throws. When it rolls a 19 or 20 on a Death Saving Throw, it gains the benefit normally gained from rolling a 20. The destruction of an ordinary individual organ doesn't automatically kill it while enough of its body remains functional.

entries.name: Perfect Resilience
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. The target permanently gains Immunity to the chosen damage type. Any Resistance it possesses to that type from Grand Design is replaced by this Immunity. This adaptation can be chosen repeatedly for different damage types.

entries.name: Colossal Anatomy
entries: The target can permanently become Huge. Its equipment can be reshaped to accommodate its body as part of the casting. Its statistics don't otherwise change merely because of its Size.

entries.name: Mutable Flesh
entries: As a Bonus Action, the target can change its cosmetic appearance and retract or manifest Grand Design's external adaptations. Retraction doesn't remove an adaptation; another Bonus Action can manifest it again.

entries.name: Perfect Adaptation
entries: Choose two Major Adaptations. Those two adaptations together consume only one adaptation choice from this casting.

entries.name: Universal Respiration
entries: The target needn't breathe and ignores ordinary hazards operating solely through prevented respiration, including suffocation, drowning, smoke inhalation, and vacuum.

entries.name: Perfect Metabolism
entries: The target no longer needs ordinary food or water to survive. It can still eat and drink normally. This doesn't remove its need for rest.

entries.name: Perfect Senses
entries: The target gains Darkvision 300 feet, Blindsight 30 feet, and Tremorsense 60 feet. If it already has one of these senses with a greater range, it retains the greater range.

entries.name: Distributed Mind
entries: The target's nervous system and cognitive functions become distributed throughout its body. It has Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws against effects that would Charm it, Frighten it, Stun it, or control its actions. Destroying or removing its head doesn't automatically kill it while enough of the rest of its body remains functional.

entries.name: Perfect Regrowth
entries: If the target loses a limb or other body part, that part naturally regrows after {@dice 1d6} hours, provided the target remains alive. A severed body part held against its original location can instead reattach over the course of 1 minute.

entries.name: Internal Armory
entries: The target can retract any natural weapon created by Grand Design completely inside its body and manifest it again as a Bonus Action. Whenever it manifests that weapon, it can change its damage type to Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing.

entries.name: Perfect Camouflage
entries: As a Bonus Action, the target can alter its exterior with such precision that it becomes Invisible until the start of its next turn, until it makes an attack roll, or until it casts a spell. It can do this a number of times equal to its Proficiency Bonus and regains all expended uses when it finishes a Long Rest.

entries.name: Living Fortress
entries: The target's body becomes extraordinarily resistant to physical harm. While it isn't wearing armor, its base AC is 18. A Shield can modify this AC normally.

entries.name: Perfect Amphibian
entries: The target can survive comfortably in air, water, extreme ocean depths, and vacuum. It suffers no harm from ordinary environmental pressure or lack of atmospheric pressure. This doesn't provide Resistance or Immunity to magical or supernatural pressure damage.

entries.name: Adaptive Immunity
entries: Whenever the target finishes a Long Rest, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Thunder. The target gains Immunity to the chosen damage type until it finishes its next Long Rest. The chosen type can be changed after each Long Rest.

entries.name: Monstrous Reach
entries: Choose one pair of limbs or one natural weapon created by Grand Design. Its reach increases by 15 feet.

entries.name: Independent Limbs
entries: Once on each turn, the target's coordinated additional limbs grant one extra object interaction and let it draw or stow up to two objects without an Action. They grant no additional Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, or attack.

entries.name: Perfect Compression
entries: The target can compress its body enough to pass through an opening as narrow as 1 inch, regardless of its Size. Equipment physically incorporated into the target's transformed anatomy compresses with it. Separately carried objects don't.

entries.name: Ageless Body
entries: The target continues aging chronologically without physical deterioration, weakness, or frailty from age alone. Other causes, including damage, disease, starvation, and suffocation, can still kill it.

spell.name: Spellheart

m.text: a flawless gemstone worth at least 2,500 GP, which the spell consumes

entries: You engrave a spell into a willing soul, making its magic an innate part of the creature.

Choose one willing creature you touch throughout the casting and one spell of 3rd level or lower that you know, have prepared, or have recorded in a spellbook you can use. The chosen spell becomes permanently embedded within the target.

entries.name: Innate Spell
entries: The target permanently gains the ability to cast the embedded spell without needing to prepare it or otherwise know it. When the spell is embedded, choose Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. The target uses that ability as its spellcasting ability for the embedded spell. If the target doesn't already have a spell save DC or spell attack modifier using that ability, its spell save DC equals 8 + its Proficiency Bonus + the chosen ability modifier, and its spell attack modifier equals its Proficiency Bonus + the chosen ability modifier.

entries.name: Casting the Embedded Spell
entries: The target can cast the embedded spell at its lowest level once per Long Rest without a slot. It can also use its own slots, including higher-level slots, normally.
The target doesn't need to possess the spell on any of its class spell lists to cast it this way.

entries.name: Components
entries: Normal Verbal, Somatic, and Material components remain required, including costly and consumed components.

entries.name: Permanent Integration
entries: After the ritual, the innate capability is permanent, not an ongoing spell. Dispel Magic can't remove it. Antimagic Field can suppress its castings and effects but not remove the capability. The caster's death or loss of the original spell source doesn't affect it.
The target doesn't need to remain near the original caster and retains the embedded spell even if it later changes class or loses access to the spell list from which the spell originally came.

entries.name: Repeated Spellheart
entries: Repeated castings can grant unlimited different embedded spells, including to yourself. Embedding an already-granted spell adds no copy or free uses.

entries.name: Replacing or Removing a Spell
entries: A later casting can remove one embedded spell or replace it with an eligible spell. Wish or similarly powerful magic can also remove one.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: You can embed a spell of 5th level or lower. The target can use the embedded spell's free casting twice per Long Rest instead of once. Both free castings are made at the embedded spell's lowest level. When using a spell slot of its own, the target can still upcast the embedded spell normally.

You can embed a spell of 7th level or lower. The target can use the embedded spell's free casting three times per Long Rest. All three free castings are made at the embedded spell's lowest level. When using a spell slot of its own, the target can still upcast the embedded spell normally.

spell.name: Soul Anchor

m.text: a specially prepared vessel worth at least 5,000 GP, which the spell consumes when the anchor activates

entries: A prepared vessel remembers a living soul and waits to restore it when death arrives.

Choose one willing living creature you touch and one object within your reach that will serve as its Soul Anchor. When the casting is completed, the target becomes permanently bound to that anchor until the bond is triggered or removed. The target can be you.

entries.name: The Anchor
entries: Choose a nonliving object capable of remaining intact as the Soul Anchor. It needn't stay nearby; the target always knows whether it exists and which plane it occupies.

entries.name: When the Target Dies
entries: On death, the anchor activates. After 1 minute, the body and equipment worn or carried at death disappear and reappear in the nearest unoccupied space within 5 feet of the anchor. The target is alive with full Hit Points, restored body parts, and its memories and equipment from death.

The creature's spell slots, expended features, charges, and other resources remain exactly as they were when it died. Conditions or effects that ended only because the creature died don't automatically return unless their own rules say otherwise. The Soul Anchor is then consumed, ending the spell.

entries.name: Forced Return
entries: Restoration doesn't require willingness at death or a free soul. The anchor attempts to reclaim trapped, imprisoned, consumed, or otherwise bound souls or consciousness, though sufficiently powerful effects can prevent this at the DM's discretion.

entries.name: Destruction of the Anchor
entries: If the Soul Anchor is destroyed before the target dies, the spell ends without triggering. Destroying the anchor doesn't harm the target.

entries.name: No Distance Limit
entries: The target and its Soul Anchor can be any distance apart, including on different planes of existence. Distance doesn't weaken the bond.

entries.name: Recasting Soul Anchor
entries: A creature can have only one Soul Anchor from this spell. Recasting replaces the old bond without otherwise harming the old anchor.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The Soul Anchor activates immediately when the target dies instead of after 1 minute. The target can also choose whether its equipment returns with it or remains where it died.
Activation doesn't consume the anchor. It becomes dormant until the target finishes 7 Long Rests, then can restore the target again while the anchor survives.

spell.name: Unbound
entries: Your body and will refuse magical restraint.
While the spell lasts, you gain the following benefits:

items: Your Speed can't be reduced, and you ignore Difficult Terrain.

You can move through the spaces of creatures and through nonmagical objects as though they were Difficult Terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 2d10 Force damage.
You can't be Grappled, Paralyzed, Petrified, Restrained, or magically put to sleep.
You can take Actions, Bonus Actions, and Reactions even if another effect would normally prevent you from taking them.
Magical effects can't force you to move, teleport you, banish you, or change your form unless you allow them to.
You can speak and provide Verbal components even while within an area of magical Silence.
You can perform Somatic components even if your hands are occupied or restrained.
You don't require Material components that lack a listed cost.

entries: For Unbound's duration, you can ignore magical limitations directly preventing movement, actions, spellcasting, or feature use. Their source effects aren't ended; unexpired effects resume restricting you afterward.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The duration becomes 8 hours, and the spell can't be ended early by Dispel Magic or a similar effect unless that effect was created with a 9th-level spell slot or is otherwise capable of ending a 9th-level spell.

spell.name: Invincible Form
entries: Your body is forced into a state that refuses to acknowledge damage as meaningful.
For the duration, you gain the following benefits:

items: You have Resistance to all damage.
Whenever you take damage, reduce that damage by 10 after applying Resistance.
Your Hit Point Maximum can't be reduced.
You can't be knocked Prone or moved against your will.
You have Advantage on Strength and Constitution saving throws.
If damage would reduce you to 0 Hit Points but not kill you outright, you drop to 1 Hit Point instead.

entries: Each time the final benefit prevents you from dropping to 0 Hit Points, its damage reduction increases by 5 for the rest of the spell.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The damage reduction becomes 15 instead of 10, and you are immune to the Grappled and Restrained conditions for the duration.
The damage reduction becomes 20, and while you have at least 1 Hit Point, damage can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point unless the damage would kill you outright.

spell.name: Worldbreaker Lance
entries: You condense overwhelming magical force into a single line and drive it through everything in its path. A 300-foot-long, 10-foot-wide line erupts from you in a direction you choose. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12} Force damage and is pushed up to 30 feet directly away from you. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pushed. Objects and structures in the line take the spell's full damage automatically.

The line ignores half cover and three-quarters cover. Nonmagical objects and structures reduced to 0 Hit Points by this spell are destroyed outright, and the line continues through them without ending. Magical barriers and created objects in the line take damage from the spell as though they were creatures. If such an effect has no Hit Points, treat it as having Hit Points equal to 20 × the level of the spell that created it for the purpose of this spell only.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The damage increases to {@damage 24d12}, and the line becomes 15 feet wide.
The damage increases to {@damage 48d12}, the line becomes 20 feet wide, and creatures that fail the saving throw are also knocked Prone.

spell.name: Arcane Cataclysm
entries: You force raw magic into a violent collapse and detonate it at a point you can see within range.

Each creature in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 10d12} Force damage and suffers one of the following effects of your choice:

items: It is knocked Prone.
It is pushed up to 30 feet directly away from the center of the sphere.
It can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.
Its Speed is halved until the end of its next turn.

entries: On a successful save, the creature takes half as much damage and suffers none of the additional effects. Objects and structures in the area take the spell's full damage automatically.

entries.name: Arcane Collapse
entries: Any spell or magical effect whose area overlaps the sphere and whose level is lower than the spell slot used to cast Arcane Cataclysm immediately ends, provided it is an effect that could normally be ended by {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The damage increases to {@damage 20d12}, and you can choose two additional effects instead of one.
The damage increases to {@damage 40d12}, and you can choose all four additional effects for creatures that fail the saving throw.

spell.name: Spell Devourer

time.condition: which you take when you are targeted by a spell or included in a spell's area

entries: You seize the magic attempting to affect you, tear it from its caster's control, and consume it as your own power. The triggering spell is the first spell devoured by this casting. If it was cast using a spell slot of 7th level or lower, it has no effect on you. If it affects other creatures or areas, it continues to affect them normally.

For the duration, whenever you are targeted by a spell or included in a spell's area, you can devour that spell as it affects you. If the spell was cast using a spell slot of 7th level or lower, it has no effect on you. A devoured spell otherwise continues to affect other creatures, objects, and areas normally.
Each time you successfully devour a spell, choose one of the following benefits:

items.name: Arcane Nourishment.
items.entry: Regain one expended spell slot of a level equal to or lower than the devoured spell's level, up to a maximum of 5th level.

items.name: Borrowed Power.
items.entry: Until Spell Devourer ends, you know the devoured spell and can cast it without expending a spell slot or providing Material components. You use your own spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC for it. Each casting uses the same spell level as the spell you devoured. If you choose this benefit for multiple spells, each of those spells remains available to you until Spell Devourer ends.

items.name: Overcharge.
items.entry: Gain Temporary Hit Points equal to 10 × the devoured spell's level. Until the end of your next turn, you have Advantage on spell attack rolls, and creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against the next spell you cast.

entries: Spell Devourer has no limit on the number of spells it can devour during its duration. If a spell was cast without using a spell slot, the GM determines its effective spell level for the purpose of this spell.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: You can devour spells of 8th level or lower, and Arcane Nourishment can restore a spell slot of up to 6th level.
You can devour spells of 9th level or lower, and Arcane Nourishment can restore a spell slot of up to 7th level.

spell.name: Sovereign Pressure
entries: You release an overwhelming magical presence that crushes resistance and forces weaker wills beneath your authority. When you cast this spell, each creature of your choice within 60 feet of you must make a Wisdom saving throw.
On a failed save, a creature is Overwhelmed for the duration. While Overwhelmed, it suffers the following effects:

items: Its Speed is halved.
