It has Disadvantage on attack rolls against you.
It has Disadvantage on saving throws against your spells and magical effects.
It can't willingly move closer to you unless you allow it.
It can't take Reactions.
The first time on each of its turns that it deals damage to you, reduce that damage by 20.

entries: At the end of each of its turns, an Overwhelmed creature can repeat the saving throw, ending the effect on itself on a success. Whenever a creature succeeds on this saving throw, you can use your Reaction to force it to reroll the save and use the new result.

entries.name: Crushing Presence
entries: Whenever a creature Overwhelmed by this spell starts its turn within 30 feet of you, it takes {@damage 4d10} Psychic damage. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage is knocked unconscious rather than killed, unless you choose otherwise.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The radius becomes 90 feet, the damage reduction becomes 30, and Crushing Presence deals {@damage 8d10} Psychic damage.

The radius becomes 120 feet, the damage reduction becomes 40, and Crushing Presence deals {@damage 16d10} Psychic damage. Creatures affected by the spell also have Disadvantage on the saving throw they make at the end of their turns to end the effect.

spell.name: Death Sentence
entries: You designate one creature you can see within range as condemned. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it becomes Condemned for the duration. On a successful save, it takes {@damage 6d10} Necrotic damage, and the spell ends.
While Condemned, the target suffers the following effects:

items: The target can't regain Hit Points.
It has Disadvantage on Death Saving Throws.
Whenever you deal damage to it, it takes an additional {@damage 3d10} Necrotic damage. This additional damage can occur only once per turn.
The first time each round the target is reduced to half its Hit Points or fewer, it must immediately make another Constitution saving throw.

entries: On a failed save against this secondary saving throw, the target takes {@damage 10d10} Necrotic damage. If this damage reduces the target to 50 Hit Points or fewer, you can execute it. If you do, the target immediately drops to 0 Hit Points. A creature that is immune to Necrotic damage can't be executed by this spell, but it can still become Condemned. At the end of each of its turns, the target can repeat the original saving throw, ending the spell on itself on a success.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The bonus damage becomes {@damage 6d10}, the secondary damage becomes {@damage 20d10}, and the execution threshold becomes 75 Hit Points.

The bonus damage becomes {@damage 12d10}, the secondary damage becomes {@damage 40d10}, and the execution threshold becomes 100 Hit Points. In addition, the target has Disadvantage on all saving throws it makes against this spell.

spell.name: Arcane Overlord
entries: You tear away the restraints on your spellcasting and force your magic to operate beyond its normal limits.
For the duration, you gain the following benefits:

items: Whenever a spell you cast deals damage, that damage is increased by {@damage 2d10} Force damage. This increase applies each time the spell deals damage.
When you cast a spell that forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw, choose one creature affected by the spell. That creature has Disadvantage on its first saving throw against that spell.
When you cast a spell with a casting time of 1 Action, you can cast it as a Bonus Action instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until the start of your next turn.
Casting a spell as a Bonus Action through this spell doesn't prevent you from casting another leveled spell during the same turn.
Your spell attacks ignore half cover and three-quarters cover.
Your spells ignore Resistance to Force, Necrotic, Psychic, Radiant, Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, and Thunder damage.
If a spell you cast would normally end because you lose Concentration, you can choose for it to remain active until the end of your next turn instead.

entries.name: Unrestricted Casting
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell using a spell slot of 5th level or lower, you can cast that spell without expending the spell slot.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The additional damage becomes {@damage 4d10}, and Unrestricted Casting can affect spells of 6th level or lower.

The additional damage becomes {@damage 8d10}, Unrestricted Casting can affect spells of 7th level or lower, and you can use the Bonus Action casting benefit twice on each of your turns instead of once.

spell.name: Grand Survey

m.text: a map, chart, or blank sheet of parchment worth at least 100 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You extend your awareness across the surrounding land and impress what you perceive onto the material used to cast the spell. When the casting is complete, choose a point on the same plane within 10 miles of you. For the duration, you gain supernatural knowledge of the area within 5 miles of that point.
You learn the location and general nature of:

items: settlements, roads, ruins, caves, tunnels, and major structures;
bodies of water, cliffs, forests, mountains, and other major terrain features;
active portals, teleportation circles, planar breaches, and extradimensional entrances;
areas affected by spells or persistent magical effects of 7th level or lower;
creatures of your choice that are Huge or larger;
any concentration of 100 or more creatures within a contiguous area;
major sources of magical power, provided they aren't concealed by an effect of a higher level than this spell.

entries: The spell doesn't automatically reveal the identities of individual creatures, the contents of sealed containers, thoughts, passwords, or information that couldn't reasonably be represented as a location or feature.

entries.name: Living Map
entries: The material component becomes a magical map for the duration. The map updates itself as terrain, creatures, magical effects, entrances, and other revealed features change.
While touching the map, you can focus on any revealed location and learn:

items: its approximate dimensions;
its distance and direction from you;
whether it is above ground, underground, underwater, or extradimensional;
and the shortest reasonably traversable route to it known to the spell.

entries: The map can reveal secret doors, hidden passages, buried chambers, and magically concealed locations if the effect hiding them was created by a spell of 7th level or lower.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The chosen point can be within 100 miles, the surveyed radius becomes 20 miles, and the duration becomes 24 hours.

You can choose any point on the same plane that you can name or clearly identify, the surveyed radius becomes 100 miles, and the duration becomes 7 days. Effects of 8th level or lower can't conceal locations or magical phenomena from the survey.

spell.name: Echoes of the Departed

components.m: an object that belonged to the deceased creature or a fragment of its remains

entries: You give residual memory a voice. Touch the component and name a creature dead no more than 100 years. Its spectral echo appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet. This reconstruction of memory, emotion, and magic is neither its soul nor a resurrection.
For the duration, the echo can:

items: speak and understand the languages the creature knew in life;
answer questions using memories the creature possessed before death;
describe creatures, locations, events, objects, and conversations it personally witnessed;
reproduce its own voice, mannerisms, and appearance as they were at any point in its life;
identify individuals, symbols, places, or objects it personally knew;
recount memories without the evasiveness normally associated with {@spell Speak with Dead|XPHB}.

entries: The echo can't deliberately lie, but its memories can still be incomplete, mistaken, altered, or missing.

entries.name: Memory Reconstruction
entries: Ask the echo to reconstruct any personally experienced memory within 30 feet. Chosen creatures can see and hear it but can't interact or alter it. Each reconstruction lasts up to 10 minutes and can be paused, replayed, or viewed from anywhere within it. Any number can be reconstructed during the spell.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The creature can have been dead for up to 1,000 years, the duration becomes 8 hours, and Memory Reconstruction can recreate an area up to 100 feet across.

There is no limit based on how long the creature has been dead, the duration becomes 7 days, and the echo can reconstruct memories even if its physical remains no longer exist, provided you possess an object that was personally significant to it.

spell.name: Witness of the Place

m.text: a silver lens worth at least 500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You awaken the memory carried by a place itself, drawing impressions from stone, soil, air, and lingering magic. Choose the area within 60 feet of you. For the duration, you can perceive significant events that occurred within that area during the previous 30 days. As an Action, choose a point in the area and a moment or event you wish to investigate. If such an event occurred there, the area produces a spectral reconstruction of it.

entries.name: Echo of Events
entries: The reconstruction can reproduce:

items: creatures that were physically present;
their appearance, movements, voices, and visible actions;
spoken conversations;
spells and magical effects that were visibly or audibly manifested;
objects that were moved, damaged, created, destroyed, or taken;
entrances, exits, hidden passages, or doors used during the event;
the sequence and approximate timing of events.

entries: This is the location's residual history, not a creature's memory. Move through it freely and pause, resume, replay, or adjust playback speed.

entries.name: Truth of the Scene
entries: Focus on a depicted creature, object, or event to learn whether illusion, shapechanging, disguise, memory manipulation, or similar magic altered it. Magic of 7th level or lower reveals both appearance and reality. The spell reveals no thoughts, intentions, unmanifested information, or events entirely outside the area.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: You can examine events from the previous 10 years, the radius becomes 300 feet, and the duration becomes 8 hours.

You can examine any event that has ever occurred within the area, the radius becomes 1 mile, and the duration becomes 7 days. Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't conceal, erase, or falsify the history revealed by this spell.

spell.name: Sanctum of Accord

m.text: a silver seal worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You inscribe a binding sanctuary into a structure, chamber, or enclosed area you touch. The protected area can fill a space up to 100 feet on a side. When you cast the spell, choose creatures individually, by a clearly defined group, or by a password or symbol known to you. Those creatures are Authorized for the duration. You decide which Authorized creatures receive each beneficial effect of the sanctum. You can grant or withhold individual benefits separately for each creature or clearly defined group.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.

entries.name: Absolute Threshold
entries: An Unauthorized creature can't enter the protected area by teleportation, planar travel, extradimensional movement, possession, or magical transformation that would place it inside. If such a creature attempts to enter by one of those means, the attempt fails and any resource used is expended. Physical entry remains possible unless prevented by another effect.

entries.name: Sanctified Interior
entries: While inside the sanctum, Authorized creatures gain the following benefits:

items: They have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.
They can't be magically Charmed, Frightened, or possessed.
Their location can't be detected by Divination spells cast from outside the sanctum.
Magical effects originating outside the sanctum can't forcibly teleport, banish, summon, or move them out of it.
Creatures outside the sanctum can't magically observe or hear events occurring inside it.

entries.name: Suppression of Intrusion
entries: Whenever an Unauthorized creature inside the sanctum casts a spell of 5th level or lower, you can cause that spell to fail. You don't need to be present or conscious to do so. The spell slot and any consumed components are still expended. You can suppress a number of spells equal to your Proficiency Bonus during the spell's duration.

entries.name: Living Seal
entries: While touching any part of the sanctum, you know:

items: how many Unauthorized creatures are currently inside;
whether an Authorized creature has entered or left since you last checked;
whether the sanctum has been targeted by a spell or magical effect;
and the location of any damaged opening, broken seal, or magical breach within the protected area.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The protected area can be up to 500 feet on a side, the duration becomes 7 days, and Suppression of Intrusion can stop spells of 6th level or lower.

The protected area can encompass an entire structure or contiguous complex no larger than 1 mile across, the duration becomes 30 days, and Suppression of Intrusion can stop spells of 8th level or lower. In addition, teleportation, planar travel, and magical observation created by spells of 8th level or lower can't bypass the sanctum.

spell.name: Name the Unseen

m.text: a polished obsidian mirror worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You call upon the hidden structure of magic to reveal the true identity of what stands concealed behind false names, disguises, altered forms, and magical deception. For the duration, whenever you can see a creature, object, or magical effect, you can use an Action to scrutinize it.
If the target is within 120 feet, you learn all of the following that apply:

items: whether it is disguised, transformed, shapechanged, possessed, duplicated, or magically concealed;
whether its current appearance differs from its natural or original form;
whether the name by which it is currently known is its true name, an alias, a title, or a fabricated identity;
whether it is under an Illusion, Transmutation, Enchantment, possession, or similar effect;
the school of magic and spell level of each spell currently affecting it, if any;
whether the creature or object is native to the plane you are currently on;
whether its body is its original body.

entries.name: True Name
entries: Focus on a creature for 1 minute without breaking line of sight. It then makes a Charisma save; failure reveals its true name, if any—the identity by which it fundamentally knows itself. Success grants immunity to this part of the spell for 24 hours.

entries.name: Unmasking
entries: If an effect concealing or altering the target was created by a spell of 7th level or lower, you can see through that effect automatically for the duration. This doesn't end the effect for other creatures.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The duration becomes 8 hours, the range becomes 1 mile, and True Name no longer requires you to maintain line of sight for the full minute after you begin focusing.

The duration becomes 7 days. You can scrutinize any creature, object, or magical effect on the same plane that you can clearly identify, even if you can't currently see it. Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't conceal a target's identity, form, origin, or true name from this spell.

spell.name: Grand Conclave

m.text: a circular mirror or polished table worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: Create a private meeting demiplane. Name or clearly identify up to twenty-four willing creatures on your plane; each senses the invitation and can accept or refuse.

Invitees can enter during the duration as tangible projections while their bodies remain in place. They perceive, move, speak, and interact through the projections. You can grant or withhold each benefit separately for individuals or groups.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.

entries.name: The Conclave
entries: The conclave is a comfortable extradimensional chamber whose appearance and layout you determine when you cast the spell. It automatically provides enough space and ordinary furnishings for all participants.
Only invitees can enter this sealed demiplane, by any means. Outsiders can't see, hear, perceive, physically interact with, or magically observe events inside.
The conclave persists independently without Concentration or proximity. You and invitees can leave and return any number of times during its duration.
While within the conclave, participants gain the following benefits:

items: They can see, hear, speak with, and physically interact with one another's projections normally.
Every participant understands the literal meaning of any language spoken by another participant.
A participant can manifest accurate representations of books, maps, diagrams, written records, tools, and other objects currently in its possession.
Participants can examine, read, copy, discuss, and work with those representations as though the original objects were physically present.
Participants can cooperate on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma ability checks and can take the Help action for one another regardless of the distance between their physical bodies.

Anything written, drawn, designed, calculated, translated, or otherwise recorded within the conclave can be reproduced perfectly onto suitable physical materials possessed by any participant when that participant leaves.

A participant can voluntarily share one of its memories. The memory manifests throughout the chamber as a sensory reconstruction that the participants can pause, replay, accelerate, slow, or examine from different viewpoints.
A participant retains complete memory of everything it personally experienced within the conclave.

entries: Entry and exit don't interrupt existing Concentration. Harmful effects created inside can't affect participants' physical bodies, and participants can't directly cast spells on or affect anything outside through the conclave.

If a participant becomes unconscious or dies, its projection disappears immediately. If it leaves the plane on which its body was located, its connection to the conclave ends until it again meets the requirements for entry. You can revoke a creature's invitation at any time while you are within the conclave. Its projection immediately disappears, and it can't return unless you invite it again.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 24 hours, and you can invite up to 100 willing creatures. Invited creatures can enter the conclave from anywhere on the same plane regardless of whether you know their current location.
{@b 9th Level.} The duration becomes 30 days, there is no limit to the number of willing creatures you can invite, and invited creatures can enter from any plane of existence.

In addition, the conclave can transport physical matter. A participant can bring objects it is carrying into the conclave and give them to another participant, with a total weight of up to 1,000 pounds per transfer. When the recipient leaves, those objects appear with it.

A willing participant can also choose another participant when leaving the conclave. Instead of returning to its original location, its physical body appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of that creature's physical body, provided both creatures are on a plane that permits planar travel.

spell.name: Living Archive

m.text: a blank master volume bound in fine materials worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: The master volume links every readable record within 300 feet into a living collection, including books, scrolls, inscriptions, maps, diagrams, and encoded documents. For the duration, access their contents through it without handling the originals.

You can ask the archive a question by speaking or writing it into the master volume. If the answer exists somewhere within the linked records, the volume immediately identifies the relevant sources and presents the information to you in a concise form.
The archive can:

items: search the entire linked collection simultaneously;
translate any written language contained within it;
reproduce text, illustrations, maps, tables, diagrams, and formulae exactly;
compare multiple records and identify where their contents agree, conflict, or differ;
reconstruct the intended reading order of damaged, scattered, or disorganized documents;
identify duplicate, altered, forged, missing, or magically modified portions of linked records;
create an index or catalogue of any subject you specify;
and copy any amount of linked information into blank books, parchment, or similar suitable materials you provide.

entries: The archive creates no absent knowledge and resolves conflicting sources only if its records establish the answer. It reads magical concealment or encryption of 7th level or lower and deciphers nonmagical codes or constructed languages when sufficient examples exist.

If a linked record is removed from the spell's area, information already indexed from it remains accessible for the rest of the duration, but the archive no longer receives changes made to that record.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The duration becomes 7 days, the radius becomes 1 mile, and the archive can link to written records contained inside extradimensional spaces whose entrances lie within the area.

The duration becomes 30 days. You can designate an entire contiguous settlement, fortress, university, library complex, or similar site no larger than 10 miles across as the linked archive, provided you cast the spell somewhere within it. Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't hide, encrypt, falsify, or prevent access to written information within the linked collection.

spell.name: Grand Reclamation

m.text: a flawless crystal prism worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: Matter recalls its past. Restore any chosen damaged, altered, ruined, or destroyed noncreature objects, structures, constructions, or terrain within range to complete states from the previous 100 years, choosing a different moment for each.
The spell can restore, among other things:

items: weapons, armor, tools, and equipment;
books, documents, paintings, statues, and other works;
doors, walls, bridges, roads, ships, vehicles, and machinery;
buildings, towers, fortifications, and other structures;
damaged or excavated terrain;
and magic items whose physical forms have been damaged or destroyed.

entries: Missing parts reform from transformed surrounding inert matter; if insufficient, necessary nonvaluable material is created. Targets regain all physical details from the chosen state, including mechanisms, inscriptions, and hidden compartments.

Magic-item properties return unless their destruction permanently removed them or used a unique method this spell can't reverse. Unchosen targets are unaffected. The spell restores no living creatures, life, souls, or things dependent on a living creature remaining alive.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: You can restore each chosen target to a state it possessed at any point within the previous 1,000 years, and the spell's range becomes 1,000 feet. You no longer need any identifiable fragment of a destroyed target if you cast the spell at a location where that target once existed.

You can restore each chosen target to any previous physical state it has ever possessed, regardless of how long ago it existed, and the spell's range becomes 5 miles. A chosen target that has been completely reduced to dust, scattered, melted, disintegrated, or otherwise physically erased can still be reconstructed if it once existed within range. An Artifact can be restored unless the method that destroyed it explicitly states that its destruction is permanent or prevents magical restoration.

spell.name: Architect's Mandate

m.text: a set of masterwork drafting instruments worth at least 2,500 gp, which aren't consumed

entries: Impose your design on any chosen nonliving, nonmagical matter within range, reshaping, moving, joining, separating, excavating, compressing, or reconstructing it into an arrangement you clearly envision.
The transformation can create or alter things such as:

items: buildings, walls, towers, bridges, roads, stairs, and fortifications;
tunnels, chambers, trenches, canals, wells, and underground complexes;
doors, windows, furniture, containers, scaffolding, and ordinary mechanisms;
ships, wagons, siege engines, and other nonmagical vehicles;
statues, monuments, signs, inscriptions, and architectural ornamentation;
or large-scale changes to stone, earth, wood, metal, glass, and similar material.

entries: You control each portion and can work multiple materials simultaneously. Results are real, permanent, nonmagical, and can't be dispelled. Understanding a construction's purpose suffices; the spell supplies ordinary engineering details for safe operation, including supports, joints, drainage, ventilation, stairs, hinges, and foundations.

The spell can't create matter from nothing, but it can freely redistribute available material within range. It can't create creatures, magic items, active magical effects, or substances whose total value would significantly exceed the materials consumed to create them. Objects worn or carried by an unwilling creature aren't affected.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The range becomes 1 mile. You can also transform nonmagical material between different mundane substances of comparable value, such as turning stone into steel, wood into glass, or earth into worked stone.

{@b 9th Level.} The range becomes 5 miles, and you can reshape all nonliving matter you choose within range simultaneously, including complete landscapes and existing settlements. You can raise mountains, excavate vast underground complexes, redirect rivers, construct cities, or completely redesign existing terrain, provided sufficient matter exists within the affected area.
At 9th level, transformations between mundane materials no longer need to be of comparable value, though this spell still can't create magical substances, Artifacts, or unique supernatural materials.

spell.name: Living Bastion

m.text: a miniature architectural model or engraved boundary marker worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You awaken a structure or territory, binding everything within its boundaries into a single obedient magical intelligence. When you cast this spell, choose either one contiguous structure you touch or a contiguous area centered on the point you touch. The chosen structure or area can be no more than 300 feet across. For the duration, it becomes your Living Bastion.

If you choose an area rather than a structure, you determine its boundaries when you cast the spell. The area can include buildings, roads, courtyards, caves, gardens, tunnels, open ground, and similar spaces. The bastion understands every language you know and follows your spoken or mentally issued instructions. It can communicate with creatures within itself through voices, writing appearing on surfaces, moving images, lights, sounds, or other manifestations appropriate to the area.

The bastion perceives its entire area and 30 feet beyond. Define categories of creatures and independently choose which services, mechanisms, routes, defenses, tasks, or other functions assist, ignore, restrict, or affect each creature or category.

The bastion can manipulate its environment throughout its entire area. It can open, close, lock, and unlock doors; operate gates, lifts, machinery, tools, traps, siege equipment, plumbing, furnaces, lights, and other mechanisms; move furniture and unattended objects; arrange rooms; extinguish ordinary fires; clean, organize, prepare, carry, retrieve, serve, pour, repair, maintain, and perform other simple tasks.
At every point, the bastion can perform simple tasks as an {@spell Unseen Servant|XPHB}, including household work, handling objects, mending, lighting fires, and operating simple tools.

It performs unlimited simultaneous simple tasks through invisible forces, not creatures, confined to its boundaries. Environmental control moves unattended objects up to 1,000 pounds; servant-like tasks have the fine control reasonably required.

It regulates ordinary lighting, temperature, ventilation, utilities, doors, and routes where existing means permit. It can operate existing weapons, traps, defenses, and machinery but creates no missing weapons, ammunition, magic items, or defenses.

The bastion remembers all it perceives and accurately answers your mental inquiries. At each hour's start, it repairs up to 100 Hit Points of damage to nonmagical objects and constructions, using materials inside or within 30 feet of its boundaries. Repair creates no valuable or magical materials.
Once created, the bastion continues to exist and obey your standing instructions even if you leave its area. You don't need to remain nearby or maintain Concentration.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 30 days, the affected structure or area can be up to 1 mile across, its perception extends 300 feet beyond its boundaries, it can manipulate unattended objects weighing up to 10,000 pounds, and it repairs up to 500 Hit Points of damage each hour.
{@b 9th Level.} The spell becomes permanent until dispelled, and the affected structure or area can be up to 5 miles across.

At 9th level, the bastion can manipulate unattended objects of any weight that can physically move within its environment, repairs up to 1,000 Hit Points of damage each hour, and can reconstruct destroyed portions of ordinary nonmagical structures and terrain within itself even when suitable replacement material is unavailable. It retains its memories indefinitely and can receive your mental commands across planar boundaries.

spell.name: Grand Waygate

m.text: two matching gate keys fashioned from precious metal worth at least 2,500 gp each, which aren't consumed

entries: You establish a stable passage through space, joining two distant locations as though they stood beside one another. Choose an unoccupied space within range large enough to contain a 20-foot-wide, 20-foot-high portal. Then choose a destination on the same plane that you have personally visited or can identify with exceptional precision. A second portal appears at an unoccupied space you choose at that destination. The two portals are connected for the spell's duration.

Passing completely through either portal immediately exits the other, with unlimited two-way traffic. You can close or reopen them without an action during the duration; closed portals remain present but intangible.

At casting or later, define Authorized creatures, groups, symbols, passwords, or conditions. Only Authorized creatures pass; for others, portals are immovable, impenetrable surfaces that teleportation, possession, transformation, or similar magic can't bypass.

You can give different Authorized creatures or groups different permissions. You decide which direction they can travel, which objects they can bring through, and, if the gate has multiple destinations, which destinations they can use.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.

Unaccompanied objects and anything fitting the opening can pass. Passage creates no harmful environmental transition; pressure, wind, water, smoke, fire, hazardous atmospheres, and similar effects don't automatically cross unattended portals without your permission.

If either portal's location becomes obstructed or unsafe, that end of the gate becomes inactive until a suitable space is available again. Once created, Grand Waygate persists for its full duration even if you leave either location, and it requires no Concentration.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 7 days, each portal can be up to 50 feet wide and 50 feet high, and the two ends can be located on different planes of existence, provided you have personally visited both locations.

{@b 9th Level.} The duration becomes permanent until dispelled, each portal can be up to 100 feet wide and 100 feet high, and you can connect any two locations you can clearly identify, even if you have never personally visited them.

At 9th level, you can also create up to six linked portals as part of the same casting. Each portal can connect to any other portal in the network. When a creature enters one, it chooses its destination from among the other linked portals it is Authorized to use.

spell.name: Land of Plenty

m.text: a vessel containing fertile soil, pure water, and seeds worth at least 1,000 gp, which aren't consumed

entries: You awaken the productive potential of the land, causing a chosen territory to sustain life with supernatural abundance. Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 1 mile across. You can freely exclude portions of the area when you cast the spell. You decide which creatures, plants, resources, and portions of the chosen land receive each beneficial effect of this spell. You can grant or withhold individual effects separately for each target, category, or portion of the area.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.
For the duration, the chosen land gains the following effects:

items: Soil becomes fertile enough to support any nonmagical plant that could reasonably survive the local environment.
Existing nonmagical plants recover from disease, drought, ordinary damage, and nutrient deficiency.
Crops and other useful plants grow at ten times their normal rate.
Harvested plants regrow when their biology would normally allow them to do so.
Natural freshwater within the area is purified of ordinary poison, disease, salt, sewage, and nonmagical contamination.
Wells, springs, and other renewable water sources replenish at the fastest rate their surroundings can naturally sustain.
Ordinary plant diseases, crop pests, and destructive infestations can't establish themselves within the area unless you allow them.
Weather within the area becomes less destructive to agriculture. Ordinary drought, frost, excessive heat, hail, and flooding are moderated enough to prevent widespread crop failure.
Damaged nonmagical ecosystems gradually recover, with native plants spreading into suitable empty ground.

Creatures gathering food, lumber, fibers, herbs, or other renewable biological resources from the area can do so without permanently exhausting those resources, provided they don't deliberately destroy the source faster than the spell can restore it.

entries: The spell accelerates and stabilizes natural production rather than creating goods, valuables, creatures, or food from nothing. Choose which vegetation and resources thrive. Magical corruption of soil, water, or vegetation from spells of 6th level or lower is suppressed while it would hinder normal land function.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 10 miles across, the duration becomes 1 year, and crops and renewable plants grow at fifty times their normal rate. Magical corruption created by spells of 7th level or lower is suppressed.
{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 50 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled.

At 9th level, the land can gradually restore severely damaged nonmagical ecosystems, depleted soil, dried natural waterways, deforested regions, and other environmental devastation so long as the necessary matter and fundamental environmental conditions still exist. Renewable biological resources within the area replenish at the fastest rate the ecosystem can support without collapsing. Magical corruption created by spells of 8th level or lower can't prevent this restoration.

spell.name: Eternal Preservation

m.text: a crystal hourglass filled with powdered diamond worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You impose perfect preservation upon a chosen place, preventing time, decay, and ordinary deterioration from claiming anything you choose within it. Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 300 feet across. When you cast the spell, you can designate any creatures, objects, substances, structures, corpses, plants, food, documents, or other matter within the area as Preserved. You can also designate categories, such as "all food," "all books," or "everything except living creatures."

You decide which eligible targets receive each benefit of this spell. You can grant or withhold preservation and other beneficial effects separately for each creature, object, substance, structure, category, or portion of the area. Perfect Stasis still follows its own saving throw rules for unwilling creatures.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified. For the duration, Preserved targets remain physically unchanged by the passage of time.

They don't rot, spoil, corrode, rust, weather, decay, dry out, become stale, lose freshness, degrade from age, or suffer ordinary wear. Dead creatures don't decompose, harvested plants remain fresh, food remains as edible as when the spell was cast, and written or painted materials don't fade. Living creatures you choose can also be preserved without being placed in suspended animation. Such creatures continue to move, act, eat, sleep, heal, and live normally, but don't physically age while within the area.

entries.name: Perfect Stasis
entries: You can place a willing creature or unattended object within the affected area into Perfect Stasis automatically. An unwilling creature within the affected area can also be placed into Perfect Stasis. When you attempt to do so, the creature must make a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it enters Perfect Stasis. On a successful save, it resists this attempt for 1 hour.

A creature placed into Perfect Stasis unwillingly repeats the Constitution saving throw at the end of each hour. On a success, the stasis ends for that creature, and it can't be placed into Perfect Stasis by this spell again for 1 hour. While in Perfect Stasis, a creature is Incapacitated, can't move or take actions, doesn't age, breathe, hunger, thirst, heal, or expend biological resources, is immune to damage and conditions, and doesn't perceive the passage of time. A willing creature can choose to end its own Perfect Stasis at the end of any hour.
You can end Perfect Stasis on any target at any time while you are on the same plane, requiring no action.

Preserved structures and objects can't be damaged by ordinary weather, erosion, pests, neglect, or similar environmental processes, though they can still be deliberately damaged by creatures, spells, hazards, and other immediate forces. If a Preserved target leaves the affected area, preservation ends for that target until it returns. Any aging or deterioration prevented by the spell doesn't occur retroactively. The spell remains for its full duration without Concentration.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 1 mile across, and the duration becomes 10 years. Preserved objects and structures also become immune to nonmagical corrosion, erosion, weathering, and environmental damage while within the area.
{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 10 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled.

At 9th level, anything placed into Perfect Stasis can remain suspended indefinitely, even if you die or leave the plane. You can also designate portions of the affected area where all nonliving matter is automatically preserved, including anything brought into those areas later. Effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't magically age, decay, spoil, corrode, or otherwise accelerate the deterioration of a Preserved target.

spell.name: Grand Manufactorum

m.text: a masterwork tool set and a miniature forge worth at least 2,500 gp total, which aren't consumed

entries: You transform a chosen workshop, factory, warehouse, forge, or contiguous area into an autonomous center of production. Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 300 feet across. For the duration, invisible magical forces within the area can process raw materials and manufacture nonmagical objects according to your instructions.
Provide verbal instructions, a sample, plans, or diagrams. The manufactorum repeatedly produces the object while materials last, performing every necessary ordinary manufacturing process.
It can create, among other things:

items: weapons, armor, ammunition, tools, and adventuring equipment;
furniture, clothing, containers, books, paper, and household goods;
mechanical components, locks, gears, pipes, fittings, and machinery;
carts, wagons, boats, siege equipment, and other nonmagical vehicles;
construction materials such as bricks, beams, panels, glass, nails, and worked stone;
food products and preserved goods from suitable ingredients;
and any other nonmagical object whose required materials are available.

entries: Any number of processes can run simultaneously, completing up to 10,000 pounds of products per hour. Complexity doesn't reduce output if instructions suffice for the required precision. It creates no raw materials, creatures, souls, Artifacts, or active magical effects.

It can manufacture components for magic items and perform mundane portions of magic-item construction, but it can't provide unique supernatural ingredients or magical power that the finished item specifically requires.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified. Once given, production instructions continue until you change them or the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected area can be up to 1 mile across, the duration becomes 30 days, and the manufactorum can complete up to 100,000 pounds of finished products each hour. It can also reproduce any nonmagical object you provide as a sample even if you don't understand how that object was originally made.

{@b 9th Level.} The affected area can be up to 5 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled. There is no fixed hourly weight limit; the manufactorum works as quickly as available space, raw materials, and the physical movement of those materials reasonably allow.

At 9th level, if you provide a complete magic-item formula and every special material required by that formula, the manufactorum can also perform the full construction process for that magic item. It doesn't waive the required materials or create unique components, but no additional workforce is required.

spell.name: Arcane Reservoir

m.text: a flawless crystal vessel worth at least 5,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You transform the material component into a stable reservoir capable of storing magical power for later use. The reservoir remains fixed at the location where the spell is cast. For the duration, a willing creature touching it can deposit an unexpended spell slot into the reservoir. The slot is expended, and the reservoir gains a number of Arcane Charges determined by the slot's level, as shown in the Arcane Charge Cost table.
The reservoir can hold a maximum of 50 Arcane Charges at one time. If depositing a spell slot would exceed this maximum, the deposit fails and the spell slot isn't expended.
A creature touching the reservoir can spend Arcane Charges in either of the following ways:

items.name: Restore a Spell Slot.
items.entry: The creature restores one expended spell slot by spending the number of Arcane Charges shown for that slot's level in the Arcane Charge Cost table. The restored slot can be no higher than 5th level.

items.name: Fuel a Spell.
items.entry: When the creature casts a spell while touching the reservoir, it can spend the number of Arcane Charges shown for the spell slot's level instead of expending one of its own spell slots. At 7th level, this can fuel a spell using a slot of no higher than 5th level.

entries: Only willing creatures can draw power. Define Authorized users by creatures, groups, passwords, symbols, or other qualifications, with separate permissions to deposit, restore slots, fuel spells, and draw up to specified slot levels.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.
Transfers are unlimited within storage capacity. You always know the stored Arcane Charges across any distance or plane; unused charges dissipate harmlessly when the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The duration becomes 1 year, the reservoir can store up to 200 Arcane Charges, and it can restore or fuel spell slots of up to 7th level.
{@b 9th Level.} The spell becomes permanent until dispelled, the reservoir can store up to 1,000 Arcane Charges, and it can restore or fuel spell slots of up to 9th level.

At 9th level, you can create a network of up to ten Arcane Reservoirs cast by you. Reservoirs in the same network share their stored Arcane Charges regardless of distance, even across planar boundaries. A creature using one reservoir can draw Arcane Charges deposited into any other reservoir in the network.

spell.name: Grand Infirmary

m.text: a crystal medical sigil set with diamond and silver worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You transform a structure or contiguous area into a supernatural place of healing, recovery, and tranquility, filling it with restorative magic and invisible attendants. Choose a contiguous structure or area centered on the point you touch and no more than 300 feet across. When you cast the spell, you can designate creatures individually, by group, symbol, password, or any other clear qualification as Patients.
You decide which creatures receive each benefit of this spell. You can grant or withhold individual benefits separately for each creature or category of creatures.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.

When a creature enters, you can apply {@spell Calm Emotions|XPHB} without a save while it remains. Suppress its Charmed and Frightened conditions and make it indifferent toward creatures inside toward which it is hostile. Indifference toward a creature ends if that creature attacks it, damages it, forces it to save, or visibly harms one of its allies. Unexpired suppressed conditions resume on exit.
A Patient can receive any of the following benefits that you choose for it:

items: It is automatically Stabilized whenever it is Dying.
It has Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
If it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains 10 Hit Points at the start of each hour.
Whenever it finishes a Short Rest, each Hit Point Die it spends restores the maximum possible number of Hit Points instead of being rolled.
Whenever it finishes a Short Rest, it also regains one expended Hit Point Die.
Ordinary diseases, infections, parasites, and nonmagical poisons can't worsen while it remains within the infirmary.
Nonmagical wounds don't become infected, reopen, or otherwise deteriorate.
Ordinary pain can be suppressed at the Patient's choice without preventing it from perceiving injuries or other bodily sensations necessary for its safety.

entries: Invisible attendants perform unlimited simultaneous routine care: dress wounds, sterilize equipment, administer prepared medicines, move willing or unconscious Patients, prepare beds, serve available food and water, and monitor visible health signs.
Once during each hour, each Patient can receive one of the following treatments of your choice:

items: regain {@dice 4d8} + your spellcasting ability modifier Hit Points;
end the Poisoned condition;
end one nonmagical disease, infection, or parasite;
restore one reduced Ability Score to its normal value, provided the reduction wasn't caused by an Artifact, Curse, or similarly exceptional effect;
or end one ordinary injury or impairment that could reasonably be corrected through nonmagical medical treatment.

entries: Each Patient receives at most one treatment per hour, chosen anew each hour. Normally, treatment doesn't restore missing organs or limbs, remove Curses, or revive the dead. The infirmary persists without Concentration or your presence, following standing instructions.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: {@b 8th Level.} The affected structure or area can be up to 1 mile across, and the duration becomes 30 days. The hourly healing treatment becomes {@dice 8d8} + your spellcasting ability modifier Hit Points. In addition, an hourly treatment can end one of the following conditions: Blinded, Deafened, Paralyzed, or Petrified.
{@b 9th Level.} The affected structure or area can be up to 5 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled.
At 9th level, the infirmary can also perform the following restorative procedures:

items: A missing limb or organ is completely regenerated after the creature spends 24 continuous hours as a Patient within the infirmary.
After 1 hour of treatment, the infirmary can end one Curse, magical disease, or other removable magical affliction created by a spell or effect of 8th level or lower.
An hourly treatment can restore a creature's Hit Point Maximum to its normal value.

A creature whose body is within the infirmary and that died there within the previous 1 minute is automatically returned to life with 1 Hit Point, provided its soul can return. The creature doesn't need to be willing.

entries: A creature restored to life by this spell can't benefit from that revival effect again until it finishes a Long Rest.

spell.name: Climate Dominion

m.text: a crystal globe containing samples of earth, water, and air worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You bind the atmosphere of a territory to your design, establishing a stable climate that persists without your presence. Choose a contiguous area centered on the point you touch and no more than 5 miles across. For the duration, you control the ordinary weather and climate throughout the area. You can divide the affected area into any number of zones and determine the conditions of each zone independently.

For the duration, you can change adjustable permissions, designations, instructions, zones, settings, benefit recipients, or similar options at any time without an action, regardless of distance or plane. This doesn't move or enlarge the original area unless specified.

Within each zone, you can determine the temperature, cloud cover and sunlight, humidity, precipitation, fog and ordinary visibility, wind direction and strength up to a strong gale, the frequency and intensity of ordinary storms, and whether the area follows its natural season or another ordinary seasonal climate you choose. Changes occur gradually over 10 minutes unless you choose for them to happen more slowly.
You can exempt designated creatures, structures, roads, farmland, water bodies, or clearly defined portions from individual climate effects.

The spell can suppress ordinary droughts, heat waves, cold snaps, floods caused by rainfall, blizzards, dust storms, and other natural weather occurring within the affected area. It can also prevent new ordinary weather from entering the area if it conflicts with the climate you established.

The spell doesn't create magical lightning, supernatural storms, damaging energy, or other inherently magical weather. It also doesn't directly alter terrain, create water from nothing, or eliminate water that already exists, though precipitation and evaporation caused by the controlled climate function normally. Climate Dominion continues for its full duration without Concentration, even if you leave the area or the plane.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The affected area can be up to 25 miles across, and the duration becomes 1 year. You can create severe natural weather, including hurricanes, tornadoes, extreme blizzards, torrential rain, prolonged drought, and similarly intense but nonmagical atmospheric conditions. You can still exclude any creatures, structures, routes, or zones you choose from individual effects.

The affected area can be up to 100 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled. You can establish a completely stable artificial climate independent of the surrounding region's latitude, altitude, season, or natural weather patterns. Different parts of the area can permanently maintain entirely different climates, such as snow-covered mountains, temperate farmland, tropical gardens, and dry desert districts existing beside one another. Weather and climate effects created by spells of 8th level or lower can't alter a portion of the dominion unless you allow them to.

spell.name: Civic Nexus

m.text: a crystal relay core engraved with interconnected sigils worth at least 2,500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: Establish a communication Nexus in a contiguous area up to 5 miles across, centered on your touch. Define Connected creatures by individual, group, symbol, password, or other clear qualifications, assigning each creature or group's permitted functions separately.

For the entire duration of the spell, you retain control over its permissions, designations, channels, settings, and other adjustable functions regardless of distance or planar boundaries. You can change any of these choices at any time without an action. This doesn't move or enlarge the spell's original area unless the spell says otherwise.
A Connected creature within the Nexus can use any of the following functions you allow:

items.name: Direct Communication.
items.entry: The creature can mentally communicate with another Connected creature within the Nexus as though speaking normally. The recipients can answer in the same way.

items.name: Group Channels.
items.entry: You can create any number of communication channels. A Connected creature can transmit a message to every creature currently authorized for a channel.

items.name: Location Sharing.
items.entry: A creature can choose to reveal its precise location within the Nexus to creatures or channels you permit. This function never reveals a creature's location against its will unless you specifically designate that creature as being subject to mandatory tracking when it first becomes Connected.

items.name: Emergency Signal.
items.entry: The creature can instantly transmit an alarm, its location, and a brief description of the danger to designated creatures or channels.

items.name: Sensory Message.
items.entry: The creature can transmit a still image, sound, short memory-like impression, map, written message, or similar simple information it can clearly perceive or recall.

items.name: Translation.
items.entry: Connected creatures understand the intended meaning of communications transmitted through the Nexus regardless of the languages they know.

items.name: Public Broadcast.
items.entry: Creatures you authorize can transmit announcements to any number of Connected creatures simultaneously.

entries: Communication is instantaneous within the area without components, slots, or a shared language. Define automatic alert conditions, such as fire, collapse, restricted entry, alarm activation, or a Connected creature becoming Unconscious; the Nexus immediately informs designated recipients or channels.

The Nexus reads only intentionally transmitted thoughts and reveals other information only through enabled functions. Magic of 6th level or lower can't intercept, alter, impersonate, or falsify messages without your permission. It needs no Concentration and persists if you leave its area or plane.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The affected area can be up to 25 miles across, and the duration becomes 1 year. Connected creatures can transmit continuous visual and auditory information through the Nexus, allowing another authorized creature to perceive what they currently see and hear. In addition, automatic alerts can respond to magical phenomena, including teleportation, planar travel, active spells, and designated magical signatures.

The affected area can be up to 100 miles across, and the spell becomes permanent until dispelled. You can link up to ten Civic Nexuses cast by you into a single network. Connected creatures can communicate between linked Nexuses regardless of distance and across planar boundaries. At 9th level, communication within the network can't be intercepted, altered, blocked, impersonated, or falsified by spells or magical effects of 8th level or lower unless you allow it.

spell.name: Sovereign Will
entries: You touch a creature and impose absolute authority over its own mind, body, and supernatural state. For the duration, hostile powers can affect the target only so far as it permits them to. The spell requires no Concentration.
While the spell lasts, the target gains the following benefits:

items: It is immune to the Charmed and Frightened conditions.
It can't be possessed or have its thoughts, memories, emotions, alignment, personality, or form altered against its will.
It can't be magically compelled to speak, remain silent, move, take an action, or refrain from taking an action.
Its Speed can't be reduced against its will, and it can't be teleported, banished, or moved to another plane against its will.
It can't be magically put to sleep or rendered Unconscious while it has at least 1 Hit Point.
A creature can't control its body, actions, senses, or movement through magic.

entries: Whenever the target would fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, it can choose to succeed instead. It can use this benefit once during each of its turns, and using it requires no action.

entries.name: Reject the Effect
entries: After learning the effect, the target can immediately reject any condition or ongoing effect imposed by magic, ending it on itself even when unable to act or react. Already-dealt damage remains, but ongoing sources of later damage can end.

entries.name: Unbroken Concentration
entries: Whenever damage would cause the target to make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration, it can choose to automatically succeed. Other effects can still end its Concentration if they explicitly end the spell itself.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: Whenever the target rejects a spell or magical effect, it can also reflect that effect back upon its source if the source is a creature within 120 feet of the target. The originating creature becomes the target of the rejected effect instead, using the original caster's spell save DC and spellcasting ability where applicable.

For the duration, the target can choose to succeed on any saving throw it makes, not only saving throws against spells or magical effects. In addition, a spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower can't alter the target's mind, body, location, form, actions, or ongoing magical state unless the target chooses to allow it.

spell.name: Ruin Cascade
entries: You compress destructive arcane force into a point you can see within range, then allow the collapse to propagate through everything caught within it. Each creature in a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Objects and structures damaged by the initial eruption or by a Secondary Rupture automatically take the maximum possible damage from that instance.

entries.name: Secondary Rupture
entries: Whenever a creature or object is reduced to 0 Hit Points or destroyed by this spell, it becomes the center of a Secondary Rupture. Each creature within 15 feet of the rupture must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 6d12} Force damage, or half as much on a successful save. This damage is always equal to half the number of damage dice rolled by the spell's initial eruption.
Ruptures can trigger further ruptures without limit. A creature can take damage from multiple ruptures in one casting, but only once per individual rupture.

entries.name: Overwhelming Collapse
entries: If a creature fails its saving throw against the initial eruption by 5 or more, it is also knocked Prone and pushed up to 30 feet directly away from the center of the spell. If it fails that saving throw by 10 or more, it instead takes an additional {@damage 6d12} Force damage.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The initial damage becomes {@damage 18d12}. Each Secondary Rupture deals {@damage 9d12} Force damage, and its radius becomes 20 feet.

The initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12}. Each Secondary Rupture deals {@damage 15d12} Force damage in a 30-foot radius. Whenever a creature succeeds on a saving throw against this spell, it takes three-quarters of the damage instead of half.

spell.name: Final Rupture
entries: You focus destructive magic into a single point within a creature's body or form, then tear that point apart from the inside. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 20d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. This damage ignores Resistance to Force damage. If the target is immune to Force damage, it instead has Resistance to this damage.

entries.name: Internal Collapse
entries: If the target fails the saving throw, the spell also ruptures its ability to recover until the end of your next turn:

items: it can't regain Hit Points;
Regeneration and similar traits don't restore Hit Points;
Temporary Hit Points can't be gained;
and any effect that would prevent it from dropping to 0 Hit Points or cause it to remain at 1 Hit Point instead is suppressed for this damage.

entries: If this spell reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, any Regeneration or feature that would automatically restore it to life or consciousness before the end of your next turn doesn't function.

entries.name: Catastrophic Failure
entries: If the target fails its saving throw by 5 or more, it takes an additional {@damage 6d12} Force damage. If it fails by 10 or more, the additional damage becomes {@damage 12d12} instead.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Force damage. Catastrophic Failure deals {@damage 10d12} on a failure by 5 or more, or {@damage 20d12} on a failure by 10 or more.

The initial damage becomes {@damage 50d12} Force damage. On a failed saving throw, the target's Immunity to Force damage is ignored entirely. Catastrophic Failure deals {@damage 15d12} on a failure by 5 or more, or {@damage 30d12} on a failure by 10 or more. In addition, if the 9th-level version reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, effects of 8th level or lower can't restore that creature to life until 24 hours have passed.

spell.name: Gravitic Implosion
entries: You collapse gravity around a point you can see within range, dragging everything nearby inward before crushing the gathered mass under impossible pressure. Each creature in a 40-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 14d12} Force damage, is pulled up to 40 feet directly toward the center, and is knocked Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pulled or knocked Prone. Objects and structures in the area automatically fail this saving throw.

entries.name: Crushing Convergence
entries: After all creatures and objects have been pulled, every creature within 10 feet of the center suffers a second gravitational collapse. Each such creature must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 8d12} Force damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. For every other creature of Medium size or larger within 10 feet of the center, this secondary damage increases by {@damage 1d12}, to a maximum increase of {@damage 10d12}.

entries.name: Compression
entries: A creature that fails both saving throws is Restrained until the end of its next turn as gravitational pressure pins it in place. A Huge or smaller unattended object caught within 10 feet of the center is crushed, folded, or compacted as appropriate. Structures take maximum damage from both instances of this spell.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The initial damage becomes {@damage 20d12}, the secondary collapse becomes {@damage 12d12}, and the sphere's radius becomes 60 feet. The maximum bonus damage from Crushing Convergence becomes {@damage 15d12}.

The initial damage becomes {@damage 32d12}, the secondary collapse becomes {@damage 20d12}, and the sphere's radius becomes 100 feet. There is no maximum to the bonus damage from Crushing Convergence; each additional Medium or larger creature pulled into the central 10 feet adds another {@damage 1d12} Force damage to the secondary collapse. A creature that fails both saving throws is Stunned until the end of its next turn instead of Restrained.

spell.name: Endless Thunderbolt
entries: You unleash a bolt of lightning so violently overcharged that its energy continues multiplying as it tears through its victims. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 14d12} Lightning damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Explosive Current
entries: Each 9, 10, 11, or 12 rolled on a damage d12 generates another d12 added to that same damage roll. Additional dice can trigger this again without limit.

entries.name: Overkill Arc
entries: Reducing a creature to 0 Hit Points lets you arc to another visible creature within 60 feet of it, resolving a fresh instance at the original slot level without an action, slot, or components.

Each new target saves and takes the full initial damage appropriate to that slot, with Explosive Current, Conductive Ruin, and Overkill Arc applying normally. Arcs are unlimited, but each creature is eligible only once per original casting.

entries.name: Conductive Ruin
entries: If a target is wearing metal armor, composed primarily of metal, or standing in a substantial body of water, it has Disadvantage on its saving throw against this spell. Objects and structures made primarily of metal automatically fail their saving throw and take maximum damage.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The initial damage becomes {@damage 20d12} Lightning damage, and Explosive Current triggers whenever a damage die rolls 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12.

The initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Lightning damage, and Explosive Current triggers whenever a damage die rolls 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, or 12. The spell ignores Resistance to Lightning damage. A creature immune to Lightning damage instead has Resistance to this spell.

spell.name: Hellstar
entries: You create a miniature star of violent magical fire at a point you can see within range. The star occupies a 5-foot-radius sphere and radiates annihilating heat through a 40-foot-radius sphere around itself. The spell requires no Concentration. Once created, the Hellstar persists for the full duration unless you cause it to collapse early. When the star appears, each creature in the affected area must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 10d12} Fire damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.
A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make the saving throw again.

entries.name: Escalating Heat
entries: After the creation round, each damage instance permanently increases the star's damage by {@damage 2d12} for the remaining duration, without limit. Its progression is {@damage 10d12}, {@damage 12d12}, {@damage 14d12}, {@damage 16d12}, and so on.

entries.name: Stellar Collapse
entries: At any time, collapse the star without an action. Every creature within 60 feet makes a Constitution save, taking Force damage equal to its current Fire damage dice, or half on success. For example, {@damage 18d12} Fire becomes {@damage 18d12} Force.
After the collapse, the spell ends. If the spell reaches the end of its duration without being collapsed early, it undergoes Stellar Collapse automatically before ending.

entries.name: Event Horizon
entries: A creature within 20 feet of the star treats the area as Difficult Terrain. Whenever a creature within that distance attempts to move farther away from the star, it must first succeed on a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, that movement costs twice as much movement. The star itself can't be moved after it is created.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The initial damage becomes {@damage 14d12}, the affected area becomes a 60-foot-radius sphere, and Escalating Heat increases the damage by {@damage 3d12} each round.

The initial damage becomes {@damage 20d12}, the affected area becomes a 100-foot-radius sphere, and Escalating Heat increases the damage by {@damage 5d12} each round. The spell ignores Resistance to Fire damage, and creatures immune to Fire damage instead have Resistance to it. When the 9th-level star undergoes Stellar Collapse, the collapse deals twice the star's current number of damage dice as Force damage.

spell.name: Heavenfall
entries: You designate a point you can see within range and tear open the sky above it. A colossal mass of condensed radiance and arcane force begins descending toward that point. The spell requires no Concentration. The impact occurs at the start of your next turn. Until then, the point of impact is visibly marked by a column of light extending into the sky, and creatures can perceive the descending catastrophe.

entries.name: Heavenfall Impact
entries: When the spell strikes, every creature in a 60-foot-radius, 100-foot-high cylinder centered on the chosen point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 12d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Objects and structures automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum damage. The impact leaves the affected ground shattered and turns it into Difficult Terrain until cleared or repaired.

entries.name: Epicenter
entries: Creatures within 20 feet of the center suffer the full force of the impact. A creature in this area that fails its saving throw takes an additional {@damage 8d12} Force damage. If it succeeds, it still takes half of this additional damage.

entries.name: Shockwave
entries: After the impact, every creature within 120 feet of the center but outside the primary area must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 6d12} Thunder damage, is pushed 60 feet directly away from the center, and is knocked Prone. On a successful save, it takes half damage and isn't pushed or knocked Prone.

entries.name: Irrevocable Descent
entries: After casting, you can't cancel the impact. Your movement doesn't redirect it, and it still strikes if you become Incapacitated, Unconscious, leave the plane, or die.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The primary damage becomes {@damage 18d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 18d12} Force damage, the Epicenter bonus becomes {@damage 12d12} Force damage, and the primary radius becomes 90 feet.

The primary damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 30d12} Force damage, the Epicenter bonus becomes {@damage 20d12} Force damage, and the primary radius becomes 150 feet. A creature in the Epicenter that fails its saving throw is also Stunned until the end of its next turn. Damage dealt by this version of the spell ignores Resistance to Radiant, Force, and Thunder damage. Immunity to any of those damage types instead functions as Resistance against this spell.

spell.name: Annihilation Beam
entries: You tear open a channel of raw destructive power and sustain it around yourself, allowing you to repeatedly discharge beams capable of stripping matter apart. The spell requires no Concentration. When you cast the spell, and once on each of your turns thereafter for the duration, you can fire a beam at one creature or object you can see within range. Firing a beam after the initial casting requires no action.

The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 10d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Objects and structures automatically fail this saving throw and take maximum damage.

entries.name: Annihilation Mark
entries: Each failed beam save adds an Annihilation Mark until the spell ends. Each existing Mark adds {@damage 3d12} Force damage to the beam: {@damage 10d12}, {@damage 13d12}, {@damage 16d12}, {@damage 19d12}, {@damage 22d12}, and so on. Marks are unlimited and successful saves don't remove them.

entries.name: Matter Breakdown
entries: A creature that has at least 3 Annihilation Marks loses Resistance to Force damage against this spell. At 5 Marks, Immunity to Force damage instead functions as Resistance against this spell. At 7 Marks, this spell ignores both Resistance and Immunity to Force damage against that creature. In addition, damage from the beam ignores Temporary Hit Points once the target has at least 5 Marks. The Temporary Hit Points aren't removed; the beam simply deals its damage directly to the creature's Hit Points.

entries.name: Terminal Discharge
entries: At any time while the spell lasts, you can end the spell and unleash all remaining destructive energy into one final beam. This requires no action. Choose one creature or object within range. It makes the normal Constitution saving throw. The beam deals {@damage 20d12} Force damage plus {@damage 5d12} for each Annihilation Mark on the target. Afterward, the spell ends.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: Each normal beam deals {@damage 15d12} Force damage, and each Annihilation Mark adds {@damage 5d12} instead of {@damage 3d12}. Terminal Discharge deals {@damage 30d12} Force damage plus {@damage 8d12} for each Annihilation Mark on the target.

Each normal beam deals {@damage 25d12} Force damage, and each Annihilation Mark adds {@damage 8d12}. Terminal Discharge deals {@damage 50d12} Force damage plus {@damage 12d12} for each Annihilation Mark on the target. You can fire two normal beams on each of your turns, choosing the same or different targets. Each beam resolves separately and can add its own Annihilation Mark.

spell.name: Ruinous Verdict
entries: You pronounce a supernatural sentence upon one creature you can see within range, binding its own actions to its destruction. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 14d12} Psychic damage and becomes Condemned for the duration. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and the spell ends. The spell requires no Concentration.

entries.name: Price of Action
entries: Each time the target does any of the following, it immediately takes {@damage 4d12} Psychic damage:

items: takes an Action;
takes a Bonus Action;
takes a Reaction;
casts a spell;
or willingly moves 10 feet or more during a turn.

entries: Count triggers separately. A single activity can't trigger the same category twice, but different categories can trigger in the same turn.

entries.name: Defiance
entries: Whenever the target succeeds on a saving throw against one of your spells or magical effects while Condemned, it takes {@damage 6d12} Psychic damage. Whenever it causes you to take damage, it takes Psychic damage equal to half the damage you actually took from that instance. This retaliatory damage can't itself trigger another instance of Defiance.

entries.name: Final Sentence
entries: Once per casting, if this spell reduces the target to 50 Hit Points or fewer, invoke Final Sentence immediately without an action. The target makes a Constitution save, taking {@damage 20d12} Psychic damage, or half on success. If this reduces it to 0 Hit Points, it can't regain Hit Points until the start of your next turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a 9th-level spell slot, the initial Psychic damage increases to {@damage 20d12}, the damage from each Price of Action trigger increases to {@damage 6d12}, the damage from succeeding on a saving throw under Defiance increases to {@damage 8d12}, and Final Sentence deals {@damage 30d12} Psychic damage. The damage reflected by Defiance and the Hit Point threshold for Final Sentence are unchanged.

spell.name: Absolute Zero
entries: You force a region toward an impossible thermal minimum, freezing matter, motion, and life with supernatural cold. Choose a point you can see within range. A 60-foot-radius sphere centered on that point becomes a zone of absolute cold for the duration. The spell requires no Concentration. When the zone appears, each creature within it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 18d12} Cold damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.
