Objects and structures in the area take maximum damage from the spell. A creature that enters the zone for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make the saving throw again.

entries.name: Thermal Collapse
entries: Whenever a creature fails its saving throw against this spell, its Speed becomes 0 until the start of its next turn, it can't take Reactions during that time, and it gains one Frost Mark until the spell ends. For each Frost Mark already on a creature, Absolute Zero deals an additional {@damage 4d12} Cold damage to it. There is no maximum number of Frost Marks a creature can accumulate.

entries.name: Frozen Solid
entries: If a creature has 3 or more Frost Marks and fails another saving throw against this spell, it becomes encased in supernatural ice. While encased, the creature is Restrained and has Total Cover against effects originating outside the ice. The ice has AC 15 and 50 Hit Points. Damage dealt to the ice doesn't damage the creature inside it. If the ice is destroyed, the creature is freed. If a creature inside the ice fails another saving throw against Absolute Zero, the Cold damage from that instance ignores Resistance to Cold damage.
At 5 Frost Marks, Immunity to Cold damage instead functions as Resistance against this spell.

entries.name: Shatter
entries: At any time while the spell lasts, you can cause every creature currently encased in ice by this spell to shatter violently. This requires no action. Each such creature takes {@damage 12d12} Force damage, and its ice is destroyed. For each Frost Mark on that creature beyond the third, this damage increases by {@damage 3d12}. A creature makes no saving throw against this damage. Using Shatter doesn't end Absolute Zero.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The zone's radius becomes 100 feet, and its initial damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Cold damage. Each Frost Mark increases subsequent damage by {@damage 8d12} instead of {@damage 4d12}. Shatter deals {@damage 20d12} Force damage plus {@damage 5d12} for each Frost Mark beyond the third. In addition, Absolute Zero ignores Resistance to Cold damage entirely, and Cold Immunity instead functions as Resistance against the spell.

spell.name: Soulburn
entries: You ignite the vital essence of one creature you can see within range, burning through flesh, spirit, and the creature's capacity to sustain itself. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 24d12} Radiant or Necrotic damage (your choice when you cast the spell). On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Burn the Soul
entries: On a failed save, the target's Hit Point Maximum is reduced by an amount equal to half the damage it actually takes from this spell. On a successful save, its Hit Point Maximum is reduced by an amount equal to one-quarter of the damage it actually takes instead. This reduction lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest. If this reduction lowers the creature's Hit Point Maximum to 0, it dies.

entries.name: Inextinguishable Wound
entries: Until the start of your next turn, the target can't regain Hit Points, can't gain Temporary Hit Points, and Regeneration and similar effects don't restore Hit Points. During that time, an effect that would restore the target to Hit Points after it is reduced to 0 doesn't function.

entries.name: Soulfire
entries: This spell ignores Resistance to the chosen damage type. If the target is immune to that damage type, it instead has Resistance to this spell. If the target has no soul or equivalent vital essence, Soulburn still functions normally by consuming whatever supernatural or biological force sustains the creature.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage becomes {@damage 40d12}. On a failed save, the target's Hit Point Maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the full damage it actually takes from this spell. On a successful save, the reduction equals half the damage taken. The reduction lasts until removed by {@spell Wish|XPHB}, Divine Intervention, or similarly powerful magic. At 9th level, this spell ignores both Resistance and Immunity to the chosen damage type.
If the spell reduces the target to 0 Hit Points, the target can't be restored to life by a spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower for 24 hours.

spell.name: Black Sun
entries: You create a sphere of collapsed radiance at a point you can see within range. The Black Sun occupies a 10-foot-radius sphere, and its destructive influence fills a 60-foot-radius sphere around it. The spell requires no Concentration. When the Black Sun appears, each creature within its influence must make a Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 12d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 12d12} Necrotic damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.

A creature that enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there must make the saving throw again. You can choose any number of creatures to be unaffected by the Black Sun, and you can change those choices at any time while the spell lasts, requiring no action.

entries.name: Light Devourer
entries: The area within 60 feet of the Black Sun is filled with supernatural Darkness. Nonmagical light can't illuminate it, and magical light created by a spell of 7th level or lower is suppressed while overlapping the area. You and creatures you choose can see normally through this Darkness.

entries.name: Life Eclipse
entries: A creature that fails its saving throw against the Black Sun can't regain Hit Points or gain Temporary Hit Points until the start of its next turn. If it fails by 5 or more, its Hit Point Maximum is also reduced by {@damage 4d12} until it finishes a Long Rest. A creature's Hit Point Maximum can't be reduced below 1 by this feature alone.

entries.name: Wandering Calamity
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can move the Black Sun up to 120 feet to a point you can see. This movement requires no action. Whenever the Black Sun enters a creature's space for the first time during this movement, that creature immediately makes the spell's saving throw. A creature can't be forced to make this additional saving throw more than once per turn from the Black Sun's movement.

entries.name: Total Eclipse
entries: At any time while the spell lasts, you can collapse the Black Sun. This requires no action. Every creature within 100 feet of it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 20d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much. A creature currently inside the Black Sun's normal 60-foot influence instead takes {@damage 30d12} Force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. Afterward, the spell ends.
If the duration ends without you using Total Eclipse, the Black Sun collapses automatically.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Black Sun's influence increases to a 100-foot radius. Its recurring damage becomes {@damage 20d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 20d12} Necrotic damage. Life Eclipse reduces Hit Point Maximum by {@damage 8d12} on a failed save by 5 or more. Total Eclipse deals {@damage 40d12} Force damage, or {@damage 60d12} Force damage to creatures inside the Black Sun's normal influence. At 9th level, damage from this spell ignores Resistance to Radiant, Necrotic, and Force damage, and Immunity to those damage types instead functions as Resistance.

spell.name: Oblivion Sphere
entries: You create a 5-foot-diameter sphere of absolute destructive force in an unoccupied space you can see within range. Matter buckles and vanishes wherever the sphere passes. The spell requires no Concentration. When the sphere appears, and once on each of your turns thereafter, you can move it up to 120 feet in any direction. Moving the sphere requires no action. The sphere can pass through creatures, objects, and structures.

entries.name: Obliteration
entries: The first time on a turn that the sphere enters a creature's space, that creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 20d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. A creature can be damaged by the sphere only once per turn. Objects and structures automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum damage. If a nonmagical object is reduced to 0 Hit Points by the sphere, it is completely destroyed.

entries.name: Tear Through
entries: Each creature reduced to 0 Hit Points grants one Oblivion Charge for the remaining duration. Each adds {@damage 4d12} damage, without limit: {@damage 20d12} at no Charges, {@damage 24d12} at 1, {@damage 28d12} at 2, and {@damage 32d12} at 3.

entries.name: Unstoppable Path
entries: The sphere ignores Difficult Terrain, physical barriers, nonmagical walls, creatures, and nonmagical objects. A magical barrier created by a spell of 7th level or lower is destroyed when the sphere passes through it if that barrier can normally be destroyed or ended by damage or {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}. The sphere doesn't need an open path to move between two points.

entries.name: Consume Magic
entries: Whenever the sphere passes through the area of a spell or magical effect of 7th level or lower that has a duration longer than Instantaneous, you can end that effect. Each magical effect ended this way grants the sphere one Oblivion Charge.

entries.name: Final Erasure
entries: At any time while the spell lasts, you can collapse the sphere. This requires no action. Each creature within 30 feet of the sphere must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 30d12} Force damage plus {@damage 5d12} for each Oblivion Charge. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Afterward, the spell ends. If the duration expires without you collapsing the sphere, Final Erasure occurs automatically.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The sphere's base damage becomes {@damage 35d12} Force, and each Oblivion Charge adds {@damage 8d12} instead of {@damage 4d12}. You can move the sphere up to 300 feet once on each of your turns. Consume Magic can end spells and magical effects of 8th level or lower. Final Erasure deals {@damage 50d12} Force damage plus {@damage 10d12} per Oblivion Charge in a 60-foot radius. At 9th level, damage from this spell ignores Resistance to Force damage, and Force Immunity instead functions as Resistance.

spell.name: Erasure
entries: You impose a single command upon matter: cease. Choose up to eight creatures or objects you can see within range. Each creature must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 18d12 + 40} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Objects automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum damage.

entries.name: Total Erasure
entries: If this spell reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points, its body is completely disintegrated, leaving behind only magic items and Artifacts it was carrying. If this spell reduces a nonmagical object or structure to 0 Hit Points, that target is completely erased. A creature disintegrated by this spell can be restored to life only by magic capable of restoring a creature without requiring its original body.

entries.name: Unmaking
entries: Damage from Erasure ignores Resistance to Force damage. A creature immune to Force damage instead has Resistance to this spell. Additionally, each target affected by the spell has one spell or magical effect of your choice of 7th level or lower currently affecting it immediately ended. You can choose a different effect for each target.

entries.name: Focused Erasure
entries: Instead of choosing multiple targets, you can choose one creature or object. If you do, the target takes {@damage 36d12 + 80} Force damage on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one. If the target fails the saving throw by 5 or more, the damage becomes {@damage 48d12 + 80} instead.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target up to twelve creatures or objects. The normal damage becomes {@damage 30d12 + 60} Force damage per target. Focused Erasure instead deals {@damage 60d12 + 120} Force damage, or {@damage 80d12 + 120} if the target fails its saving throw by 5 or more. At 9th level, the spell ignores both Resistance and Immunity to Force damage; Unmaking can end magical effects of 8th level or lower; and a creature disintegrated by this spell can't be restored to life by a spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower.

spell.name: Bloodforged Cataclysm
entries: You convert your own vital force into raw destructive power and detonate it at a point you can see within range. Choose a point within range. Each creature of your choice in a 40-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 18d12} Necrotic damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Blood Offering
entries: When you cast the spell, before any saving throws are made, you can sacrifice any amount of your current Hit Points. This loss of Hit Points can't be reduced or prevented, ignores Temporary Hit Points, doesn't count as damage, and can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point. For every 10 Hit Points sacrificed, the spell deals an additional {@damage 2d12} Necrotic damage to every target. There is no maximum to the number of additional damage dice you can gain this way other than the Hit Points you are capable of sacrificing.
For example, sacrificing 50 Hit Points increases the spell from {@damage 18d12} to {@damage 28d12}.

entries.name: Life Beyond Flesh
entries: After sacrificing Hit Points, you can reduce your Hit Point Maximum by any multiple of 10. For every 10 Hit Points of Hit Point Maximum sacrificed this way, add another {@damage 3d12} Necrotic damage. This reduction lasts until you finish a Long Rest. Your Hit Point Maximum can't be reduced below 1 by this spell.

entries.name: Overflow
entries: If the total damage dice of Bloodforged Cataclysm reaches {@damage 30d12}, the spell ignores Resistance to Necrotic damage. If the total damage dice reaches {@damage 40d12}, Necrotic Immunity instead functions as Resistance against this spell. If the total damage dice reaches {@damage 50d12}, the spell ignores both Resistance and Immunity to Necrotic damage. If the spell reaches {@damage 60d12} or more, a creature that fails its saving throw also can't regain Hit Points until the end of your next turn.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The base damage becomes {@damage 30d12} Necrotic damage, and the radius becomes 60 feet. Each 10 Hit Points sacrificed adds {@damage 3d12} instead of {@damage 2d12}. Each 10 Hit Points of Hit Point Maximum sacrificed adds {@damage 5d12} instead of {@damage 3d12}. At 9th level, there is no minimum damage threshold required to bypass defenses: the spell always ignores Resistance to Necrotic damage, and Necrotic Immunity functions as Resistance until the spell reaches {@damage 50d12}, at which point it is ignored entirely.

spell.name: Elemental Extinction
entries: You unleash an elemental catastrophe powerful enough to overwhelm even creatures naturally adapted to its destruction. Choose a point you can see within range and choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder. Each creature of your choice in a 60-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 30d12} damage of the chosen type. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Objects and structures in the area automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum damage.
When you cast the spell, you can choose any number of creatures or objects in the area to be completely unaffected.

entries.name: Overwhelming Element
entries: Damage from this spell ignores Resistance to the chosen damage type. If a creature is immune to the chosen damage type, that Immunity instead functions as Resistance against this spell.

entries.name: Elemental Aftermath
entries: The chosen element also leaves an immediate effect throughout the spell's area:

items.name: Acid.
items.entry: Nonmagical objects and structures take an additional {@damage 10d12} Acid damage.

items.name: Cold.
items.entry: Creatures that fail the save have their Speed reduced to 0 until the end of their next turn.

items.name: Fire.
items.entry: Creatures that fail the save take an additional {@damage 6d12} Fire damage at the start of their next turn.

items.name: Lightning.
items.entry: Creatures that fail the save can't take Reactions until the end of their next turn and take an additional {@damage 6d12} Lightning damage if they are wearing metal armor or primarily made of metal.

items.name: Thunder.
items.entry: Creatures that fail the save are pushed up to 60 feet directly away from the center and knocked Prone.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage becomes {@damage 50d12}. The radius becomes 100 feet. At 9th level, this spell ignores both Resistance and Immunity to the chosen damage type. In addition, you can choose two damage types when you cast the spell and divide the damage dice between them however you wish, with a minimum of {@damage 10d12} assigned to either type. Both corresponding Elemental Aftermath effects occur.

spell.name: Horizon Sever
entries: You draw a single line through space and sever everything caught along it. Choose two points you can see within range that are no more than 500 feet apart. A razor-thin wave of destructive force travels along a 20-foot-wide, 100-foot-high line between those points. Each creature in the line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 32d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

The severing wave passes through creatures, objects, structures, and nonmagical barriers. Cover provides no benefit against the spell. Objects and structures automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum damage.

entries.name: Deep Severance
entries: A creature that fails its saving throw by 5 or more is Deeply Severed until the end of your next turn. While Deeply Severed, the creature can't regain Hit Points, its Speed is halved, and whenever it takes damage from another source, it takes an additional {@damage 4d12} Force damage. This additional damage can occur once per turn. If the creature fails the save by 10 or more, the additional damage becomes {@damage 8d12} instead.

entries.name: Sundering Matter
entries: Any nonmagical object or section of a structure reduced to 0 Hit Points by this spell is cleanly cut apart along the path of the wave. The spell can cut through walls, towers, ships, bridges, fortifications, and similar structures rather than merely damaging their outer surface. Magical barriers created by spells of 7th level or lower that intersect the wave are immediately ended if they can normally be ended by {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The two endpoints can be up to 1 mile apart, and the wave becomes 40 feet wide and 300 feet high. The damage becomes {@damage 50d12} Force damage. Deep Severance deals an additional {@damage 8d12} once per turn, or {@damage 16d12} if the target failed the initial saving throw by 10 or more. At 9th level, the spell ignores Resistance to Force damage, Force Immunity instead functions as Resistance, and magical barriers created by spells of 8th level or lower can be severed.

spell.name: Doomspear
entries: You forge a spear of compressed radiance and destructive force and hurl it across the battlefield with overwhelming precision. Make a ranged spell attack against one creature or object you can see within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 16d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 16d12} Force damage. This attack ignores Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover. Objects and structures take maximum damage from this spell on a hit.

entries.name: Perfect Strike
entries: If your attack roll exceeds the target's AC by 5 or more, the target takes an additional {@damage 8d12} Force damage. If your attack roll exceeds its AC by 10 or more, this additional damage becomes {@damage 16d12} Force damage instead. These bonuses don't stack.

entries.name: Doom Critical
entries: Doomspear scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 19 or 20. When you score a Critical Hit with this spell, roll all of the spell's damage dice twice, including any damage from Perfect Strike. In addition, the target is knocked Prone, can't regain Hit Points until the end of your next turn, and loses Resistance to Radiant and Force damage until the end of your next turn. If the target is immune to either damage type, that Immunity instead functions as Resistance during that time.

entries.name: Unerring Destruction
entries: If the attack misses, the spear explodes at the target's location. The target still takes {@damage 8d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 8d12} Force damage. This damage doesn't count as a hit and can't trigger Perfect Strike or Doom Critical.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage on a hit becomes {@damage 24d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 24d12} Force damage. Perfect Strike adds {@damage 12d12} Force damage when you exceed the target's AC by 5 or more, or {@damage 24d12} Force damage when you exceed it by 10 or more. Doomspear scores a Critical Hit on a roll of 18, 19, or 20. The miss damage becomes {@damage 12d12} Radiant damage plus {@damage 12d12} Force damage. At 9th level, damage from this spell ignores Resistance to Radiant and Force damage, and Immunity to either damage type instead functions as Resistance.

spell.name: Extinction Chain
entries: You detonate a sphere of destructive energy that feeds upon every life it extinguishes, using each death to ignite another catastrophe. Choose a point you can see within range. Each creature of your choice in a 40-foot-radius sphere centered on that point must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 24d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Objects and structures automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum damage.

entries.name: Extinction
entries: If at least one creature is reduced to 0 Hit Points by the initial explosion, choose another point you can see within 120 feet of the first explosion's center. A new 40-foot-radius explosion occurs at that point. Every creature of your choice in the new explosion makes a new Constitution saving throw and takes the spell's full {@damage 24d12} Force damage again on a failed save, or half as much on a successful one.
This second explosion is treated as a new instance of Extinction Chain for all purposes except that it costs no action, components, or spell slot.

entries.name: Chain Cataclysm
entries: Each explosion reducing at least one creature to 0 Hit Points permits another full explosion at a point you choose within 120 feet of its center, without chain limit. Each creature can be damaged only once per original casting.

entries.name: Feeding the Chain
entries: For every three creatures reduced to 0 Hit Points by a single explosion, the next explosion gains {@damage 4d12} Force damage. For example, defeating 0–2 creatures causes the next blast to deal {@damage 24d12}; 3–5 causes {@damage 28d12}; 6–8 causes {@damage 32d12}; and 9 causes {@damage 36d12}. There is no maximum to this bonus. The bonus applies only to the next explosion, which then determines its own bonus based on the creatures it defeats.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The base damage becomes {@damage 40d12} Force damage. Each explosion has a 60-foot radius, and the next explosion can be placed within 300 feet of the previous one's center. Feeding the Chain grants {@damage 8d12} Force damage for every three creatures reduced to 0 Hit Points by the previous explosion. At 9th level, the spell ignores Resistance to Force damage, and Force Immunity instead functions as Resistance.

spell.name: Grand Expedition

m.text: a masterwork compass, a silver key, and a miniature pavilion worth at least 5,000 gp total, none of which are consumed

entries: You establish an extradimensional refuge bound to a portable magical anchor, creating a secure base that can accompany an expedition anywhere it travels. Touch one Tiny nonmagical object during the casting. It becomes the Expedition Anchor for the duration. While carrying or touching the Anchor, an Authorized creature can open a doorway into the refuge in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of itself. Opening or closing the doorway requires no action.

You decide which creatures, groups, symbols, passwords, or other clear qualifications are Authorized. For the entire duration, you can change permissions, internal arrangements, and other adjustable functions of the spell regardless of distance or planar boundaries, requiring no action.

entries.name: The Refuge
entries: Design an interior with up to 100,000 square feet of usable space, including living quarters, workshops, laboratories, stores, gardens, or other facilities. Rearrange unoccupied portions at any time without an action.

The refuge automatically provides comfortable temperature and breathable air, clean water, ordinary illumination, sanitation, beds and basic furnishings, and sufficient ordinary food and drink for up to 100 creatures each day. Food, water, and other matter created solely by the refuge cease to exist if removed from it.

entries.name: Expedition Storage
entries: Objects pass normally, with storage up to 1,000,000 pounds beyond furnishings. You always know stored contents and locations. Without an action, move an unattended stored object to your hand or an unoccupied space within 10 feet of an open doorway, if it could fit through.

entries.name: Secure Retreat
entries: Only Authorized creatures can perceive or use the doorway. Unauthorized creatures can't enter the refuge by teleportation, planar travel, extradimensional movement, possession, or similar means. Spells and magical effects of 7th level or lower can't observe, enter, open, or interfere with the refuge from outside it unless you allow them to. Closing the doorway doesn't expel creatures already inside. The refuge continues to exist even if the Anchor is carried to another plane.

entries.name: Mobile Base
entries: The refuge and its occupants remain safe as the Anchor moves or changes planes. Exit uses a doorway at the Anchor's current location unless you permit otherwise. If destroyed, the Anchor reforms in your possession after 1 hour if you live; meanwhile, no new doorway can open.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell becomes permanent until dispelled. The refuge can contain up to 1,000,000 square feet of interior space and has no fixed limit on the weight of ordinary material stored within it beyond what the available space can physically contain. It can sustain up to 1,000 creatures indefinitely. In addition, while inside the refuge, you can open a second doorway to any clearly identifiable location you have personally visited, even on another plane. The secondary doorway remains open until you close it and can be used by any creature you authorize.
Spells and magical effects of 8th level or lower can't observe, enter, open, suppress, or interfere with the refuge unless you allow them to.

spell.name: Grand Armament

m.text: a masterwork engraving set and a flawless lodestone worth at least 5,000 gp total, neither of which is consumed

entries: You inscribe grand enchantments upon equipment fit for legendary conflict. During casting, touch up to twelve non-Artifact objects, enchanting each for the duration as a Grand Armament with two selected Armament Properties. Each can benefit from only one casting at a time. No Concentration is required.
You can change the properties of any Grand Armament at any time during the spell's duration, regardless of distance or planar boundaries, requiring no action.

entries.name: Supreme Edge
entries: If the object is a weapon, it gains a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls. If it already has a magical bonus, use whichever bonus is higher. Its attacks count as magical and ignore Resistance to damage from attacks made with that weapon.

entries.name: Spell Conduit
entries: If the object is a Spellcasting Focus, the wielder gains a +3 bonus to spell attack rolls and spell save DCs. If another effect already grants such a bonus, use the higher bonus rather than adding them together. In addition, once on each of the wielder's turns when a spell deals damage or restores Hit Points, one roll of that spell deals or restores an additional {@damage 3d12}.

entries.name: Impervious Plate
entries: If the object is armor or a shield, it grants an additional +2 bonus to AC. The wearer also gains Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries.name: Elemental Core
entries: Choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Radiant, or Thunder. A weapon deals an additional {@damage 3d12} damage of the chosen type whenever it hits. For a Spellcasting Focus, once per turn when the wielder deals damage with a spell, one target of that spell takes an additional {@damage 3d12} damage of the chosen type.

entries.name: Breaker
entries: Damage dealt using the object ignores Resistance. If the target is Immune to that damage type, the Immunity instead functions as Resistance. Objects and structures damaged using the Grand Armament take maximum damage from its damage dice.

entries.name: Unerring
entries: Attack rolls made using the object ignore Half Cover and Three-Quarters Cover. A weapon attack that misses its target by 5 or less instead hits. A spell attack made through a Spellcasting Focus that misses by 5 or less instead deals half its normal damage without counting as a hit.

entries.name: Guardian
entries: While the creature is wearing, carrying, or wielding the object, it has Advantage on all saving throws. Once per round when it fails a saving throw, it can reroll that saving throw and must use the new result.

entries.name: Relentless
entries: At the start of each of its turns, the wielder gains 20 Temporary Hit Points. If it already has Temporary Hit Points granted by this property, those Hit Points are replaced rather than added together.

entries.name: Swift Casting
entries: If the object is a Spellcasting Focus, once on each of the wielder's turns it can cast a spell with a casting time of 1 Action as a Bonus Action instead. Using this property doesn't prevent the creature from casting another leveled spell during the same turn.

entries.name: Perfect Balance
entries: A weapon bearing this property has its normal and long ranges doubled if it has a range. It can be drawn, stowed, or recovered instantly. If thrown, it returns to the wielder's hand immediately after the attack resolves. The wielder can't be disarmed of it unless willing.

entries.name: Sovereign Ownership
entries: Authorize creatures separately for each object's properties; others can carry it but receive no spell benefits. Change permissions and selected properties at any time without an action, across any distance or plane.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell becomes permanent until dispelled, and you can enchant up to twenty-four objects. Each Grand Armament can have four Armament Properties instead of two. Supreme Edge becomes +4. Spell Conduit becomes +4 to spell attacks and spell save DCs, and its additional effect becomes {@damage 6d12}. Impervious Plate becomes +3 AC. Elemental Core becomes {@damage 6d12}. Relentless grants 40 Temporary Hit Points. Guardian allows its reroll once per turn instead of once per round.
Breaker ignores both Resistance and Immunity to damage dealt through the object.

spell.name: Grand Purification

m.text: a flawless silver basin and a purified crystal worth at least 1,000 gp total, neither of which is consumed

entries: You perform a complete magical purification, stripping away hostile alterations, corruption, bindings, and supernatural contamination from multiple subjects at once. During the casting, choose up to twenty creatures or objects that remain within 30 feet of you for the duration of the ritual. When the ritual is completed, apply every effect below to each chosen subject.

entries.name: Complete Cleansing
entries: End all curses, possession, the Charmed and Frightened conditions, the Petrified condition, magical paralysis, magical diseases and poisons, magical transformations the subject doesn't wish to retain, reductions to Ability Scores, reductions to Hit Point Maximum, effects preventing healing or regeneration, magical aging, magical exhaustion, and magical effects suppressing or interfering with the subject's normal abilities. The subject chooses whether to retain any beneficial effect that would otherwise be removed.

entries.name: Break the Binding
entries: End chosen spells or magical effects of 7th level or lower even if they normally require a specific removal method, including contracts, geases, compulsions, seals, transformations, bindings, possession, and marks. Artifact properties remain untouched.

entries.name: Restore the Body
entries: A creature affected by the ritual regains all lost limbs and organs, has ordinary scars and permanent injuries restored if it wishes, restores all reduced Ability Scores to their normal values, restores its Hit Point Maximum to its normal value, and removes all Exhaustion. This doesn't restore expended spell slots, class resources, magic item charges, or other limited-use abilities.

entries.name: Purify the Object
entries: An affected object is cleansed of curses, hostile magical bindings, unwanted attunement restrictions created by spells, possession, magical contamination, and spells or magical effects of 7th level or lower attached to it. You can preserve any magical property you want to keep. The ritual doesn't destroy or suppress the intrinsic properties of an Artifact.

entries.name: Sever the Connection
entries: You can also end unwanted magical links between the chosen subjects and other creatures, objects, places, or planes. This includes scrying anchors, tracking marks, remote-control links, possession channels, magical ownership bindings, or similar effects created by magic of 7th level or lower.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can affect up to one hundred creatures or objects. The ritual can end spells and magical effects of 8th level or lower. In addition, it can restore a creature even from effects that normally state they can be removed only by {@spell Wish|XPHB}, provided the effect wasn't created by an Artifact or a 9th-level spell. A creature purified by the 9th-level version is also immune for 30 days to any curse, possession, forced transformation, magical disease, or magical effect of 8th level or lower that attempts to recreate an effect removed by this ritual.

spell.name: Arcane Reforging

m.text: a masterwork arcane forge-hammer and a flawless transmutation gem worth at least 2,000 gp total, neither of which is consumed

entries: You reforge an item's magic into a new vessel. During the ritual, touch one non-Artifact magic item and one suitable non-Artifact receiving object. On completion, you can transfer the item's magical properties to the receiver.

entries.name: Transfer Enchantment
entries: Transferred properties leave the original and become permanent in the receiver, including bonuses, charges and recovery, abilities, Attunement, curses, sentience, command words, and restrictions. A changed form alone doesn't change rarity.

entries.name: New Form
entries: The new vessel may be a different item type if it reasonably supports the transferred properties. Adapt form-dependent properties where reasonably possible.
A property that requires a weapon attack functions through the new weapon. A property requiring armor functions through the new armor, and so on.

entries.name: Preserve the Power
entries: Charges, expended uses, recharge state, and other limited resources transfer unchanged; reforging restores none.

entries.name: Selective Reforging
entries: Transfer any selected properties, leaving others on the original. You recognize a curse you transfer even if previously hidden.

entries.name: Merge Enchantments
entries: A receiving non-Artifact magic item retains its existing properties. For direct conflicts, choose which takes precedence each time. The combined result is one item requiring Attunement if any constituent property requires it.

A creature attuned to it uses only one attunement slot, regardless of how many properties were merged into it. You can merge magic from no more than two source items into the same receiving item through this casting.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: Existing attunement to an item doesn't automatically transfer to its new form. When the ritual ends, you can choose one creature currently attuned to the original item. That creature can remain attuned to the reforged item without spending time attuning again.

entries.name: Artifacts
entries: This spell can't transfer, remove, suppress, duplicate, or merge the properties of an Artifact.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can reforge and combine up to five non-Artifact magic items during the same ritual. You can distribute their magical properties among up to five suitable objects in any arrangement you choose. Alternatively, you can combine all selected properties into one item. The resulting item still occupies only one attunement slot, regardless of how many constituent items originally required attunement.

In addition, you can freely adapt properties between compatible item categories, such as weapon properties between different weapon types, armor properties between different armor types, focus properties between staves, rods, wands, or similar implements, and worn-item properties between rings, amulets, cloaks, gauntlets, boots, and similar objects. The spell still can't alter an Artifact.

spell.name: Eternal Binding

m.text: a set of silver sealing nails, engraved chains, and a flawless warding crystal worth at least 2,000 gp total, none of which are consumed

entries: You impose a layered supernatural seal upon a creature, object, portal, doorway, container, chamber, or other clearly defined subject, restricting its movement, activation, access, and magical interaction. The spell requires no Concentration. For the entire duration, you retain control over every adjustable function of the seal regardless of distance or planar boundaries. You can change permissions, restrictions, exceptions, release conditions, and similar settings at any time without an action.

entries.name: Choose the Subject
entries: When you cast the spell, choose one subject you touch: one creature; one object; one portal or planar aperture; one doorway, gate, hatch, container, or similar access point; or one enclosed area no larger than 100 feet across. The subject becomes Sealed for the duration.

entries.name: Seal of Restraint
entries: If the subject is a creature, choose any number of the following restrictions: its Speed becomes 0; it can't teleport; it can't travel between planes; it can't become Incorporeal or pass through solid matter; it can't transform into another form; it can't possess another creature; it can't summon creatures or create portals; or it can't willingly move more than a distance you specify from the location where the ritual was completed. The creature can still speak, perceive, think, and take actions unless you impose another effect through the seal.

A creature restrained by this spell can make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC at the end of each Long Rest. On a success, it can ignore one restriction of its choice until the end of its next Long Rest.

entries.name: Seal of Silence
entries: You can prevent the Sealed subject from producing, transmitting, or receiving specified forms of supernatural communication. You can suppress telepathy, magical sending, dream communication, scrying links, remote control, magical tracking, summoning calls, command-word activation from outside the seal, or similar magical connections. You choose which forms remain permitted.

entries.name: Seal of Power
entries: For a creature, object, portal, or device, suppress any chosen magical properties or supernatural abilities, including spellcasting, Recharge, transformation, item activation, portals, extradimensional access, and summons. Properties remain but can't function; restore or suppress each without an action.
This spell can't suppress the intrinsic properties of an Artifact.

entries.name: Seal of Access
entries: For accessible subjects, specify permissions to open, enter, leave, activate, touch, transfer objects, or otherwise interact, defined by creature, group, symbol, phrase, token, or other clear qualification. Unauthorized creatures can't bypass them through supernatural travel, possession, or incorporeal movement.

entries.name: Seal of Containment
entries: In an enclosed area, designated Contained creatures, objects, gases, liquids, magic, summons, incorporeal entities, or other identifiable contents can't leave by any means except allowed exceptions. Containment alone harms nothing.

entries.name: Seal of Release
entries: Set any number of objectively determinable conditions to alter or release parts of the seal. You can also release any part manually at any time without an action across any distance or plane.

entries.name: Absolute Ward
entries: Spells and magical effects of 7th level or lower can't dispel the seal, suppress it, bypass its restrictions, teleport through it, open a Sealed portal, or alter its permissions unless you allow them to. A creature affected by the seal still benefits from effects that don't conflict with the restrictions you imposed.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The spell becomes permanent until dispelled. You can affect either up to ten separate subjects during the same ritual or one enclosed area up to 1 mile across. Spells and magical effects of 8th level or lower can't suppress, bypass, dispel, or alter the seal unless you allow them. In addition, a creature bound by Seal of Restraint no longer receives the automatic Long Rest saving throw.

A 9th-level Eternal Binding can also contain a creature or magical effect that would normally escape through death, destruction of its body, banishment, possession, planar displacement, or similar means, provided the creature or effect still exists in some form and isn't protected by an Artifact or another 9th-level effect.

spell.name: Exalt Companion

m.text: a jeweled collar, crest, or bonding token worth at least 1,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You elevate a creature already bound to you by magic, training, or supernatural companionship, drawing out power far beyond the limits of an ordinary familiar or companion. Touch one willing creature that is your familiar, bonded companion, controlled mount, magically created companion, or another creature that has willingly accepted a lasting companion bond with you. The spell requires no Concentration. Choose four Exaltations below. The creature gains them for the duration.

entries.name: Empowered Body
entries: The companion's Hit Point Maximum increases by 100, and its AC increases by 3.

entries.name: Perfected Strikes
entries: Its weapon and natural weapon attacks gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls, count as magical, and ignore Resistance to their damage.

entries.name: Titanic Blows
entries: Once on each of its turns when it deals damage, it deals an additional {@damage 6d12} Force damage.

entries.name: Unbound Movement
entries: Its walking, climbing, swimming, and flying Speeds become at least 60 feet. If it lacks one of those movement types, it gains it. Its Fly Speed allows it to hover.

entries.name: Arcane Resistance
entries: The companion has Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects and gains Resistance to damage from spells. In addition, if it succeeds on a saving throw against a spell or magical effect that would normally deal half damage or impose a reduced effect on a successful save, it instead takes no damage and suffers no effect from that spell or magical effect.

entries.name: Indomitable Life
entries: At the start of each of its turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains 20 Hit Points.

entries.name: Unyielding
entries: It is immune to the Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, and Stunned conditions and can't be knocked Prone or moved against its will.

entries.name: Shared Senses
entries: You and the companion can perceive through each other's senses at any distance, including across planar boundaries, without losing access to your own senses.

entries.name: Perfect Bond
entries: You and the companion can communicate telepathically regardless of distance or plane. Either of you always knows the other's location, current Hit Points, and conditions.

entries.name: Spell Conduit
entries: When you cast a spell with a range other than Self, you can have the spell originate from the companion's space instead of yours, regardless of the distance between you, provided you're on the same plane.

entries.name: Guardian Bond
entries: When either you or the companion takes damage while on the same plane, the other can use its Reaction to take that damage instead. The transferred damage can't be transferred again.

entries.name: Greater Action
entries: The companion gains one additional Action on each of its turns. This Action can be used only to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Help, Hide, Search, or Use an Object.

entries.name: Deathless Bond
entries: The first time during the spell's duration that the companion is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it instead drops to 1 Hit Point and immediately regains 50 Hit Points. This Exaltation can activate once per Long Rest.

entries.name: Independent Companion
entries: The companion retains its identity, personality, intelligence, memories, and free will. This grants no compelled obedience; existing command rules remain unless an Exaltation changes them.

entries.name: Reconfiguration
entries: Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace any number of the companion's Exaltations with different ones from this spell. You can do so regardless of distance or planar boundaries.
A creature can benefit from only one casting of Exalt Companion at a time.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The transformation becomes permanent until you or the companion willingly end it. The companion gains seven Exaltations instead of four. Empowered Body grants 200 Hit Points and +5 AC. Perfected Strikes becomes +5. Titanic Blows becomes {@damage 12d12} Force. Indomitable Life restores 40 Hit Points each turn. Spell Conduit functions even across planar boundaries. Deathless Bond restores the companion to full Hit Points when triggered. Greater Action has no restriction on which Action the companion can take.

spell.name: Legion Covenant

m.text: a ceremonial standard and a flawless summoning crystal worth at least 1,000 gp total, neither of which is consumed

entries: You establish a lasting magical covenant and call forth a company of extraplanar or supernatural beings to serve beneath its terms. When the ritual is completed, choose one creature type from the following: Celestial, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, or Undead. You summon creatures of the chosen type into unoccupied spaces within 30 feet of you. The summoned creatures can have a combined Challenge Rating of up to 20. A creature without a Challenge Rating can't be summoned by this spell.
You choose the creatures when you complete the ritual, subject to the DM determining whether a particular creature exists and can be called.

entries.name: The Legion
entries: The summoned beings are real creatures, temporarily present for the duration. They retain their statistics, abilities, and their own Initiative, understand your verbal commands regardless of language, regard you and creatures you designate as allies, and obey to the best of their abilities. You can telepathically command any members regardless of distance on the same plane.
Issuing or changing a command requires no action.

entries.name: Division of Power
entries: Divide the CR allowance freely; creatures below CR 1 count as at least CR 1/4 each.

entries.name: Replace the Fallen
entries: If a member of the Legion dies or is permanently dismissed, its portion of the spell's CR allowance becomes available again. By performing a 10-minute ritual while touching the material component, you can summon replacement creatures using the available CR allowance. This doesn't expend another spell slot. You can't exceed the spell's normal CR limit.

entries.name: Dismissal and Recall
entries: You can dismiss any member of the Legion at any time without an action. A dismissed creature returns to its original location or plane. Once per Short or Long Rest, you can also cause any number of members of the Legion on the same plane as you to teleport to unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you. This requires no action.

entries.name: Selective Command
entries: Without an action, assign groups, commanders, orders, allies, enemies, prohibitions, patrols, destinations, or releases throughout the duration. Changes reach affected members anywhere on your plane.

entries.name: Covenant Protection
entries: A summoned creature can't be magically compelled by another creature to act directly against you or another member of the Legion by a spell or magical effect of 7th level or lower. Such an effect can still affect the creature normally in every other respect.

entries.name: End of the Covenant
entries: When the spell ends, all remaining summoned creatures return safely to the locations or planes from which they came. A creature slain during the covenant remains dead unless its own nature or another effect would restore it.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a 9th-Level Spell Slot
entries: The covenant becomes permanent until you dismiss it or it is dispelled. The Legion can have a combined Challenge Rating of up to 40. In addition, you can summon creatures from two creature types instead of one; Recall functions across planar boundaries; your telepathic commands function across planar boundaries; replacing fallen members takes only 1 minute; and spells or magical effects of 8th level or lower can't compel, banish, dismiss, or seize control of a member of your Legion unless you allow them.
You can still never exceed the Legion's maximum combined Challenge Rating.

spell.name: Genesis

m.text: a flawless planar seed worth at least 2,000 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: Create a genuine, independent plane, initially up to 100 miles across within an impassable planar boundary. You determine its physical structure; it persists after casting.

entries.name: Shape the World
entries: Fill it with ordinary nonmagical geography and the stone, soil, water, air, ice, vegetation, and other natural matter required. You control elevations, depths, waterways, coastlines, and other large-scale features.
It can't directly create precious metals, gemstones, magic items, Artifacts, or other material whose primary purpose is generating wealth.

entries.name: Laws of the Realm
entries: When you create the plane, determine its fundamental environmental laws. You can choose the direction and strength of gravity; whether the realm has a sun, moons, stars, or another source of illumination; the length of its day and night; its seasons; temperature ranges; weather patterns; atmospheric composition; whether it has oceans, tides, or similar cycles; and the apparent appearance of its sky and horizon. These properties are real within the plane.

entries.name: Living World
entries: Populate it with real nonmagical plants and non-sapient beasts suited to its environments, capable of normal lifecycles and ecosystems. You can't create sapient beings, souls, classed or legendary creatures, or supernatural abilities.

entries.name: Sovereign Passage
entries: When the plane is created, a permanent portal appears within 10 feet of you and at a location of your choice within the new realm. The portal can be opened or closed by you at any time without an action. You determine who is permitted to perceive the portal, open it, travel through it, or bring creatures and objects through it. You can change these permissions at any time, regardless of distance or planar boundaries, requiring no action. You can also create or dismiss additional portals between the plane and locations you have personally visited.
You can maintain up to ten such portals at once.

entries.name: Architect's Authority
entries: While on your plane, use an Action to permanently reshape nonmagical terrain in a 1-mile-radius sphere centered on any point you perceive there, including landforms, watercourses, lakes, vegetation, islands, and coastlines.
Creatures and attended objects aren't directly created, destroyed, or transformed by this feature.

entries.name: Dominion of Climate
entries: You control the plane's ordinary weather and climate. At any time, requiring no action, you can alter temperature, cloud cover, precipitation, fog, wind, storms, seasonal conditions, and other natural weather in any portion of the plane. Changes can occur immediately or gradually, as you choose.

entries.name: Planar Stability
entries: The plane is naturally stable and doesn't collapse if you die. It doesn't require Concentration, continued spellcasting, or magical upkeep. Spells and magical effects of 8th level or lower can't destroy the plane, merge it with another plane, rewrite its fundamental laws, seize control of its portals, or sever your authority over it.

entries.name: Return to Genesis
entries: You always know the direction of the plane relative to your current planar location. Once per Long Rest, you can transport yourself and up to twenty willing creatures you can see directly to any unoccupied locations you choose within your plane. This requires an Action and doesn't expend a spell slot. While inside your plane, you can return the same creatures to the locations from which they entered using the same ability.

entries.name: Expand Creation
entries: Each additional casting of Genesis can target a plane you previously created with this spell instead of creating a new one.
When you do, choose one:

items: {@b Expand.} Increase the plane's maximum dimensions by another 100 miles in any directions you choose.
{@b Reshape the Laws.} Permanently redefine any of the realm's environmental or physical laws established by this spell.
{@b Deepen Creation.} Create another distinct layer, region, moon, floating continent, underground world, oceanic depth, or similar major realm connected to the existing plane.

entries: There is no maximum number of times you can expand the same plane through additional castings.

entries.name: True Genesis
entries: A plane created by this spell is a genuine location for teleportation, planar travel, resurrection, divination, permanent structures, ecosystems, settlement, and other effects that depend on a real place existing. It remains in existence until destroyed by an effect capable of destroying an entire plane or by another effect of comparable power.

spell.name: Creation of Life

m.text: a flawless life-crystal worth at least 5,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: Shape prepared organic matter into a permanent living creature, designing its body, instincts, capabilities, and optional soul.

entries.name: Creation Rules
entries: Choose one Body Preset for the creature. The creature uses a +4 Proficiency Bonus unless another feature says otherwise. Distribute the following Ability Scores as you choose: 22, 20, 18, 16, 14, 10. Then choose eight Creation Traits. The creature can't gain Legendary Actions, Mythic Actions, Lair Actions, class levels, or 6th-level or higher spellcasting from this spell. A creature can't have more than two Damage Immunities granted by its Creation Traits.

entries.name: Brute
entries: AC 17, 220 Hit Points, Speed 40 feet. Attack Bonus +9, Save DC 17. It makes two attacks when it takes the Attack action, each dealing up to {@damage 4d10+6} damage.

entries.name: Hunter
entries: AC 19, 170 Hit Points, Speed 50 feet. Attack Bonus +10, Save DC 17. It makes three attacks when it takes the Attack action, each dealing up to {@damage 3d8+5} damage.

entries.name: Guardian
entries: AC 20, 200 Hit Points, Speed 30 feet. Attack Bonus +8, Save DC 17. It makes two attacks when it takes the Attack action, each dealing up to {@damage 3d10+5} damage.

entries.name: Mystic
entries: AC 17, 160 Hit Points, Speed 30 feet. Spell Attack Bonus +9, Spell Save DC 18. It can possess Innate Spellcasting with spells of 5th level or lower. It can have no more than one 5th-level spell that recharges on a Long Rest.

entries.name: Creation Traits
entries: Choose eight of the following.

entries.name: Flight
entries: The creature gains a Fly Speed of up to 60 feet. It can also gain Hover.

entries.name: Aquatic
entries: The creature gains a Swim Speed of up to 60 feet and can breathe both air and water.

entries.name: Burrower
entries: The creature gains a Burrow Speed of up to 40 feet through earth, sand, clay, and similar nonmagical material.

entries.name: Climber
entries: The creature gains a Climb Speed of up to 60 feet and can move across ceilings without making an ability check.

entries.name: Darkvision
entries: The creature gains Darkvision out to 300 feet.

entries.name: Blindsight
entries: The creature gains Blindsight out to 60 feet.

entries.name: Tremorsense
entries: The creature gains Tremorsense out to 120 feet.

entries.name: Truesight
entries: The creature gains Truesight out to 60 feet.

entries.name: Damage Resistance
entries: Choose two damage types. The creature gains Resistance to both. This trait can be selected more than once, choosing different damage types each time.

entries.name: Damage Immunity
entries: Choose one damage type. The creature gains Immunity to that damage type. This trait can be selected no more than twice.

entries.name: Condition Immunity
entries: Choose three conditions. The creature is immune to them. This trait can be selected more than once, choosing different conditions each time.

entries.name: Magic Resistance
entries: The creature has Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.

entries.name: Evasion
entries: When the creature is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage on a successful save and half damage on a failed save.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of its turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains 10 Hit Points.

entries.name: Relentless
entries: Once per Long Rest, when the creature would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it is reduced to 1 Hit Point instead.

entries.name: Natural Armor
entries: Increase the creature's AC by 2.

entries.name: Thick Hide
entries: Increase the creature's Hit Point Maximum by 50.

entries.name: Swift
entries: Increase all of the creature's Speeds by 20 feet.

entries.name: Reach
entries: The creature's natural weapon attacks gain 10-foot reach.

entries.name: Powerful Strikes
entries: The creature's natural weapon attacks deal an additional {@damage 2d10} damage.

entries.name: Multiattack
entries: The creature makes one additional attack whenever it takes the Attack action. This trait can't increase its total number of attacks beyond three.

entries.name: Breath Weapon
entries: The creature gains a Recharge 5–6 ability. Choose a 30-foot cone or 60-foot line and one damage type. Creatures in the area make a Dexterity or Constitution saving throw against the creature's Save DC, chosen when the trait is created. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 10d10} damage of the chosen type, or half as much on a successful save.

entries.name: Destructive Burst
entries: The creature gains a Recharge 5–6 ability. Choose a point within 120 feet. Creatures of its choice within a 20-foot-radius sphere centered there make a saving throw against its Save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 8d10} damage of a chosen type, or half as much on a successful save.

entries.name: Damaging Aura
entries: Choose a damage type. A creature of the created creature's choice that starts its turn within 10 feet of it takes {@damage 3d10} damage of that type. A creature can take this damage only once per turn.

entries.name: Fear Aura
entries: A creature of the created creature's choice that starts its turn within 20 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against its Save DC or become Frightened until the start of its next turn.

entries.name: Reactive Defense
entries: Once per round when the creature is hit by an attack, it can reduce the damage by {@damage 3d10}.

entries.name: Reactive Strike
entries: When a creature within its reach damages it, the created creature can use its Reaction to make one natural weapon attack against that creature.

entries.name: Spell Reflection
entries: Once per round when the creature succeeds on a saving throw against a spell that targets only it, it can redirect the spell back at the caster. The original caster becomes the new target using the original spell attack bonus or save DC.

entries.name: Innate Magic
entries: Choose up to three spells of 3rd level or lower. The creature can cast each chosen spell once per Long Rest without material components that have a listed gold cost. Use Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as its spellcasting ability, chosen when the creature is created.

entries.name: Greater Innate Magic
entries: Choose one spell of 5th level or lower. The creature can cast that spell once per Long Rest without material components that have a listed gold cost. This trait can be selected more than once, choosing a different spell each time.

entries.name: Teleport
entries: As a Bonus Action, the creature teleports up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space it can see.

entries.name: Phase Movement
entries: The creature can move through other creatures and nonmagical objects as if they were Difficult Terrain. It takes {@damage 1d10} Force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.

entries.name: Amorphous
entries: The creature can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch wide without squeezing.

entries.name: Spider Climb
entries: The creature can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings, without making an ability check.

entries.name: Siege Monster
entries: The creature deals double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Immutable Form
entries: The creature is immune to any spell or effect that would alter its form unless it is willing.

entries.name: Freedom of Movement
entries: Difficult Terrain doesn't cost the creature extra movement, and magic can't reduce its Speed or cause it to be Paralyzed or Restrained.

entries.name: Legendary Endurance
entries: Once per Long Rest, when the creature fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Death Ward
entries: The first time each Long Rest the creature would die instantly or be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it instead remains alive at 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Spellguard
entries: If the creature succeeds on a saving throw against a spell or magical effect that would normally deal half damage or impose a reduced effect on a success, it instead takes no damage and suffers no effect from it.

entries.name: Adaptive Body
entries: At the end of each Long Rest, choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Radiant, or Thunder. The creature gains Resistance to that damage type until the end of its next Long Rest.

entries.name: Powerful Build
entries: The creature counts as one Size larger when determining its carrying capacity and the weight it can push, drag, or lift. It also has Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.

entries.name: Unyielding Mind
entries: The creature is immune to magical possession and has Advantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saving throws.

entries.name: Perfect Recovery
entries: Whenever the creature finishes a Long Rest, it regains all of its Hit Points and ends one curse, disease, poison, or condition currently affecting it, provided that effect wasn't created by an Artifact or 9th-level spell.

entries.name: Creature Type and Form
entries: Choose one creature type other than Construct or Undead. Choose a Size from Tiny to Huge. You determine the creature's appearance, anatomy, natural weapons, number and arrangement of limbs, sex or reproductive roles if any, diet, respiration, body temperature, lifespan, maturation, sleep requirements, natural habitat, languages, and ordinary biological characteristics. These are genuine parts of the creature rather than cosmetic magical effects.

entries.name: Natural Weapons
entries: Choose natural attack forms appropriate to the anatomy. Use Body Preset attack bonuses and base damage, distributing attacks among natural weapons as desired.

entries.name: True Life
entries: The creature isn't summoned or automatically controlled. You choose initial instincts and temperament, but its personality, desires, loyalties, and future behavior remain free.

entries.name: Sapience
entries: A sapient creature begins with at least one language, knowledge of its body and abilities, basic independent functioning, and normal learning and social capacity. It gains no unexperienced memories, professional training, class levels, or historical knowledge.

entries.name: New Soul
entries: The spell creates a new soul for the creature. This soul is a new individual and isn't copied, divided, or stolen from another creature.

entries.name: Existing Soul
entries: A willing existing soul can enter the created body. The soul must still exist and be able to return to life. The creature retains the soul's identity, memories, personality, languages, proficiencies, Feats, class levels, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, and other learned abilities. It uses the created body's Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Hit Points, Armor Class, movement, senses, natural weapons, and Creation Traits.

If a retained class feature depends on anatomy the new body doesn't possess, that feature functions only if the new anatomy can reasonably support it. This spell alone can't force an unwilling soul into a body.

entries.name: Empty Vessel
entries: You can create the body without a soul. The body remains alive, stable, and Unconscious but possesses no independent will or personality. A suitable magical effect can later place a soul into the body.

entries.name: Reproduction
entries: Define reproductive capability and method, fertility, gestation or incubation, offspring number, maturation, heredity, and compatible partners. Natural descendants are real creatures, not magical effects.

entries.name: Stable Species
entries: Compatible creatures of substantially the same design can found a permanent species. Descendants reproduce and vary normally, can't be dispelled, and don't depend on this spell.

entries.name: Designed Limitations
entries: You may impose biological limitations, such as environmental or dietary dependence, vulnerability, infertility, or shortened life. These grant no extra Creation Traits unless the DM allows it.

entries.name: Forbidden Creation
entries: This spell can't directly grant Legendary Actions, Mythic Actions, Lair Actions, class levels to a newly created soul, spellcasting of 6th level or higher, divine rank, Artifact properties, or an exact duplicate of a unique named creature. It also can't copy or divide an existing soul.

entries.name: Greater Genesis
entries: When you cast Creation of Life again using a design you have previously created with this spell, you can create up to twenty creatures during the same ritual instead of one. Each uses that fundamental design, but you can vary appearance, sex, Ability Score placement, language, personality, and up to two Creation Traits between individuals. Existing souls can be placed into any of these bodies individually, provided each soul satisfies the normal requirements.

entries.name: Legacy
entries: Created creatures are permanent living beings with normal capacity to reproduce, learn, develop, and form societies. They aren't maintained by an ongoing spell and can't simply be ended by {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}.

spell.name: Eternal Ascension

m.text: a flawless immortal crystal worth at least 5,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You permanently sever a willing creature from the ordinary cycle of aging and natural death, transforming its life into a self-restoring existence. Touch one willing living creature throughout the casting. When the ritual is completed, the creature becomes Immortal. This transformation isn't an ongoing spell effect and can't be ended by {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}.

entries.name: Ageless
entries: The Immortal creature no longer ages unless it chooses to. It can choose its apparent physical age when the ritual is completed and can thereafter alter its apparent age at the end of any Long Rest. This change never reduces its physical capabilities. The creature can't die from old age, ordinary disease, natural organ failure, starvation, dehydration, suffocation, or other purely natural deterioration. It can still eat, drink, sleep, and breathe normally if it wishes.

entries.name: Perfect Vitality
entries: The Immortal creature is immune to disease, magical aging, reductions to its Hit Point Maximum caused by aging or bodily deterioration, and effects that would cause its body to permanently decay. Lost limbs and organs regrow when it finishes a Long Rest. At the end of a Long Rest, the creature can also restore its body to its preferred natural form, removing ordinary scars, permanent wounds, and nonmagical physical deformities if it chooses.

entries.name: Refusal of Death
entries: On death, the Immortal can spend an available use to return after 1 minute with full Hit Points, even from total bodily destruction. Reform from surviving remains or, if none exist, where it died or the nearest suitable unoccupied space.
The creature can use Refusal of Death twice, and regains all expended uses when it finishes a Long Rest. If it dies while it has no uses remaining, it doesn't return to life automatically.

entries.name: Immortal Remains
entries: If it doesn't return through Refusal of Death, its corpse still restores to its complete, undamaged form. If no usable remains exist, a complete corpse reforms after 1 minute where it died or in the nearest suitable unoccupied space.

items: The corpse doesn't rot or decompose.
The corpse doesn't age.
The corpse can't become Undead unless the creature's soul willingly allows it.
The corpse remains physically identical to the creature's preferred immortal form.
The corpse remains a valid body for resurrection magic regardless of how long it has been dead.

entries: It remains dead until otherwise revived. Its soul is free to exist after death; later revival returns it to the preserved body unless another effect specifically supplies a different one.

entries.name: Unending Soul
entries: The creature's soul remains anchored to its immortal existence. Its soul can't be unwillingly transformed, consumed, destroyed, divided, or permanently separated from its identity by a spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower. If such an effect attempts to trap or prevent the soul from returning through Refusal of Death, the creature still reforms normally.

entries.name: Death Beyond Death
entries: The creature fails to return through Refusal of Death only if one of the following occurs:

items: Its soul is permanently destroyed by an Artifact or a 9th-level effect specifically capable of destroying souls.
Its soul is successfully imprisoned by an Artifact or another 9th-level effect that explicitly prevents resurrection or return.
The creature willingly chooses not to return.
An effect explicitly capable of permanently killing an immortal creature overcomes this spell.

entries: If the preventing effect later ends while the soul still exists and the creature has a use of Refusal of Death available, the creature immediately begins reforming and returns after 1 minute.

entries.name: Eternal Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of its turns, if the Immortal creature has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains 20 Hit Points. If it begins its turn at 0 Hit Points but isn't dead, it instead immediately regains 20 Hit Points and becomes conscious. This regeneration doesn't function until the start of the creature's next turn after it takes damage from an Artifact or a 9th-level spell.

entries.name: Immutable Existence
entries: The creature can't be permanently transformed into another creature, object, or state against its will. Temporary transformations still function normally, but when they end, the Immortal creature always returns to its immortal body. A spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower can't permanently erase its identity, replace its soul, rewrite its fundamental nature, permanently transform its body, or remove its immortality.

entries.name: Immortal Continuity
entries: Death and restoration preserve identity, memories, class levels, Feats, proficiencies, and Attunement but restore no spent slots, class resources, item charges, Hit Dice, or other limited uses.

entries.name: Chosen End
entries: The Immortal creature can permanently relinquish its immortality during a 24-hour ritual requiring no spell slot. Once relinquished, Eternal Ascension ends permanently for that creature. It immediately begins aging normally from its current physical age and can thereafter die normally.

entries.name: One Eternal Life
entries: A creature can benefit from Eternal Ascension only once. Casting it again on an already Immortal creature has no additional effect.

spell.name: Second Sun

m.text: a flawless golden sphere worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You kindle a new celestial light and permanently bind it to the sky of the plane you occupy. At the end of the casting, choose a point in the sky you can see. A supernatural sun forms there. It is a genuine permanent celestial phenomenon, but possesses no physical mass and exerts no gravitational force unless you choose otherwise.

entries.name: Celestial Body
entries: Set the sun's apparent size, color, brightness, sky-path, rising and setting, speed, and day-night cycle, including a stationary position. Change them without an action anywhere on the same plane.

entries.name: Light of a New Sun
entries: The Second Sun produces true sunlight. You choose its maximum sphere of influence when creating it, up to 1,000 miles in radius. Within that area, you can independently determine how much light each region receives, from complete darkness to bright sunlight. This sunlight counts as natural sunlight for creatures, plants, spells, and other effects that distinguish sunlight from ordinary light.

entries.name: Gift of Warmth
entries: You determine the amount of heat the Second Sun provides throughout its area. You can maintain ordinary habitable temperatures even in polar regions, permanent winter, high mountains, underground regions exposed to its light, or magically cold environments. You can alter the temperature of different portions of the area independently, but the spell can't directly use heat to damage creatures.

entries.name: Living Radiance
entries: Nonmagical plants exposed to the Second Sun can grow normally even if the original environment lacks sufficient natural sunlight. You can cause a region receiving its light to count as having ideal natural sunlight for agriculture and ordinary plant growth. The spell doesn't instantly create plants or accelerate their growth beyond their normal biological limits.

entries.name: Solar Dominion
entries: Exempt any creatures, objects, structures, or regions from individual properties. Change permissions and regional settings at any time without an action on the same plane.

entries.name: Solar Purity
entries: You can suppress magical Darkness of 8th level or lower and illuminate ordinary supernatural darkness. Creatures suffer only sunlight's normal effects; the light counts as genuine sunlight for all such requirements.

entries.name: Eclipse
entries: As an Action while on the same plane, you can cause the Second Sun to vanish from the sky. Its effects immediately cease. You can restore it as an Action, causing it to reappear in its assigned position. The sun isn't destroyed while eclipsed.

entries.name: Solar Avatar
entries: Once per Long Rest, while beneath the Second Sun, you can use an Action to call a fragment of it down to a point you can see within 1 mile. A 300-foot-radius sphere centered on that point is flooded with overwhelming solar radiance. Creatures of your choice in the area make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 30d12} Radiant damage and is Blinded for 1 minute. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't Blinded. Undead and creatures vulnerable to sunlight automatically fail the saving throw.
Afterward, the area remains filled with bright sunlight for 1 hour. Using this feature doesn't diminish the Second Sun.

entries.name: Eternal Star
entries: The Second Sun doesn't require Concentration, maintenance, fuel, or the continued survival of its creator. An effect of 8th level or lower can't dispel it, permanently extinguish it, seize control of it, alter its path, or change its properties. If you die, its current settings remain in effect permanently unless altered by another effect capable of controlling a 9th-level creation.

entries.name: Multiple Suns
entries: You can cast Second Sun more than once. Each casting creates a separate sun with its own path, area, and properties. There is no inherent maximum number of Second Suns a world or plane can contain.

spell.name: Apotheosis

m.text: a flawless divine prism worth at least 5,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You awaken a transcendent spark within one willing creature you touch throughout the casting. When the ritual ends, the creature undergoes Apotheosis. This transformation is permanent, isn't an ongoing spell effect, and can't be ended by {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}. The creature retains its identity, species, class levels, memories, Feats, and other abilities, then gains the following benefits.

entries.name: Transcendent Form
entries: Choose one of the creature's Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma scores. That score increases by 4, to a maximum of 30. Then choose two different Ability Scores. Each increases by 2, also to a maximum of 30. The creature's Hit Point Maximum increases by 100.

entries.name: Divine Resilience
entries: The creature gains Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage; Resistance to two other damage types of its choice; Immunity to disease; Immunity to magical aging; and Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects. If the creature already has Resistance to a damage type chosen here, it instead gains Immunity to that damage type.

entries.name: Transcendent Nature
