entries: The creature no longer needs to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep, though it can still do so. It can't be permanently transformed against its will by an effect of 8th level or lower. Its creature type doesn't change unless it chooses one of the Ascendant Gifts that changes it.

entries.name: Ascendant Gifts
entries: Choose five of the following gifts.

entries.name: Divine Body
entries: Increase the creature's Hit Point Maximum by another 100, and its AC increases by 2.

entries.name: Perfect Ability
entries: Increase one Ability Score by 4, to a maximum of 30. This gift can be chosen more than once for different Ability Scores.

entries.name: Supreme Resistance
entries: Gain Immunity to two damage types.

entries.name: Unassailable
entries: Gain Immunity to three conditions of your choice.

entries.name: Regeneration
entries: At the start of each of its turns, if it has at least 1 Hit Point, it regains 30 Hit Points.

entries.name: Divine Speed
entries: Increase every Speed the creature possesses by 30 feet, and it gains a Fly Speed of 60 feet with Hover if it doesn't already have one.

entries.name: Perfect Senses
entries: Gain Truesight out to 120 feet, and the creature can't be surprised.

entries.name: Divine Strike
entries: Once on each of its turns when it deals damage, it deals an additional {@damage 6d12} Radiant, Necrotic, Force, or Psychic damage, chosen when this gift is gained.

entries.name: Overwhelming Power
entries: The creature's attacks and damaging abilities ignore Resistance to damage. Immunity is treated as Resistance instead.

entries.name: Divine Magic
entries: Choose three spells of 5th level or lower. The creature can cast each once per Long Rest without material components that have a listed cost.

entries.name: Greater Divine Magic
entries: Choose one spell of 8th level or lower. The creature can cast it once per Long Rest without material components that have a listed cost. This gift can be chosen only once.

entries.name: Unbound Movement
entries: Difficult Terrain doesn't cost extra movement, and the creature can move through creatures and nonmagical objects as Difficult Terrain.

entries.name: Planar Step
entries: As a Bonus Action, the creature teleports up to 120 feet to a space it can see. Once per Long Rest, it can instead transport itself and up to ten willing creatures it can see to another plane.

entries.name: Sovereign Presence
entries: The creature can communicate telepathically with any creature it can see within 1 mile that knows a language. As an Action, it can project its voice to any number of creatures within 10 miles.

entries.name: Divine Recovery
entries: When the creature finishes a Long Rest, it regains all Hit Points, ends all conditions affecting it, and ends one curse or other magical effect of 8th level or lower affecting it.

entries.name: Deathless Spark
entries: When the creature dies, its body doesn't decay. Unless its soul is destroyed or imprisoned, it can be restored to life regardless of how long it has been dead and without requiring its original body.

entries.name: Expanded Being
entries: The creature becomes one of the following types in addition to its existing type: Celestial, Fey, Fiend, or Elemental. Effects that interact with either type can affect it.

entries.name: Colossal Presence
entries: The creature can become one Size larger or smaller as a Bonus Action, up to Gargantuan or down to Small. Its equipment changes size with it.

entries.name: Legendary Endurance
entries: Three times per Long Rest, when the creature fails a saving throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

entries.name: Unstoppable Will
entries: The creature is immune to possession and to any effect that would control its actions unless it willingly allows that effect.

entries.name: Divine Presence
entries: The ascended creature produces a subtle supernatural manifestation of its choice, such as a halo, unnatural eyes, shifting shadows, celestial markings, a spectral crown, an aura, or another visible sign. It can suppress or restore this manifestation at any time without an action.

entries.name: Beyond Mortal Limits
entries: Apotheosis doesn't grant class levels, Legendary Actions, Mythic Actions, Lair Actions, divine rank, or the authority of a true deity. However, the creature is permanently considered a transcendent being for effects that distinguish ordinary mortals from beings that have surpassed mortal existence.

entries.name: Unique Ascension
entries: A creature can benefit from Apotheosis only once. Its Ascendant Gifts are chosen when the ritual is completed and normally can't be changed afterward.

spell.name: World Tree

m.text: a living seed encased in amber and precious metals worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You plant a seed and force it beyond every natural limit, creating a colossal living tree whose roots and crown become part of the world itself. At the end of the casting, the tree erupts from the ground at the point you touched.

entries.name: Colossal Growth
entries: You determine the tree's appearance and general shape. It can grow up to 5 miles tall, 3 miles across at its crown, and extend its root network up to 20 miles from its trunk. Its growth doesn't crush creatures or occupied structures unless you deliberately choose an unoccupied path that allows it. The tree is alive, but it isn't a creature.

entries.name: Living Structure
entries: You can shape hollows, chambers, bridges, tunnels, platforms, stairways, reservoirs, and passages throughout the trunk, branches, and roots as the tree grows. The tree can comfortably support a permanent population of up to 100,000 creatures. Its internal spaces remain naturally ventilated, structurally stable, and protected from ordinary weather.

entries.name: Heartwood
entries: At the center of the tree is a living Heartwood Core. The tree can't be permanently killed while its Heartwood remains intact. If portions of the tree are burned, cut away, shattered, diseased, or otherwise destroyed, they regrow completely within 24 hours. An effect of 8th level or lower can't permanently destroy the Heartwood.

entries.name: Worldroot Network
entries: The tree's roots can pass through ordinary earth and stone without damaging structures you choose to preserve. Within the root network, soil becomes fertile, fresh water naturally collects where needed, ordinary plants can grow even in poor soil, erosion and desertification gradually reverse, and nonmagical plant disease is suppressed. You can exclude any region from these effects.

entries.name: Verdant Dominion
entries: While on the same plane as the World Tree, you can alter its living growth at any time without an action. You can create or close passages, grow or remove branches, open or seal chambers, redirect roots, create bridges and platforms, grow walls of living wood, or reshape inhabited sections of the tree. These changes occur gradually over 1 minute unless you choose a slower growth.

entries.name: Life-Giving Sap
entries: The World Tree produces an inexhaustible but controlled supply of supernatural sap. A creature that drinks a dose gains one of the following benefits of your choice: regains {@damage 10d12+40} Hit Points; ends one disease or poison; ends one level of Exhaustion; regrows one lost limb or organ over 1 hour; or gains enough nourishment and water for 7 days. A creature can benefit from the sap only once per Long Rest. You decide who is permitted to harvest or receive it.

entries.name: Branches Between Worlds
entries: You can designate up to ten great branches or roots as Worldgates. Each Worldgate can connect to a location on another plane that you have personally visited. A creature you permit can pass through the gate as though crossing an ordinary doorway. You can open or close each gate, change its destination, determine who can perceive it, determine who can use it, and determine what creatures or objects can pass through it. You can change these settings at any time while on the same plane, requiring no action.

entries.name: Sanctuary of Life
entries: Within 20 miles of the tree, ordinary plants grow at twice their normal rate, natural water doesn't become stagnant, nonmagical crops don't fail from ordinary soil exhaustion, magical effects of 8th level or lower can't permanently blight the land unless you allow them, and you can cause ordinary forests and vegetation to gradually reclaim barren ground. This doesn't create creatures or force existing creatures to remain in the area.

entries.name: Seed of Continuance
entries: Once every year, the World Tree produces one Worldseed. A Worldseed remains viable indefinitely. A creature capable of casting 9th-level spells can use the Worldseed as the material component for another casting of World Tree, requiring no additional costly material component.

entries.name: Eternal Growth
entries: The World Tree doesn't require Concentration, maintenance, or your continued survival. It can live indefinitely. If you die, its current shape, gates, permissions, and other settings remain unchanged. An effect of 8th level or lower can't permanently kill the tree, seize control of it, corrupt its Heartwood, redirect its Worldgates, or overwrite your permissions.

entries.name: Multiple World Trees
entries: You can cast this spell more than once. Each casting creates a separate World Tree. If the root networks of two World Trees you created overlap, you can choose for them to recognize each other as part of the same Worldroot Network, allowing their Worldgates and living passages to be managed as one connected system.

spell.name: Raise Continent

m.text: a flawless miniature globe carved from stone worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You command the deep structure of the world and permanently create, raise, lower, or reshape a vast landmass. When you complete the casting, choose a point on natural ground or a body of water you can see. Choose one of the following transformations.

entries.name: Raise Land
entries: You create a new continuous landmass up to 100 miles across. The land can rise from an ocean, from a lake, from underground, from an existing plain, or from another natural surface capable of supporting it. You determine its coastline, elevation, mountains, valleys, plateaus, cliffs, beaches, rivers, lakes, caves, and general geological structure. The land is genuine stone, soil, sand, clay, and other ordinary geological material. It isn't magical once created.

entries.name: Reshape Land
entries: Instead of creating new land, choose an existing natural region up to 100 miles across. You can permanently reshape its geography. You can raise mountains, flatten mountains, carve valleys, create canyons, redirect rivers, create or drain natural lakes, form islands, connect islands to a mainland, separate land with channels, create natural harbors, open cave systems, or alter elevation by up to 5 miles.

entries.name: Sink the Land
entries: You can lower an area of natural terrain up to 100 miles across. You determine its final elevation. This can create inland seas, straits, enormous lakes, island chains, flooded basins, or entirely submerged regions. Water from nearby sources fills the new geography naturally where appropriate.

entries.name: Worldshaping Design
entries: You decide the final form of the affected region during the casting. The transformation occurs over 1 hour after the spell is completed. You can designate any number of creatures, structures, roads, settlements, dungeons, monuments, or other existing features to be preserved. The earth reshapes itself around preserved features rather than crushing, burying, or destroying them. You can also choose for preserved creatures and unattended objects to be carried safely with the changing terrain.

entries.name: Living Geography
entries: You can create ordinary geological deposits appropriate to the new terrain, such as common stone, clay, sand, salt, coal, iron ore, copper ore, and similar naturally occurring materials. You can't deliberately create concentrated deposits of precious metals, gemstones, magical materials, supernatural substances, or material whose primary purpose is generating wealth.

entries.name: Waterways
entries: You can establish natural watersheds as part of the transformation. You determine the initial courses of rivers, streams, lakes, aquifers, springs, and drainage basins. The spell can create ordinary fresh water sufficient to establish these systems. Afterward, they behave according to the world's normal natural laws.

entries.name: Fertile Beginning
entries: Any soil created by the spell can begin as fertile ordinary soil suitable for natural plant growth. You may also populate the reshaped land with ordinary grasses, mosses, shrubs, trees, algae, and other nonmagical plants. These plants are real and thereafter live, reproduce, and die normally. The spell doesn't create animals, sapient creatures, or supernatural organisms.

entries.name: Geological Stability
entries: You determine whether the newly shaped terrain begins geologically stable. If you choose stability, the transformation doesn't inherently cause earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions, landslides, or uncontrolled collapse. Normal geological processes can still affect the region afterward.

entries.name: Continental Authority
entries: During the 1-hour transformation, you can alter any part of your design at any time without an action. Once the transformation is complete, the new geography becomes ordinary permanent terrain and no longer depends on the spell. It can't be dispelled.

entries.name: Deep Foundation
entries: The spell reshapes the world deeply enough to support the terrain it creates. A mountain created by this spell isn't a hollow mound resting on the surface, and a new continent doesn't simply float unless you deliberately design it that way. The necessary underlying rock and geological foundation are created or displaced as part of the spell.

entries.name: Repeated Worldshaping
entries: You can cast Raise Continent repeatedly. Separate affected regions can overlap. Each new casting can further enlarge, merge, divide, elevate, submerge, or completely redesign terrain created by previous castings. There is no inherent limit to how much of a world can eventually be reshaped through repeated castings.

spell.name: Resurrection of an Age

m.text: a flawless white diamond worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You call across death itself and restore an entire host of the departed to life.
When you begin the casting, choose up to 1,000 dead creatures that meet at least one of the following conditions:

items: their remains are within range;
you know their true identity and have an object that belonged personally to them;
or you are touching a monument, tomb, archive, battlefield, settlement, or similar place strongly connected to them.

entries: There is no limit on how long the creatures have been dead.

entries.name: Return of the Dead
entries: At the end of the ritual, each chosen creature whose soul exists, is free, and is willing returns to life. Each creature returns with all its Hit Points; its original identity and memories; its class levels, Feats, proficiencies, and other learned abilities; and a complete healthy body appropriate to the age it had when it died. The spell removes all Exhaustion and ordinary diseases and poisons affecting the restored creature.

entries.name: Bodies from Nothing
entries: A corpse isn't required. If a creature's body was disintegrated, cremated, consumed, lost, reduced to dust, destroyed by time, or otherwise completely unavailable, the spell creates a new living body for it. Missing limbs and organs are restored automatically.

entries.name: No Mortal Time Limit
entries: The creature can have been dead for days, centuries, millennia, or longer. Age of death alone can never prevent this spell from restoring it.

entries.name: The Undead Returned
entries: You can choose a dead creature whose remains have become an Undead creature. If its original soul is willing and available, the Undead form is destroyed without harming the returning soul, and the original creature returns to life normally. A sapient Undead that is itself a distinct person rather than merely the remains of the original creature can't be destroyed in this way unless it willingly allows it.

entries.name: Restore the People
entries: If several chosen creatures belonged to the same destroyed settlement, culture, army, family, order, or civilization, you can cause them to appear together in safe unoccupied spaces anywhere within range. You determine how the restored creatures are distributed. The spell doesn't compel their loyalty or behavior.

entries.name: Lost Knowledge
entries: Returned creatures retain memories they genuinely possessed in life. Thus, the spell can restore forgotten languages, lost craftsmanship, extinct magical traditions, historical testimony, ancient cultural knowledge, and other information genuinely known by the restored individuals. It doesn't grant them knowledge acquired after their deaths.

entries.name: Beyond Lesser Death Magic
entries: A spell or magical effect of 8th level or lower can't prevent a soul from returning solely because too much time has passed, no corpse remains, the body was destroyed, the creature died of old age, or another resurrection spell would normally be unable to restore it. This spell doesn't overcome an Artifact or 9th-level effect that explicitly destroys, imprisons, or permanently prevents the return of a soul.

entries.name: Return from Old Age
entries: A creature that died of old age can be restored. When it returns, choose one: it returns at the physical age it had immediately before death; or its body returns at a healthy mature age appropriate to its species. This doesn't inherently make the creature immortal. It ages normally afterward.

entries.name: Greater Restoration of a People
entries: Each additional time you cast Resurrection of an Age at the same location, you can restore another 1,000 creatures. There is no inherent maximum number of creatures that can eventually be returned through repeated castings. A city that died thousands of years ago can therefore, given enough castings, quite literally live again.

spell.name: Grand Excision

m.text: a flawless silver blade and a black diamond worth at least 2,000 gp total, both of which are consumed

entries: You identify a single harmful phenomenon and cut its presence from the plane you occupy. When the ritual ends, choose one Excision Target that currently exists on the plane.

entries.name: Excision Target
entries: Choose one of the following:

items: one specific disease;
one specific poison or toxin;
one specific curse;
one specific magical affliction;
one specific parasitic organism;
one specific invasive non-sapient species;
one specific supernatural corruption;
one specific magical plague;
or another similarly identifiable harmful phenomenon.

entries: The target must be sufficiently specific to distinguish it from unrelated phenomena. For example, you could choose a particular magical plague, but not all disease; one supernatural parasite, but not all parasites; or one curse tradition, but not all curses.

entries.name: Planetary Purge
entries: Every instance of the chosen target on the plane is immediately removed from creatures, objects, structures, soil, water, air, plants, corpses, food, stored samples, magical reservoirs, and other places where it currently exists. Creatures affected by it are freed from that target without suffering harm from its removal.

entries.name: Restore the Damage
entries: When the target is removed, the spell also repairs damage caused directly by it where possible. This can restore Hit Point Maximum reduced by it, end conditions caused by it, restore damaged organs, remove mutations caused by it, cleanse contaminated soil or water, restore plants damaged by it, and reverse other direct ongoing consequences. The spell doesn't restore creatures that already died from the target.

entries.name: Eradication
entries: After the purge, the chosen phenomenon can't naturally reappear on that plane for 100 years. During this time, surviving hidden samples fail to activate, natural reproduction of the target fails, spontaneous recurrence fails, and ordinary magical effects of 8th level or lower can't recreate it.

entries.name: Deliberate Recreation
entries: A creature capable of casting 9th-level spells can deliberately recreate the excised phenomenon using appropriate magic. If successfully recreated this way, the new instance isn't automatically destroyed.

entries.name: Sapient Protection
entries: This spell can't erase a sapient species, individual person, soul, culture, language, memory, or identity. If the chosen phenomenon has become an inseparable part of a sapient creature's identity, the spell removes only the harmful portion that can be separated without destroying that creature's personhood.

entries.name: Artifact and Ninth-Level Resistance
entries: An instance protected by an Artifact or a 9th-level effect isn't automatically removed. You become aware that such protected instances exist, though not necessarily where they are.

entries.name: Permanent Cleansing
entries: Changes produced by Grand Excision are genuine. Purified water remains purified. Healed creatures remain healed. Removed parasites don't reappear merely because the spell ends. The spell itself doesn't remain active after the ritual except for the 100-year Eradication.

entries.name: Repeated Excision
entries: You can cast Grand Excision multiple times. Each casting can eradicate a different phenomenon. Given enough castings, entire worlds can be cleansed of successive plagues, curses, magical contaminations, invasive organisms, and supernatural corruptions.

spell.name: Arcane Awakening

m.text: a flawless prism saturated with magical energy worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You awaken the capacity for true magic within living creatures, permanently altering what they and their descendants can become. Choose up to 1,000 willing creatures within range when the ritual is completed. Each chosen creature undergoes an Arcane Awakening. This transformation isn't an ongoing spell effect and can't be dispelled.

entries.name: Awakened Magic
entries: Each affected creature chooses Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as its Awakened Spellcasting Ability. It learns three cantrips of its choice from any spell list, two 1st-level spells, one 2nd-level spell, and one 3rd-level spell. The creature can cast each leveled spell learned from this feature once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot. It can also cast those spells using any spell slots it possesses.

entries.name: Growing Gift
entries: The awakening develops as the creature grows in personal power.
When its Proficiency Bonus reaches the listed value, it chooses another spell:

entries.caption: Growing Gift
rows: one spell of 4th level or lower
one spell of 5th level or lower
one spell of 6th level or lower

entries: Each of these spells can be cast once per Long Rest without a spell slot. The creature doesn't need to belong to a spellcasting class to gain these benefits.

entries.name: Arcane Adaptation
entries: For every spell gained from this spell, the creature ignores any requirement for a spellcasting focus, can provide Somatic components even while its hands are occupied, and Material components without a listed cost aren't required. Costly or consumed components are still required normally.

entries.name: Choose the Expression
entries: Each creature's awakened magic can manifest differently. You may allow each creature to choose its own spells, or you may establish a common Arcane Lineage during the ritual. If you establish a lineage, you choose some or all of the spells and the Awakened Spellcasting Ability shared by creatures of that lineage.

entries.name: Hereditary Magic
entries: When completing the ritual, you decide whether the awakening is Heritable. If it is, a naturally born descendant of an awakened creature can inherit the Arcane Awakening. You determine whether inheritance is guaranteed, possible but not certain, dependent on having one or more awakened parents, or dependent on another biological or magical condition you define. Inherited awakening is a genuine trait of the descendant and isn't considered an active magical effect.

entries.name: Stable Bloodline
entries: After an awakened lineage produces naturally born descendants carrying the gift, the lineage no longer depends on this spell. Those descendants can pass the awakening to later generations according to the inheritance rules you established. An effect that dispels magic can't remove this hereditary trait.

entries.name: Magical Evolution
entries: When establishing an Arcane Lineage, you can also choose one Lineage Gift:

entries.name: Arcane Resilience
entries: Gain Resistance to one damage type associated with the lineage.

entries.name: Mage Sight
entries: Gain Darkvision 120 feet and the ability to perceive the presence of magic within 30 feet.

entries.name: Natural Focus
entries: The creature itself counts as a spellcasting focus.

entries.name: Spellguard
entries: Gain Advantage on saving throws against spells.

entries.name: Arcane Recovery
entries: Once per Long Rest, regain one expended spell use gained from Arcane Awakening.

entries.name: Mystic Movement
entries: Gain a special movement trait appropriate to the lineage, such as a 30-foot Fly, Swim, or Climb Speed, or a 30-foot teleport once per Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Living Magic
entries: Choose one of the lineage's cantrips. The creature can cast it as a Bonus Action a number of times equal to its Proficiency Bonus per Long Rest.

entries.name: No Forced Loyalty
entries: Arcane Awakening doesn't alter a creature's personality, memories, alignment, loyalties, beliefs, or free will. You grant power, not obedience.

entries.name: A New Magical People
entries: You can cast Arcane Awakening repeatedly. You can awaken additional populations, establish different magical lineages, introduce magic into a people that previously possessed none, or gradually transform an entire civilization into a naturally magical population. There is no inherent limit to how many creatures can ultimately inherit magic through descendants of those you awaken.

spell.name: Moonbirth

m.text: a flawless sphere of moonstone worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You create a new celestial body and bind it permanently to the world or plane you occupy. At the end of the ritual, a new moon appears in the sky.

entries.name: New Moon
entries: You determine the moon's apparent size, color and surface appearance, orbital path, orbital period, phases, direction of movement, and whether it is visible during day, night, or both. The moon can appear anywhere from a small distant satellite to an enormous moon dominating the night sky.

entries.name: Celestial Moon
entries: The moon is a supernatural celestial body. It has no physical mass, produces no unwanted gravitational effects, and can't be physically reached unless you permit it.

entries.name: Physical Moon
entries: The moon is a genuine physical world in orbit. You determine its diameter up to 500 miles. It possesses ordinary gravity, stone, soil, caves, mountains, plains, and other nonvaluable natural geological material. You determine whether it has an atmosphere and breathable air. The spell automatically establishes a stable orbit that doesn't catastrophically disrupt the world.

entries.name: Lunar Light
entries: The moon produces moonlight throughout every region from which it is visible. You determine whether its light is dim or bright, ordinary moonlight, supernatural moonlight, or reflected sunlight. You can cause specific creatures, regions, or effects to perceive a different intensity of moonlight.

entries.name: Tides
entries: You determine how strongly the moon influences natural tides. You can choose no tidal influence, ordinary tides, stronger or weaker tides, or different tidal patterns for different oceans. The spell establishes these cycles safely rather than producing an immediate catastrophic flood.

entries.name: Lunar Cycle
entries: You design the moon's phase cycle. It can have ordinary waxing and waning, no phases, multiple full moons during each orbit, extremely long phases, or another regular cycle you define. Effects that depend on lunar phases recognize the created moon as a genuine moon.

entries.name: Lunar Dominion
entries: While on the same plane, you can alter the moon's adjustable properties at any time without an action. You can change its visible phase, brightness, apparent color, tidal influence, orbital speed, who receives or is affected by its light, and whether it is currently visible. These changes don't destabilize its orbit.

entries.name: Lunar Blessing
entries: Choose three Lunar Blessings when you create the moon.

entries.name: Guiding Moon
entries: Creatures able to see the moon always know true north and the approximate local time.

entries.name: Dream Moon
entries: Creatures you designate gain Advantage on saving throws against magical effects that disturb sleep or dreams while sleeping beneath its light.

entries.name: Healing Moon
entries: Creatures you designate regain an additional 2 Hit Dice whenever they finish a Long Rest beneath its light.

entries.name: Veiled Moon
entries: Creatures you designate gain Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks made in its moonlight.

entries.name: Revealing Moon
entries: Invisible creatures and objects beneath its light produce a faint visible outline.

entries.name: Warding Moon
entries: Creatures you designate gain +2 AC against attacks made by Undead, Fiends, or Aberrations while beneath its light.

entries.name: Arcane Moon
entries: Once per Long Rest, a designated creature that finishes a Long Rest beneath its light can regain one expended spell slot of 3rd level or lower.

entries.name: Verdant Moon
entries: Ordinary plants exposed to its light can slowly grow even without sunlight, though they still require water and nutrients.

entries.name: Fey Moon
entries: You can cause the moonlight in selected regions to count as a suitable environment for harmless minor Fey phenomena.

entries.name: Silent Moon
entries: You can cause selected regions beneath its light to become unnaturally quiet, granting Advantage on checks made to avoid being heard.

entries.name: Lunar Gate
entries: If you created a Physical Moon, you can establish up to ten permanent Lunar Gates between locations on the moon and locations on the world below that you have personally visited. Authorized creatures can pass through them as ordinary doorways. You determine who can perceive each gate, who can use it, what can pass through, and whether each gate is currently open.

entries.name: Eternal Orbit
entries: The moon requires no Concentration, maintenance, or fuel. An effect of 8th level or lower can't permanently destroy it, remove it from orbit, seize control of it, alter its cycle, or change its properties. If you die, its current state continues permanently.

entries.name: Many Moons
entries: Each casting creates an independent moon, with no maximum number. Their orbits remain stable unless you deliberately alter them with a sufficiently powerful separate effect.

spell.name: Sky Kingdom

m.text: a flawless lodestone crown worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You sever a vast region of land from the world and raise it into the sky as a permanent floating domain. Choose a contiguous area of ground you touch up to 10 miles across and up to 1 mile deep. At the end of the ritual, the chosen landmass separates cleanly from the surrounding terrain and rises into the air.

entries.name: Floating Domain
entries: The landmass can hover at any altitude from ground level to 20 miles above the surface. It remains perfectly stable regardless of wind, storms, earthquakes, ordinary gravity, or the distribution of weight upon it. Existing structures, roads, forests, lakes, creatures, and objects within the chosen area are carried with it unharmed.

entries.name: Sovereign Movement
entries: You can command the Sky Kingdom to move. It can travel up to 200 miles per day in any horizontal direction. It can ascend or descend up to 5 miles per hour. You can start, stop, accelerate, decelerate, or change its direction at any time while on the same plane, requiring no action. Its movement never causes creatures or structures upon it to experience dangerous acceleration.

entries.name: Controlled Gravity
entries: You determine the direction and strength of gravity within the Sky Kingdom. You can maintain ordinary downward gravity regardless of the kingdom's orientation or movement. You can also designate specific regions where gravity weakens, strengthens, reverses, points toward another surface, or becomes weightless. You can change these regions at any time while on the same plane.

entries.name: Preserved Land
entries: Separating the land doesn't cause the kingdom's rivers, lakes, wells, soil, vegetation, buildings, or underground structures to collapse or spill away. Water remains naturally contained unless deliberately redirected. The exposed underside becomes stable stone rather than loose unsupported earth.

entries.name: Climate Boundary
entries: The Sky Kingdom maintains a breathable atmosphere and survivable pressure regardless of altitude. You can cause its interior climate to follow the surrounding world's weather, its original climate, or a stable climate you establish during the ritual. This doesn't create extreme damaging weather.

entries.name: Edge of the Kingdom
entries: You decide the appearance of the landmass's outer boundary. It can form sheer cliffs, sloping stone, hanging roots, waterfalls, crystalline edges, smooth walls, or another natural form. Creatures and objects aren't prevented from leaving the edge unless another effect stops them.

entries.name: Sovereign Descent
entries: You can permanently return the Sky Kingdom to the surface. Choose an unoccupied region large enough to receive it. Over 1 hour, the kingdom descends and seamlessly reconnects with the world's terrain. You can instead land it upon an ocean, forming a permanent island. Once rejoined, the land remains there normally unless this spell is cast on it again.

entries.name: Skyfall
entries: As an Action while on the same plane, you can cause the entire Sky Kingdom to descend rapidly. You determine its destination and speed. The descent can never accidentally destroy the kingdom itself or creatures you designate as protected. If you deliberately use the kingdom as a weapon, creatures and structures in the impact region are affected as the DM determines for a geological catastrophe of that scale. After the impact, you can cause the kingdom to resume hovering if enough of its structure remains intact.

entries.name: Eternal Foundation
entries: The magical principle keeping the kingdom aloft can't be permanently dispelled or suppressed by an effect of 8th level or lower. If you die, the kingdom remains where it is and continues following its last movement and climate instructions. Before the ritual ends, you can designate up to ten creatures as Regents. A Regent on the same plane can issue the same movement, gravity, climate, and landing commands you can.

entries.name: Kingdoms of the Sky
entries: Each casting creates an independent Sky Kingdom, with no maximum number. You can permanently join two you control into one floating landmass when they touch.

spell.name: Cycle of Rebirth

m.text: a flawless wheel-shaped crystal worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You establish a permanent cycle of reincarnation for a willing people, lineage, or community. When the ritual ends, choose up to 1,000 willing creatures within range. Each becomes bound to the Cycle of Rebirth. This bond is permanent, isn't an ongoing spell effect, and can't be dispelled.

entries.name: Return Through Birth
entries: When a bound creature dies and its soul is free and willing, it doesn't pass beyond reach. Instead, its soul enters the Cycle. The next time a suitable child is naturally conceived or otherwise begins life within the chosen lineage or community, the soul can choose to be reborn into that body. The reborn creature is genuinely born rather than resurrected.

entries.name: New Life
entries: A reborn creature begins life normally for its new body. It doesn't immediately regain all memories or abilities from its previous life. Instead, those return gradually as it matures.

entries.name: Returning Memory
Early Childhood
entries: It begins experiencing dreams, instincts, emotional memories, and fragments of its previous life.

entries.name: Adolescence
entries: It remembers its former identity, important relationships, languages, and major life events.

entries.name: Maturity
entries: It regains all memories, proficiencies, Feats, class levels, and learned abilities from its previous life.
The creature retains everything learned during its new life as well.

entries.name: Continuous Identity
entries: Rebirth doesn't create a duplicate soul. The reborn creature is the same person continuing through a new life. Its personality can still change through new experiences, upbringing, and choices.

entries.name: New Body
entries: The creature uses the species, ancestry, Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, natural traits, and other physical properties of its new body. It retains its restored Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, class levels, Feats, proficiencies, languages, and learned abilities. If an old feature depended on anatomy the new body doesn't possess, it functions only if the new body can reasonably support it.

entries.name: Choice of Return
entries: A soul is never forced to reincarnate. It can enter the next suitable birth, wait for a later one, permanently leave the Cycle, or accept another resurrection effect instead. If restored to life by another effect before reincarnating, it leaves the waiting state but remains bound to the Cycle for future deaths.

entries.name: The Waiting Souls
entries: You and creatures you designate can communicate with souls waiting within the Cycle while on the same plane. Waiting souls remain conscious in a dreamlike state and can communicate telepathically, but can't normally affect the physical world.

entries.name: Lineage Rules
entries: When establishing the Cycle, you define what counts as a suitable rebirth. This can be based on descendants of the original participants, membership in a particular species, a family or bloodline, citizens of a particular community, members of an order, or another clearly defined group. A creature must still be born normally into a physically viable body.

entries.name: Hereditary Cycle
entries: You can choose for naturally born descendants of bound creatures to become bound to the Cycle automatically. If you do, the Cycle can persist indefinitely through generations. A descendant can willingly reject the bond upon reaching maturity.

entries.name: No Soul Theft
entries: A returning soul can't displace or overwrite another soul. If a developing body already possesses another soul, it isn't a valid vessel for reincarnation. The Cycle waits for another suitable birth instead.

entries.name: Beyond Lesser Death Magic
entries: An effect of 8th level or lower can't permanently sever a willing soul from the Cycle, force it into an unwanted rebirth, erase its accumulated past-life memories, or prevent it from entering a valid future birth solely because too much time has passed. Artifacts and 9th-level effects can interfere according to their own capabilities.

entries.name: Eternal Cycle
entries: The Cycle persists without Concentration, maintenance, or your survival. Bound souls can reincarnate, wait between lives, and continue through generations without limit.

spell.name: Godseed

m.text: a flawless divine seed worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed

entries: You kindle a new divine consciousness and release it into existence. At the end of the ritual, a Nascent Deity is born. It is a genuine sapient divine being with its own soul, personality, will, and identity. It isn't summoned, controlled, or owned by you.

entries.name: Divine Identity
entries: When creating the deity, you determine its initial name, appearance, holy symbol, voice, general temperament, and up to three Divine Aspects. Examples of Divine Aspects include Fire, Knowledge, Death, Life, War, Sea, Night, Craft, Travel, Dreams, Justice, Magic, Storms, Secrets, or another broad concept. These establish what kinds of divine power the deity naturally understands and influences.

entries.name: Nascent Divinity
entries: The deity begins as a Lesser Deity rather than a mortal creature. It doesn't require food, water, air, sleep, or ordinary biological survival. It doesn't age and can't die from natural causes. Its true divine essence isn't a normal physical body. It can create or dismiss a physical manifestation of itself as an Action.

entries.name: Divine Manifestation
entries: When physically manifested, use the following statistics unless the DM chooses to create a more detailed stat block:

items: AC 22
400 Hit Points
Speed 40 ft., Fly 80 ft. (Hover)
Proficiency Bonus +6
Saving Throws: +12 to all
Truesight 120 ft.
Resistance to all damage
Immunity to Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned, and disease

entries: Its Ability Scores are: 24, 20, 24, 24, 26, 26. If its manifestation is reduced to 0 Hit Points, the manifestation disappears rather than the deity dying. It can manifest again after 24 hours.

entries.name: Divine Magic
entries: The deity can cast spells without material components unless those components are consumed or have a listed cost. It can cast cantrips at will; spells of 1st–5th level at will; spells of 6th–8th level once each per Long Rest; and one 9th-level spell once per 7 days. Its available spells should suit its Divine Aspects. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma, with spell save DC 22 and +14 to spell attacks.

entries.name: Miracles
entries: Once per Long Rest, the deity can perform one Miracle related to one of its Divine Aspects. A Miracle can produce an effect comparable in scale to an 8th-level spell or lower without requiring that exact spell to exist. A Miracle can't duplicate another 9th-level spell.

entries.name: Grant Divine Power
entries: The deity can willingly empower worshipers, priests, champions, or other followers. A willing creature recognized by the deity can use the deity as a legitimate source of Cleric magic, divine rituals, holy symbols, religious magic, and other features that require a divine patron or divine source. The spell itself doesn't grant class levels.

entries.name: Divine Boons
entries: The deity can maintain up to 100 Divine Boons at one time.
A creature can receive one boon chosen by the deity:

entries.name: Blessed Body
entries: Increase Hit Point Maximum by 20.

entries.name: Sacred Resistance
entries: Gain Resistance to one damage type related to the deity.

entries.name: Divine Sight
entries: Gain Darkvision 120 feet or Truesight 30 feet.

entries.name: Sacred Gift
entries: Learn one cantrip and one 1st-level spell thematically related to the deity. The spell can be cast once per Long Rest without a spell slot.

entries.name: Chosen Voice
entries: Communicate telepathically with the deity while on the same plane.

entries.name: Death's Favor
entries: Gain Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
A deity can revoke or change one of its granted Boons at any time.

entries.name: Hear Prayer
entries: The deity can hear a prayer deliberately directed toward it from anywhere on the same plane. It doesn't automatically hear every spoken mention of its name. It can choose to answer telepathically.

entries.name: Divine Realm
entries: The deity can designate one location it willingly inhabits as its Sanctum. While within its Sanctum, it always knows when a creature enters or leaves and can perceive any point within it. The Sanctum can occupy an area up to 1 mile across. If the deity later acquires or creates a plane of its own, it can designate that plane as its divine realm instead.

entries.name: Faith and Growth
entries: The deity can grow through worship, extraordinary deeds, divine power, or other setting-appropriate means. This spell places no limit on its eventual growth.

entries.name: True Divinity
entries: The Nascent Deity isn't an ongoing spell effect. It can't be dispelled. Its existence continues even if you die. An effect of 8th level or lower can't erase its divine essence, strip away its divinity, permanently destroy it, or force it to obey another creature. Destroying the deity permanently requires an Artifact, an appropriate 9th-level effect, the destruction of its divine essence by another deity, or another comparably powerful means.

entries.name: Many Gods
entries: Each casting creates a separate deity with no inherent loyalty to you or other deities.

spell.name: Sovereign Possession
entries: You abandon your physical presence and force your entire existence into another creature, taking complete command of its body while retaining everything that was yours. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must make a Charisma saving throw. A willing creature can choose to fail this saving throw. On a failed save, you permanently possess the target. The possession isn't an ongoing spell effect and requires no Concentration.

entries.name: Total Transfer
entries: Your original body and all worn or carried objects disappear into the host, including containers and their contents. They remain intact within your transferred existence. Objects you couldn't normally carry aren't transferred.

entries.name: Sovereign Control
entries: You have complete control over the host's body. You determine its Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, movement, speech, spellcasting, and other voluntary activity. The host remains conscious and aware of its surroundings and everything you do through its body, but it can't control its body unless you allow it. You and the host can communicate telepathically with one another at any time. You can voluntarily allow the host to control any or all of its body and can reclaim control at any time without an action.

entries.name: Your Identity
entries: Possession doesn't replace or alter your identity. You retain all of your own memories, personality, alignment if used, Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, languages, proficiencies, Expertise, Feats, class levels, subclass features, spellcasting, Pact Magic, prepared and known spells, class resources, supernatural abilities, and other traits or features you possessed before entering the host. Your consciousness remains distinct from the host's.

entries.name: Complete Access
entries: While possessing the host, you can also use all statistics, traits, features, abilities, and resources belonging to the host as though you were the host.

This includes, but isn't limited to, its Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Hit Points, Hit Dice, Armor Class, Speeds, Size, senses, creature type, species traits, natural weapons, damage Resistances and Immunities, condition Immunities, regeneration, innate abilities, Innate Spellcasting, Spellcasting, Pact Magic, class levels, subclass features, Feats, proficiencies, Expertise, Fighting Styles, Maneuvers, Rage, Sneak Attack, Channel Divinity, Wild Shape, Metamagic, Sorcery Points, Ki or Focus Points, spell slots, prepared spells, known spells, Recharge abilities, Legendary Actions, Legendary Resistance, Mythic traits, Lair Actions, supernatural abilities, and any other feature or resource the host legitimately possesses.
A Lair Action still requires the host to be in a location where that Lair Action could normally function. You retain all of your own abilities while gaining access to the host's abilities.

entries.name: Dual Repertoire
entries: Your abilities and the host's remain distinct. Use your statistics for your features and the host's statistics for its features, including spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus.

entries.name: Separate Resources
entries: Your resources and the host's remain separate unless a feature states otherwise. Track each creature's spell slots, Sorcery Points, Hit Dice, limited uses, Recharge abilities, and other resources separately; expending one creature's resource doesn't expend the other's.

entries.name: Absolute Compatibility
entries: You can use the host's features regardless of your own species, class, subclass, level, Ability Scores, Feats, alignment, or similar prerequisites. The host must still possess any anatomy a feature requires.

entries.name: Host Knowledge
entries: You can freely access the host's memories and learned knowledge, including information needed to use its abilities. Its memories remain distinguishable from yours and don't overwrite your personality, beliefs, or identity.

entries.name: Carried Arsenal
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can manifest one or more objects that were transferred with you. A manifested object appears worn, equipped, held, or in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the host, as appropriate. You can dismiss any transferred object back into your possession state at any time without an action. Transferred objects retain their magical properties, charges, attunement, curses, remaining uses, and other existing states.

entries.name: Equipment Adaptation
entries: Transferred clothing, armor, and other wearable equipment can temporarily alter their size and shape to fit the host's anatomy. This adaptation doesn't change an item's statistics or magical properties. If an item fundamentally can't function with the host's anatomy, it can instead manifest in an unoccupied space within 5 feet. When the possession ends, every surviving transferred item returns to its normal form.

entries.name: Attunement
entries: You retain your existing attunements while possessing the host. The host also retains its own attunements. You can use a magic item attuned to the host as though you were the host. Your attuned items remain attuned to you. Possessing a creature doesn't automatically allow you to attune additional items beyond whatever limits normally apply separately to you or the host.

entries.name: Host Body
entries: Damage dealt to the host reduces the host's Hit Points. Healing applied to the host restores the host's Hit Points. Your original body's Hit Points aren't reduced merely because the host takes damage. Effects targeting the body you currently occupy affect the host unless they specifically target your soul, mind, consciousness, or another part of your transferred existence.

entries.name: Effects on You
entries: Effects that specifically target your soul, mind, consciousness, identity, or your own magical resources can still affect you while you are inside the host if they are capable of reaching you. The host and you remain separate creatures for determining which personal resources, memories, souls, and identities belong to each of you.

entries.name: Permanent Occupation
entries: The possession has no time limit. The host receives no additional saving throws after failing the initial saving throw. An effect of 8th level or lower can't dispel the possession, suppress it, force you out, sever you from the host, take control of the host away from you, separate you from your transferred equipment, or transfer your soul elsewhere against your will. An Artifact or appropriate 9th-level effect can attempt to interfere with the possession according to its own rules.

entries.name: Competing Possession
entries: While you possess the host, an effect of 8th level or lower can't allow another creature to possess or take direct control of that host unless you willingly permit it. If another 9th-level effect or an Artifact attempts to take control of the host, resolve the conflict according to the effects involved.

entries.name: Voluntary Departure
entries: At any time, requiring no action, you can end the possession. Choose an unoccupied space within 10 feet of the host. Your original body and all transferred possessions immediately reform in that space. Your original body returns with the Hit Points and physical state it had when you entered the host, modified by any effects that actually affected your original existence during the possession. Resources you spent while possessing the host remain spent.

entries.name: Transfer Between Hosts
entries: While possessing a creature, you can cast Sovereign Possession again. Choose a new creature normally. If the new target fails its Charisma saving throw, you transfer directly from the current host into the new host. Your original body doesn't reappear between transfers. All objects still stored within your transferred existence move with you. The previous host immediately regains full control of its body.

entries.name: Host Death
entries: If the host dies, the possession ends immediately. Your original body and all transferred possessions reform in the nearest suitable unoccupied space within 10 feet of the host's remains. You don't die merely because the host dies. The death of the host doesn't restore resources you expended during the possession.

entries.name: Destruction of the Host
entries: If the host is completely destroyed, disintegrated, reduced to ash, erased physically, or otherwise leaves no usable corpse, you are still expelled normally. Your body reforms in the nearest suitable unoccupied space to the location where the host was destroyed.

entries.name: Soul of the Host
entries: Possession doesn't destroy, consume, copy, or merge with the host's soul. The host remains the same individual throughout the possession. If the host dies, its soul departs normally unless another effect prevents it. You gain access to the host's abilities and memories, but they don't become permanently yours after you leave the host.

entries.name: Willing Host
entries: You can share control with a willing host, allowing any of its voluntary activities or full control for as long as you choose. You can reclaim control at any time without an action.

entries.name: End of Possession
entries: When the possession ends for any reason, you return to your original body; the host regains exclusive control of its body if alive; your transferred possessions return with you unless they were manifested and left behind, destroyed, consumed, or otherwise lost; you lose access to the host's statistics, memories, features, abilities, and resources; and both creatures retain all genuine changes and resources expended during the possession. The possession itself doesn't erase memories of what occurred.

spell.name: Sovereign Fusion
entries: You fuse yourself with one willing creature you touch, creating a single permanent being that contains both of you. The fusion is immediate, permanent, and isn't an ongoing spell effect.

entries.name: One Body
entries: Choose which participant's body becomes the Primary Form, or create a blended form combining physical traits from both creatures. The fused being uses the better Strength score of the two; the better Dexterity score; the better Constitution score; the better Armor Class; the better Speed of each movement type; all senses possessed by either creature; all natural weapons and biological traits possessed by either creature; and the larger Hit Point Maximum of the two, plus half the other creature's Hit Point Maximum.
Its Size can be either participant's Size or any Size between them that is physically reasonable.

entries.name: Unified Mind
entries: The fused being retains all memories, personalities, languages, proficiencies, Expertise, Feats, class levels, subclass features, spellcasting, Pact Magic, learned abilities, and supernatural abilities of both participants. Both sets of memories remain distinguishable. The fusion can think with both perspectives simultaneously.

entries.name: Shared Identity
entries: When the fusion is created, choose one of the following:

entries.name: Dominant Identity
entries: One participant becomes the primary personality, while the other remains fully conscious and can communicate internally.

entries.name: Dual Identity
entries: Both personalities share control equally and can freely communicate internally.

entries.name: Unified Identity
entries: The two personalities permanently merge into a new single personality that inherits the memories, values, and emotional history of both.
This choice is permanent unless altered by an appropriate 9th-level effect.

entries.name: Complete Ability Access
entries: The fused being can use all features, abilities, spells, resources, traits, and special actions possessed by either participant. This includes spell slots, Sorcery Points, Ki or Focus Points, Rage, Wild Shape, Channel Divinity, Action Surge, Sneak Attack, Fighting Styles, Maneuvers, Metamagic, Legendary Actions, Legendary Resistance, Mythic traits, Recharge abilities, Lair Actions where appropriate, Innate Spellcasting, and any other feature either participant legitimately possessed.

entries.name: Separate Resources
entries: Each participant's resources, including spell slots, limited uses, Sorcery Points, and Hit Dice, remain separate unless both abilities explicitly share a pool. Expending one pool doesn't expend the other.

entries.name: Dual Spellcasting
entries: The fusion can cast spells known or prepared by either participant. When it casts a spell from one participant's spellcasting feature, use that participant's spellcasting ability, spell save DC, spell attack bonus, known or prepared spells, and spell slots.

entries.name: Combined Defenses
entries: The fused being gains all damage Resistances, damage Immunities, condition Immunities, saving throw proficiencies, Magic Resistance, regeneration, and other defensive traits possessed by either participant. If both creatures possess the same Resistance, it becomes Immunity. If one already has Immunity, it remains Immunity.

entries.name: Combined Equipment
entries: All equipment worn or carried by either participant remains available to the fused being. Equipment can resize or reshape to fit the fused body's anatomy without changing its statistics. The fused being retains all existing attunements from both participants.

entries.name: Absolute Compatibility
entries: The fused being can use a feature from either participant even if the other participant wouldn't normally meet that feature's prerequisites. A feature still requires whatever physical anatomy or environmental condition it normally needs.

entries.name: Death and Separation
entries: If the fused being dies, both participants die. A resurrection effect that restores the fused being restores the fusion rather than only one participant unless the effect specifically separates them.

entries.name: Voluntary Separation
entries: At any time, the fused being can willingly end the fusion during a 1-hour ritual requiring no spell slot. Both original creatures reappear in adjacent unoccupied spaces. Each returns with its own memories, its own abilities, its own equipment, and the resources it personally had remaining within the fusion. Damage suffered by the fusion is divided between the two as evenly as possible when separation occurs.

entries.name: Forced Separation
entries: An effect of 8th level or lower can't forcibly separate the fusion. An Artifact or appropriate 9th-level effect can attempt to do so.

entries.name: Repeated Fusion
entries: Repeated castings can add one willing creature at a time to the fusion, with no maximum number. Each adds its memories, abilities, features, resources, and compatible physical traits.

spell.name: Sovereign Metamorphosis
entries: You gain absolute authority over your own physical form, allowing you to permanently assume and combine the forms of creatures you have studied. When you cast this spell, choose one creature you can see or one creature whose form you have previously Recorded with this spell. You transform into that creature. This transformation is permanent, requires no Concentration, and isn't an ongoing spell effect.

entries.name: Complete Transformation
entries: Your body becomes a true version of the chosen creature's form. You gain all of its Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Hit Points, Hit Dice, Armor Class, Size, Speeds, senses, creature type, natural weapons, Resistances and Immunities, condition Immunities, regeneration, innate traits, supernatural abilities, Innate Spellcasting, Spellcasting, Recharge abilities, Legendary Actions, Legendary Resistance, Mythic traits, and other abilities intrinsic to that form.

You retain all of your own Intelligence, Wisdom, Charisma, memories, personality, languages, proficiencies, Feats, class levels, subclass features, spellcasting, Pact Magic, class resources, and learned abilities.

entries.name: Recorded Forms
entries: Whenever you can see a creature within 120 feet for at least 1 minute, you can Record its form, requiring no action. You can also Record a creature by touching its corpse for 1 minute. A Recorded Form permanently remains available to you. There is no limit to the number of forms you can Record.

entries.name: Assume Form
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can assume any Recorded Form or return to your original form. Each form lasts indefinitely.

entries.name: Equipment
entries: Whenever you transform, choose for each object you are wearing or carrying to remain equipped, resize and reshape to fit the new form, merge harmlessly into your body, or appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet. Merged equipment remains available to you and can be manifested or merged again at any time without an action. Magic items retain their properties and attunement.

entries.name: Retained Power
entries: Your own abilities function in every form unless physically impossible. For example, you can still cast your Wizard spells while transformed into a Dragon, provided you can supply the required components. If a form lacks hands, speech, or another physical requirement, you can still satisfy Somatic and Verbal components through the transformed body's equivalent anatomy.

entries.name: Form Resources
entries: Each Recorded Form retains its own limited-use resources. If you use a form's Legendary Resistance, Recharge ability, spell slot, limited-use feature, or similar resource, that resource remains expended if you leave and later return to that form. Resources recover according to that form's normal rules. Changing forms doesn't refresh them.

entries.name: Hybrid Form
entries: You don't need to copy a Recorded Form exactly. As a Bonus Action, you can create a Hybrid Form based on your current form. Choose up to five physical or intrinsic traits from other Recorded Forms and add them to the current form. Examples include wings and a Fly Speed, a Dragon's Breath Weapon, regeneration, natural armor, additional limbs, a Burrow Speed, Truesight, Amphibious, a damage Immunity, a supernatural movement ability, or another bodily or innate trait. You can change your chosen Hybrid Traits whenever you transform.

entries.name: Perfect Anatomy
entries: Your transformed anatomy adapts to support all selected traits together, without natural weapons interfering with spellcasting or biological structures conflicting.

entries.name: Greater Hybridization
entries: If two Recorded Forms possess different values for the same physical statistic, you may use whichever value you choose. This includes Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Armor Class, Speed, senses, Size, and natural weapon damage. However, choosing a statistic from another form counts as one of your five Hybrid Traits.

entries.name: Identity Beyond Form
entries: No transformation changes your identity or soul. Effects that identify you by soul, true identity, or similar fundamental qualities recognize you regardless of your current body. Your transformations don't create duplicate souls or separate creatures.

entries.name: Death and Form
entries: If a transformed body is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you don't automatically revert. You remain in that form and resolve death normally using that body's statistics. If you are later restored to life, you can return in your original body or any Recorded Form of your choice.

entries.name: Absolute Metamorphosis
entries: An effect of 8th level or lower can't force you into another form, prevent you from transforming, permanently suppress a Recorded Form, erase a Recorded Form from you, or trap you permanently in one body. An Artifact or appropriate 9th-level effect can interfere normally.

entries.name: Endless Evolution
entries: You can Record new forms without limit, regardless of species, creature type, Size, or anatomy, provided the creature exists and you observe it as required.

spell.name: Sovereign Existence
entries: You establish absolute authority over your own existence. From this moment onward, no external force can alter your body, mind, soul, position, identity, or state without your consent, except as described by this spell. This effect is permanent, requires no Concentration, and isn't an ongoing spell effect.

entries.name: Absolute Consent
entries: Whenever an effect would affect you in a way specifically covered by one of this spell's features, you can choose whether that effect is allowed to affect you. This decision requires no action and can be made even if you are Incapacitated, Unconscious, Stunned, Paralyzed, Petrified, dead, outside time, or otherwise unable to act. If you refuse an effect under a feature of this spell, that feature resolves the interaction as described.

entries.name: Sovereign Body
entries: You can refuse any effect that would transform you, age you, alter your Size, modify your anatomy, reduce your Hit Point Maximum, remove or alter your limbs or organs, change your species, alter your creature type, modify your physical Ability Scores, or otherwise forcibly change your body. You can still willingly accept any such effect.

entries.name: Sovereign Mind
entries: You can refuse any effect that would Charm you, Frighten you, dominate you, control your actions, alter your emotions, read your thoughts, erase or alter your memories, implant memories, change your personality, compel speech or behavior, or otherwise interfere with your mind.

entries.name: Sovereign Soul
entries: Your soul can't be trapped, consumed, destroyed, divided, replaced, exchanged, copied, bound, possessed, forcibly reincarnated, or removed from your body unless you allow it. If an effect would normally affect both your body and soul, you can permit one portion while refusing the other.

entries.name: Sovereign Position
entries: You can refuse any effect that would teleport you, banish you, move you to another plane, forcibly move you, knock you Prone, grapple or restrain you through magical force, pull or push you, imprison you in an extradimensional space, or otherwise change your location against your will. You can permit individual instances of movement normally.

entries.name: Sovereign Time
entries: You remain aware during effects that alter or suspend time. You can refuse any effect that would stop your personal time, accelerate or reverse your age, remove you from the normal flow of time, trap you in temporal stasis, rewind your personal state, erase actions you have already taken, or replace you with an earlier or later version of yourself. If time is stopped for other creatures, you can continue acting normally.

entries.name: Sovereign Magic
entries: When you are affected by a spell or magical effect, you can invoke your sovereignty to resist it. You can use this feature three times per Long Rest.
When you do, choose one of the following:

items: automatically succeed on one saving throw against that spell or magical effect;
gain Resistance to all damage dealt to you by that effect until the end of the current turn;
or ignore one condition, forced movement, transformation, or other non-damaging effect it would impose on you.

entries: If the effect has multiple different consequences, you protect yourself from only the consequence you choose. An effect of 8th level or lower can't prevent you from using this feature.

entries.name: Selective Harm
entries: Your sovereign nature allows you to reject the worst of incoming harm, but not indefinitely. Once per turn, when you take damage, you can reduce that damage by {@damage 5d12} + your character level. No action is required. If this reduces the damage to 0, you suffer no secondary effect that occurs only because that damage was dealt. In addition, once per Long Rest, when you would take damage from a single source, you can instead reduce that instance of damage to 0.
This protection doesn't restore Hit Points or prevent costs you willingly pay with your own Hit Points.

entries.name: Conditions
entries: Whenever you would gain a condition, you can refuse it. You can also end any condition currently affecting you at any time without an action.

entries.name: Self-Definition
entries: At any time, requiring no action, you can restore yourself to a state you personally consider your true form. This can restore your normal appearance, missing limbs or organs, your original Size, your natural anatomy, your original creature type, your normal Ability Scores, and other aspects of your body that were altered against your wishes. This doesn't restore expended spell slots, class resources, magic item charges, or other limited-use resources.

entries.name: Absolute Identity
entries: No effect can make another creature become you, replace your identity, or cause you to cease being yourself unless you willingly allow it. Copies, clones, simulacra, shapeshifters, or transformed creatures can resemble you, but effects that distinguish true identity recognize you as the original individual.

entries.name: Death Is Still a Choice
entries: When you would die, you can choose whether death is allowed to occur. If you refuse, you instead remain alive at 1 Hit Point. Once you refuse death this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest. If you allow yourself to die, Sovereign Existence remains part of you. While dead, your soul retains the protections of this spell, and you decide whether any resurrection, reincarnation, possession, soul-binding, or similar effect can affect you.

entries.name: Ninth-Level Conflict
entries: Effects of 8th level or lower can't override your choices under this spell. If an Artifact or another 9th-level effect directly contradicts Sovereign Existence, you still make any saving throw normally required by that effect. On a success, your sovereignty prevails completely. On a failure, the opposing effect functions normally only for that specific interaction.

entries.name: Chosen Vulnerability
entries: You can voluntarily allow yourself to be affected by anything this spell could prevent. You can make that choice for one instance, for one creature, for one spell, for one type of effect, or indefinitely. You can revoke that permission at any time without an action.

spell.name: Regalia of Ascendance

m.text: a masterwork wearable item and rare magical materials worth 5,000 gp, which the spell consumes

entries: You transform a masterwork wearable object into a supreme magical regalia designed to elevate its bearer beyond mortal limits. Choose one wearable object, such as a crown, helm, mask, mantle, cloak, robe, armor, gauntlets, boots, belt, amulet, ring, bracers, or similar worn item. The item becomes a permanent Artifact. While worn and attuned, the Regalia reshapes itself to fit the bearer perfectly.

entries.name: Ascendant Frame
entries: While wearing the Regalia, your Hit Point Maximum increases by 50, your AC increases by 2, your walking Speed increases by 10 feet, and you have Advantage on Death Saving Throws.

entries.name: Perfect Bearing
entries: Choose one Ability Score when the Regalia is created. While wearing it, that score increases by 4, to a maximum of 30. The Regalia can be created with this feature multiple times only if specifically allowed by another property.

entries.name: Sovereign Presence
entries: You have Advantage on Charisma checks, you are immune to the Frightened condition, and creatures of your choice within 30 feet have Advantage on saving throws against being Frightened or Charmed. As a Bonus Action, you can intensify the aura for 1 minute. During that time, hostile creatures that start their turn within 30 feet must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or become Frightened of you until the start of their next turn. Once activated, this intensified aura can't be used again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Living Ward
entries: At the start of each of your turns, if you have at least 1 Hit Point, you regain 10 Hit Points. This regeneration doesn't function for 1 round after you take damage from an Artifact or a 9th-level spell.

entries.name: Chosen Immunity
entries: When the Regalia is created, choose one damage type. While wearing it, you are immune to that damage type. Choose one additional damage type. You have Resistance to that type.

entries.name: Perfect Motion
entries: While wearing the Regalia, Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement, your movement can't be reduced below half your normal Speed by an effect of 8th level or lower, and you can stand from Prone without spending movement. If the Regalia is appropriate to flight, levitation, or supernatural movement, you also gain a Fly Speed equal to your walking Speed and can hover.

entries.name: Untouchable Form
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects. In addition, once per Long Rest, when you fail a saving throw, you can succeed instead.

entries.name: Regalia Manifestation
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can change the Regalia's appearance, including its apparent materials, ornamentation, glow, symbols, and silhouette, without changing its statistics.

entries.name: Armored Soul
entries: While wearing the Regalia, your soul can't be possessed, trapped, removed, replaced, consumed, or forcibly transferred by an effect of 8th level or lower.

entries.name: Majesty Unbound
entries: Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can enter an exalted state for 1 minute. While in this state, your Speed increases by 20 feet, you gain Resistance to all damage, you can't be Charmed or Frightened, you gain a Fly Speed of 60 feet and can hover, your attacks and damaging spells deal an additional {@damage 2d12} Force or Radiant damage once per turn, and at the start of each of your turns you regain 20 Hit Points if you have at least 1 Hit Point.

entries.name: Last Vestment
entries: If you die while wearing the Regalia, your body and the Regalia remain linked. The Regalia can't be forcibly removed from your corpse by an effect of 8th level or lower unless you allowed it before death. Once every 7 days, if your soul is willing and free, the Regalia can restore you to life at dawn with full Hit Points, all missing body parts restored, and the Regalia already worn and attuned.

entries.name: Bound to the Bearer
entries: When the Regalia is created, choose one of the following:

entries.name: Open Regalia
entries: Any creature meeting its Attunement requirements can use it.

entries.name: Chosen Regalia
entries: Only creatures specifically designated by the creator can Attune to it.

entries.name: Bloodbound Regalia
entries: Only members of a chosen lineage can Attune to it.

entries.name: Soulbound Regalia
entries: It can be Attuned only by one specific individual.
If the Regalia is Soulbound, no creature can break that Attunement by force unless using an Artifact or appropriate 9th-level effect.

entries.name: Indestructible Vestment
entries: Ordinary damage can't destroy the Regalia. An effect of 8th level or lower can't permanently destroy it, disenchant it, erase it, or suppress all of its powers. When the Regalia is created, define one extraordinary Method of Destruction capable of permanently destroying it.

entries.name: Legacy of the Regalia
entries: The Regalia can gain powers, forms, or symbolic meaning through extraordinary events, with no inherent limit to its growth.

spell.name: Worldbreaker
entries: You gather destructive power into a single point and unleash a strike capable of breaking creatures, fortifications, and the land beneath them. Choose a point you can see within range. A column of annihilating force crashes down at that point.

entries.name: Worldbreaking Impact
entries: Each creature in a 60-foot-radius, 200-foot-high cylinder centered on that point must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 30d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. This damage ignores Resistance to Force damage. A creature immune to Force damage instead has Resistance to this damage.

entries.name: Direct Hit
entries: Choose one creature or object within 10 feet of the center of the impact. That target is struck by the heart of the attack. It makes its saving throw with Disadvantage and takes an additional {@damage 20d12} Force damage on a failed save, or half as much additional damage on a successful one. The additional damage also ignores Resistance, and Immunity functions as Resistance.

entries.name: Break the Unbreakable
entries: Damage from this spell ignores Resistance granted by spells of 8th level or lower, damage reduction from spells of 8th level or lower, temporary immunity granted by spells of 8th level or lower, and magical effects of 8th level or lower that would reduce the damage to 0. This spell can damage creatures and objects that are normally incorporeal, Ethereal, immune to ordinary physical interaction, or protected by magical barriers. It doesn't automatically bypass total cover unless that cover is destroyed by the spell.

entries.name: Structural Annihilation
entries: Objects and structures automatically fail their saving throws and take maximum damage from this spell. The spell deals double damage to buildings, walls, fortifications, vehicles, siege engines, magical structures, and Constructs. A non-Artifact object reduced to 0 Hit Points by this spell is completely destroyed.

entries.name: Shattering Wave
entries: After the initial impact, destructive force erupts outward. Each creature of your choice within 300 feet of the impact point must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is pushed up to 100 feet directly away from the center, knocked Prone, and takes {@damage 8d12} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't pushed or knocked Prone.

entries.name: Broken Ground
entries: The ground in the initial 60-foot-radius area is devastated. Choose the resulting shape of the destruction, such as a crater, shattered terrain, a deep fissure, a field of pulverized stone, or another physically reasonable result. The affected ground becomes Difficult Terrain. You can create a crater or fissure up to 100 feet deep. Structures unsupported by the resulting terrain can collapse normally.

entries.name: Irresistible Impact
entries: A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by Worldbreaker can't use a Reaction or feature triggered specifically by being reduced to 0 Hit Points to immediately move, teleport, or avoid falling Unconscious unless that feature comes from an Artifact, a 9th-level spell, or a feature of comparable power.
