entries: For each spell slot level above 4, Living Lightning damage increases by {@scaledamage 4d8|4-9|1d8}, and Stormcharged Strikes damage increases by {@scaledamage 2d8|4-9|1d8}.

spell.name: Unhouse the Soul

components.m: a cracked mirror

entries: You pull a pale spirit from its shadow, leaving a silver thread between silent flesh and struggling soul.

Choose one creature you can see within range. Constructs and Undead are unaffected. The target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, its spirit is expelled into an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of it. Its body falls {@condition prone|XPHB|Prone} and has the {@condition paralyzed|XPHB|Paralyzed} condition for the duration.

entries.name: Divided Existence
entries: The target controls its spirit while its body remains motionless. The spirit uses the target's statistics and shares its Hit Points and ongoing effects, but has a Fly Speed of 30 feet and can hover. Conditions affecting the target apply to both forms, except that the {@condition prone|XPHB|Prone} and {@condition paralyzed|XPHB|Paralyzed} conditions imposed by this spell apply only to its body.

The spirit has the {@condition incapacitated|XPHB|Incapacitated} condition. It can't attack, cast spells, manipulate objects, or take Reactions. It can move and can take only the action described in Return to Flesh, despite its {@condition incapacitated|XPHB|Incapacitated} condition. The target's Concentration ends when it fails the initial saving throw. The spirit can pass through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, but can't willingly end its turn inside an object or move more than 120 feet from its body.

entries.name: Exposed Vessel
entries: The body has Vulnerability to Necrotic damage. The body and spirit can both be targeted, and damage dealt to either reduces the target's Hit Points. If the same effect would damage both forms simultaneously, apply only the higher damage amount after accounting for each form's defenses.

entries.name: Soul Leash
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can move the spirit up to 30 feet in a direction you choose without a saving throw. You must see the spirit within 90 feet of yourself. This movement can pass through creatures and objects, doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks, and must end in an unoccupied space within 120 feet of its body.

entries.name: Return to Flesh
entries: While within 5 feet of its body, the spirit can take an action to repeat the Charisma saving throw, ending the spell on a success. Taking damage doesn't grant an additional saving throw against this spell. When the spell ends, the spirit immediately returns to its body. The {@condition paralyzed|XPHB|Paralyzed} and {@condition incapacitated|XPHB|Incapacitated} conditions imposed by this spell end.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can target one additional creature for each spell slot level above 4. When you use Soul Leash, you can move any number of spirits affected by this spell that meet its requirements.

spell.name: Theft of Nature
entries: You tear a thread from another creature's nature, claiming its movement, senses, or resilience.

Choose one creature you can see within range. You learn which of the properties listed below it possesses, including their types and numerical values. Choose one of those properties. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you steal the chosen property for the duration:

entries.name: Movement
entries: Choose the target's Climb, Fly, or Swim Speed. The target loses that speed, and you gain it, including the ability to hover if applicable. If you already have that type of speed, use whichever is higher. A target that loses its Fly Speed falls unless another effect holds it aloft.

entries.name: Senses
entries: Choose the target's Blindsight, Darkvision, Tremorsense, or Truesight. The target loses that sense, and you gain it with the same range and any associated limitations.

entries.name: Resistance
entries: Choose one damage type to which the target has Resistance. The target loses that Resistance, and you gain Resistance to that damage type.

You can use a stolen property without possessing the target's anatomy. This spell can't steal a property granted by an Artifact or a spell of level 5 or higher. At the end of each of its turns, the target repeats the Constitution saving throw, ending the spell on a success. When the spell ends, the stolen property returns to the target, and you lose the benefit granted by this spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can steal one additional eligible property from the same target for each spell slot level above 4. A single saving throw determines whether all chosen properties are stolen.

spell.name: Hands of the Colossus
entries: Two enormous hands unfold from pale light, their fingers flexing at your command. You summon them in unoccupied spaces you can see within range. Each uses the Colossal Hand stat block for the spell slot expended and lasts for the duration, disappearing if reduced to 0 Hit Points.

entries.name: Paired Command
entries: When you cast the spell and as a Bonus Action on subsequent turns, you can command both hands. Each can move up to 60 feet and take one action from its stat block, including Multiattack. You can move each hand before or after its action, or split its movement between both.

The hands act independently and can use the same action or different actions against the same target or different targets. Both can use Multiattack as part of the same command, making a separate attack roll for each Slam. Each hand must remain within 120 feet of you. Neither hand has a turn of its own or can take Bonus Actions or Reactions.

entries.name: Interposing Palm
entries: When a creature you can see within a hand's reach is hit by an attack, you can take a Reaction to make that hand the target instead. The attack hits the hand regardless of its AC. The hand takes the attack's damage, and the original target suffers none of the attack's effects. This uses your Reaction, not a Reaction of the hand.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: Use the Colossal Hand stat block matching the spell slot expended. For each spell level above 4, each hand gains 15 Hit Points; its Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution scores each increase by 2; and its Slam, Seize, Crush, and Hurl damage each increases by 1d8. Each of those damage rolls also adds the hand's Strength modifier. Size, reach, and lifting capacity increase as shown below. At spell level 5+, Seize can target creatures of any size, and Slam can push or knock Prone creatures of any size.
Multiattack allows each hand to make a number of Slam attacks equal to one-third of the spell's level (round down). Each hand can replace one of these attacks with Seize, Crush, or Hurl.

spell.name: Ruinous Descent
entries: An unseen weight crashes onto your enemy, driving them toward the earth.

Choose one creature you can see within range. The target makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 8d10} Force damage, has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and is driven up to 120 feet straight downward, stopping when it reaches a solid surface. Until the end of its next turn, its Speed is 0, and it can't end the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition on itself. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}, moved, or otherwise hindered.

If the target fails its save while on a solid surface or reaches one because of this spell, the impact releases a shock wave. Each other creature within 15 feet of the target makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} Thunder damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. The target takes no falling damage from the movement caused by this spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Force damage increases by {@damage 2d10}, and the Thunder damage increases by {@damage 2d6}, for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Faultline
entries: A jagged gesture splits the ground with erupting light. Choose a point on the ground you can see within range. From that point, a fissure follows a continuous path 60 feet long and 10 feet wide along the ground. It can turn in any direction, but every part must remain within range.

Each creature in the path makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 7d8} Thunder damage, is pushed up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction you choose, and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. A creature makes this save only once, even if the path crosses its space more than once.

The eruption damages objects and structures in the path that aren't being worn or carried, dealing double damage to them. It leaves broken ground along the path, which becomes Difficult Terrain until cleared. Each 5-foot-square portion requires at least 1 minute to clear by hand.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@scaledamage 7d8|4-9|2d8}, and the path's length increases by 20 feet, for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Banquet of Borrowed Hours

m.text: a silver serving dish worth 1,000 GP

entries: A candlelit meal unfolds from unseen steam, offering peace amid the world's haste. You conjure a table, seating, and nourishing food for up to eight willing creatures in unoccupied spaces within range. The furnishings fit the guests' sizes and vanish when the spell ends.
A creature that spends 10 uninterrupted minutes eating at the table gains the following benefits:

entries.name: Borrowed Rest
entries: It gains the benefits of a Short Rest, including the opportunity to spend Hit Point Dice. It regains the maximum number of Hit Points from each die spent during this rest.

entries.name: Food and Comfort
entries: It receives enough nourishment for 24 hours and gains {@dice 2d8} + your spellcasting ability modifier Temporary Hit Points.

entries.name: Rested Traveler
entries: For the next 8 hours, it has Advantage on saving throws made to avoid or end {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

A creature can benefit from this spell only once per Long Rest. Combat or other strenuous activity interrupts its meal, requiring it to begin the 10 minutes again. Uneaten food vanishes when removed more than 30 feet from the table or when the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The meal accommodates four additional creatures, and the Temporary Hit Points increase by {@scaledice 2d8|4-9|1d8}, for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Company of Unseen Hands

m.text: a miniature silver tool set worth 1,000 GP

entries: Tools rise in unseen hands, and silent work begins. You conjure twenty invisible workers in unoccupied spaces within range. Each is a Medium, shapeless magical force with AC 18, 20 Hit Points, Strength 20, and a Fly Speed of 60 feet (hover). A worker disappears at 0 Hit Points and can't attack, activate magic items, or take Reactions.

entries.name: Tireless Labor
entries: The workers can carry, dig, excavate, clean, cook, assemble, repair, and perform other physical tasks that a skilled laborer could accomplish. Each performs work at four times the pace of one ordinary laborer and requires no rest. Each worker can carry up to 600 pounds and push, drag, or lift up to 1,200 pounds. Multiple workers can combine these capacities when handling the same load.

entries.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: Each worker can manifest nonmagical tools needed for its assigned work, including artisan's tools, shovels, picks, saws, ropes, and pulleys. These tools function only while the worker uses them and vanish when released. The workers still require construction materials, ingredients, and other consumable supplies.

For ability checks made to perform assigned work, a worker uses your spellcasting ability modifier plus twice your Proficiency Bonus. This spell doesn't grant knowledge of a design, formula, or construction method you don't know, and it can't replace magical crafting requirements.

entries.name: Shared Instructions
entries: When you cast the spell, assign tasks to any or all workers. They follow your instructions until their work is complete, then remain available for further orders. You can issue or change instructions at any time without an action, regardless of distance or planar boundaries.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You conjure ten additional workers for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Salvager's Reversal

m.text: a platinum wedge worth 1,000 GP

entries: Nails rise and woven threads unwind as construction yields to your touch. Choose any number of nonmagical objects, sections of structures, or manufactured debris entirely within a 40-foot Cube within range. A target can't be worn or carried by an unwilling creature.

You dismantle the targets into reusable materials without damaging them. You can selectively remove particular materials or components while leaving the rest intact. Doors, windows, mechanisms, and other components you choose to preserve remain assembled and functional if their required parts are present.

entries.name: Orderly Salvage
entries: Recovered materials settle in unoccupied spaces you choose within range, sorted, stacked, bundled, or coiled as you wish. They can't be placed so that they fall onto or trap a creature. The spell safely lowers creatures and objects directly supported by dismantled material up to 60 feet onto an unoccupied supporting surface. If no such surface exists, enough supporting material remains intact to hold them.

entries.name: Material Renewal
entries: Broken pieces rejoin, bent components straighten, and rust, corrosion, rot, and other nonmagical deterioration are reversed. Materials regain their original quality but gain no additional value or properties beyond that restoration. Missing material isn't replaced. You can separate alloys, mixtures, and composite materials into their constituent substances without loss, provided those substances are still physically present. This doesn't reverse combustion, digestion, or other processes that consumed the original material.

entries.name: Careful Extraction
entries: You can free embedded or enclosed objects without damaging them, including objects behind walls or inside wreckage. Magic items can be extracted and relocated intact, but the spell can't dismantle, repair, or alter them. It can't undo construction still sustained by an active spell or restore expended consumables.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Cube's side length increases by 20 feet for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Weavebend
entries: You twist an unfinished spell into a new possibility. The next time you cast a spell before this spell ends, you can apply one Metamagic option of your choice to it, even without knowing the option or having the Metamagic feature. You expend no Sorcery Points. The spell must meet the option's requirements, and the option otherwise functions normally. Weavebend then ends.

entries.name: Unrestricted Casting
entries: The spell slot expended to cast Weavebend doesn't count against the limit of expending only one spell slot to cast a spell on a turn. You can cast Weavebend even if you have already expended a spell slot to cast another spell that turn. This exception doesn't grant additional actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions.
A spell can benefit from only one casting of Weavebend at a time. The chosen option follows the normal rules for combining Metamagic options with other Metamagic applied to that spell.

spell.name: Loaded Fate

time.condition: which you take when one or more dice are rolled by a creature you can see within 60 feet

entries: You turn one face of fate toward the light. After the triggering roll, but before its effects resolve, choose one die rolled and replace its result with any number it could normally roll. That number becomes its actual result.

entries.name: Absolute Die Control
entries: The altered die is treated as though it had naturally rolled the chosen number. Changing a d20 to 20 creates a natural 20, while changing it to 1 creates a natural 1. The altered result can affect Critical Hits, Death Saving Throws, Recharge rolls, random tables, damage rolls, healing rolls, and any other effect that depends on the number actually rolled.

entries.name: Multiple Dice
entries: If the triggering roll contains multiple dice, you initially control only one of them. You can control additional dice from the same roll. For each additional die beyond the number you can control for free, you take escalating Psychic damage: {@damage 1d10} for the first additional die, {@damage 2d10} for the second, {@damage 3d10} for the third, and so on. This damage can't be reduced or prevented. Each controlled die can be assigned a different result.

entries.name: Advantage and Disadvantage
entries: If a d20 roll is made with Advantage or Disadvantage, you can alter either die before the final die is selected. If you control both dice, you can choose the result of each separately.

entries.name: Fortune and Ruin
entries: You aren't required to improve a roll. You can set a die to any legal result, whether that benefits or harms the creature making the roll.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: You can control one additional die for free for each spell slot level above 3. When cast using a level 9 spell slot, you can assign any legal result to any number of dice in the triggering roll without taking Psychic damage for controlling additional dice.

spell.name: Temporal Storage

time.condition: which you take when a creature you can see within 60 feet begins an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction

entries: You seize a creature's imminent action and remove that moment from the normal flow of time. When a creature you can see within range begins an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, but before that action produces any effect, you can store that action. The triggering action is immediately removed from time before it resolves.

The creature still spends the Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction it attempted to use, and any resources committed to that action are expended normally, including Spell Slots, charges, ammunition, limited-use features, Material components, or similar resources. The action itself produces no effect. Instead, the entire moment becomes a Stored Action held by this spell.

entries.name: Stored Action
entries: The Stored Action preserves that action as performed by its original creature; it doesn't become yours or transfer to another creature. It has no expiration, and no time passes for it while stored.

The Stored Action preserves everything necessary to reproduce the action as it existed when it was captured, including the original creature's relevant Ability Scores, Proficiency Bonus, attack bonuses, Spell Save DC, spell attack modifier, weapons, Magic Items, class features, traits, active effects relevant to the action, spell level, damage dice, and other statistics directly required to resolve that action. Changes to the original creature after the action is stored don't alter the Stored Action.

If the original creature later loses the weapon, spell, feature, Magic Item, or other capability that produced the action, the Stored Action can still reproduce it. If the original creature dies, the Stored Action remains.

entries.name: Releasing a Stored Action
entries: While you hold a Stored Action, you can take a Bonus Action to release it. When you do so, choose any valid target, destination, direction, area, or point you can see within 60 feet, as appropriate for the Stored Action. A temporal manifestation of the original creature appears only long enough to reproduce the Stored Action. The manifestation isn't the original creature and doesn't move the original creature from its current location. It disappears immediately after the Stored Action finishes resolving.
The Stored Action is performed by a temporal manifestation of the original creature, using that creature's preserved statistics.
You don't gain or use the original creature's ability by releasing the Stored Action.

entries.name: Position of the Manifestation
entries: When released, the temporal manifestation appears in the nearest unoccupied space from which the Stored Action can legally affect the chosen target or area. If multiple spaces are equally valid, you choose the space. The manifestation exists only for purposes of resolving the Stored Action. It can't move except as part of the Stored Action itself, take additional Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions, be targeted or damaged, interact with anything except as required to perform the Stored Action, or remain after the Stored Action resolves.
If there is no valid position from which the Stored Action could legally occur, that Stored Action can't be released against the chosen target or area.

entries.name: New Targets and Choices
entries: When you release the Stored Action, you make any choices necessary to direct the preserved action into its new circumstances. Unless a choice is inseparable from the nature of the Stored Action, you can choose new targets, destinations, directions, areas, points of origin, damage types when the original action allowed a choice, or other options normally selected when performing the action.

All choices must still obey the original action's rules. A stored melee weapon attack must still target something the manifestation can reach, and a stored spell must still obey its normal range and targeting restrictions.

entries.name: Rolls
entries: Any rolls that hadn't been made when the action was stored are made when the Stored Action is released, using the preserved statistics of the original creature. This includes attack rolls, damage rolls, ability checks, and other rolls made by the original creature. Saving throws caused by the Stored Action are made normally by creatures affected when it is released.

entries.name: Resources
entries: All costs are paid when the action is captured, including Spell Slots, ammunition, charges, limited uses, and consumed Material components. Releasing it doesn't pay those costs again.

entries.name: Concentration
entries: If a Stored Action produces an effect that requires Concentration, the original creature must begin concentrating on that effect when the Stored Action is released. The original creature can do so regardless of distance, provided it is alive and capable of concentrating. If the original creature is already concentrating on another effect, its existing Concentration ends if it begins concentrating on the released effect.

If the original creature is dead, Incapacitated, or otherwise unable to concentrate when the Stored Action is released, an effect requiring Concentration lasts only until the end of the current turn unless another rule would end it sooner.

entries.name: One Stored Action
entries: You can hold only one Stored Action created by this spell at a time. If you successfully store another action while already holding one, the previously Stored Action is lost.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of level 5 or higher, the Stored Action can be released multiple times before the preserved moment finally collapses.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The Stored Action can be released twice.
The Stored Action can be released three times.
The Stored Action can be released four times.

entries: Each release creates a separate temporal manifestation of the original creature and reproduces the same Stored Action. For each release, you can choose new valid targets, destinations, directions, areas, or points of origin. Each release otherwise uses the same preserved statistics and properties. After the Stored Action has been released its maximum number of times, it disappears permanently.

spell.name: Hour Between Seconds

components.m: an hourglass

entries: You open a hidden interval between two consecutive moments and draw a portion of reality into it. Choose yourself and up to twelve willing creatures you can see within range. You can also choose any unattended objects within range that can fit within a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on you. The chosen creatures and objects disappear from normal time and enter a stable temporal space called the {@b Hidden Hour}. Inside the Hidden Hour, {@b 1 hour passes while only 1 minute passes in the outside world}.

entries.name: The Hidden Hour
entries: The Hidden Hour contains a perfect temporal copy of the area within 30 feet of you when the spell is completed. Creatures can move, interact, rest, work, and perform any activity possible with the creatures and objects present.

entries.name: Resting
entries: A creature can complete a {@b Short Rest} within the Hidden Hour. At its base level, the Hidden Hour doesn't last long enough to complete a Long Rest. A creature can complete a {@b Long Rest} within the Hidden Hour only if this spell is cast using a spell slot that provides at least 8 hours of internal time. A rest completed within the Hidden Hour restores resources exactly as that type of rest normally would.

entries.name: Temporal Workshop
entries: Objects created, repaired, modified, written upon, consumed, destroyed, or otherwise altered inside the Hidden Hour retain those changes when they return to normal time. Crafting, copying spells, research, training, and similar activities use the full amount of subjective time spent inside the Hidden Hour. Materials, tools, components, and other resources required for those activities must still be provided normally.

entries.name: Magic Within the Hidden Hour
entries: Spells and magical effects can be used normally inside the Hidden Hour. Time spent inside counts normally against the duration of spells, conditions, poisons, diseases, and other effects affecting creatures or objects within it. A spell or effect created within the Hidden Hour can persist after leaving it if its duration hasn't expired. An effect outside the Hidden Hour doesn't progress merely because additional subjective time passes within it unless that effect is also affecting something inside.

entries.name: External Time
entries: Only 1 minute passes outside the Hidden Hour regardless of how much subjective time is experienced within it. Effects tied to an external event such as dawn, dusk, midnight, the position of the sun or moon, or another event occurring in the outside world don't trigger merely because enough subjective time passes inside. This restriction doesn't prevent features or resources that normally recharge when a creature completes a Short or Long Rest from recharging.

entries.name: Protected Interval
entries: Nothing outside the Hidden Hour can perceive, target, damage, enter, or otherwise interact with a creature or object inside it. Likewise, creatures inside the Hidden Hour can't perceive, target, affect, or communicate with anything outside it. The Hidden Hour can't be entered through teleportation, planar travel, divination, or similar magic unless an effect specifically allows interaction with temporal spaces.

entries.name: Leaving the Hidden Hour
entries: A creature can choose to leave the Hidden Hour at any time. When it does, it returns to the space it occupied when the spell was completed, or the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied. From the perspective of the outside world, a creature that leaves returns when the spell's 1 minute of external time has elapsed. A creature that leaves can't reenter that same Hidden Hour. When the available internal time expires, all remaining creatures and objects return automatically.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot above level 5, the amount of subjective time available within the Hidden Hour increases, while only 1 minute continues to pass outside.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The Hidden Hour lasts 4 hours internally.
The Hidden Hour lasts 8 hours internally, allowing enough time to complete a Long Rest.
The Hidden Hour lasts 24 hours internally.
The Hidden Hour lasts 7 days internally.

spell.name: Appointment with Tomorrow

components.m: a sealed clock set to a future time

entries: You designate a moment in the future and remove willing creatures from every moment between now and then. Choose yourself and up to eight willing creatures within range. When the ritual is completed, choose a duration of up to 24 hours. The chosen creatures immediately vanish from the present. For them, no time passes at all. When the chosen duration has elapsed in the outside world, every affected creature reappears simultaneously in the space it occupied when it vanished, or the nearest unoccupied space.

entries.name: Skipped Time
entries: A creature affected by this spell doesn't experience the intervening time.

items: It doesn't age.
It doesn't sleep or rest.
It doesn't regain resources.
It doesn't become hungry or thirsty.
It doesn't make saving throws against ongoing effects.
It doesn't experience the duration of spells, conditions, poisons, diseases, or other effects affecting it.
It doesn't perceive anything that happens while it is absent.

entries: From the creature's perspective, the instant of disappearance and the instant of return are consecutive moments.

entries.name: Outside Time
entries: While absent, an affected creature doesn't exist in the normal flow of time. It can't be perceived, targeted, contacted, summoned, teleported, damaged, healed, or otherwise affected. It isn't transported to another plane. An effect that specifically manipulates time can interact with an affected creature at the GM's discretion.

entries.name: Carried Objects
entries: Everything a creature is wearing or carrying when it vanishes travels with it. An unattended object doesn't accompany the creature unless it is entirely contained within something the creature is wearing or carrying.

entries.name: Returning to a Changed World
entries: The spell doesn't preserve or protect the location where the creatures will return. If a creature's original space is occupied when it returns, it appears in the nearest unoccupied space. If the original location has been destroyed or no valid space exists nearby, the creature appears in the nearest safe space that can accommodate it. Changes to the world during the skipped interval remain exactly as they occurred.

entries.name: Early Recall
entries: When you cast this spell, you can designate one Recall Condition that can cause the affected creatures to return before the chosen duration ends. The condition must describe an observable event, such as a particular door being opened, a location being attacked, or a particular phrase being spoken while holding the spell's Material component. The condition can't depend on hidden thoughts, intentions, future knowledge, or information that couldn't be directly observed.
If the specified condition occurs before the chosen duration ends, all affected creatures immediately return.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot above level 4, the maximum duration you can skip into the future increases.

spell.name: Chronal Vault

components.m: a small silver key worth at least 100 GP

entries: You remove an object from the present and entrust it to a moment that has not yet arrived. Touch one unattended object that fits within a 5-foot cube and weighs no more than 1,000 pounds. When the ritual is completed, the object vanishes entirely from the current timeline and becomes {@b Chronally Stored}. The object isn't transported to another plane or location. It simply doesn't exist during the interval between storage and retrieval.

entries.name: Chronal Storage
entries: While Chronally Stored, the object can't be detected, targeted, summoned, damaged, stolen, or interacted with; doesn't age or decay; doesn't experience the passage of time; can't be reached through teleportation or planar travel; and retains exactly the state it had when stored. Any spell durations, charges that recover with time, biological processes, burning, corrosion, or similar ongoing processes affecting the object are paused while it is stored.

entries.name: Retrieval
entries: After storing the object, you can retrieve it as an Action at any later time. The object appears in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of you large enough to contain it. There is no maximum amount of time the object can remain stored. You don't need to be at the place where the object was originally stored. You must be on the same plane on which you originally cast this spell.

entries.name: Delayed Retrieval
entries: When casting the ritual, you can instead designate a specific future date, time, duration, or observable event. When that moment arrives, the object automatically returns. You also choose whether it returns to its original location, within 10 feet of you, or beside a creature or object you designate during the ritual. If the chosen destination is invalid when the object returns, it appears in the nearest safe space capable of containing it.

entries.name: Stored Creatures
entries: A creature can't normally be stored with this spell. If a living creature is inside or physically attached to the object when the ritual would finish, the spell fails.

entries.name: Multiple Vaults
entries: You can maintain a number of Chronally Stored objects equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you exceed this limit, you must immediately choose one stored object to return.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot above level 4, the maximum size and weight of the object increase.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: Up to a 10-foot cube and 10,000 pounds.
Up to a 20-foot cube and 100,000 pounds.
Up to a 50-foot cube with no weight limit.
Up to a 200-foot cube, allowing ships, siege engines, or small buildings.
You can store one connected nonliving object or structure regardless of size or weight.

spell.name: Time-Locked Sanctuary

components.m: a silver pendulum worth at least 500 GP

entries: You sever a small region from the passage of time, leaving everything within it suspended at a single instant. Choose a point within range. A 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point becomes Time-Locked when the ritual is completed. Everything wholly contained within the sphere at that moment is frozen in time.

entries.name: Temporal Suspension
entries: A Time-Locked creature or object doesn't experience time.

items: A suspended creature can't move or take Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions.
It doesn't age.
It doesn't breathe, eat, drink, sleep, or rest.
It can't perceive the passage of time.
It doesn't make saving throws against ongoing effects.
It doesn't experience the durations of conditions, spells, poisons, diseases, or similar effects.

entries: To a suspended creature, no time passes between the instant the sanctuary begins and the instant it ends. Objects likewise don't decay, burn, cool, corrode, discharge, recharge, or otherwise change with time.

entries.name: Frozen Moment
entries: All ongoing events wholly inside the sphere, including movement, projectiles, falling objects, flowing liquid, flames, explosions, and resolving magical effects, are suspended. When the Time-Lock ends, each resumes from the instant it stopped.

entries.name: Boundary
entries: Nothing inside the sanctuary can affect anything outside it while the Time-Lock persists. Nothing outside can enter, move, damage, target, teleport, summon, or otherwise affect anything suspended within. The boundary isn't a physical wall; anything attempting to cross it simply can't progress through the frozen interval.

entries.name: Ending the Sanctuary
entries: When you cast the ritual, choose one or more ways the Time-Lock can end:

items: after a specified amount of outside time;
at a specific date and time;
when a specified observable event occurs;
when a designated creature outside the sanctuary touches the boundary and willingly ends it;
or when you willingly end it while on the same plane.

entries: You can choose multiple conditions. The first one that occurs ends the sanctuary. There is no minimum duration. At 5th level, the Time-Lock can persist for a maximum of 24 hours.

entries.name: Preserved Effects
entries: Time spent suspended doesn't count against the duration of anything inside the sanctuary.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot above level 5, the maximum amount of outside time for which the sanctuary can remain Time-Locked increases.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: The Time-Lock has no maximum duration.

spell.name: Accelerated Age

components.m: a miniature hourglass filled with powdered amber

entries: You force matter within a chosen region to experience years of natural change in a single moment. Choose a point you can see within range. You can affect any number of unattended nonmagical objects, materials, corpses, and nonmagical plants of your choice within a 30-foot-radius sphere centered on that point. For each target, choose an amount of accelerated time up to 10 years. The target immediately changes as though that amount of time had naturally passed for it.

entries.name: Controlled Passage
entries: For each target, you choose which natural processes are accelerated and which remain suspended.

items: growth and maturation;
ripening, fermentation, and aging;
drying, curing, settling, and hardening;
rust and corrosion;
weathering and erosion;
rotting and decomposition;
growth of moss, fungi, roots, or similar natural organisms;
weakening caused by ordinary age;
crystallization, sedimentation, or other slow physical processes;
and any similar change that would naturally occur through the passage of time.

entries: You can apply different processes and different amounts of time to different targets.

entries.name: Forced Maturation
entries: Accelerated processes experience ordinary favorable conditions throughout the chosen period. The spell creates no rare substances, magical reagents, nutrients beyond those reasonably available through natural growth, or products the process couldn't naturally produce.

entries.name: Age to Ruin
entries: You can accelerate natural deterioration of nonmagical objects and structures. They rust, rot, weather, weaken, collapse, decay, or become unusable as appropriate to the chosen period.

entries.name: Temporal Production
entries: Processes whose primary requirement is waiting can be completed entirely through this spell.

items: aging wine or spirits;
fermenting food;
seasoning lumber;
curing leather;
drying herbs;
curing concrete or mortar;
growing ordinary crops;
ripening fruit;
composting organic matter;
allowing crystals or sediments to form;
or similar passive processes.

entries: Work requiring deliberate actions, decisions, craftsmanship, or research isn't performed automatically. The spell can, however, instantly complete any waiting periods between such stages.

entries.name: Living Plants
entries: Nonmagical plants can undergo their complete natural life cycle through this spell. You can accelerate germination, growth, flowering, fruit production, seed production, aging, or death. Any produce, seeds, wood, fibers, or other materials naturally created by the plant during this growth are real and remain after the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot above level 4, both the maximum accelerated time and the affected area increase.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: Up to 100 years; radius increases to 60 feet.
Up to 1,000 years; radius increases to 120 feet.
Up to 10,000 years; you can also affect nonmagical structures regardless of size, provided some portion of the structure is within the affected area.
Up to 1 million years. You can also affect non-Artifact Magic Items, though the spell can only accelerate changes that the item is actually capable of undergoing with time.
You can impose any amount of elapsed natural time, from a single moment to geological ages, and the affected radius increases to 1 mile.

spell.name: Prime of Ages

components.m: a flawless seed preserved in crystal

entries: You compel time to relinquish the wear it has placed upon a creature or object, restoring the target toward the natural prime of its existence. Touch one creature or nonmagical object.

entries.name: Living Creature
entries: If the target is a willing creature, choose an amount of its physical aging to remove, up to 10 years. Its body becomes physically younger by that amount.

items: weakened muscles;
reduced mobility;
age-related frailty;
gray hair;
wrinkles;
deteriorated eyesight or hearing caused by ordinary aging;
and other natural physical deterioration caused solely by age.

entries: The creature's memories, personality, class levels, Ability Scores, proficiencies, learned abilities, and accumulated experience aren't lost. This spell doesn't undo injuries, diseases, curses, mutations, or other changes merely because they occurred while the creature was older. A creature can't be made physically younger than the beginning of its natural adulthood with this spell.

entries.name: Return to Prime
entries: Instead of choosing a number of years, you can restore the target to the physical prime of its natural adult life. Its chronological history remains unchanged; only its body's biological age is altered. A creature restored this way retains everything it has learned and experienced.

entries.name: Nonliving Objects
entries: If the target is a nonmagical object, you can remove up to 10 years of deterioration caused naturally by age. Rust vanishes. Weathering recedes. Rotten material becomes sound again. Natural discoloration fades. Age-weakened material regains its former integrity. Missing matter lost specifically through gradual corrosion, erosion, decay, or similar age-related processes is restored.
Damage caused by attacks, deliberate destruction, crafting, fire, spells, or other discrete events isn't repaired unless that damage subsequently worsened through natural aging.

entries.name: Corpses
entries: A corpse can be restored to the physical condition it possessed shortly after death. This doesn't return the creature to life, restore its soul, or reverse the cause of its death.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot above level 4, its reach into biological and material age increases.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: Remove up to 100 years of physical aging.
Remove up to 1,000 years, and you can affect creatures whose natural lifespan greatly exceeds that of Humans.
You can restore a willing creature to any younger adult biological age it has previously possessed, regardless of how long ago that was.
You can also affect non-Artifact Magic Items, restoring deterioration caused solely by age without restoring expended charges or consumed magical power.

You can return a willing creature or object to its ideal physical prime, even if countless years have passed. A creature affected this way ceases to suffer any physical deterioration caused by its accumulated age, though it can begin aging normally again afterward.

spell.name: Starbreaker
entries: You condense a fragment of violent stellar radiance and hurl it toward a point you can see within range. The fragment detonates in a 20-foot-radius sphere. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 8d8} Radiant damage plus {@damage 4d6} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Shattering Impact
entries: A creature that fails the saving throw is pushed 20 feet directly away from the center of the explosion and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Objects and structures in the area take maximum Force damage from this spell.

entries.name: Burning Core
entries: The exact point at the center of the explosion remains violently energized until the start of your next turn. The first creature that enters that space or starts its turn there takes {@damage 4d8} Radiant damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The Radiant damage increases by {@damage 2d8}, the Force damage increases by {@damage 1d6}, and the Burning Core damage increases by {@damage 1d8} for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Magma Coffin
entries: You tear molten stone from beneath a creature and close it around them like a burning tomb. Choose one creature you can see within range. The target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 8d8} Fire damage plus {@damage 4d6} Bludgeoning damage and has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition inside a shell of molten rock. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and isn't Restrained.

entries.name: Molten Prison
entries: While Restrained by the spell, the target has Total Cover against effects originating outside the Magma Coffin, and creatures outside have Total Cover against effects originating from the target. At the start of each of the target's turns, it takes {@damage 4d8} Fire damage. The target can use its Action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against your spell save DC, escaping on a success.

Another creature can attack the Magma Coffin instead. It has AC 15, 30 Hit Points, and immunity to Fire, Poison, and Psychic damage. When the Coffin is reduced to 0 Hit Points, it shatters and the target is freed.

entries.name: Violent Escape
entries: When the Magma Coffin is destroyed, each creature other than the trapped target within 10 feet of it must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 4d6} Fire damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each spell slot level above 4, the initial Fire damage increases by {@damage 2d8}, the initial Bludgeoning damage increases by {@damage 1d6}, the ongoing Fire damage increases by {@damage 1d8}, and the Magma Coffin gains 10 additional Hit Points.

spell.name: Executioner's Comet
entries: You condense destructive force into a single blazing projectile and drive it through one target with catastrophic precision. Make a ranged spell attack against one creature within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 10d10} Force damage.

entries.name: Penetrating Impact
entries: If the attack hits, the projectile continues through the target in a 60-foot-long, 5-foot-wide line extending directly away from you. Each other creature in that line must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 6d8} Force damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Execution
entries: If the original target is below half its Hit Point maximum when the spell hits, the initial damage becomes {@damage 12d10} Force damage instead. If the target is reduced to 0 Hit Points by the initial damage, the projectile doesn't lose any force passing through it. Creatures struck by Penetrating Impact instead take {@damage 8d8} Force damage on a failed save.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each spell slot level above 4, the initial damage increases by {@damage 2d10}, the Execution damage increases by an additional {@damage 1d10}, and Penetrating Impact increases by {@damage 2d8}.

spell.name: Predator Lightning
entries: You create a living bolt of lightning that tears through one creature, then immediately hunts for another. Choose one creature you can see within range. It must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 8d10} Lightning damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Hunt
entries: After the damage is resolved, if the target failed its saving throw, the lightning leaps to another creature of your choice within 30 feet of it. The new target makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 6d8} Lightning damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one. The lightning can continue leaping this way as long as each new target fails its saving throw. Each successive leap deals {@damage 2d8} less damage than the previous leap, to a minimum of {@damage 2d8}. A creature can be targeted only once by a single casting of this spell.

entries.name: Blood in the Storm
entries: If any target is reduced to 0 Hit Points by this spell, the lightning becomes empowered. The next leap deals the same damage as the attack that killed that creature instead of decreasing. If that leap also reduces its target to 0 Hit Points, the effect repeats.

entries.name: Refuse to Die
entries: If the lightning reaches {@damage 2d8} and the target fails its saving throw, it doesn't dissipate. Instead, it remains crackling around that creature until the end of your next turn. The next time that creature takes damage before then, the lightning detonates and deals an additional {@damage 4d8} Lightning damage to it.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each spell slot level above 4, the initial damage increases by {@damage 2d10}, the first Hunt leap increases by {@damage 1d8}, and Refuse to Die increases by {@damage 1d8}.

spell.name: Ruin Lance
entries: You compress destructive magic into a needle-thin lance and drive it through a creature's defenses. Make a ranged spell attack against one creature within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 10d10} Force damage.

entries.name: Rupture
entries: The lance leaves an unstable fracture inside the target until the end of your next turn. The next time the target takes damage, the fracture erupts, dealing an additional {@damage 4d10} Force damage.

entries.name: Chain Rupture
entries: If Rupture is triggered by damage from another creature, the explosion tears outward. Each creature of your choice within 10 feet of the target must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d6} Force damage on a failed save or half as much on a successful one.

entries.name: Break the Unbreakable
entries: Damage dealt by this spell ignores Resistance to Force damage. If the target is Immune to Force damage, it is treated as having Resistance instead.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each spell slot level above 4, the initial damage increases by {@scaledamage 10d10|4-9|2d10}, Rupture increases by {@scaledamage 4d10|4-9|1d10}, and Chain Rupture increases by {@scaledamage 4d6|4-9|1d6}.

spell.name: Ruin Distribution
entries: You create a reservoir of destructive force and decide exactly how its violence is divided. Choose any number of creatures you can see within range. You create {@damage 12d10} Force damage dice and distribute those dice among the chosen creatures in any combination you choose before rolling. For example, you could assign all {@damage 12d10} to one creature, {@damage 6d10} each to two creatures, or {@damage 3d10} each to four creatures.
Each target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes the damage rolled from the dice assigned to it. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Concentrated Ruin
entries: If you assign at least 8 damage dice to a single creature and it fails its saving throw, it is also pushed 20 feet in a direction of your choice and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If you assign all damage dice to a single creature, that creature makes its saving throw with Disadvantage.

entries.name: Excess Destruction
entries: If a target is reduced to 0 Hit Points before all damage assigned to it would be necessary to do so, any excess damage isn't lost. Choose another creature within 30 feet of that target. It takes the excess Force damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each spell slot level above 4, the spell creates {@scaledamage 12d10|4-9|3d10} additional damage dice.

spell.name: Buried Cataclysm

components.m: a shard of obsidian buried at the center of the area

entries: You bury destructive magic beneath a location and leave it waiting for the moment you choose. Touch a solid surface and choose a 20-foot-radius sphere centered on that point. The spell becomes dormant and is imperceptible except to effects that detect magic. When you cast the spell, choose one Trigger.

entries.name: Trigger
entries: The Cataclysm can activate when an observable condition within 120 feet of its center occurs, such as a creature entering or leaving the area; a particular creature or creature type entering; an object being moved, opened, broken, or touched; a specific word being spoken; another spell being cast in the area; a particular amount of time passing; or another similarly observable circumstance occurring.

You can make the condition as specific as you wish, provided the spell can determine whether it occurred without reading thoughts, intentions, alignment, or hidden information. You can also activate the Cataclysm yourself as a Reaction while you are on the same plane.

entries.name: Detonation
entries: When triggered, the stored magic erupts. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 8d10} Force damage plus {@damage 4d6} Fire damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Unattended objects and structures in the area automatically fail the saving throw.

entries.name: Prepared Destruction
entries: Because the spell remains dormant until triggered, you can have a number of Buried Cataclysms active at once equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Casting the spell beyond this limit causes the oldest one to harmlessly dissipate.

entries.name: Linked Detonation
entries: When one of your Buried Cataclysms detonates, you can cause any number of your other Buried Cataclysms within 300 feet of it to detonate simultaneously. A creature caught in multiple overlapping detonations makes a separate saving throw against each one and can take damage from each.

entries.caption: Buried Cataclysm Progression
rows: The radius becomes 30 feet and the damage becomes {@damage 10d10} Force plus {@damage 5d6} Fire.
The radius becomes 40 feet and the damage becomes {@damage 12d10} Force plus {@damage 6d6} Fire.
The radius becomes 60 feet and the damage becomes {@damage 14d10} Force plus {@damage 8d6} Fire.
The radius becomes 90 feet and the damage becomes {@damage 16d10} Force plus {@damage 10d6} Fire.
The radius becomes 120 feet and the damage becomes {@damage 20d10} Force plus {@damage 12d6} Fire, and there is no limit to how many Buried Cataclysms you can maintain from this casting level.

spell.name: Sympathetic Execution

components.m: an effigy worth at least 50 GP and a physical fragment or personal possession of the intended target

entries: You bind a creature's physical identity to an effigy, creating a weapon that can reach it regardless of distance. Choose one creature represented by the material component. The spell succeeds only if the component genuinely belonged to, came from, or was part of that creature. The prepared effigy remains linked until the spell ends.

entries.name: Execute
entries: While holding the effigy, you can use an Action to destroy it and release the stored curse. The target is affected even if you can't see it, regardless of distance, provided it is on the same plane. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 8d10} Necrotic damage plus {@damage 4d6} Psychic damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. The effigy is destroyed whether the target succeeds or fails.

entries.name: Intimate Connection
entries: The strength of the sympathetic link depends on the material used. If the component is merely a possession frequently carried by the target, the saving throw is made normally. If the component is a piece of the target's body—such as blood, hair, scales, a tooth, or similar tissue—the target makes the saving throw with Disadvantage.

entries.name: Choose the Wound
entries: When you perform Execute, you can choose one of the following additional effects. It applies only if the target fails its saving throw.

items: {@b Break.} The target has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, and its Speed becomes 0 until the end of its next turn.
{@b Bleed.} The target takes an additional {@damage 3d10} Necrotic damage at the start of its next turn.
{@b Silence.} The target can't speak or provide Verbal components until the end of its next turn.
{@b Blind.} The target has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Death Knows the Name
entries: Changing appearance, transforming, becoming Invisible, assuming another form, or being polymorphed doesn't break the sympathetic link. If the target dies before the effigy is activated, the effigy becomes inert.

entries.caption: Sympathetic Execution Progression
rows: The damage becomes {@damage 10d10} Necrotic plus {@damage 5d6} Psychic.
The damage becomes {@damage 12d10} Necrotic plus {@damage 6d6} Psychic, and you choose two Wound effects.
The damage becomes {@damage 14d10} Necrotic plus {@damage 8d6} Psychic, and the spell can reach the target on another plane if you know which plane it occupies.
The damage becomes {@damage 16d10} Necrotic plus {@damage 10d6} Psychic, and you choose three Wound effects.
The damage becomes {@damage 20d10} Necrotic plus {@damage 12d6} Psychic, and you can choose all four Wound effects.

spell.name: Bottled Thunderhead

components.m: a crystal vessel worth at least 100 GP

entries: You compress the violence of an entire storm into a vessel small enough to hold in one hand. At the end of the casting, the material component becomes a Thunderhead Vessel containing the spell. The vessel remains charged until discharged or destroyed.

entries.name: Release the Storm
entries: A creature holding the vessel can use an Action to throw it at a point it can see within 120 feet. The vessel shatters on impact, releasing a 20-foot-radius sphere of lightning, thunder, and violent pressure. Each creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 8d10} Lightning damage plus {@damage 4d6} Thunder damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries.name: Eye of the Thunderhead
entries: The creature or object struck by the vessel itself suffers the concentrated center of the storm. When the vessel is thrown, the thrower can make a ranged spell attack using your spell attack modifier against one creature or object at the chosen point. On a hit, that target takes an additional {@damage 4d10} Lightning damage before the explosion occurs.

entries.name: Concussive Storm
entries: A creature that fails the saving throw is pushed up to 20 feet directly away from the center and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. Unattended objects and structures automatically fail the saving throw and take maximum Thunder damage.

entries.name: Carry the Catastrophe
entries: The Thunderhead Vessel can be carried, hidden, traded, or given to another creature. The creature releasing it doesn't need to be a spellcaster. All attack rolls, saving throws, and spell effects use your spellcasting statistics from when you created the vessel. You can have a number of Thunderhead Vessels created by this spell equal to your Proficiency Bonus at one time. Creating another beyond this limit causes the oldest vessel to harmlessly discharge its stored energy.

entries.caption: Bottled Thunderhead Progression
rows: The damage becomes {@damage 10d10} Lightning plus {@damage 5d6} Thunder, and Eye of the Thunderhead deals {@damage 5d10} Lightning damage.
The damage becomes {@damage 12d10} Lightning plus {@damage 6d6} Thunder, the radius becomes 30 feet, and Eye of the Thunderhead deals {@damage 6d10} Lightning damage.
The damage becomes {@damage 14d10} Lightning plus {@damage 8d6} Thunder, the radius becomes 40 feet, and Eye of the Thunderhead deals {@damage 8d10} Lightning damage.
The damage becomes {@damage 16d10} Lightning plus {@damage 10d6} Thunder, the radius becomes 60 feet, and Eye of the Thunderhead deals {@damage 10d10} Lightning damage.

The damage becomes {@damage 20d10} Lightning plus {@damage 12d6} Thunder, the radius becomes 90 feet, Eye of the Thunderhead deals {@damage 12d10} Lightning damage, and Thunderhead Vessels created using a 9th-level slot don't count against your maximum number of vessels.

spell.name: Inheritance Seal

m.text: a blank metal seal worth at least 250 GP

entries: You take something a creature knows how to do and give that capability a physical form. Choose one willing creature you touch throughout the ritual. It becomes the Donor. Then choose one eligible capability the Donor currently possesses. The metal seal becomes an Inheritance Seal containing that capability.

entries.name: What Can Be Inherited
entries: Choose one of the following:

items: one Skill proficiency;
one Tool proficiency;
one Weapon proficiency;
one Armor proficiency;
one language;
one Weapon Mastery property the Donor can use;
one Fighting Style;
one cantrip the Donor knows;
or one non-resource passive feature granted by its species, background, class, subclass, or Feat.

entries: A passive feature must function continuously or modify something the creature can already do. It can't itself grant Spellcasting, Extra Attack, an Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, transformation, summon, companion, resource pool, Legendary Action, or similar major subsystem.

entries.name: The Donor Keeps It
entries: Creating the seal doesn't remove or suppress the capability from the Donor. The spell creates a transferable magical copy.

entries.name: Claim the Inheritance
entries: A creature holding the seal can spend 1 minute attuning itself to the stored inheritance. Once it does, it gains the stored capability as though it naturally possessed it. The creature doesn't need to meet the normal class, species, Feat, ability-score, or level prerequisite of that capability unless the capability would literally be unusable without another required game statistic. The inheritance remains until the creature willingly releases it, the seal is destroyed, or the spell ends. Only one creature can benefit from a particular seal at a time.

entries.name: Borrowed Expertise
entries: If the seal contains a proficiency and the Donor had Expertise with it, the recipient gains Expertise as well. If the seal contains a Fighting Style or Weapon Mastery, the recipient uses it exactly as the Donor could. If it contains a cantrip, the recipient chooses Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma as its spellcasting ability for that cantrip when claiming the inheritance.

entries.name: No False Limitation
entries: If the inherited feature refers to the Donor's class, subclass, species, or similar origin only to determine where the feature came from, the recipient counts as satisfying that reference. For example, a feature saying 'your Wizard spells' doesn't make the recipient a Wizard, but a feature saying 'when you use this feature granted by your species' still functions for the recipient as the inherited feature.

entries.name: Multiple Inheritances
entries: A creature can benefit from a number of Inheritance Seals equal to its Proficiency Bonus simultaneously. You can maintain a number of seals created by this spell equal to your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.caption: Higher-Level Benefits
rows: You can store an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction feature that normally has no more than Proficiency Bonus uses per Long Rest.
You can store one Feat in its entirety, including all of its features.
You can store one class or subclass feature of 10th level or lower.
You can store one class or subclass feature of 15th level or lower, including a feature that uses its own resource pool; the recipient gains that resource pool as part of the inheritance.

You can store any one non-Spellcasting class, subclass, species, background, or Feat feature the Donor possesses, regardless of level. A seal created with a 9th-level slot doesn't count against your maximum number of maintained Inheritance Seals.

spell.name: Witness in Matter
entries: You awaken the impressions clinging to matter without giving it thought or consciousness. Touch one nonmagical object and choose a moment within the previous 24 hours.

For the duration, you perceive sights and sounds from the object's location beginning at the chosen moment, experiencing events as though you occupied the object's space at that time. The recollection progresses forward in real time while you maintain Concentration.

items: You can look in any direction from the object's location, regardless of the direction the object was facing.
Your vision is limited by whatever could actually have been seen from that position at the time.
Walls, containers, darkness, magical concealment, and similar obstructions function as they did during the recalled moment.
You hear sounds that reached the object's location normally.
The spell doesn't reveal thoughts, invisible creatures, magically concealed information, or anything the object had no physical means of witnessing.
Moving the object during the casting doesn't change the viewpoint; you perceive events from wherever the object actually was during the recalled time.
If the object itself was moved during the recalled period, your viewpoint moves with it.

entries: As an Action while the spell lasts, you can jump forward or backward to another moment within the same 24-hour period. You can end the spell early after identifying a particular moment. If you cast Witness in Matter on the same object again within 1 hour, you can begin directly from that moment without searching for it again.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The accessible past expands to 7 days with a 4th-level slot, 30 days with a 5th-level slot, 1 year with a 6th-level slot, and the object's entire physical existence with a 7th-level or higher slot.

spell.name: Summon Crown-Bound Object
entries: This is a summon-reference entry for {@optfeature Edict of the Unthinking|FftForbiddenTome}. It exists so the appropriate Crown-Bound Object stat block can be selected and summoned easily in tools such as 5etools and Foundry. Using this reference doesn't grant Edict of the Unthinking, doesn't create an object by itself, and doesn't replace the Invocation's normal targeting, action economy, duration, control, or other rules. Use the actual Size of the object or mass you animate.

entries.caption: Crown-Bound Object
rows: 15 or the object's original AC, whichever is higher or more appropriate
5 + three times your level, or the object's original Hit Points if higher or more appropriate
15 or the object's original AC, whichever is higher or more appropriate
10 + four times your level, or the object's original Hit Points if higher or more appropriate
16 or the object's original AC, whichever is higher or more appropriate
15 + five times your level, or the object's original Hit Points if higher or more appropriate

spell.name: Disable Function
entries: You suppress one specific function of a creature, object, or magical construct without otherwise damaging or transforming it. Choose one target you can see within range, then name one function the target is currently capable of performing.

items: A creature's ability to fly.
A creature's ability to speak.
A creature's ability to see.
A creature's ability to teleport.
A weapon's ability to cut.
A firearm's ability to fire.
A door's ability to open.
A lock's ability to lock or unlock.
A vehicle's ability to move.
A magic item's ability to expend charges.
A portal's ability to transport creatures.
A magical construct's ability to receive commands.

entries: If the target is an unwilling creature, it makes a Constitution saving throw. On a success, the spell fails. For the duration, the chosen function doesn't work. This doesn't remove the underlying feature, destroy any component, expend any resource, or prevent unrelated functions of the target. For example, disabling a dragon's flight doesn't remove its wings, disabling a sword's ability to cut doesn't prevent it from being carried, and disabling a magic staff's ability to expend charges doesn't suppress its other properties.

entries.name: Specific Function
entries: The function must be described specifically enough to identify a particular capability. You can disable "teleportation," "flight," "speech," or "the ability to fire this weapon," but you can't choose an unrestricted concept such as "movement," "magic," "combat," or "everything this creature can do." A function can include all uses of the same underlying capability. For example, disabling a creature's teleportation prevents every ability it possesses that actually causes it to teleport.

entries.name: Magical Functions
entries: This spell can suppress a function created or maintained by another spell or magical effect without ending that effect. If the function belongs to an effect created by a spell of a higher level than this spell, make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + that spell's level. On a failure, that function isn't disabled.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of level 5 or higher, you can disable one additional function for each slot level above 4th. The additional functions can belong to the same target or different targets within range.

spell.name: Remembered Return

m.text: a diamond worth at least 2,000 gp, which is consumed, and one object strongly associated with the deceased

entries: Memory guides a lost soul home. Choose one dead creature whose identity you know; no corpse or remains are required. At least one willing creature that personally knew it in life must remain within 10 feet of you throughout the casting.
When the spell is completed, the deceased's soul is called back and a new living body forms in an unoccupied space within range. The creature returns with all its Hit Points.

entries.name: Rebuilt from Memory
entries: The new body is the creature's true body as it existed during its life, not an illusion, duplicate, Construct, or magical disguise. It restores missing limbs and organs, scars and permanent physical characteristics, natural biological traits, supernatural physical traits that were genuinely part of the creature, and its normal age at the time of death. Equipment, carried objects, implanted Magic Items, and possessions aren't recreated.

entries.name: The Soul Corrects the Memory
entries: Witnesses' memories guide the soul but don't determine its identity. It returns with its own personality, memories, abilities, and experiences, unaffected by witnesses' mistaken or incomplete recollections.

entries.name: Memory Anchors
entries: Each additional willing creature that personally knew the deceased can participate in the casting.
For every three Memory Anchors participating, choose one of the following benefits:

items: Reduce the diamond cost by 500 gp, to a minimum of 500 gp.

One magical effect suppressing, imprisoning, concealing, binding, or otherwise preventing the soul from returning is subjected to a spellcasting ability check against DC 10 + the effect's spell level. On a success, that effect is suppressed long enough for the soul to return.

entries: A creature can count as only one Memory Anchor.

entries.name: The Last Person Who Remembers
entries: If exactly one living creature in existence still personally remembers the deceased, that creature alone is sufficient. For the purpose of using that creature as your Memory Anchor, the spell's range becomes 1 mile, and the creature doesn't need to be physically present with you during the casting. You must know that creature exists and deliberately use its memory as the anchor.

entries.name: Forgotten Dead
entries: If no living creature personally remembers the deceased, this spell normally fails. Records, portraits, books, recordings, statues, and historical knowledge alone aren't sufficient. However, an object containing a genuine preserved memory of the deceased can serve as one Memory Anchor.

entries.name: Unwilling or Missing Soul
entries: The spell fails if the soul is unwilling to return. If the soul has been destroyed entirely, the spell fails unless the effect that destroyed it explicitly allows the soul to be restored. If the soul is trapped, bound, sealed, or otherwise prevented from returning, Memory Anchors can help overcome that obstruction as described above.

entries.name: No Remains Required
entries: The spell works regardless of time since death or the condition and location of any remains, even if none survive.

spell.name: Borrowed Life

m.text: a diamond worth at least 500 gp, which isn't consumed

entries: You call a dead creature back into its body without fully severing its connection to death. Touch the corpse of one dead creature. If its soul is willing and able to return, the creature returns to life for the duration. There is no limit on how long the creature has been dead, but enough of its body must remain to function as a body. The spell repairs ordinary decomposition and lethal injuries, restores missing organs necessary for life, and rejoins severed body parts that are present. It doesn't recreate an entirely missing body.
The creature returns with half its Hit Point maximum, rounded up.

entries.name: Fully Alive
entries: For the duration, the creature is genuinely alive. It can act normally, regain Hit Points, cast spells, use class features, attune to Magic Items, rest, and otherwise function exactly as a living creature. It isn't Undead and can't be turned or affected as Undead merely because this spell restored it.

entries.name: What Returns
entries: The creature returns with the spell slots, Hit Dice, Charges, limited-use abilities, and other expendable resources it possessed when it died. Resources expended before death aren't restored. Any conditions that would normally end when a creature dies remain ended. Diseases, curses, poisons, and other effects that can persist through death return with the creature if they still meaningfully affect its restored body or soul.

entries.name: Death Is Waiting
entries: The creature knows exactly how much time remains before the spell ends. When the duration ends, the creature dies instantly.

items: This death deals no damage.
This death can't be prevented by Temporary Hit Points or healing.
This death doesn't trigger an effect that activates only when damage reduces a creature to 0 Hit Points.
This death leaves the body intact.

entries: The creature's soul departs normally.

entries.name: Make the Return Permanent
entries: While the creature is alive through this spell, another spell or effect capable of permanently returning the dead to life can target it as though it were still dead. If that effect succeeds, Borrowed Life ends immediately and the creature remains alive permanently. The permanent resurrection effect doesn't need to wait for the creature to die again.

entries.name: Dying Early
entries: If the creature dies before this spell ends, Borrowed Life ends immediately. The creature can subsequently be returned to life normally.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: When you cast this spell using a spell slot of level 5 or higher, its duration increases as shown in the Borrowed Life Duration table.
At 9th level, the creature no longer dies merely because the spell is dispelled. Instead, once it has remained alive for 30 consecutive days, its return becomes permanent and the spell ends.

spell.name: Incomplete Resurrection

m.text: a diamond worth at least 750 gp, which the spell consumes

entries: Life returns to a body still rebuilding itself. Touch a meaningful portion of one dead creature's remains, such as a skull, heart, major bone, or preserved organ. If its soul is willing and able to return, it returns permanently to life, regardless of time since death.

entries.name: Immediate Return
entries: The creature returns with 1 Hit Point, conscious, and with no Exhaustion caused by this spell. It returns with its identity, memories, class levels, Feats, proficiencies, and abilities intact. Its spell slots, Hit Dice, class resources, item Charges, and other limited resources remain in the state they were in when it died. Resources already expended before death aren't restored.

entries.name: Unfinished Body
entries: The spell immediately creates whatever organs and structures are necessary for the creature to live, but its body remains incomplete. When the creature first returns, its Hit Point maximum becomes 25 percent of its normal Hit Point maximum, rounded up. This reduction isn't damage and can't be removed by Greater Restoration, Remove Curse, healing magic, or similar effects. The creature can regain Hit Points normally up to this reduced maximum.

entries.name: Rebuilding Through Rest
entries: Each time the creature finishes a Long Rest, its body becomes more complete. Its Hit Point maximum becomes the value shown in the Rebuilding Through Rest table.
Once it reaches 100 percent, the reconstruction is complete.

entries.name: Returning Body Parts
entries: The body reconstructs progressively during this recovery. When the creature returns, all organs necessary for immediate survival are restored. After its first Long Rest, all major missing limbs and sensory organs are restored. After its second Long Rest, scars, damaged tissue, lost teeth, minor missing structures, and other physical injuries can be restored at the creature's choice. After its third Long Rest, its body is fully restored to the healthy physical state appropriate to it immediately before the injury or condition that caused its death.

entries.name: Functional Before Complete
entries: An incomplete body is still a living body.

items: The creature can move normally.
The creature can attack and cast spells.
The creature can use class and species features.
The creature can regain Hit Points.
The creature can take Short and Long Rests.
The creature can attune to Magic Items.
The creature can gain levels.
The creature can use abilities requiring a living creature.

entries: A temporarily missing limb or organ can still prevent actions that physically require it until that part is restored.

entries.name: Interrupted Recovery
entries: If the creature dies again before its reconstruction is complete, the rebuilding process ends. It can be resurrected again normally, including by another casting of this spell.

entries.name: Faster Reconstruction
entries: Whenever the creature receives healing from a spell of 5th level or higher, the caster can choose to use that healing to advance the reconstruction instead of restoring Hit Points. If they do, the creature immediately gains the benefit of one additional completed Long Rest from Rebuilding Through Rest. A creature can't advance beyond full reconstruction.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
