entries: When you cast this spell using a higher-level spell slot, the creature returns in a more complete state as shown in the Incomplete Resurrection table.
With a 7th-level or higher slot, the creature returns with its normal Hit Point maximum and all missing body parts restored immediately.

spell.name: Chain Resurrection

m.text: diamond dust worth at least 1,000 gp, which the spell consumes

entries: You restore one dead creature to life and leave a portion of the resurrection magic burning inside it, allowing that life to call another dead creature back in turn. Touch the remains of one dead creature. If its soul is willing and able to return, it returns permanently to life with all its Hit Points. The creature must have enough physical remains to identify the body, but the remains don't need to be intact. The spell restores missing vital organs and repairs damage necessary for the creature to live.
There is no limit on how long the creature has been dead.

entries.name: Carry the Return
entries: For the next 24 hours, the resurrected creature carries the unused momentum of this spell. Once during that duration, it can touch the remains of another dead creature and spend 10 minutes transferring the magic. No spell slot or Material component is required for this transfer. At the end of the 10 minutes, the second creature returns permanently to life with all its Hit Points if its soul is willing and able to return. The first creature then loses the ability to continue the chain.

entries.name: The Chain Continues
entries: A creature restored through Carry the Return gains the same ability. It can therefore restore another dead creature within 24 hours of its own resurrection, passing the chain onward again. There is no inherent maximum number of creatures that can eventually be restored by a single casting. However, at any moment, only the most recently resurrected creature carries the power to continue that chain.

entries.name: Broken Chain
entries: The chain ends if any of the following occurs:

items: The current bearer allows its 24-hour window to expire.
The current bearer dies before passing the resurrection onward.
The current bearer willingly dismisses the remaining magic.
A transfer fails because the chosen soul doesn't exist or can't return.

entries: If a soul is merely unwilling, the bearer can choose not to complete the transfer, and the chain isn't lost.

entries.name: Restored Body
entries: Each returned creature receives a complete body capable of sustaining its life. The spell restores missing vital organs, severed or destroyed limbs, damage caused by decomposition, and ordinary physical injuries that existed when the creature died. If at least a meaningful portion of the corpse remains, the rest of the body can be reconstructed around it.

If no physical remains survive, the current bearer can instead use an object that belonged personally to that creature during its life. In that case, the spell creates a complete new body for the returning creature.

entries.name: What Death Doesn't Restore
entries: Resurrection doesn't replenish resources. A returned creature retains the state of its spell slots, Hit Dice, class resources, limited-use abilities, Magic Item Charges, and similar resources from immediately before it died. Resources already expended remain expended.

entries.name: Returning Again
entries: A creature previously restored by this spell can be restored by it again after a later death. Being part of one resurrection chain doesn't permanently mark or restrict the creature.

spell.name: Last Reserve

components.m: a drop of blood, which isn't consumed

entries: You force a recently departed creature to spend the last reserves of vitality still bound to its body. Touch the corpse of one creature that died within the last 10 minutes. If its soul is willing and able to return, and it had at least one unexpended Hit Die when it died, you can return it to life.

entries.name: Spend Hit Dice
entries: Choose and expend any number of the creature's remaining Hit Dice. Roll them, adding its Constitution modifier to each die. It returns to life with Hit Points equal to the total (minimum 1).

entries.name: Its Own Life
entries: Only the dead creature's own Hit Dice can fuel this spell. Another creature can't contribute Hit Dice, Hit Points, Temporary Hit Points, spell slots, or other resources. If the creature had no Hit Dice remaining when it died, the spell fails.

entries.name: Recent Death
entries: The spell can close lethal wounds and restore damaged organs enough for the creature to survive, but it can't recreate major missing portions of the body.
It fails if the creature:

items: has been dead for more than 10 minutes;
died of old age;
has been decapitated and the head isn't present;
is missing a vital organ or major portion of its body;
has been completely destroyed;
or has a soul that can't return.

entries.name: Remaining Resources
entries: Nothing else is restored. Spell slots, class resources, Magic Item Charges, limited-use features, and all Hit Dice not spent through this spell remain exactly as they were when the creature died.

entries.name: Hit Dice Recovery
entries: Hit Dice expended by this spell are ordinary expended Hit Dice. The creature regains them normally when it finishes Long Rests.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: At 5th level or higher, you may reroll any Hit Die rolled for this spell once, but must use the new roll. At 6th level or higher, the spell can restore missing limbs and destroyed vital organs, provided at least half of the creature's body remains.

spell.name: Steal Resistance
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range and choose one damage type that creature has Resistance or Immunity to. The target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, you steal that protection for the duration.

items: If the target had Resistance, it loses that Resistance, and you gain Resistance to that damage type.
If the target had Immunity, it loses that Immunity, and you gain Immunity to that damage type.

entries: The target regains its normal Resistance or Immunity when the spell ends. If the target succeeds on the saving throw, the spell has no effect.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each slot level above 5th, you can steal protection against one additional damage type from the same target. The target makes only one saving throw.

spell.name: Steal Concentration
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range that is concentrating on a spell of 5th level or lower. The creature must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, it stops concentrating on that spell, but the spell doesn't end. You immediately begin concentrating on it instead.
While you maintain Concentration:

items: the spell continues for its remaining duration;
you make any choices the original caster could normally make while the spell is active;
you control any creatures, objects, areas, or movable effects the spell allows its caster to control;
the spell continues using the original caster's spell save DC and spell attack bonus.

entries: You don't learn the stolen spell and can't cast it yourself. If your Concentration ends, the stolen spell ends normally.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The maximum level of spell you can steal increases by 1 for each slot level above 5th.

spell.name: Duplicate Effect
entries: Choose one creature you can see within range that is currently affected by a spell of 5th level or lower. Then choose up to two other creatures within range that could normally be affected by that spell. Each chosen creature gains the same spell effect for the original effect's remaining duration. An unwilling creature can make a Charisma saving throw, avoiding the copied effect on a success. The copied effect uses the original spell's spell save DC, spell attack bonus, damage, and all other statistics.

Each copied effect is independent of the original. Ending, dispelling, or removing the original effect doesn't end the copies. If the original spell requires Concentration, the copied effects don't require Concentration. Any choices already made for the original spell are copied unless that spell normally allows those choices to be changed during its duration.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: For each slot level above 5th, you can affect one additional creature and the maximum spell level you can copy increases by 1.

spell.name: Pact of Alchemy Attack
entries: This is a roll-reference entry for the single-target attack granted by {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}. It doesn't grant an additional use of the Pact or change its action economy, range, area, material requirements, or other rules. Make an Invocation attack roll against one creature allowed by the Pact. On a hit, the target takes {@scaledamage 2d10|5,9|2d10} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, your choice. At Level 9, you can instead choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage.
Use your primary ability score as the spellcasting ability for this reference entry.
spell.foundryAdvice: Use the same primary ability score used by Pact of Alchemy as this reference entry's spellcasting ability.

spell.name: Pact of Alchemy Area Attack
entries: This is a roll-reference entry for the area attack granted by {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}. It doesn't grant an additional use of the Pact or change its action economy, range, area, material requirements, or other rules.

Choose a point allowed by the Pact. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of that point make a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@scaledamage 2d10|5,9|2d10} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, your choice. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. At Level 9, you can instead choose Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder damage. Use your primary ability score as the spellcasting ability for this reference entry.
spell.foundryAdvice: Use the same primary ability score used by Pact of Alchemy as this reference entry's spellcasting ability.

spell.name: Pact of Alchemy Move
entries: This is a roll-reference entry for the forced-movement option granted by {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}. It doesn't grant an additional use of the Pact or change its action economy, range, area, material requirements, or other rules. One creature allowed by the Pact makes a Strength Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failed save, you push or pull it up to 20 feet, knock it {@condition Prone|XPHB}, or move it vertically up to 20 feet using the transmuted matter.
Use your primary ability score as the spellcasting ability for this reference entry.
spell.foundryAdvice: Use the same primary ability score used by Pact of Alchemy as this reference entry's spellcasting ability.

spell.name: Pact of Alchemy Restrain
entries: This is a roll-reference entry for the restraint option granted by {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}. It doesn't grant an additional use of the Pact or change its action economy, range, area, material requirements, duration, or other rules. One creature allowed by the Pact makes a Strength or Dexterity Saving Throw, its choice, against your Invocation Save DC. On a failed save, it is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} by the transmuted matter until the start of your next turn.
Use your primary ability score as the spellcasting ability for this reference entry.
spell.foundryAdvice: The target chooses Strength or Dexterity. Use the same primary ability score used by Pact of Alchemy as this reference entry's spellcasting ability.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Gate
entries: You possess a key to doors that were never built. You create a supernatural object called your Gate Key. It can take any form you choose—a key, coin, card, ring, shard, or similar Tiny object. If the Gate Key is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest, causing the previous Gate Key to disappear.

entries.name: Open the Way
entries: As a Bonus Action while holding your Gate Key, choose an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. You create two linked gateways: one in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you and one at the chosen destination. Each gateway is a vertical opening up to 5 feet wide and 10 feet tall. The gateways last until the start of your next turn. A creature or object entering one gateway immediately exits the other, preserving its direction and momentum. Passing through a gateway isn't considered teleportation.

entries.name: Reach Through
entries: You can see and hear through either gateway. You can make attacks, cast spells, interact with objects, and move through the gateways using normal movement. Distance measured through the gateways is measured from one opening to the other as though the two openings were adjacent.

entries.name: Moving Gate
entries: Once on each of your turns while the gateways exist, you can move either gateway up to 10 feet to another unoccupied space you can see. This requires no action.

entries.caption: Level Progression
rows: The maximum distance of Open the Way increases to 60 feet.
The maximum distance increases to 120 feet, and the gateways can also be horizontal.

The maximum distance increases to 300 feet. You create three gateways instead of two, and any gateway can connect to either of the others. A creature entering a gateway chooses which other gateway it exits from.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Mirror
entries: Your reflection has learned that it need not remain on the other side of the glass. You create a supernatural Pact Mirror, a Tiny reflective object whose appearance you choose, such as a hand mirror, polished coin, crystal shard, metal plate, or glass eye. If it is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest, causing the previous Pact Mirror to disappear.

entries.name: Living Reflection
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can cause your reflection to step out of the Pact Mirror and appear in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet. The reflection looks and sounds exactly like you, occupies its space, has your Size, is intangible, can't attack, manipulate objects, or directly affect creatures, and has a Speed equal to your Speed. It can move through creatures and objects as Difficult Terrain and disappears if it ends its turn inside an object.
You can have only one Living Reflection at a time. It lasts until dismissed, you create another, you become Incapacitated, or it is more than 300 feet away from you.

entries.name: Borrowed Position
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can instantly exchange positions with your Living Reflection. This movement isn't teleportation. Your body and the reflection simply exchange which position each occupies. You can use Borrowed Position a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Mirror Casting
entries: When you cast a spell or use an ability that originates from you, you can choose for it to originate from your space or your Living Reflection's space. You still make all attacks, choose all targets, and provide all components normally. Range is measured from the chosen origin. The reflection itself isn't considered the caster or user of the effect.

entries.name: False Target
entries: When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to exchange places with your Living Reflection immediately before the attack is resolved. The attack then targets whichever of you now occupies your former space. Because the reflection is intangible, an attack directed at it automatically misses unless the effect can affect incorporeal magical manifestations. Using False Target expends one use of Borrowed Position.

entries.name: Through the Looking Glass
entries: While your Living Reflection exists, you can see and hear from its space in addition to your own. You can perceive through it even if you don't have line of sight to it, provided it remains within 300 feet of you.

entries.caption: Level Progression
rows: Your Living Reflection can exist up to 1 mile from you.
You can maintain two Living Reflections simultaneously. When using Borrowed Position or Mirror Casting, choose either reflection.
You can maintain three Living Reflections, and once on each of your turns you can exchange positions with one of them without expending a use of Borrowed Position.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Arsenal
entries: You carry no arsenal upon your back. Steel, ammunition, and instruments of battle wait beyond ordinary space for the instant you call. Every weapon entrusted to the Arsenal remembers your hand. Disarm you, and another blade appears. Empty your quiver, and another arrow is already nocked. So long as the Arsenal answers, you are never truly unarmed. You possess a supernatural extradimensional armory called your Arsenal.

entries.name: Bound Arsenal
entries: During a Short or Long Rest, you can place any number of weapons, shields, ammunition, spellcasting focuses, and tools you are touching into the Arsenal. You can also place an eligible object into the Arsenal as a Bonus Action while holding it.

An object stored there has no weight or bulk for you, is inaccessible to other creatures through ordinary means, doesn't age, rust, decay, or deteriorate while stored, retains its magical properties, charges, and other characteristics, and remains attuned to its current wielder if storing it wouldn't normally end that Attunement. You always know every object currently stored in your Arsenal. There is no inherent limit to the number of eligible objects it can contain.

entries.name: Call to Hand
entries: Once on each of your turns, you can summon one stored object directly into an empty hand without using an action. You can simultaneously return one eligible object you are holding to the Arsenal. If you have no free hand, you can instead cause the summoned object to appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you.

entries.name: Instant Exchange
entries: Whenever you make an attack with a weapon from your Arsenal, you can return it and summon another stored weapon into the same hand before or after that attack, no action required. You can therefore wield different weapons for different attacks made during the same turn.

entries.name: Unbroken Armament
entries: A weapon from your Arsenal recognizes you as its intended wielder. While you wield it, you are proficient with it and you can't be unwillingly disarmed of it unless you are Incapacitated. If it leaves your grasp unwillingly, you can immediately return it to the Arsenal, no action required. A weapon you throw can return to the Arsenal immediately after the attack resolves. This doesn't override an Artifact or another item's property that specifically determines who can wield or possess it.

entries.name: Arsenal Ammunition
entries: Ammunition stored in the Arsenal can appear directly inside a weapon as part of loading or firing that weapon. You don't need a free hand to retrieve ammunition from the Arsenal. After ammunition from the Arsenal hits or misses, you can cause it to return to the Arsenal at the end of the turn if it still exists.

entries.name: Familiar Grip
entries: While wielding a weapon from your Arsenal, you can use Strength or Dexterity for its attack and damage rolls, regardless of which ability that weapon normally uses. This doesn't change any other property of the weapon.

entries.name: Level 2 — Arsenal Enhancement
entries: Every weapon in your Arsenal gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls while you wield it. This bonus becomes +2 at 7th level and +3 at 13th level. If a weapon already grants a bonus to its attack or damage rolls from being a Magic Item, use the higher bonus rather than adding the bonuses together.

entries.name: Level 5 — Awakened Arsenal
entries: Every weapon in your Arsenal is considered magical while you wield it.
Whenever you summon a weapon using Call to Hand, you can immediately alter its handling until it leaves your grasp. Choose one of the following options:

items: {@b Swift.} If the weapon lacks the Finesse property, it gains Finesse.
{@b Far-Reaching.} If it is a melee weapon, its reach increases by 5 feet.
{@b Returning.} If it has the Thrown property, its normal and long ranges are doubled, and it returns to your hand immediately after the attack.
{@b Unburdened.} The weapon loses the Heavy property for you.

entries: You choose again whenever that weapon is summoned.

entries.name: Extra Attack
entries: Starting at 5th level, you can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

entries.name: Level 11 — Arsenal Without Pause
entries: You can summon or return any number of objects from your Arsenal during your turn, provided each exchange occurs immediately before or after you make an attack, cast a spell, or interact with an object. You can summon or dismiss a Shield as part of these exchanges. Changing weapons never interferes with making multiple attacks. A weapon you summon is immediately ready to use, including loaded ammunition if appropriate. You can summon a spellcasting focus from the Arsenal as part of casting a spell and return it immediately afterward.

entries.name: Arsenal Reach
entries: When you make a weapon attack, you can cause the weapon to emerge from the Arsenal at a point you can see within 30 feet of you. Make the attack as though you occupied that point for determining the attack's reach and line of attack. After the attack resolves, the weapon immediately returns to your Arsenal or your hand. You can use Arsenal Reach once per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Armory
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon from your Arsenal, you can make one additional weapon attack with a different stored weapon as part of the same Action. This additional attack requires no Action or Bonus Action.

entries.name: Rain of Steel
entries: Once per Long Rest, you can use an Action to open the Arsenal around yourself. Choose any number of creatures you can see within 60 feet, up to your Proficiency Bonus. For each chosen creature, select a weapon currently stored in your Arsenal and make one weapon attack against that creature with the selected weapon. A weapon can be used for only one of these attacks. After all attacks resolve, every weapon used immediately returns to the Arsenal.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Vessel
entries: Magic need not be spent when it is cast. Some power can be caught, sealed, and taught to wait. You create a supernatural container called your Pact Vessel. Its form is your choice: a bottle, lantern, gemstone, scroll case, orb, reliquary, card, ring, or another Tiny object capable of symbolically containing something. If the Vessel is lost or destroyed, you can recreate it during a Short or Long Rest. Creating a new Vessel causes the previous one to disappear, but any magic stored within it is preserved.

entries.name: Seal a Spell
entries: When you cast a spell with a casting time of an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, you can seal the spell inside your Pact Vessel instead of producing its normal effect. The spell is cast normally: a spell slot is expended normally, Material components are provided and consumed normally, and any other resources required by the spell are expended normally. The spell produces no effect when sealed. The Vessel can hold one sealed spell at a time. You can't seal a spell whose level is higher than the maximum shown by Deepening Vessel.

entries.name: Release the Spell
entries: While holding your Pact Vessel, you can release a sealed spell using the same type of action required by the spell's normal casting time. When released, no spell slot is expended and no Material components are required again. You make all targeting and other choices at the moment of release, and range and area are measured from the releaser's current position. The spell uses the same spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus it had when sealed, and it counts as being cast by the creature that originally sealed it.
Once released, the spell disappears from the Vessel.

entries.name: Held Casting
entries: A sealed spell remains in the Vessel until it is released, replaced, or willingly erased. There is no time limit on how long it can remain sealed, and finishing a rest doesn't remove it.

entries.name: Pass the Vessel
entries: Another creature can hold your Pact Vessel and release a spell stored within it. When it does so, the spell still uses the original caster's spellcasting statistics and treats the creature releasing it as the point of origin. The creature doesn't need to know the spell or possess spellcasting. If the spell requires Concentration, the creature that released the spell maintains that Concentration.

entries.name: Replace the Contents
entries: If you seal another spell while the Vessel already contains one, you can erase the existing spell and replace it. The erased spell and resources originally spent to cast it aren't refunded.

entries.name: Level 5 — Greater Vessel
entries: You can seal spells of 2nd level or lower. Your Vessel can now hold two spells simultaneously. When you seal a spell, choose which space within the Vessel contains it.

entries.name: Level 11 — Vault of Spells
entries: You can seal spells of 4th level or lower, and your Vessel can hold three spells simultaneously. when a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell of a level you can store, you can use your Reaction to attempt to capture it. Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability against a DC equal to 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the spell is sealed inside an empty space in your Vessel instead of taking effect. The original caster still expends the spell slot and any components normally.
Once you successfully capture a spell this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Vessel
entries: You can seal spells of 6th level or lower, and your Vessel can hold five spells simultaneously.

items: {@b Swift Release.} Once on each of your turns, when you release a spell with a casting time of an Action, you can release it as a Bonus Action instead.
{@b Perfect Capture.} When you use your Reaction to capture a spell of 6th level or lower, you no longer make an ability check. The spell is automatically sealed if your Vessel has an empty space.
{@b Overflow.} If your Vessel is full when you successfully capture a spell, you can immediately erase one stored spell to make room for the captured one.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Brand
entries: Some marks are written on flesh. Yours is written on certainty. Once you have claimed a creature with your Brand, distance becomes less useful, concealment less reliable, and escape increasingly difficult. You gain the ability to place a supernatural mark called your Pact Brand upon another creature.

entries.name: Place the Brand
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet. The creature becomes Branded by you until you dismiss the Brand, you Brand another creature, or the creature dies. You can have only one Branded creature at a time. The Brand can appear visibly on the creature in a form you choose, or remain completely invisible. Placing the Brand doesn't require a saving throw and doesn't by itself Charm, damage, or otherwise control the creature.

entries.name: Hunter's Certainty
entries: While the Branded creature is on the same plane as you, you always know its direction from you, its approximate distance from you, whether it is conscious or unconscious, and whether it is currently moving. The creature gains no indication that you are sensing this information.

entries.name: Marked Beyond Sight
entries: You can perceive the Branded creature even when it is Invisible, Heavily Obscured, Hidden from you, or behind ordinary walls or other physical cover. This doesn't allow you to see the surrounding area through those obstructions. You simply perceive the creature's exact position as a supernatural outline. The Brand doesn't grant line of effect through barriers.

entries.name: Claim the Opening
entries: Once on each of your turns when you deal damage to the Branded creature, you can deal an additional {@damage 1d6} Force or Psychic damage, your choice. You choose the damage type each time.

entries.name: Refuse Escape
entries: When the Branded creature willingly teleports or otherwise instantly moves to another space within 120 feet of you, you can use your Reaction to immediately move to an unoccupied space within 10 feet of it. This movement isn't teleportation, and you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks from this movement.

entries.name: Level 5 — Relentless Mark
entries: Claim the Opening increases to {@damage 1d8}. The Branded creature gains no benefit against you from being Invisible. You can target it with attacks and effects that require you to see the target as long as your Brand allows you to perceive its exact position.

entries.name: Level 11 — Unbroken Pursuit
entries: You can maintain Brands on two creatures simultaneously. When you use Place the Brand while already at this limit, choose which existing Brand ends. Refuse Escape can trigger when a Branded creature teleports or instantly moves from anywhere within 300 feet of you. When you follow it, you can appear within 5 feet of the creature instead of 10 feet.

entries.name: Level 17 — No Refuge
entries: You can maintain Brands on up to three creatures simultaneously. Your Brand functions across planar boundaries. You always know which plane each Branded creature occupies.

entries.name: Follow Anywhere
entries: When a Branded creature teleports, travels to another plane, or is magically transported elsewhere, you can use your Reaction to follow it. You appear in the nearest safe unoccupied space within 10 feet of the creature, even if doing so crosses planar boundaries.

entries.name: Final Claim
entries: Claim the Opening increases to {@damage 2d8}.
Once on each of your turns when you damage a Branded creature, you can also choose one of the following effects:

items: {@b Hamper.} Its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
{@b Expose.} It can't benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover against you until the start of your next turn.

{@b Anchor.} Until the start of your next turn, if it attempts to teleport or travel to another plane, you immediately know and can use Follow Anywhere even if you would normally be unable to perceive the attempt.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of Alchemy
entries: {@i Understand. Deconstruct. Reconstruct.}

Once on each of your turns, requiring no Action, choose a point you can see within 30 feet. You can transmute nonliving matter within a 15-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point. You can reshape, separate, combine, move, compress, expand, repair, dismantle, or reconstruct the affected matter with perfect precision. You can't create matter from nothing, but you can freely redistribute the matter available within the Sphere. You automatically understand the composition and physical structure of matter you transmute.

For example, you can raise walls or pillars, create spikes, trenches, bridges, restraints, weapons, armor, tools, or openings, repair broken objects, dismantle structures, reshape terrain, or reconstruct available material into another form. Everything created by the transmutation is physically real and permanent. You can't directly transmute a creature's body.

Whenever this Pact requires an attack roll or Saving Throw, use your primary ability score as though it were your spellcasting ability. Your Invocation attack modifier equals your Proficiency Bonus + your primary ability modifier, and your Invocation Save DC equals 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your primary ability modifier.
Whenever you transmute matter, you can also choose one of the following effects as part of the same use:

items: Make an Invocation attack roll against one creature within the Sphere. On a hit, it takes {@scaledamage 2d10|5,9|2d10} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, your choice.

Choose one creature within the Sphere. It makes a Strength Saving Throw. On a failed save, you push or pull it up to 20 feet, knock it {@condition Prone|XPHB}, or move it vertically up to 20 feet using the transmuted matter.

Choose one creature within the Sphere. It makes a Strength or Dexterity Saving Throw, its choice. On a failed save, it is {@condition Restrained|XPHB} by the transmuted matter until the start of your next turn.

Choose a point within the Sphere. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet of that point make a Dexterity Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@scaledamage 2d10|5,9|2d10} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, your choice. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

entries: These effects can take whatever physical form the available matter allows, such as stone spikes erupting from the ground, a wall slamming into a creature, metal closing around its limbs, pillars launching it upward, or debris striking everything in an area. For roll controls in 5etools and Foundry, use {@spell Pact of Alchemy Attack|FftForbiddenTome|Attack}, {@spell Pact of Alchemy Area Attack|FftForbiddenTome|Area Attack}, {@spell Pact of Alchemy Move|FftForbiddenTome|Move}, or {@spell Pact of Alchemy Restrain|FftForbiddenTome|Restrain}.

{@b Level 5.} Your range becomes 60 feet. Each use affects a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered at a point within range; you can redistribute matter anywhere within it. You can transmute worn or carried nonmagical objects, but not a creature's body. Pact damage becomes {@damage 4d10}. An effect that normally targets one creature can target up to two instead.

{@b Level 9.} Your range becomes 120 feet, and each use can affect a 60-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you choose within that range. You can transmute magical matter and Magic Items, except Artifacts. You can also rearrange matter at the atomic level, converting available nonliving matter into different nonliving substances of equal total mass. Damage dealt by this Pact becomes {@damage 6d10} and can be Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Piercing, Slashing, or Thunder damage. When you use one of this Pact's Saving Throw effects, you can affect any number of creatures of your choice within the transmuted Sphere.

optionalfeature.name: Matter Reserve
entries: {@i Nothing is wasted. You simply haven't used it yet.}

Whenever you use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can store any amount of affected nonliving matter instead of leaving it behind. Stored matter has no weight or volume, doesn't decay or change, remains indefinitely, and has no storage limit. Whenever you use Pact of Alchemy, stored matter counts as though it were physically present within its range.
You can also:

items: Store complete non-Artifact objects and release them exactly as stored, including contents, moving parts, ammunition, charges, and magical properties.
Store liquids, gases, heat, pressure, electrical charge, momentum, and other physical states you can manipulate through {@optfeature State Exchange|FftForbiddenTome}.
Instantly replace matter you transmute with something from your reserve, allowing one material to disappear as another takes its place.
Store a structure, machine, vehicle, weapon, or other construction in separate pieces and later reconstruct the complete object automatically.
Record the physical structure of anything you store. If you later have sufficient material, Pact of Alchemy can reproduce that structure without requiring the original object.
Recall any nonliving matter or object you previously released from the reserve back into it while it remains within Pact of Alchemy's range.
When something created primarily from your stored matter is broken or destroyed, you can return its remaining material to the reserve immediately, requiring no Action.
Release stored matter already moving, spinning, pressurized, heated, charged, or otherwise carrying any physical state it possessed when stored.
Use stored compatible matter for {@optfeature Reconstruction|FftForbiddenTome}, including blood, bone, organs, and other physical tissue.
Permanently erase anything stored in the reserve without releasing it.

entries: When an unattended non-Artifact object, projectile, collapsing structure, falling debris, liquid, gas, or other nonliving matter within range would affect a creature or area, you can use your Reaction to store all or part of it before it resolves.
{@b Level 13.} You can store or release unattended nonliving matter within Pact of Alchemy's range at any time on your turn, requiring no Action.

You can also release any number of stored objects or constructions simultaneously. They can appear assembled, positioned, oriented, and moving however you choose, provided each could be produced through Pact of Alchemy. When you release a stored construction, you can automatically integrate it with surrounding matter. A stored door can appear already fitted into a wall, a bridge can connect two surfaces, armor can appear already worn by a willing creature, or machinery can appear already connected to an existing system.
{@b Level 17.} Your reserve can be accessed from any distance or plane.

Stored matter counts as present wherever you use Pact of Alchemy, {@optfeature Reconstruction|FftForbiddenTome}, {@optfeature Transmutation Array|FftForbiddenTome}, or another Pact of Alchemy Invocation. Anything you can affect through Transmutation Array can be stored directly into the reserve or replaced with stored matter. In addition, when you transmute something using stored matter, you can have every unused fragment, excess material, waste product, heat, momentum, or other physical remainder return directly to the reserve instead of being lost.

optionalfeature.name: Deconstruction
entries: {@i Reconstruction is a choice. Breaking something down is much easier.}

Whenever you deal damage with {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can make the damage Force damage. This damage ignores Resistance; Immunity is treated as Resistance, which you then ignore. Against objects and structures, you deal maximum damage, double that damage, and ignore Damage Thresholds, hardness, and similar defenses.

When you hit a creature with Pact of Alchemy, it must make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failed save, choose two of the following effects. On a successful save, choose one:

items: Its AC is reduced by 2 until the start of your next turn.
Its Speed is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.
It can't take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
It has Disadvantage on the next Saving Throw it makes against Pact of Alchemy before the start of your next turn.
One non-Artifact object it is wearing or carrying is dismantled into its component materials. If the object is magical, this option only works once you reach Level 9.

entries: {@b Level 9.} On a failed save, choose three effects instead of two. You can also use Pact of Alchemy to dismantle magical barriers, constructs, and non-Artifact magical objects as though they were ordinary matter.

If a magical effect has created or is sustaining the matter you attempt to dismantle, make an ability check using your primary ability modifier against DC 10 + the spell's level. On a success, that portion of the effect is destroyed.

optionalfeature.name: Reconstruction
entries: {@i If the structure still exists, it can be rebuilt.}
You can use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome} on yourself and willing creatures, allowing you to transmute living tissue without changing the creature's identity, memories, or soul.
Whenever you do so, choose one creature within the Pact's Sphere and one of the following:

items: Restore {@dice 4d10} + your primary ability modifier Hit Points. You can restore Hit Points this way a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your primary ability modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
End the {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}, or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition.
Repair broken bones, damaged organs, scars, burns, and other physical injuries.
Restore a missing limb or body part if enough living tissue remains to reconstruct it.
Reshape the creature's physical appearance, including height, build, facial features, voice, hair, skin, and similar traits. The creature's statistics don't change.

entries: You can also use this Invocation on a creature at 0 Hit Points. It immediately regains Hit Points instead of making Death Saving Throws.
{@b Level 9.} Healing becomes {@dice 6d10} + your primary ability modifier. The number of times you can restore Hit Points this way doesn't change.

You can restore missing limbs or organs even if none of the original tissue remains, and you can also end the {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, {@condition Petrified|XPHB}, or {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition. If a creature died within the last minute and its body is still present, you can use Pact of Alchemy on it to reconstruct the body and return it to life with 1 Hit Point, provided its soul is free and willing.

optionalfeature.name: Reactive Transmutation
entries: {@i Anything nearby can become a defense before the attack finishes.}

When you or a creature you can see within range is targeted by an attack, spell, or other harmful effect, you can use your Reaction to immediately transmute nearby nonliving matter before the effect is resolved.
Choose one of the following:

items: Raise or reshape material into cover. The target gains +5 AC against the triggering attack and Resistance to all damage dealt by that attack.
If the triggering effect requires a Saving Throw, the target gains Advantage on that save. If it succeeds, it takes no damage from the effect; if it fails, it takes only half damage.

Create a barrier between the source and the target. If the triggering attack, spell, or effect requires a clear path, line of sight, or line of effect, it fails against that target unless it can pass through or destroy the barrier.

If a creature moves through or into matter you can transmute, force it to make a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, its movement immediately ends, it is knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}, and becomes {@condition Restrained|XPHB} until the start of your next turn.

If the triggering effect would push, pull, lift, knock Prone, or otherwise forcibly move a creature, you can reshape the surrounding matter to anchor that creature in place. The forced movement and Prone effect fail.

entries: You can use this Invocation a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your primary ability modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can affect up to two creatures with the same Reaction if both are within range. The matter created or altered by this Reaction remains physically real afterward.
{@b Level 9.} You can affect any number of creatures of your choice within range with the same Reaction.

If your transmutation causes the triggering attack or effect to miss, fail, or deal no damage to at least one protected creature, you can immediately make one Pact of Alchemy attack against the source of the triggering effect as part of the same Reaction. If that attack hits, it deals the Pact's normal damage and you can also apply one of Pact of Alchemy's Saving Throw effects to the same target without replacing the attack.

optionalfeature.name: Soul Binding
entries: {@i The body is only one vessel.}

When a willing creature within range dies, you can use your Reaction to bind its soul to one non-Artifact object, suit of armor, statue, or construct within range. The creature immediately returns to consciousness with 1 Hit Point, using the chosen object as its new body. It retains its identity, memories, class features, proficiencies, Ability Scores, spellcasting, and other abilities, but its creature type becomes Construct. It doesn't need to eat, drink, breathe, or sleep, and it is immune to disease and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

Its new body can move and manipulate objects as though it possessed a normal body. If the chosen vessel has no natural means of movement or manipulation, alchemy reshapes it enough to provide them without changing its fundamental form. Its AC becomes at least 18, its Speed becomes at least 30 feet, and damage to the vessel reduces the creature's Hit Points normally. Repairing the vessel through {@optfeature Reconstruction|FftForbiddenTome} can restore its Hit Points normally.

The creature remains bound indefinitely. Destroying the vessel doesn't destroy its soul; the soul remains attached to the remains until restored, transferred to another suitable vessel, or returned to a living body through {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}. You can use this Invocation a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your primary ability modifier (minimum of once), regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

{@b Level 9.} You can bind a willing living creature without requiring it to die first, transferring its soul directly into a chosen vessel within range. Its original body becomes Unconscious but remains alive, and you can later return the soul to that body or transfer it into another suitable vessel through Pact of Alchemy.

optionalfeature.name: Alchemical Armament
entries: {@i Anything you can shape can become a weapon.}

Whenever you use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can immediately form available nonliving matter within range into weapons, armor, shields, ammunition, or other combat equipment and place them directly into the hands or onto the bodies of willing creatures within range. Equipment created this way can reshape itself whenever its wielder attacks, is attacked, moves, or uses it, requiring no Action.
A weapon created or altered this way:

items: can use your primary ability modifier for its attack and damage rolls instead of Strength or Dexterity;
counts as magical;
gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls;
can deal Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, chosen for each attack;
can possess any weapon properties appropriate to its current form;
can use any Weapon Mastery property appropriate to its current form if its wielder can use Weapon Mastery;
immediately reforms in its wielder's hand after being thrown, dropped, broken, or disarmed;
deals an additional {@damage 1d10} damage once on each of its wielder's turns when it hits.

entries: Armor or a shield created or altered this way can be donned or removed instantly, imposes no Strength requirement or Stealth Disadvantage, and grants its wearer a +1 bonus to AC in addition to its normal AC. Once per round when a creature wearing armor or wielding a shield you created takes damage, you can immediately reshape the equipment, requiring no Action or Reaction, reducing that damage by {@dice 1d10} + your primary ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

{@b Level 7.} The bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, and AC becomes +2. The additional weapon damage becomes {@damage 2d10}, and the damage reduction becomes {@dice 2d10} + your primary ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
{@b Level 9.} The bonus to attack rolls, damage rolls, and AC becomes +3.

Weapons created through this Invocation can deal Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Thunder, Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, chosen for each attack. Their damage ignores Resistance, and Immunity to that damage is treated as Resistance, which the attack then ignores. The additional weapon damage becomes {@damage 4d10}. Once on each turn when one of these weapons hits, its wielder can also apply one of Pact of Alchemy's single-target Saving Throw effects to the target without replacing the attack.
The damage reduction becomes {@dice 4d10} + your primary ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

optionalfeature.name: Transmutation Array
entries: {@i You don't need to be standing where the transmutation begins.}

By touching a nonliving surface for 1 minute, you can permanently inscribe {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome} into it. The inscription can be visible, hidden inside the material, or completely indistinguishable from the surrounding surface. You can maintain a number of these inscriptions equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your primary ability modifier.

Whenever you use Pact of Alchemy, you can cause it to originate from any inscription you created on the same plane, regardless of distance. The Pact's range is measured from that inscription rather than from you.
While an inscription exists:

items: You know whether it still exists, its general surroundings, and the composition and structure of matter within the normal range of Pact of Alchemy around it.
You can perceive contact, pressure, vibration, movement, temperature, damage, and other physical changes occurring through matter around it.
You don't need line of sight to use Pact of Alchemy through it.
You can use Pact of Alchemy's attacks and Saving Throw effects through it against creatures whose location you can determine through the surrounding matter.
You can reconstruct, dismantle, repair, open, seal, reshape, or otherwise transmute matter around it remotely.

You can record the exact structure of an object or construction you transmute through it. You can later reproduce that structure from suitable matter without needing to remember every individual component yourself.

You can specify a physical condition that causes a transmutation to occur automatically, such as a creature stepping somewhere, a door opening, an object being removed, a particular substance appearing, the surface taking damage, or a specified amount of weight touching it.
A transmutation triggered this way requires no Action or Reaction from you and can occur even while you are Unconscious or on another part of the plane.
An automatic transmutation doesn't prevent you from using Pact of Alchemy normally on that turn.

You can leave an instruction for the inscription to continuously maintain a physical result. It can repair a structure when damaged, keep a passage open or sealed, maintain a particular shape, remove unwanted material as it appears, or repeatedly perform another purely physical transmutation you could normally perform with Pact of Alchemy.
You can change or erase any instruction you placed in one of your inscriptions regardless of distance.

entries: You can also transfer nonliving matter between two of your inscriptions on the same plane. Matter entering the range of one inscription can be deconstructed and reconstructed within range of another inscription, preserving its total mass unless another feature allows you to ignore that restriction. This can transport objects, raw materials, ammunition, equipment, liquids, gases, or entire sections of structures. You can dismiss any inscription at any time, requiring no Action and regardless of distance.
{@b Level 15.} Your inscriptions become a connected network.

Whenever you use Pact of Alchemy through one inscription, you can cause the same use to originate simultaneously from any number of your inscriptions. Each location can produce a different physical transmutation and can choose a different Pact of Alchemy combat effect. A creature can be affected separately by each inscription that can reach it.

You can also transmit physical changes through the network. For example, damage to one structure can cause another structure to change, movement at one inscription can operate machinery somewhere else, or material supplied to one inscription can be reconstructed simultaneously at several others. You can move a complete nonliving object from one inscription to another without dismantling it in the process.
{@b Level 17.} Your inscriptions no longer need to be on the same plane as you or each other.

You can use Pact of Alchemy through any of them across planar boundaries and transfer matter between them. You can also transport willing creatures between two inscriptions. The creature is deconstructed at one and reconstructed at the other without changing its identity, memories, equipment, or soul. Whenever an inscription is destroyed, you can immediately use Pact of Alchemy through it one final time before it ceases to exist, requiring no Action or Reaction.

optionalfeature.name: Catalysis
entries: {@i Every reaction is just matter waiting for permission.}

Whenever you use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can control chemical and physical reactions within the affected matter. You can make them occur instantly, slow them, stop them, reverse them, or determine exactly how they proceed.
You can:

items: Ignite, extinguish, corrode, dissolve, crystallize, precipitate, oxidize, reduce, neutralize, polymerize, decompose, or trigger similar reactions.
Ignore normal requirements such as ignition, catalysts, pressure, temperature, activation energy, or reaction time.
Choose the exact products of a reaction whenever multiple physically possible results exist.
Prevent unwanted byproducts and produce materials at effectively perfect purity.
Force a reversible reaction completely toward either side.
Generate or consume heat, pressure, electricity, gases, acids, fuels, and other products available from the reacting matter.
Cause matter to combust, detonate, rupture, rapidly expand, collapse, freeze, melt, vaporize, or undergo another physically possible phase reaction.
Instantly neutralize poisons, acids, explosives, reactive chemicals, unstable materials, and similar substances you can transmute.
Determine every physically possible reaction available to matter you understand and what each reaction would produce.
Cause a reaction to continue automatically as long as suitable material remains.

entries: When you deal damage through Pact of Alchemy, the damage can be Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, or Thunder, and you can determine the physical reaction responsible. When one of your reactions would release destructive energy, you can direct that energy instead of allowing it to disperse naturally. You can concentrate it into one creature, spread it through an area, redirect it elsewhere within Pact of Alchemy's range, or store it through {@optfeature Matter Reserve|FftForbiddenTome} if that Invocation can contain the resulting physical state.
{@b Level 15.} You have complete control over how your reactions spread.

A reaction affects only the matter, creatures, objects, or spaces you choose and stops exactly where you decide. It can travel through compatible material regardless of ordinary reaction speed. You can also make several different reactions sustain one another. For example, one reaction can generate heat for another, produce gas that fuels a third, or continuously recycle its products back into usable reactants.
If a reaction would normally consume a finite reagent, you can precisely control how much is consumed, down to an individual portion of the material.
{@b Level 17.} Starting conditions no longer matter.

If the final result is a physically possible arrangement of the available matter and energy, you can force the entire process to occur directly, regardless of whether a natural reaction pathway exists.
You can also:

items: Reverse a completed reaction back into its original reactants.
Convert the energy released by one reaction directly into another physical form, such as heat into electricity, pressure into motion, or combustion into a shockwave.
Maintain matter in a normally unstable physical or chemical state indefinitely until you allow it to react.
Make a reaction occur throughout any amount of matter affected by the same use of Pact of Alchemy simultaneously.
Cause a reaction to repeatedly cycle between states without consuming additional material unless energy or matter actually leaves the system.

entries: If you also possess {@optfeature Philosopher's Stone|FftForbiddenTome}, conservation is no longer required; you can supply or remove whatever matter or energy a reaction lacks.

optionalfeature.name: Living Transmutation
entries: {@i Living matter is still matter.}
You can use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome} to directly transmute the bodies of creatures within range.

A willing creature can be altered freely. An unwilling creature must make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failed save, choose two of the following effects. On a successful save, choose one:

items: The creature takes {@damage 8d10} Force damage as part of its body is broken down and reconstructed.
Its Speed becomes 0 until the end of your next turn.
It becomes {@condition Blinded|XPHB}, {@condition Deafened|XPHB}, or {@condition Restrained|XPHB} until the end of your next turn.
It can't take Reactions until the end of your next turn.
Reduce its AC by 3 until the end of your next turn.

Alter, remove, or create limbs, eyes, natural weapons, wings, gills, or similar physical structures. A change that would remove one of the creature's movement modes, senses, or natural attacks lasts until the creature finishes a Long Rest or is restored by magic capable of repairing its body.
Change its Size by up to two categories, to a minimum of Tiny and maximum of Gargantuan, until you change it again or the effect is removed.

Reshape its body enough to prevent one physical ability of your choice from functioning, such as flight from wings, a Bite attack, a Breath Weapon requiring physical organs, or another ability that depends directly on its anatomy. This doesn't suppress spellcasting or abilities that don't depend on its physical body.

entries: You can freely use these changes for noncombat purposes on willing creatures, including changing appearance, sex, height, build, voice, anatomy, biological functions, or other physical traits. These alterations can be permanent. You can't alter a creature's memories, personality, class features, learned abilities, identity, or soul with this Invocation.
{@b Level 17.} On a failed Saving Throw, choose any number of the effects instead of two.

You can also completely reconstruct a creature's body into another physical form you understand. The creature retains its identity, memories, Ability Scores, class features, and soul, but you can replace its anatomy, Size, movement organs, natural weapons, senses, and other physical structures with those you know how to create. A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by the Force damage can instead be completely deconstructed, leaving no corpse unless you choose otherwise.

optionalfeature.name: State Exchange
entries: {@i Matter doesn't care where a property came from.}

Whenever you use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can transfer, exchange, divide, or combine physical properties between creatures, objects, structures, or substances within range. An unwilling creature makes a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, it can be affected normally.
You can manipulate:

items: Hit Point damage, injuries, physical conditions, diseases, poisons, and missing body parts.
Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Hit Point Maximum, AC, Size, mass, weight, density, and physical age.
Anatomy, movement speeds, senses, Natural Armor, natural weapons, regeneration, and other bodily traits.
Physical Resistances, Immunities, and Vulnerabilities.
Material composition and properties such as hardness, flexibility, conductivity, friction, temperature, pressure, momentum, and electrical charge.
Physical transformations or magical effects whose primary effect is altering the target's body or material form.

entries: The transferred property becomes physically real on its new subject. Pact of Alchemy automatically reconstructs the receiving subject enough for it to function. You can store transferred properties inside unattended objects, divide one property among several subjects, or combine the same property from several subjects into one. When a creature you can see within range would take damage, gain a physical condition, or be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can use your Reaction to transfer all or part of that result to another valid subject before it occurs.
Changes made this way can be permanent. You can't transfer memories, personality, knowledge, class levels, learned abilities, identity, or souls.
{@b Level 17.} You can copy a physical property instead of removing it from its source and apply it to any number of subjects within range.

You can also isolate individual parts of a larger trait, such as taking only wings, regeneration, Strength, Natural Armor, a Breath Weapon's physical anatomy, or a damage Immunity. If you possess {@optfeature Philosopher's Stone|FftForbiddenTome}, you no longer need a source. You can directly create, remove, increase, reduce, or rewrite any physical property you understand.

optionalfeature.name: Magic Is Matter
entries: {@i Magic is still something. Something can be transmuted.}

Starting at 5th level, spells and magical effects within {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}'s range can be treated as matter. You can reshape, move, divide, combine, solidify, dismantle, absorb, or otherwise restructure them.

entries.name: Magical Energy
entries: Magic you absorb can be stored as Magical Energy. There is no maximum to how much Magical Energy you can hold, it remains until spent, and Short Rests, Long Rests, and similar recovery never restore it. You must acquire it yourself from spells, magical effects, magical phenomena, enchanted locations, or other suitable magical sources.
A magical source without a spell level has an equivalent level based on its magical strength. You can drain all or only part of a source.

entries.name: Absorb Magic
entries: When a spell is cast or would resolve within your Pact's range, you can use your Reaction to absorb it before it takes effect. Make a check using your primary ability modifier and Proficiency Bonus against DC 10 + the spell's level. On a success, the spell produces no effect and you gain the Magical Energy shown on the table. Magic you control can be absorbed automatically.

entries.name: Creating Spells
entries: You can spend Magical Energy to reproduce any spell you know of and understand, regardless of Spell List. You don't need to know or prepare it through a class, expend a Spell Slot, or provide Verbal or Somatic components. There is no per-rest use limit; Magical Energy is the resource.

You can't reproduce a spell above the maximum shown for your character level. Use your Invocation Save DC and Invocation Attack Modifier. Concentration applies normally if the original spell requires it.

entries.name: Spell Transmutation
entries: Whenever you reproduce or manipulate a spell through this Invocation, you can freely alter its magical structure as part of the same use. You can change its damage type, area shape, point of origin, direction or path, area and proportions, which valid creatures, objects, or spaces are affected, and its magical or physical manifestation. You can combine these changes, and they don't normally alter the spell's level or Magical Energy cost.
For example, you could turn {@spell Fireball|XPHB} into a Line, make {@spell Lightning Bolt|XPHB} a Sphere, curve a spell around allies, or change {@spell Disintegrate|XPHB} to deal Cold damage.

entries.name: Costly Components
entries: If a spell has a Material component with a listed monetary value, you can pay that value using any combination of the normal component or money, 1 additional Magical Energy per 100 gp rounded up, or your own vitality at a rate of 10 Hit Points per 1 Magical Energy equivalent.

You can also offer your own possessions, blood, body parts, organs, senses, knowledge, memories, or another genuine personal sacrifice of comparable value. Anything sacrificed this way is actually lost; restoring it later doesn't refund the payment. Hit Points sacrificed this way aren't damage. Any portion of a costly component replaced by Magical Energy, Hit Points, or another sacrifice must be paid each time you reproduce the spell.

{@b Level 9.} You gain finer control over existing magic. You can move an ongoing effect or its point of origin, transfer it between valid creatures, objects, or areas, reshape magical barriers and create openings through them, and store transmuted magic through {@optfeature Matter Reserve|FftForbiddenTome}. You can also preserve the magical structure of effects you personally transmute.
{@i Example: move magical darkness onto an object, transfer an ongoing effect to another valid target, or open a doorway through a Wall of Force without destroying the whole wall.}

{@b Level 13.} You can separate, combine, and transfer distinct magical properties such as damage, damage type, light, darkness, flight, restraint, concealment, protection, or another separable property. You can attach them to another compatible magical effect or non-Artifact object.
{@i Example: remove magical fire from one weapon and place it into another object, or remove the damaging part of an effect while leaving its restraint intact.}

{@b Level 15.} You can transmute pure magic even when it has no physical manifestation, and you can affect Instantaneous spells and magical effects during the instant they resolve. Your Reaction can reshape, redirect, divide, merge, solidify, dismantle, absorb, or transfer all or part of an incoming magical effect before it finishes resolving.
{@i Example: split an incoming Fireball into several smaller explosions, redirect part of an Instantaneous magical blast, or absorb it entirely before it takes effect.}

{@b Level 17.} You can permanently reforge magical structures. You can extract properties from non-Artifact Magic Items, permanently graft magical properties onto compatible non-Artifact objects, stabilize temporary effects beyond their normal duration or Concentration, turn magical effects into permanent magical objects or back into active magical manifestations, and reconstruct magical effects you previously transmuted by supplying their Magical Energy cost.
{@i Example: move a Magic Item's property into another suitable object, make a temporary magical wall permanent, or solidify a magical effect into an object and later release it again.}

entries.name: With Philosopher's Stone
entries: If you possess {@optfeature Philosopher's Stone|FftForbiddenTome}, equivalent exchange no longer applies. You can create the matter, energy, and magic required by this Invocation from nothing. You can reproduce any spell of 9th level or lower that you know of and fully understand with no Magical Energy cost, Spell Slot, components, costly or consumed components, Hit Point sacrifice, existing magical source, or other payment. There is no usage limit. You can still freely alter the spell through Spell Transmutation.

Outside reproducing a spell's normal effect, this Invocation can't directly create or duplicate Artifacts or directly alter souls, time, causality, memories, personality, or identity. You can voluntarily sacrifice your own memories through Costly Components.

optionalfeature.name: Philosopher's Stone
entries: {@i Equivalent exchange is no longer a requirement.}

Your understanding of transmutation exceeds the ordinary laws that govern matter. When you use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can create nonliving matter from nothing, erase it completely, or alter its mass, volume, density, composition, state, and physical properties without preserving any of them. Matter you create is real, stable, and permanent.

You can create any nonliving substance whose composition you understand, including precious materials, complex compounds, magical materials, and substances that normally require extraordinary circumstances to exist. Artifacts can't be created or duplicated this way.
In addition, Pact of Alchemy gains all of the following capabilities:

items: You can directly transmute living creatures. An unwilling creature makes a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, you can alter its flesh, bones, organs, limbs, Size, physical structure, or appearance. You can't directly alter its memories, personality, identity, or soul.
You can transmute energy into matter and matter into energy. Fire can become stone, lightning can become metal, a wall can become heat or force, and similar conversions are possible.

When Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, or Thunder damage would be dealt within range, you can use your Reaction to transmute the energy before it takes effect. You can prevent that damage, redirect it to another creature or point within range, change its damage type to another of those types, or convert it into physical matter.

You can transmute an ongoing spell or magical effect that has a physical manifestation within range. You can reshape its manifested matter or energy, change its physical form, divide it, combine it with another manifestation, move it, or convert it between matter and energy. This doesn't grant control over minds, souls, time, space, or purely informational effects.

You can reconstruct a non-Artifact object that has been completely destroyed even if none of its original matter remains, provided you have previously examined it closely enough to understand its structure.

You can create complete functioning mechanisms, machines, weapons, armor, vehicles, buildings, and other nonliving constructions directly from raw or created matter. If you understand what the creation is intended to do, the transmutation supplies the physical structure required for it to function.
You can separate mixtures and compounds into their individual substances with perfect precision, or combine substances into any chemically or physically possible material you understand.
You can freely change matter between solid, liquid, gas, plasma, and other physically possible states without requiring the usual temperature or pressure.
You automatically understand the composition, internal structure, weaknesses, damage, impurities, and physical properties of any matter you can perceive within range.

You can cause a transmutation to remain unfinished until a condition you specify occurs. When that condition occurs, the remaining transformation completes instantly. You can have a number of these delayed transmutations equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your primary ability modifier at one time.

You can make a transmutation continuously respond to its surroundings. A wall can repair itself when damaged, armor can reshape around attacks, a bridge can extend as creatures cross it, or a structure can alter itself when specified physical conditions occur. These changes require no further Action from you.

entries: Whenever you use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can perform any number of separate transmutations within its affected area. Each creature, object, structure, or portion of matter can undergo a different transformation. For each of those transmutations, you can use two of Pact of Alchemy's combat effects instead of one, including choosing the same effect twice. Pact of Alchemy's damage becomes {@damage 10d10}, and you can deal maximum damage instead of rolling.

Whenever you use {@optfeature Reconstruction|FftForbiddenTome}, you can recreate missing tissue even when no original matter remains, rebuild a completely destroyed body, restore a creature regardless of how long it has been dead if its soul is free and willing, or restore its Hit Points to its maximum by expending two uses of Reconstruction's healing.

Whenever you use {@optfeature Soul Binding|FftForbiddenTome}, you can create the vessel from nothing as part of the same use. You can also construct a fully functional artificial body rather than binding the soul to an existing object. You can affect Artifacts with your transmutations, but you can't create, duplicate, permanently destroy, or remove an Artifact's intrinsic magical properties unless that Artifact could normally be affected in that way.
A permanent transmutation you create can't be reversed, suppressed, or dispelled against your will except by an Artifact or an effect of 9th level or higher.

entries.name: Perfect Understanding
entries: Anything within {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}'s range that you can perceive is immediately understood by you, including its composition, structure, function, physical properties, magical properties, and any spell or magical effect affecting it. For {@optfeature Magic Is Matter|FftForbiddenTome}, any spell or magical effect you perceive is considered fully understood.

entries.name: Create Magic Items
entries: You can create any non-Artifact Magic Item from nothing if you understand its physical and magical properties. The item is real and permanent, requiring no materials, gold, crafting time, or existing magical source. You can also freely add, remove, combine, or rewrite magical properties of non-Artifact Magic Items.

entries.name: Universal Conversion
entries: Matter, energy, and magic are interchangeable through {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}. You can freely convert one into another without requiring an equivalent source.

entries.name: Perfect Creation
entries: Anything you create through {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome} can appear already complete, assembled, functional, and in any state you understand. This can include machines, vehicles, buildings, weapons, armor, biological tissue, magical devices, and other complex structures.

entries.name: Unlimited Transmutation
entries: Whenever you use {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome}, you can perform any number of separate transmutations within its affected area. Each creature, object, structure, or portion of matter can undergo a different transformation.

entries.name: Absolute Transmutation
entries: You no longer need to follow normal physical, chemical, biological, or magical processes to reach a result. If the final state is something your Pact could create or alter, you can transform directly into that state.

entries.name: No Equivalent Exchange
entries: Any feature originating from {@optfeature Pact of Alchemy|FftForbiddenTome} or one of its Invocations that normally requires matter, energy, Magical Energy, money, components, physical material, or another equivalent payment can ignore that requirement. {@optfeature Philosopher's Stone|FftForbiddenTome} supplies whatever matter, energy, or magic is missing.

optionalfeature.name: Living Margins
entries: The words in your tome have grown restless. Ink crawls between paragraphs. Pages turn without wind. When commanded, fragments of the book tear themselves free—not as paper, but as living extensions of the knowledge written within. Your Pact Tome can manifest supernatural Living Pages that act as extensions of yourself.

entries.name: Awaken the Pages
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can cause a number of spectral pages equal to your Proficiency Bonus to emerge from your Pact Tome. The Living Pages remain until you dismiss them, your Pact Tome ceases to exist, or you are Incapacitated. They can appear as parchment, floating runes, strips of glowing text, black sheets covered in shifting script, or another form appropriate to your Tome. The pages aren't creatures and can't be targeted or damaged individually.

entries.name: Wandering Script
entries: As part of your movement on your turn, you can move the Living Pages up to 60 feet to a point you can see.

items: They can fly and hover.
They can pass through spaces as narrow as 1 inch.
They can turn pages, open unlocked doors, pull levers, and perform simple object interactions.
They can carry unattended objects weighing no more than 10 pounds per Living Page.
They can write, erase, copy, or arrange ordinary text.
They can retrieve or return objects to you.

entries: You perceive the exact location of every Living Page.

entries.name: Eyes Between the Lines
entries: As a Bonus Action, you can perceive through any one of your Living Pages until the start of your next turn. While doing so, you can see and hear from its position as though you occupied its space. You retain awareness of your own surroundings. A Living Page has Darkvision out to 60 feet for this purpose.

entries.name: Spell Through the Page
entries: When you cast a spell with a range other than Self, you can choose one Living Page within 60 feet as the spell's point of origin. You still cast the spell and provide all components normally. Range, areas of effect, and lines of effect are measured from the chosen Living Page. If the spell requires you to see a target, you must be able to see it either normally or through that Living Page. After originating a spell in this way, that Living Page disappears.

entries.name: Hand of the Tome
entries: When you cast a spell with a range of Touch, one Living Page can deliver it to a creature or object within 5 feet of that page. The page disappears after delivering the spell.

entries.name: Written Relay
entries: You can write a message of up to 25 words into your Pact Tome and send one Living Page to a creature you know. The page travels toward that creature by the most direct route it can navigate at a flying speed of 120 feet. When it reaches the creature, your message appears upon the page in whatever language you wrote it. The recipient can write a response of up to 25 words, after which the page returns to you. There is no fixed maximum distance, but the page can't cross planar boundaries.

optionalfeature.name: Scripted Recursion
entries: Some spells are written to be cast once. Yours are written to remember the shape of their own casting. Your Pact Tome can preserve a magical pattern after you cast it, allowing the book to reproduce that spell again.

entries.name: Record the Casting
entries: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher using a spell slot, you can cause your Pact Tome to record that exact casting as a Recursion Script. The script records the spell, the level at which it was cast, any choices made as part of the spell that are determined when casting it, and the spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus used. The script doesn't record targets, locations, or directions unless the spell itself permanently requires those choices when cast.
You can have only one Recursion Script recorded at a time. Recording a new one erases the old script.

entries.name: Recast the Script
entries: While holding your Pact Tome, you can cast the recorded spell from the Recursion Script without expending a spell slot or providing any components. You choose targets, points of origin, directions, and other choices that are normally made at the moment of casting. The spell is cast at the same level stored in the script. Once you use the Recursion Script, it disappears.

entries.name: Persistent Formula
entries: A Recursion Script remains in your Pact Tome until you use it, replace it, or willingly erase it. Finishing a Short or Long Rest doesn't remove it. The script also survives the destruction or recreation of your Pact Tome and reappears within the recreated Tome.

entries.name: Level 11 — Double Script
