entries: You can maintain two Recursion Scripts at once. Each script can hold a different spell or a different casting of the same spell. when you cast a spell recorded in one of your scripts using a spell slot normally, you can refresh that script with the new casting instead of erasing it.

entries.name: Level 15 — Perfect Repetition
entries: When you use a Recursion Script, roll a d6. On a 5 or 6, the script isn't erased. You can immediately use it again later. A script preserved this way can continue to preserve itself repeatedly.

entries.name: Level 17 — Recursive Chain
entries: You can maintain three Recursion Scripts at once. Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell from a Recursion Script with a casting time of an Action, you can immediately begin a Recursive Chain. If you cast a different spell before the end of your next turn, you can record that spell into the script you just consumed instead of losing the script completely. The newly recorded spell can be of any level you are normally capable of casting.

entries.name: Level 19 — The Tome Casts Again
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell from a Recursion Script, you can command the Tome to reproduce the script without consuming it. The spell is cast normally from the script, but the Recursion Script remains intact automatically. If Scripted Recursion would already preserve the script from another effect, that doesn't grant an additional casting.

optionalfeature.name: Unwritten Chapter
entries: There are pages in your tome that were never written. They wait for knowledge you don't possess. When need becomes great enough, the empty page supplies its own answer. Your Pact Tome contains a supernatural section called the Unwritten Chapter.

entries.name: Write the Unknown
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose one spell from any spell list. The spell appears within your Pact Tome as though written there by an unseen hand. The spell remains in the Unwritten Chapter until you replace it after another Long Rest. You don't need to have previously seen, learned, prepared, or encountered the spell.

entries.name: Borrowed Formula
entries: While the spell remains written in your Unwritten Chapter, you can cast it using any spell slots you possess of the appropriate level. The spell counts as prepared for you. It doesn't need to belong to any spell list normally available to you. You use your normal spellcasting ability for it. You can cast it at higher levels normally if you have higher-level spell slots. You provide the spell's components normally.

entries.name: The Tome Understands
entries: The Unwritten Chapter contains enough supernatural instruction for you to cast its spell correctly even if you don't understand its original magical tradition. For example, the Tome could contain a divine prayer, primal invocation, occult formula, or arcane theorem without requiring you to adopt the tradition it came from. The spell remains the spell it normally is; the Tome simply gives you a usable formula for it.

entries.name: Level 13 — Two Answers
entries: Your Unwritten Chapter can contain two spells simultaneously. When you finish a Long Rest, you can replace either or both.

entries.name: Level 17 — Forbidden Chapter
entries: Your Unwritten Chapter can contain three spells simultaneously. When you finish a Long Rest, you can replace any or all of them.

entries.name: Level 19 — The Missing Spell
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you encounter a problem and realize that a particular spell would solve it, you can use a Bonus Action to immediately replace one spell in your Unwritten Chapter with another spell of your choice. You don't need to finish a Long Rest. The newly written spell is immediately available to cast. You can do this even during combat.

optionalfeature.name: Pages of Appraisal
entries: The tome doesn't merely record what something appears to be. It watches. Compares. Corrects. Every action becomes another line of evidence, until disguise gives way to understanding. Your Pact Tome can create supernatural dossiers on creatures you encounter.

entries.name: Open a Dossier
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one creature you can see within 60 feet. A page in your Pact Tome becomes dedicated to that creature as its Dossier. You can maintain a number of Dossiers equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If you exceed this limit, choose one existing Dossier to erase. A Dossier remains until you erase it, even if the creature dies or leaves your plane of existence.

entries.name: Initial Appraisal
entries: When you create a Dossier, the Tome immediately records the creature's creature type, Size, current and maximum Hit Points, Armor Class, Speeds, senses, languages it can speak, damage Vulnerabilities, Resistances, and Immunities, and condition Immunities. The creature isn't aware that this information has been recorded.

entries.name: Observed Truth
entries: Whenever a creature with a Dossier uses a trait, action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, supernatural ability, Legendary Action, or similar feature that you can perceive, the Tome permanently records that feature. The entry includes enough information for you to understand what the feature does, its range and area, its damage or healing, its saving throw or attack roll if any, its recharge or usage limitation, whether it requires Concentration, and any trigger or condition required to use it.
You don't need to spend an action reading a feature already recorded by the Tome; you can recall its contents perfectly.

entries.name: Updating Record
entries: While a creature with a Dossier is within 120 feet of you, its page updates automatically. You always know its current Hit Points, current conditions, whether it is concentrating, and whether it has expended or regained a feature already recorded in the Dossier. The Tome doesn't reveal a feature it has never observed merely because that feature exists.

entries.name: Level 9 — Read the Pattern
entries: After observing a creature with a Dossier for at least 1 round, the Tome also records its Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores, its saving throw bonuses, its skill proficiencies and bonuses, its Proficiency Bonus, and its spellcasting ability, spell save DC, and spell attack bonus, if any. whenever the creature casts a spell you can perceive, the Tome records the spell's name and level before its effects resolve.

entries.name: Level 13 — Predictive Annotation
entries: Your Tome begins predicting behavior from everything it has recorded. Once on each of your turns when you make an attack roll against a creature with a Dossier, you can gain Advantage on that roll. Alternatively, when that creature makes a saving throw against one of your spells or abilities, you can impose Disadvantage on that saving throw. You can use only one of these benefits per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Complete Dossier
entries: After you have observed a creature with a Dossier for at least 1 minute, the Tome completes its analysis. It reveals every currently existing trait, action, spell, reaction, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, transformation, resource, and other game feature possessed by that creature, including those you haven't personally witnessed.

It also reveals which features are currently available or expended, any alternate forms it possesses, the conditions required to activate those forms or features, any regeneration, resurrection, or death-prevention abilities it possesses, and any specific method described in its statistics for bypassing, suppressing, or defeating one of its features.

entries.name: Exploit the Margin
entries: Once on each of your turns when you damage a creature whose Dossier is complete, you can choose one damage type dealt by that attack, spell, or effect. For that instance of damage, the creature's Resistance to that damage type is ignored. If it is Immune instead, treat that Immunity as Resistance for that instance. This doesn't permanently alter the creature's defenses.

optionalfeature.name: Stolen Footnote
entries: Not every secret is a spell. Some are written in muscle, blood, instinct, training, divinity, monstrous anatomy, or stranger things. Your tome has never cared about the distinction. Your Pact Tome can record a feature possessed or used by another creature and preserve it as a Stolen Footnote.

entries.name: Cite the Ability
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet uses or visibly demonstrates a feature, you can use your Reaction to record that feature in your Pact Tome after its use resolves. A passive or continuous feature can be recorded when you directly observe its effect or otherwise learn that the creature possesses it.

You can record a trait, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, spell, Spellcasting feature, class feature, species feature, monster feature, Legendary Action, Lair Action, Mythic Action, Multiattack, transformation, movement mode, sense, aura, regeneration, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, or another game feature or statistic with a defined mechanical effect. The Tome records the chosen feature as it exists for that creature. You don't need to understand how the creature performs it.
You can maintain one Stolen Footnote at a time. Recording another replaces the previous one.

entries.name: Use the Footnote
entries: While holding your Pact Tome, you can use the recorded feature as though it appeared among your own features. If the feature normally uses an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, you use the same type of action. If it uses a special action economy you don't possess, such as a Legendary Action, Lair Action, or Mythic Action, you use it as a Bonus Action instead unless the feature itself already requires an Action or Reaction.

If the feature is passive or continuous, you can invoke it as a Bonus Action and gain its benefits for 1 minute, or until you are Incapacitated. If the feature represents a movement mode, sense, resistance, immunity, vulnerability, aura, regeneration, Armor Class calculation, or similar continuous statistic, it functions for that duration exactly as recorded, using the adaptations described below when necessary.

If the feature is a spell or Spellcasting feature, you can use it without needing the original creature's class, spell list, spellbook, focus, or other unique spellcasting structure. Any spell slot or unique resource supplied by the recorded feature is provided by the Footnote for that use. Components required by a spell are still required unless the recorded feature itself ignores them. After you use or invoke the Stolen Footnote, it disappears from the Tome unless another part of this invocation preserves it.

entries.name: Translate the Feature
entries: Your Tome translates the recorded feature into a form you can perform. You don't need the anatomy, species, creature type, class, size, equipment, lair, legendary status, transformation, or physical structure normally required to use it. The Tome creates a magical analogue whenever necessary. Spectral wings can perform a wing attack, spectral jaws can reproduce a bite, runes can reproduce a gaze, the Tome can supply a monstrous roar, and an effect tied to a lair can manifest from the Tome or the space around you.

If the feature requires an attack roll, use your spell attack modifier unless the recorded feature specifies another fixed bonus. If it requires a saving throw, use your spell save DC unless the recorded feature specifies another fixed DC.

If it uses the original creature's ability modifier, Proficiency Bonus, level, Hit Dice, or similar personal statistic to calculate a number, use your corresponding statistic when possible. If no corresponding statistic exists, use your spellcasting ability modifier, your Proficiency Bonus, or your character level, whichever most closely matches the original calculation.

If the feature creates or depends on an object, body part, weapon, organ, limb, terrain element, or other prerequisite you don't possess, the Tome can manifest a temporary magical analogue that exists only for the feature's duration. Copying a feature doesn't permanently change your creature type, body, statistics, class, species, or identity unless the feature itself explicitly changes one of those things.

entries.name: Everything Can Be Cited
entries: Stolen Footnote isn't limited by the origin of a feature. If it has a defined game effect and belongs to or is used by a creature you can observe, the Tome can record it. This includes passive defenses, supernatural anatomy, special senses, alternate forms, innate spellcasting, entire activated traits, Legendary and Mythic features, and abilities that would normally be impossible for your body to reproduce.

If a recorded entry contains several linked effects as one feature, such as Multiattack or a transformation that grants a package of abilities, the Footnote records the complete feature rather than only one sentence from it.

entries.name: Level 13 — Two Footnotes
entries: Your Pact Tome can hold two Stolen Footnotes simultaneously. They can come from the same creature or different creatures. If a recorded feature normally has limited uses, a Recharge roll, Legendary Action cost, Mythic requirement, or a resource unique to its original creature, your single use of the Stolen Footnote supplies that requirement automatically. You don't need the original creature's resource.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Citation
entries: Your Tome can hold three Stolen Footnotes simultaneously. When you use or invoke a Stolen Footnote, roll a d6. On a 5 or 6, the Footnote remains in your Tome instead of disappearing.

entries.name: Rewrite the Scale
entries: When you use a recorded feature, you can calculate any damage, healing, range, area, number of targets, or similar value that normally scales from the original creature's CR, level, Hit Dice, Proficiency Bonus, or similar progression using your character level or Proficiency Bonus instead, using the nearest equivalent progression represented by the feature. If the feature doesn't scale, it remains unchanged.

entries.name: Level 19 — Plagiarism Perfected
entries: Once per Long Rest, when a creature you can see within 120 feet uses or reveals an eligible feature, you can record it without using your Reaction. You can then immediately use or invoke that Stolen Footnote as part of the same trigger, provided the recorded feature can meaningfully function at that moment. Doing so doesn't erase another Footnote if you have an empty Footnote slot.

optionalfeature.name: Wellspring of the Tome
entries: Every spell leaves something behind. Power gathers between the lines, beneath the ink, and within the spaces no reader notices. As the tome deepens, those remnants cease to be traces. They become an entire second reservoir of magic. Your Pact Tome develops its own reserve of magical power, granting you additional spell slots called Tome Slots.

entries.name: Tome Slots
entries: Tome Slots are additional spell slots separate from those granted by your classes, species, feats, magic items, or other features. You can expend a Tome Slot whenever you would normally expend a spell slot. A Tome Slot can also be used to upcast a spell normally. You regain all expended Tome Slots when you finish a Long Rest. Destroying, dismissing, or recreating your Pact Tome doesn't restore expended Tome Slots.

entries.name: Level 5 — First Reservoir
entries: You gain one 1st-level Tome Slot, one 2nd-level Tome Slot, and one 3rd-level Tome Slot.

entries.name: Level 9 — Deep Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 4th-level Tome Slot and one 5th-level Tome Slot. You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 5th.

entries.name: Level 13 — Greater Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 6th-level Tome Slot and one 7th-level Tome Slot. You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 7th.

entries.name: Level 17 — Endless Reservoir
entries: You additionally gain one 8th-level Tome Slot and one 9th-level Tome Slot. You now have one additional spell slot of every level from 1st through 9th.

entries.name: Reflow the Ink
entries: When you finish a Short Rest, you can restore expended Tome Slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed your Proficiency Bonus + your spellcasting ability modifier. For example, with a Proficiency Bonus of +6 and a spellcasting ability modifier of +5, you could restore up to 11 total levels of Tome Slots. Once you use Reflow the Ink, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 19 — Overflowing Archive
entries: You gain a second Tome Slot of each of the following levels: 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th.

entries.name: Bottomless Page
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you expend a Tome Slot of 6th level or higher, you can cause the Tome to restore that slot immediately after the spell resolves. You choose to use Bottomless Page after the spell resolves.

optionalfeature.name: Ascending Formula
entries: Most spell formulas end exactly where the power invested in them ends. Your tome has learned to keep writing. One more line. One more circle. One more impossible step beyond what the spell slot should have been able to sustain. While holding your Pact Tome, you can use its accumulated knowledge to cast spells at a higher level than the spell slot you expend.

entries.name: Overcast
entries: When you cast a spell using a spell slot, you can cause your Pact Tome to increase the spell's effective spell level by 1. For example, a spell cast using a 2nd-level slot functions as though cast with a 3rd-level slot, a spell cast using a 4th-level slot functions as though cast with a 5th-level slot, and a spell cast using an 8th-level slot functions as though cast with a 9th-level slot. You still expend only the original spell slot.

The spell uses its increased level for all purposes, including At Higher Levels effects, damage and healing scaling, number of targets, duration or area increases, interactions with effects that check spell level, and any other feature that checks the spell's level. Overcast can't increase a spell beyond 9th level unless Formula Beyond Measure specifically allows otherwise. You can use Overcast a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 11 — Deep Formula
entries: When you use Overcast, you can increase the spell's effective level by up to 2 levels instead of 1. Using either a +1 or +2 increase expends only one use of Overcast. For example, a spell cast using a 3rd-level slot can function as though cast using a 5th-level slot.

entries.name: Level 15 — Efficient Ascension
entries: Once on each of your turns when you use Overcast to increase a spell by only 1 level, roll a d6 after the spell resolves. On a 4–6, the use of Overcast isn't expended. This doesn't restore the spell slot.

entries.name: Excess Formula
entries: If a spell has no benefit from being cast at one of the intermediate levels you pass through, that doesn't prevent you from Overcasting it. For example, a spell that gains a new effect only at 6th level can be cast using a 4th-level slot and increased by 2 levels to gain that 6th-level benefit.

entries.name: Level 17 — Grand Overcast
entries: You can increase a spell by up to 3 levels with a single use of Overcast. For example, a 3rd-level slot can produce a 6th-level casting, a 5th-level slot can produce an 8th-level casting, and a 6th-level slot can produce a 9th-level casting. once per Long Rest, you can use Overcast without expending one of its uses.

entries.name: Level 19 — Formula Beyond Measure
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell using a spell slot of 5th level or higher, you can invoke Formula Beyond Measure. The spell is treated as though it were cast using a 9th-level spell slot, regardless of the slot actually expended. This doesn't expend a use of Overcast.

entries.name: Overflow Beyond Ninth
entries: If you expend an actual 9th-level spell slot, you can instead use Formula Beyond Measure to treat the casting as 10th level solely for determining numerical or scalable effects that explicitly increase when cast using a higher-level spell slot. This doesn't create a 10th-level spell, doesn't allow you to learn or cast spells above 9th level, and doesn't bypass restrictions that specifically require something other than spell level.
For example, a spell that deals one additional damage die for each slot level above its base level gains one additional step of scaling beyond its normal 9th-level casting.

optionalfeature.name: Condensed Formula
entries: Most spell formulas waste power. Tradition calls the excess necessary. Your tome calls it poor notation. Line by line, the formula contracts until the same miracle fits inside a smaller measure of magic. Your Pact Tome can compress spells into more efficient forms, allowing you to cast them using lower-level spell slots without weakening the resulting spell.

entries.name: Spell Compression
entries: When you cast a spell of 2nd level or higher that is written in your Pact Tome, you can cast it using a spell slot 1 level lower than the spell's normal level. The spell still functions as a spell of its original level. For example, a 2nd-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 4th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, and a 7th-level spell can use a 6th-level slot.

For every purpose other than the slot actually expended, the spell retains its normal level. This includes damage and healing, saving throws and attack rolls, Counterspell and Dispel Magic interactions, effects that check the spell's level, Concentration, duration, area, and number of targets. You can use Spell Compression a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. A spell can never be compressed below a 1st-level spell slot.

entries.name: Level 13 — Deep Compression
entries: You can reduce the required spell slot by up to 2 levels instead of 1. For example, a 3rd-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 5th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, and a 9th-level spell can use a 7th-level slot. Using either one or two levels of compression expends only one use.

entries.name: Compressed Upcasting
entries: You can also apply Spell Compression to an upcast spell. Determine the level at which you want the spell to function, then reduce the slot actually expended. For example, you could cast a 3rd-level spell as a 6th-level casting while expending only a 4th-level spell slot. The spell functions as a 6th-level spell for all purposes.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Compression
entries: You can reduce the required slot by up to 3 levels. For example, a 4th-level spell can use a 1st-level slot, a 6th-level spell can use a 3rd-level slot, an 8th-level spell can use a 5th-level slot, and a 9th-level spell can use a 6th-level slot. the first time after each Long Rest that you use Spell Compression, it doesn't expend one of your uses.

entries.name: Efficient Notation
entries: When you use Spell Compression and expend a spell slot of 3rd level or lower, roll a d6 after the spell resolves. On a 5 or 6, the use of Spell Compression isn't expended. The spell slot is still expended normally.

entries.name: Level 19 — Formula Without Waste
entries: Your mastery of compressed spellcraft becomes extreme. Once per Long Rest, when you cast a spell written in your Pact Tome, you can use Perfect Formula.

entries.name: Perfect Formula
entries: Choose the level at which the spell will function, up to 9th level. You expend a spell slot only half that level, rounded up.
The spell functions at its full chosen level for every purpose. Perfect Formula doesn't expend a use of Spell Compression.

optionalfeature.name: Sovereign Armament
entries: Your pact weapon no longer behaves like an ordinary weapon enchanted by magic. It recognizes only one authority: yours. Its shape, balance, and method of killing rearrange themselves around your intent. In your hands, a single weapon can answer problems that would normally demand an entire arsenal. Whenever you summon or bond with your Pact Weapon, you can cause it to take the form of any Simple or Martial melee or ranged weapon. You are proficient with every form it takes.

Changing its form requires no action, and you can do so immediately before or after any attack you make with it. A magical weapon bonded through Pact of the Blade retains its magical properties regardless of the form, unless a property logically requires its original form.

Whenever the weapon changes form, choose up to two of the following properties for it: Finesse, Light, Reach, Thrown (30/90), Two-Handed, or Versatile (1d10). If it already has a property you choose, choose another instead. You can also remove the Heavy property whenever you change its form. While you wield it, the Pact Weapon ignores ordinary limitations of shape. You can use it even when its form would normally be impractical for your Size, and changing its form never causes you to drop it.
If the weapon requires ammunition, it creates the mundane ammunition needed for each attack as part of that attack. The ammunition disappears after the attack resolves.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: Your Pact Weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls unless it already has an equal or greater bonus. Whenever you hit with it, you can choose for the attack to deal Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, or Force damage regardless of the weapon's form.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You can have three of the listed weapon properties on your Pact Weapon simultaneously. Immediately before each attack, you can independently change its form, damage type, and chosen weapon properties for that attack. Its inherent magical properties remain through these transformations.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: Your Pact Weapon gains a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls unless it already has an equal or greater bonus. It can have any number of the listed weapon properties simultaneously. Its Reach increases by 5 feet. Its normal and long ranges are doubled whenever it is in a ranged or Thrown form. Its attacks ignore Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, and Force damage. It can't be forcibly removed from your grasp while you are conscious.
If it leaves your hand, it can return to you immediately after the attack or effect resolves, requiring no action.

optionalfeature.name: Severing Edge
entries: Your pact weapon has learned to cut things that were never meant to possess an edge. A ward can be split. A curse can be opened. A spell can be wounded until its structure collapses. Where ordinary steel meets magic and stops, your weapon continues. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with your Pact Weapon, you can choose one spell or magical effect currently affecting that creature that you are aware of.

Make an ability check using your spellcasting ability. The DC equals 10 + the spell's level. On a success, that spell or magical effect ends on the creature as though successfully dispelled. If the effect has no spell level, the GM determines an equivalent level for this purpose.

When your Pact Weapon damages a creature that is concentrating, the creature has Disadvantage on the Constitution saving throw it makes to maintain Concentration from that damage. If the attack is a Critical Hit, the creature instead automatically fails that Concentration saving throw.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: Your Pact Weapon can strike magical effects directly. As an Action, you can make one attack with your Pact Weapon against a magical barrier, ward, conjured structure, magical restraint, magical portal, or similar magical manifestation you can perceive. On a hit, choose one: deal the weapon's normal damage to the manifestation if it can take damage; make a spellcasting ability check against DC 10 + the effect's spell level to end it as though successfully dispelled; or suppress one of its magical properties until the start of your next turn.

If the effect has no spell level, the GM determines an equivalent level for the ability check. A manifestation with no AC has an AC equal to 10 + its spell level, or a value determined by the GM if it has no spell level.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you hit a creature or magical manifestation with your Pact Weapon, choose one magical effect affecting the target that you are aware of. That effect ends immediately without an ability check if it was created by a spell of level 8 or lower. For a 9th-level spell, Artifact, deity-created effect, or magic of comparable power, make a spellcasting ability check against DC 19 instead. On a success, the effect ends on that target.

optionalfeature.name: Spell-Eater
entries: Magic that fails to take hold of you doesn't simply disperse. You tear the dying spell from the Weave, swallow its structure whole, and keep it inside yourself until you decide what to do with it. When a creature casts a spell of level 1 or higher that targets you or includes you in its area, you can use your Reaction to devour that spell after it fails to affect you because its spell attack misses you, you succeed on its saving throw and suffer no effect from it, or another feature causes the spell to have no effect on you.

You can keep one spell devoured this way at a time. Devouring another spell replaces the one you were already keeping. A spell you keep this way remains available until you finish a Long Rest. While you are keeping a spell this way, you can cast it once without expending a spell slot. You use your own spellcasting ability, spell attack modifier, and spell save DC, use the level at which the spell was originally cast, and make any choices normally made by the caster.
You must still provide any Material component that has a listed cost or is consumed by the spell. After you cast the spell, you are no longer keeping it.

entries.name: Level 5
entries: You can devour a spell of up to 3rd level.

entries.name: Level 11
entries: You can devour a spell of up to 6th level. You can keep up to two spells devoured this way simultaneously.

entries.name: Level 17
entries: You can devour spells of any level. You can keep up to three spells devoured this way simultaneously. When you successfully devour a spell that targets only you, you can cause it to be completely consumed. If it would normally produce a lingering effect after resolving, that effect isn't created.

optionalfeature.name: Unseen Dominion
entries: Your influence reaches farther than your hands ever could.

entries.name: Invisible Grasp
entries: You can manipulate unattended objects within 60 feet of you as though you were touching them. You can open doors, pull levers, draw or stow objects, use tools, pour liquids, and perform similar interactions remotely. You use your normal Strength and Dexterity for anything that would require them. Invisible Grasp doesn't require Concentration. Manipulating an object through it uses the same action economy as manipulating that object normally; an interaction that would require no Action at your reach requires no Action at range.

entries.name: Level 11 — Seize the Held
entries: As an Action, choose one object you can see within 60 feet that is being held or carried by a creature. The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or the object is pulled from its grasp and flies to your hand or to an unoccupied space you choose within 5 feet of you. A creature has Advantage on the save if the object is secured to its body.

entries.name: Level 17 — Dominion Without Distance
entries: The range of Invisible Grasp and Seize the Held becomes 300 feet. you can use Invisible Grasp on objects you can see even if a transparent barrier separates you from them, provided there is a physical path the object could travel to reach you.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Crown
entries: Your words carry the weight of a crown, making obedience feel inevitable.

entries.name: Commanding Presence
entries: Whenever you make a Charisma check, you can treat a d20 roll of 7 or lower as an 8. This requires no action.

entries.name: Assume Command
entries: As part of speaking to a creature that understands you, issue a short, direct instruction; no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction is required. If it is nonhostile, you have Advantage on your next Charisma check to convince it to follow that instruction.

If it is hostile and within 60 feet, you can force it to make a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failure, it must obey until the end of its next turn, using its movement, Action, Bonus Action, Reaction, and other available abilities as necessary to the best of its ability. You can force each creature to make this save only once per turn.

The instruction can be any reasonably expressible direct command, such as "Attack him," "Protect me," or "Stop casting spells." If it becomes impossible, the creature follows it as closely as reasonably possible.

entries.name: The Voice That Carries
entries: While speaking, you can make your voice clearly audible to any creatures you choose within 300 feet, even through loud noise. This doesn't reveal your exact location unless a listener can already determine it.

entries.name: Level 5: Authority Takes Root
entries: When a creature fails its save against Assume Command, you can extend the command to 1 minute. It repeats the Wisdom saving throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the command on a success. An immediately completable command ends when fulfilled. On Charisma checks against nonhostile creatures that can hear you, Commanding Presence lets you treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10 instead.

entries.name: Level 9: Command the Many
entries: Assume Command can target up to your Proficiency Bonus in hostile creatures. Each must be within 60 feet, hear and understand you, and make its own Wisdom saving throw. You can give them the same or different commands. Outside combat, when addressing a group that can hear you, you can make one Charisma check for the same attempt against the whole group, where appropriate.

entries.name: Level 13: Royal Decree
entries: A creature that succeeds on its save against Assume Command must still obey one reasonable portion of the command you choose until the end of its next turn. That portion can't require its entire turn. For example, "Drop your weapon and leave" can still force it to drop the weapon. Creatures Charmed or Frightened by you have Disadvantage on saves against Assume Command.

entries.name: Level 17: The Crown Is Absolute
entries: Once per turn when you use Assume Command, you can declare an Absolute Command, which can contain complex instructions. A creature that fails its save obeys for 1 minute without repeating the save, until the command is completed, becomes impossible, or the duration ends. It uses its movement, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, speech, objects, and other available abilities as necessary to fulfill the command to the best of its ability. You can have only one Absolute Command active; creating another immediately ends the previous one.

optionalfeature.name: Edict of the Iron Throne
entries: The Crown no longer merely demands attention. Its commands begin to carry the weight of law. You gain the following additional Decrees for your Pact of the Crown.

entries.name: Halt
entries: The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or its Speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Drop
entries: The creature must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or immediately drop one object of your choice that it is holding. The object lands in its space.

entries.name: Level 11 — Obey
entries: You gain another Decree:

{@b Obey.} Choose one simple physical action the creature could immediately perform, such as move 10 feet, open that door, release that creature, stand up, or drop Prone. The creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or immediately perform that action if physically possible. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
The Decree can't force a creature to directly damage itself.

entries.name: Level 17 — Imperial Edict
entries: Once per turn when a creature fails a saving throw against one of your Decrees, you can immediately issue a second different Decree to that creature without using an Action or Bonus Action.

optionalfeature.name: Threshold Without Warning
entries: Your gateways no longer merely connect two places. They begin to decide where motion itself is allowed to finish. You gain the following improvements to your Pact of the Gate.

entries.name: Intercepting Gate
entries: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of one of your gateways willingly moves at least 10 feet, you can use your Reaction to move one gateway into an unoccupied space along that creature's path immediately before it enters that space. If the creature continues moving through the gateway, it exits from the linked gateway normally.

entries.name: Level 11 — Redirect the Blow
entries: When an attack or spell effect travels through one of your gateways and targets a creature, you can move the linked gateway up to 10 feet immediately before the attack or effect resolves. This movement can change the point from which the attack or effect emerges, potentially changing line of sight, cover, or whether the original target is still valid.

entries.name: Level 17 — Sovereign Threshold
entries: Once on each of your turns, when a creature or object passes through one of your gateways, you can:

items: Preserve its momentum normally.
Reduce its momentum to 0.
Redirect its movement in any direction as it exits.

entries: If a falling creature passes through one of your gateways, you can therefore cause it to exit without retaining its falling speed.

optionalfeature.name: Hold the Door
entries: Your gateways no longer flicker shut the moment their immediate purpose is fulfilled. Once you open a path, you can hold it against the natural shape of space. Those who travel through it do so because you have chosen to leave the door open.

entries.name: Held Threshold
entries: When you use Open the Way, you can hold your gateways open. If you do, they last for 1 minute instead of until the start of your next turn. The gateways end early if you dismiss them (no action required), you create a new set of gateways with Open the Way, or you become Incapacitated. While the gateways remain open, you retain all benefits of Reach Through and Moving Gate.

entries.name: Keeper of Passage
entries: Whenever a creature you can see attempts to pass through one of your gateways, you can choose whether that gateway carries it to another gateway. If you refuse passage, the creature doesn't pass through the gateway and its movement into the gateway's space is halted immediately before the opening. This requires no action from you. You can make this choice separately for each creature each time it attempts to enter a gateway.

entries.name: Open for the Chosen
entries: When you create your gateways, you can designate any number of creatures you can see. A designated creature can pass through your gateways even while Incapacitated, Grappled, or being carried, provided some part of it or the creature or object carrying it enters the gateway. In addition, a willing designated creature can move through one of your gateways once on each of its turns without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that movement.

entries.name: The Door Makes Room
entries: Your held gateways can momentarily expand to accommodate those you permit to pass. When you or a willing creature, or an unattended object, would enter one of your held gateways but is too large to fit through its normal opening, you can cause every gateway involved in that passage to expand just enough for it to pass. This can accommodate a creature or object of up to Huge size. The gateways return to their normal dimensions immediately after the passage is complete.
A creature or object can't emerge into a space that is too small to physically contain it; if there is no suitable space at the exit, it can't pass through that gateway.

entries.name: Level 11 — Door That Refuses to Close
entries: Your held gateways can last for 10 minutes. Becoming Incapacitated no longer immediately ends them. Instead, they remain until the end of your next turn, giving you a chance to recover before they collapse.

entries.name: Level 17 — Permanent Invitation
entries: Your held gateways no longer have a maximum duration. They remain until you dismiss them, create another set of gateways, die, or are on a different plane from every gateway. In addition, creatures you designated with Open for the Chosen can always identify which gateway they will emerge from before entering one.

optionalfeature.name: There Is Always Another Door
entries: A wall is only a door that has not been opened yet. Distance matters less when you already know where the other side must be. Where others see a sealed path, you see another threshold waiting to exist. When you use Open the Way, you can place one of your gateways against a solid surface, such as a wall, door, floor, ceiling, or similar barrier.

The linked gateway can appear in an unoccupied space on the opposite side of that surface even if you can't see that space, provided the destination is within the normal range of Open the Way and you know or can reasonably determine where that space is. If no suitable unoccupied space exists at the destination, the gateway doesn't form, and you don't expend the Bonus Action used to create it.

entries.name: Level 5 — Find the Other Side
entries: When you place a gateway against a solid surface with There Is Always Another Door, you can sense whether a suitable unoccupied space exists on the opposite side within the range of Open the Way. You learn the direction and approximate distance to the nearest space large enough for the gateway to form, but you learn nothing else about that space or anything within it. You can choose that space as the destination even if you can't see it.

optionalfeature.name: Step Between Heartbeats
entries: There is a moment between intent and impact when a path still exists. You have learned to find that path before the blow can finish falling. To everyone else, you simply vanish from the place where you were about to be struck.

entries.name: Instant Passage
entries: When a creature you can see targets you with an attack, you can use your Reaction to create your gateways immediately before the attack roll is made. One gateway must appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of you, and the other in an unoccupied space you can see within the normal range of Open the Way. You can immediately move through the adjacent gateway and emerge from the linked gateway without expending movement and without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

If this movement places you outside the attack's reach or range, or causes the attacker to lose line of sight or line of effect to you, the attack automatically misses. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Level 11 — Take Them With You
entries: When you use Step Between Heartbeats, you can bring one willing creature within 5 feet of you through the gateway with you. The creature appears in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of your exit and doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from this movement.

entries.name: Level 17 — Before the World Can React
entries: When you use Step Between Heartbeats, you can create the gateways and move through them even if you are Grappled or Restrained. In addition, after you emerge, you can immediately make one weapon attack, cast one cantrip with a casting time of an Action, or use one feature that normally requires an Action.

optionalfeature.name: The World Is Full of Entrances
entries: Distance has ceased to be an obstacle. Every place you have stood has become another possible doorway. The world is vast only to those who must travel across it.

entries.name: Familiar Destination
entries: When you use Open the Way, one of your gateways can appear at any location on the same plane that you have personally visited, regardless of distance and without requiring you to see the destination. You must be able to identify the destination from memory, such as a particular room, street, rooftop, chamber, clearing, or other distinct place. The gateway forms in the nearest suitable unoccupied space to the location you remember. If no suitable space exists, the gateway fails to form, and you don't expend the Bonus Action used to create it.
You immediately know whether the gateway successfully formed.

entries.name: Distant Threshold
entries: A gateway created with Familiar Destination functions exactly like any other gateway created by Open the Way. You can see and hear through it, move through it, make attacks through it, cast spells through it, and allow other creatures or objects to pass through it normally. Distance between the gateways doesn't alter these functions.

entries.name: Level 17 — Every Plane Has a Door
entries: When you use Open the Way, one of your gateways can appear at a location on another plane of existence. If you have personally visited the destination, the gateway can open there regardless of planar distance. If you haven't personally visited it, you must be able to clearly identify the destination through a reliable description, map, magical observation, or similar source.

The gateway forms in the nearest suitable unoccupied space to the intended destination. If no suitable space exists, it fails to form, and you don't expend the Bonus Action used to create it. A gateway created this way functions normally for passage, sight, attacks, spells, creatures, and objects. Planar boundaries, planar distance, and effects that merely prevent teleportation or planar travel don't stop a gateway created by this feature.

optionalfeature.name: Fractured Counterpart
entries: Your reflections have stopped behaving like copies. Each now seems to remember a slightly different version of what you were about to do.

entries.name: Reflected Motion
entries: Whenever you take the Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, or Help action, each of your Living Reflections can immediately move up to half your Speed, no action required from you. This movement can occur before or after the action resolves.

entries.name: Level 11 — Mirror Feint
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you make an attack or cast a spell originating from your Living Reflection's space through Mirror Casting, you can cause another Living Reflection—or yourself—to perform the same visible motions.
Choose one creature that can see at least two of those positions. Until the attack or spell resolves:

items: The creature can't determine which position is the true origin by sight alone.
The first attack roll you make against that creature has Advantage.
If the creature makes a saving throw against the effect, it has Disadvantage on the first saving throw it makes against it.

entries: Choose the benefit when you use Mirror Feint.

entries.name: Level 17 — Impossible Reflection
entries: Once on each of your turns when you cast a spell or use an ability through Mirror Casting, you can choose two different origins among yourself and your Living Reflections. The effect still occurs only once, but for determining range, line of sight, cover, and the direction or point of origin of an Area of Effect, you can use whichever of the two origins is more favorable for each target affected by that single use. For example, a creature behind Total Cover from one reflection might still be affected if the second chosen origin has a clear path to it.

optionalfeature.name: War Without a Hand
entries: The Arsenal no longer waits for your hand. Its weapons have learned to answer violence on their own.

entries.name: Arsenal Strike
entries: Once on each of your turns when you take the Attack action, you can cause one weapon stored in your Arsenal to appear momentarily in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet and make one attack with it. You make the attack as though you were wielding the weapon, using your normal attack modifier for it. The weapon vanishes back into the Arsenal immediately after the attack. This attack is part of the same Attack action and doesn't require a free hand.

entries.name: Level 11 — Crossfire Arsenal
entries: Once per turn when Arsenal Strike hits, you can immediately summon a different stored weapon from another unoccupied space within 30 feet and make one additional attack with it against the same target. You can make this additional attack only once per turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — Battlefield Arsenal
entries: The range of Arsenal Strike becomes 120 feet. once on each of your turns when you use Arsenal Strike, you can cause the weapon to attack from up to three different possible spaces within range. Choose which space is the true origin only when the attack is resolved. For determining range, line of sight, and cover, use whichever of those spaces is most favorable to the attack. The weapon still makes only one attack.

optionalfeature.name: The Vessel Remembers
entries: Magic sealed long enough begins to leave an impression. Even after release, the Vessel remembers what it once contained.

entries.name: Refuse to Empty
entries: When you release a sealed spell and that spell fails to affect any creature because every spell attack misses, every affected creature succeeds on its initial saving throw, or every intended target becomes invalid before the spell resolves, the spell isn't removed from your Pact Vessel. Any resources spent when the spell was originally sealed remain spent. You can attempt to release the spell again normally.

entries.name: Level 11 — Vessel Concentration
entries: When a Concentration spell is released from your Pact Vessel, the creature releasing it can cause the Vessel to maintain Concentration instead.
While doing so:

items: The releaser doesn't need to concentrate on the spell.
The Vessel can maintain only one spell at a time.
It makes no Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration.
Starting Concentration on another spell this way ends the previous one.

entries: The Concentration ends if the Vessel is destroyed or if it is more than 300 feet from the creature that released the spell.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Memory
entries: Once per Long Rest, when you release a spell from your Pact Vessel, you can choose for the Vessel to retain a perfect copy of that sealed spell instead of removing it. The released spell functions normally, while the identical spell remains stored in the same space of the Vessel and can be released again later.

optionalfeature.name: Claim Beyond Barriers
entries: The mark is no longer merely something you can sense. It becomes a point through which your power can reach.

entries.name: Brand Conduit
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack or cast a spell that targets only one of your Branded creatures, you can treat the Brand itself as the point of origin for determining range and line of sight. You still need to be within the normal range of the attack or spell measured to the Branded creature, but ordinary cover and intervening creatures don't block the effect. This doesn't allow an Area of Effect to originate from the Brand.

entries.name: Level 11 — No Wall Between Us
entries: Brand Conduit can function even if the Branded creature is behind Total Cover or enclosed within a mundane solid structure. A spell or attack used this way can affect only the Branded creature and can't damage or pass through the intervening structure.

entries.name: Level 17 — The Brand Is the Opening
entries: Once on each of your turns when you cast a spell with an Area of Effect, you can cause that Area of Effect to originate from the space of one of your Branded creatures instead of from you or the spell's normal point of origin. You make all choices for the spell normally, and the Branded creature can be affected by the spell normally. distance on the same plane no longer prevents you from using Brand Conduit, though the spell or attack must otherwise be capable of targeting that creature.

optionalfeature.name: Momentum Thief
entries: Movement is only borrowed certainty. You have learned how to take some of it for yourself.

entries.name: Steal the Step
entries: Once per turn, when a creature you can see within 60 feet willingly moves at least 10 feet, you can reduce the remaining movement it can make during that turn by 10 feet. Until the end of your next turn, your Speed increases by the same amount. This requires no Action or Reaction. A creature's Speed can't be reduced below 5 feet by this invocation.

entries.name: Level 11 — Take the Momentum
entries: When you use Steal the Step, you can instead steal up to 20 feet of movement.
until the end of your next turn, you can spend stolen movement in any combination to:

items: Increase your walking Speed.
Increase a Climb or Swim Speed you possess.
Stand from Prone without spending movement.
Move 5 feet immediately after a creature misses you with an attack, without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Each 5 feet moved this way consumes 5 feet of stolen movement.

entries.name: Level 17 — No Motion Is Wasted
entries: You can use Steal the Step once on each creature's turn, rather than once per round. Stolen movement accumulates until the end of your next turn, to a maximum of 60 feet.
you can spend 20 feet of stolen movement to immediately move up to 20 feet when:

items: You succeed on a saving throw.
A creature misses you with an attack.
A creature you can see within 60 feet begins moving.

entries: This movement requires no Action or Reaction and doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

optionalfeature.name: Mastery Beyond Training
entries: You have stopped treating weapons as fixed techniques. Every grip, angle, and impact is another answer waiting to be used. Choose two kinds of weapons with which you are proficient. You gain access to their Weapon Mastery properties. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace either choice with another weapon with which you are proficient. When you make an attack with a weapon whose mastery you can use, you can use its normal mastery property or one other mastery property for which that weapon qualifies.

At Level 11, you no longer need to choose specific weapons. You can use Weapon Mastery with every weapon with which you are proficient, and each time you attack you can choose any mastery property for which that weapon qualifies. At Level 17, once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon, you can apply two different mastery properties to that attack instead of one.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Aegis
entries: Some bargains grant weapons. Yours taught the space around your body to refuse harm. You can manifest a supernatural Aegis around yourself as a Bonus Action. Its appearance is entirely your choice: spectral armor, overlapping runes, floating plates, a second shadow, hardened light, invisible force, or another protective manifestation. The Aegis lasts until you dismiss it, become Incapacitated, or manifest it again.
While the Aegis is active:

items: If you aren't wearing armor, your base AC becomes 13 + your Dexterity modifier.
You can use the Aegis as a Shield, gaining the normal +2 AC benefit while one of your hands is free.
Using it as a Shield doesn't place an object in that hand and doesn't interfere with Somatic components.
You are proficient with the Aegis.
It can't be disarmed, removed, or destroyed separately from you.

entries: Whenever you take damage, you can use your Reaction to reduce that damage by 1d10 + your Charisma modifier. You can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, regaining all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. At Level 5, the reduction becomes 2d10 + your Charisma modifier. when you reduce damage to 0, you can immediately move up to 10 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

At Level 11, while the Aegis is active, whenever you succeed on a saving throw that would cause you to take half damage, you instead take no damage. If you fail that saving throw, you take only half damage. At Level 17, the damage reduction becomes 4d10 + your Charisma modifier, and using it no longer requires your Reaction once on each round. You can still spend your Reaction to use it an additional time during the same round.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Martial Discipline
entries: Your patron did not teach you a spell. It taught you how to fight. When you gain this Pact, choose two Fighting Style feats of your choice. You gain those feats, and this Pact counts as the Fighting Style feature for the purpose of meeting their prerequisites. You can choose a Fighting Style even if its prerequisite normally requires you to possess the Fighting Style feature from a particular class, but you must meet any other prerequisites it has.

Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can replace any Fighting Style gained from this Pact with another Fighting Style you qualify for. You can't choose the same Fighting Style more than once through this Pact. whenever a Fighting Style you gained from this Pact allows you to make an attack, move, Grapple, Shove, or otherwise perform an effect without an action, doing so doesn't interfere with or prevent another Fighting Style gained from this Pact from triggering from the same attack, movement, or event.

At Level 5, you gain a third Fighting Style. At Level 11, you gain a fourth Fighting Style. At Level 17, you gain a fifth Fighting Style. All Fighting Styles gained from this Pact can be active simultaneously, provided the conditions of each Fighting Style are met.

optionalfeature.name: Discipline Without Boundaries
entries: Weapons are tools. Stances are habits. A discipline mastered deeply enough no longer depends on either.

entries.name: Universal Application
entries: When a Fighting Style gained from Pact of the Martial Discipline requires you to wield a particular type of weapon, use a particular weapon property, fight with a specific number of weapons, have a free hand, or wear a particular category of armor, you can ignore one such equipment requirement. The Fighting Style must still be capable of producing a meaningful effect.

For example, a Fighting Style intended for ranged weapons could function with a thrown weapon, one intended for two-handed weapons could function with a one-handed weapon, or one requiring an empty hand could remain functional while that hand is occupied. This feature doesn't change the weapon's own properties, damage die, range, or other statistics.

entries.name: Level 11 — Technique Over Tool
entries: You can ignore all equipment requirements of Fighting Styles gained from this Pact. Whenever one of those Fighting Styles refers to a specific weapon category or property, you can apply its benefit to any weapon attack or Unarmed Strike for which the effect can meaningfully function. A Fighting Style still can't create an impossible effect; for example, a benefit that modifies ammunition doesn't create ammunition for a weapon that doesn't use it.

entries.name: Level 17 — Discipline Defines the Weapon
entries: Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with a weapon or an Unarmed Strike, you can treat that attack as possessing any weapon property or equipment qualification required by one of your Fighting Styles gained from this Pact, solely for determining whether that Fighting Style applies. This doesn't actually grant the property to the weapon and doesn't alter the attack for any other rule.

optionalfeature.name: Unrestricted Discipline
entries: Rules exist to teach a technique safely. Mastery begins when you understand which parts of those rules were never essential. Your disciplines no longer demand perfect circumstances before they answer you.

entries.name: Loosen the Form
entries: Whenever a Fighting Style gained from Pact of the Martial Discipline has a restriction on how its benefit can be used, you can relax one of the following restrictions each time that Fighting Style applies:

items: A required minimum distance moved is reduced by 10 feet, to a minimum of 0 feet.
A required distance from a creature is reduced by 5 feet, to a minimum of 0 feet.
A range or reach limitation imposed specifically by the Fighting Style increases by 10 feet.
A requirement that you haven't moved, have moved, or remain in a particular position can be ignored.
A requirement concerning whether the target is adjacent to, within reach of, or farther away from another creature can be ignored.
A Fighting Style that requires a particular direction of movement, such as moving toward or away from a creature, can function with movement in any direction.

entries: You can relax only one restriction of a Fighting Style at a time. This feature doesn't remove resource costs, action costs, requirements to hit or miss, or limitations on how often a Fighting Style can be used.

entries.name: Level 11 — Flexible Execution
entries: You can relax up to two restrictions simultaneously whenever a Fighting Style gained from this Pact applies. In addition, if a Fighting Style requires a specific type of combat event to trigger, such as making an Opportunity Attack, entering a creature's reach, leaving a creature's reach, or taking a particular combat action, you can treat a closely equivalent combat event as satisfying that trigger. For example, a feature that triggers when a creature enters your reach could also trigger when you move into that creature's reach.

entries.name: Level 17 — Technique Without Constraint
entries: Whenever a Fighting Style gained from Pact of the Martial Discipline applies, you can ignore any positional, movement, distance, facing, adjacency, or target-placement restriction imposed by that Fighting Style. You must still satisfy its core trigger, expend any required resource, and obey any limit on how often it can be used.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of Hunger for Power
entries: Power is never enough. Every victory reveals another height you have yet to reach, and every height conquered only reveals another beyond it. Your hunger isn't for flesh, wealth, or knowledge. You crave the strength possessed by those powerful enough to stand in your way. By overcoming worthy opponents, you can seize fragments of that strength and permanently reshape yourself with them. You gain the following benefits.

Power first changes the vessel that contains it. The first thing your hunger devours is weakness itself, and your body begins discarding needs that once dictated whether you lived or died. Power begins to flow through your body with greater efficiency. Movements that once required effort become instinctive, fluid, and unnaturally precise. The power within you is no longer dormant. It begins to follow every attack you make, adding a fraction of your accumulated strength to every blow.

Your body has endured enough force to understand how to resist it. Moving you against your will becomes increasingly difficult, and every layer of power makes your body harder to break. The limitations you were born with cease to be absolute. Strength, speed, endurance, intellect, instinct, and presence become qualities that can simply be pushed further. Your power begins reinforcing more than flesh. Fear loses its grip, influence struggles to take root, and your mind becomes increasingly difficult to bend against your will.

Your body no longer adapts only to mundane hardship. Poison, flame, steel, supernatural energy, and even hostile magic become forces your growing existence learns to endure. Gravity and physical restraint begin to lose their authority over you. Your own power becomes sufficient to support your body where the world no longer does. You have grown tired of being told that something can't be harmed. Resistance is merely another obstacle, immunity merely a greater one, and obstacles exist to be surpassed.
Survival is no longer a struggle your body must consciously endure. It has become the natural state to which your existence constantly returns.

entries.name: Sense Power
entries: After you observe a creature take an action, make an attack, cast a spell, or use a feature, you can tell whether its Challenge Rating is high enough to grant you Power Points through Claim Power. You don't learn its exact Challenge Rating. If the creature has no Challenge Rating, use its character level instead.

entries.name: Claim Power
entries: When a hostile creature that you participated in defeating is reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can claim a fragment of its power. The creature must have a Challenge Rating equal to or greater than your Proficiency Bonus. You gain Power Points equal to the creature's Challenge Rating. If the creature has no Challenge Rating, you instead gain Power Points equal to its character level. Once you gain Power Points this way, you can't gain Power Points again until you finish a Short or Long Rest. The same individual creature can grant you Power Points only once.

A creature created, summoned, controlled, or deliberately provided by you or one of your allies can't grant you Power Points. Your Power Points have no maximum, don't disappear when you rest, and remain until you spend them.

entries.name: Endless Growth
entries: When you finish a Short or Long Rest, you can spend your accumulated Power Points on any improvement below that your current level has unlocked. Unless an improvement says otherwise, you can purchase it more than once. All improvements gained through this feat are permanent.

entries.name: Level 1 — Fortify
entries: You no longer need to eat, drink, or breathe. You can still eat, drink, and breathe normally if you choose to. You have Advantage on saving throws against Exhaustion.

entries.name: Tireless Body
entries: You require only 4 hours of rest to complete a Long Rest. During those 4 hours, you don't need to sleep. You can spend the time sitting, keeping watch, reading, maintaining equipment, eating or drinking by choice, meditating, or performing other light activity. You can't perform strenuous activity during this time, such as fighting, casting spells, traveling at a normal pace, or performing heavy physical labor. You can still benefit from only one Long Rest in a 24-hour period, as normal.

entries.name: Fortify
entries: 3 Power Points → Increase your Hit Point Maximum by 1. Your Hit Point maximum permanently increases by 1. You can purchase this improvement any number of times.

entries.name: Level 3 — Refine
entries: Your Speed increases by 5 feet. Your jump distance is doubled. Standing up from Prone costs you only 5 feet of movement.

entries.name: Unrestricted Movement
entries: You gain a Climb Speed and Swim Speed equal to your Walking Speed.

entries.name: Refine
entries: 4 Power Points → Refine one Skill. Choose one skill. If you aren't proficient in that skill, you gain proficiency in it. If you're already proficient in that skill, you instead gain Expertise in it. You can't purchase this improvement more than once for the same skill.

entries.name: Level 5 — Empower
entries: Your Speed increases by an additional 5 feet, for a total increase of 10 feet from this feat. You gain a bonus to Initiative equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded up.

entries.name: Overwhelming Strength
entries: Your attacks deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Empower
entries: 6 Power Points → Increase your Power Damage by 1. Your Power Damage bonus starts at 0 and permanently increases by 1 each time you purchase this improvement. Whenever you deal damage with an attack, that attack deals additional damage equal to your Power Damage bonus. The additional damage is one damage type already dealt by the attack. This benefit applies to every attack you make. Your Power Damage bonus can't exceed your Proficiency Bonus.

entries.name: Example
entries: If your Power Damage bonus is +3 and you hit with four attacks, each of those attacks deals 3 additional damage.

entries.name: Level 7 — Harden
entries: You count as one Size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift. You have Advantage on ability checks and saving throws made to resist being Grappled, Restrained, knocked Prone, pushed, or otherwise forcibly moved.

entries.name: Unbreakable Landing
entries: Whenever you take Falling damage, reduce that damage by an amount equal to 5 × your character level, to a minimum of 0.

entries.name: Harden
entries: 8 Power Points → Increase your Armor Class by 1. Your AC permanently increases by 1. You can purchase this improvement a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If your Proficiency Bonus later increases, the maximum number of times you can purchase this improvement increases accordingly. This bonus applies whether you are armored, unarmored, or wielding a Shield.

entries.name: Level 9 — Transcend
entries: When you make an ability check using a skill or tool in which you have proficiency, a d20 roll of 4 or lower is treated as a 5. Aging no longer causes your physical capabilities to deteriorate.

entries.name: Purified Body
entries: You are Immune to Disease. You also have Advantage on saving throws against the Poisoned condition.

entries.name: Transcend
entries: 10 Power Points → Increase one Ability Score by 1. Choose Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. The chosen Ability Score permanently increases by 1. You can purchase this improvement any number of times, and you can choose the same Ability Score repeatedly. There is no maximum Ability Score imposed by this feat. This improvement can increase an Ability Score beyond its normal maximum.

entries.name: Level 11 — Unyielding
entries: You have Advantage on saving throws against being Charmed or Frightened. Whenever you fail a saving throw against either of those conditions, you can repeat that saving throw at the end of your next turn, even if the effect wouldn't normally allow another saving throw at that time.

entries.name: Unconquered Mind
entries: You can't be magically put to sleep. You also have Advantage on saving throws against effects that would possess you or directly control your actions.

entries.name: Unyielding
entries: 10 Power Points → Gain proficiency in one Saving Throw. Choose Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability. If you already have proficiency in that saving throw, you must choose another. Each saving throw can benefit from this improvement only once.

entries.name: Level 13 — Adapt
entries: You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws. You also have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.

entries.name: Reject Magic
entries: When you fail a saving throw against a spell or magical effect, you can reroll the saving throw and must use the new roll. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Adapt
entries: 15 Power Points → Gain one Damage Resistance. Choose any damage type. You permanently gain Resistance to the chosen damage type. This can include Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Acid, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Thunder, or another damage type that exists in the game. You can purchase this improvement multiple times, choosing a different damage type each time. Choosing a damage type to which you already have Resistance provides no additional benefit.

entries.name: Level 15 — Unshackle
entries: You can Hover. While conscious, you can remain suspended in the air up to 10 feet above a surface capable of supporting you. While hovering this way, you can move horizontally using your normal Speed and can ascend or descend within this 10-foot limit. You don't fall at the end of your turn while hovering. at the start of each of your turns, you can choose one of the following conditions affecting you: Grappled, Prone, or Restrained.

If that condition was caused by a creature or effect whose Challenge Rating is lower than your character level, you immediately end the chosen condition on yourself. If the source has no Challenge Rating, use its character level instead.

entries.name: Defy the Fall
entries: While you are conscious, you take no Falling damage.

entries.name: Unshackle
entries: 20 Power Points → Gain one Condition Immunity. Choose one condition. You permanently gain Immunity to the chosen condition. You can purchase this improvement multiple times, choosing a different condition each time.

entries.name: Level 17 — Break Resistance
entries: Your Hover develops into true flight. You gain a Flying Speed equal to your Walking Speed, and you can Hover. You ignore Difficult Terrain. Your Speed can't be reduced below half its normal value by a spell or magical effect unless that effect reduces your Speed to 0. Your attacks and damaging effects count as magical whenever a rule or feature distinguishes between magical and nonmagical damage.

entries.name: Unstoppable Motion
entries: If your Speed is 0 at the start of your turn, you can end one spell or magical effect on yourself that is causing your Speed to become 0. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

entries.name: Break Resistance
entries: 20 Power Points → Overcome one Damage Resistance. Choose one damage type. The first time you purchase this improvement for that damage type, damage you deal of that type ignores Resistance. You can purchase this improvement a second time for the same damage type. If you do, damage you deal of that type also ignores Immunity.

items: First Purchase. Ignore Resistance to the chosen damage type.
Second Purchase. Ignore both Resistance and Immunity to the chosen damage type.

entries: Further purchases for the same damage type provide no additional benefit.

entries.name: Level 19 — Absolute Adaptation
entries: Whenever you finish a Short or Long Rest, you remove one level of Exhaustion. You no longer suffer penalties caused solely by extreme heat, extreme cold, high altitude, atmospheric pressure, underwater pressure, or similar environmental conditions. This doesn't prevent damage or other specific effects that such an environment directly causes. You also have Resistance to damage dealt by spells.

entries.name: Existence Without Need
entries: You no longer need sleep. You can't be magically aged. You must still complete a Long Rest to regain features and resources, but you can remain conscious throughout the entire rest and spend it performing the same kinds of light activity permitted by Tireless Body.

entries.name: Absolute Adaptation
entries: 35 Power Points → Gain one Damage Immunity. Choose one damage type to which you already have Resistance. Your Resistance to that damage type permanently becomes Immunity. You can purchase this improvement multiple times, choosing a different qualifying damage type each time.

entries.name: Example of Growth
entries: A Level 13 character with a Proficiency Bonus of +5 participates in defeating a CR 9 hostile creature and gains 9 Power Points. They can't gain Power Points through Claim Power again until they finish a Short or Long Rest. After taking a Short Rest, they later participate in defeating a CR 12 creature and gain another 12 Power Points, giving them 21 Power Points total.

They could spend 15 Power Points to gain Fire Resistance through Adapt and retain 6 Power Points; or spend 10 Power Points to increase Strength by 1 through Transcend and 6 Power Points to increase Power Damage by 1 through Empower, retaining 5 Power Points. They can instead spend nothing and save all 21 Power Points for a more expensive improvement.

There is no maximum to the amount of Power Points you can accumulate, and Hunger for Power has no fixed endpoint. As long as you can continue overcoming sufficiently powerful opponents, you can continue using their power to surpass your previous limits.

optionalfeature.name: The Strong Feed the Strong
entries: Power recognizes power. The greater the thing you overcome, the more of it remains for you to claim. You have learned not to let any of that strength go to waste. Your hunger no longer quiets after feeding once. Power only makes you capable of consuming more.

entries.name: Greater Prey
entries: When Claim Power grants you Power Points from a creature whose Challenge Rating or character level is greater than your character level, you gain additional Power Points equal to the difference. For example, if you are level 10 and claim power from a CR 14 creature, you gain 18 Power Points instead of 14.

entries.name: Level 11 — Nothing Wasted
entries: When you would gain Power Points through Claim Power, you can gain at least an amount equal to your character level, even if the defeated creature's Challenge Rating is lower. The creature must still meet every normal requirement of Claim Power, including the minimum Challenge Rating requirement.

entries.name: Level 17 — Bottomless Hunger
entries: The restriction in Claim Power that prevents you from gaining Power Points again until you finish a Short or Long Rest no longer applies. You can gain Power Points from every qualifying hostile creature you participate in defeating. All other restrictions of Claim Power still apply, including that the same individual creature can grant you Power Points only once and that creatures created, summoned, controlled, or deliberately provided by you or your allies can't grant Power Points.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Stolen Gift
entries: What another creature possesses is only theirs until you decide otherwise.

entries.name: Claim Slots
entries: You have a number of Claim Slots equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended Claim Slots when you finish a Long Rest.

entries.name: Claim a Gift
entries: Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet uses a feature, trait, spell, special attack, movement mode, sense, Resistance, Immunity, or another distinct ability, you can record that ability as a Gift. Recording a Gift requires no action and expends no Claim Slot. You retain a Gift after recording it and can remember any number of Gifts. You don't need to keep the original creature nearby, and the creature doesn't lose the ability you copied.
You learn enough about the Gift to understand broadly what it does, but you don't automatically learn unrelated statistics or hidden information about the creature.

entries.name: Use a Gift
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one Gift you have recorded and expend 1 Claim Slot. For the next 1 hour, you gain an imitation of that Gift. Unless the Gift says otherwise, you use your own statistics rather than those of the creature you copied it from. If the Gift requires an Attack Roll, you can use Charisma for that attack. If the Gift requires a Saving Throw, its save DC is 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + your Charisma modifier.

A Gift can reproduce abilities such as Flying, Climbing, Swimming, Burrowing, Hovering, Darkvision, Blindsight, Tremorsense, Truesight, Damage Resistance or Immunity, natural weapons, unusual attacks, supernatural movement, regeneration, defensive traits, activated creature abilities, spells, or other distinct abilities you have witnessed.
