If a Gift depends on a resource belonging specifically to the original creature, you don't gain that creature's resource pool unless the Gift itself explicitly provides one.

entries.name: Stolen Spell
entries: If the Gift is a spell, you can cast that spell once while the Gift is active without expending a Spell Slot. You don't need Material Components unless the spell's Material Component has a listed cost. There is no restriction based on the spell's level. Once you cast the stolen spell, that Gift immediately ends.

The spell remains recorded in your collection. You can activate the same Spell Gift again later by expending another Claim Slot, allowing you to cast it once again. A Spell Gift has no separate cooldown or once-per-rest restriction beyond your available Claim Slots.

entries.name: Permanent Gifts
entries: If a Gift normally represents a passive ability rather than something used a limited number of times, you retain that ability for the full 1-hour duration. For example, if you activate a recorded Truesight, Damage Resistance, or Flying Speed, you retain that copied trait until the Gift ends. If the Gift itself has a shorter duration or naturally ends under certain conditions, those restrictions still apply.

entries.name: Things That Cannot Be Taken
entries: You can't record or reproduce Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic transformations, an entire Spellcasting or Pact Magic feature, an entire class, subclass, or collection of class levels, an entire stat block, an ability whose primary purpose is creating permanent duplicates of yourself, or an ability whose primary purpose is permanently creating additional creatures. However, an individual spell or individual distinct ability used through one of those larger features can still be recorded as a Gift.
For example, you can't steal a Wizard's entire Spellcasting feature, but you can record a specific spell you witness that Wizard cast.

entries.name: Multiple Gifts
entries: Starting at Warlock level 11, you can have up to two Gifts active simultaneously. At Warlock level 17, you can have up to three Gifts active simultaneously. Each Gift still requires its own Claim Slot. If activating a new Gift would cause you to exceed your maximum number of active Gifts, you choose one of your currently active Gifts to end immediately.

optionalfeature.name: I Saw That
entries: You don't need to understand a Gift before you take it. Observation is enough. One moment of exposure is all the invitation you require.

entries.name: Instant Claim
entries: When a creature you can see within 60 feet uses an ability that you can record as a Gift, you can immediately activate that Gift as part of the same moment, expending 1 Claim Slot but requiring no Bonus Action. The Gift becomes active after the triggering ability finishes resolving. You must still be able to record that ability normally through Claim a Gift.

entries.name: Level 11 — Steal the Timing
entries: When you activate a Gift with Instant Claim, you can use that Gift immediately if it normally requires an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction. Doing so requires no additional action. If the Gift is a spell, you can cast the stolen spell immediately as part of this use.

entries.name: Level 17 — Better the Original
entries: The first time you use a Gift activated through Instant Claim, choose one of the following benefits that can apply to that use:

items: Gain Advantage on one Attack Roll made with the Gift.
Impose Disadvantage on one Saving Throw caused by the Gift.
Maximize one damage or healing die of the Gift.
Increase the Gift's range by 60 feet.
Double one movement speed granted by the Gift until the end of the turn.

optionalfeature.name: Composite Theft
entries: A stolen Gift doesn't need to remain whole. You have learned to separate function from form, keeping only the parts worth taking. What others possess as one ability, you can rebuild into something better suited to you.

entries.name: Borrowed Pieces
entries: When you activate a Gift, you can choose one distinct component of another Gift you have recorded and graft that component onto the active Gift for its duration.
The borrowed component must be something that can function independently, such as:

items: a movement mode
a sense
a Damage Resistance
a natural weapon damage type
a range increase
a secondary movement rider
a passive defensive trait
a non-resource passive effect

entries: You don't gain the entire second Gift, only the chosen component. Using Borrowed Pieces doesn't expend an additional Claim Slot.

entries.name: Level 11 — Two Things Worth Taking
entries: You can graft up to two components from recorded Gifts onto a single active Gift. The two components can come from the same Gift or from different Gifts.

entries.name: Level 17 — Perfect Reconstruction
entries: When you activate a Gift, you can rebuild it from pieces of your recorded collection. Instead of activating one recorded Gift exactly as copied, choose up to three compatible components from Gifts you have recorded and combine them into one reconstructed Gift for 1 hour. The reconstructed Gift still counts as one active Gift and costs only one Claim Slot. A reconstructed Gift can't reproduce an ability prohibited by Things That Cannot Be Taken, and the DM determines whether chosen components are mechanically compatible.

optionalfeature.name: Pact of the Unwritten Rule
entries: Once a limitation has stopped you, it never gets to stop you the same way again.

entries.name: Record a Restriction
entries: Whenever a rule, condition, environmental restriction, magical effect, or defensive property directly prevents, limits, or reduces something you attempted to do, you can record that restriction. Recording a restriction requires no action. You can remember any number of recorded restrictions.

entries.name: Break the Rule
entries: As a Bonus Action, choose one restriction you have recorded. For 1 hour, you can ignore that restriction whenever it would apply to you.

Examples of restrictions you could record include Difficult Terrain slowing you, needing a free hand to perform something, being unable to speak because of Silence, being unable to see a target because of Darkness, needing to breathe underwater, being unable to move through a particular kind of barrier, a spell preventing teleportation, a condition preventing a particular action, a feature requiring you to remain on the ground, an effect preventing healing, an effect preventing you from taking Reactions, a magical effect limiting your Speed, an effect preventing you from casting spells, or a creature's Damage Resistance reducing damage you deal.

You ignore only the specific restriction you recorded, not the entire source that created it. For example, recording "I can't cast spells while Silenced" would let you cast despite that restriction, but wouldn't automatically make you immune to every other effect of the spell or area.

entries.name: Break Resistance
entries: If a creature's Damage Resistance reduces damage dealt by one of your attacks or damaging effects, you can record that Resistance as a restriction. While you are ignoring that recorded restriction, your attacks and damaging effects ignore that creature's Resistance to the recorded damage type.

entries.name: It Must Stop You First
entries: You can only record a restriction after it has actually affected you or something you attempted to do. Knowing that something could stop, limit, or reduce you isn't enough. You have to personally encounter the limitation at least once.

entries.name: No Longer Applicable
entries: Once you activate a recorded restriction, that restriction simply doesn't apply to you for the duration. If it says "You can't take Reactions," you can take Reactions. If it says "Your Speed becomes 0," that part doesn't affect you. If it says "You can't regain Hit Points," you can regain Hit Points normally. It doesn't automatically end or dispel the original effect; you just ignore the recorded limitation.

entries.name: More Than One Rule
entries: At Warlock level 11, you can have two recorded restrictions ignored simultaneously. At Warlock level 17, you can have three. Activating each restriction requires its own Bonus Action.

optionalfeature.name: Once Is Enough
entries: You no longer need to be the one who suffers first. A rule only has to prove that it exists once. After that, you already know where it breaks.

entries.name: Witnessed Restriction
entries: When a rule, condition, environmental restriction, magical effect, or defensive property directly prevents, limits, or reduces something attempted by a creature you can see within 60 feet, you can record that restriction as though it had affected you personally. You must be able to perceive what actually prevented or limited the creature. Merely knowing that a restriction exists isn't enough. This counts as satisfying It Must Stop You First for that restriction.

entries.name: Level 11 — Shared Exception
entries: When you use Break the Rule, you can choose one willing creature you can see within 30 feet. For as long as you ignore the chosen restriction, that creature ignores the same restriction whenever it would apply to it. You can change the chosen creature as a Bonus Action without ending Break the Rule.

entries.name: Level 17 — Precedent
entries: Once you have recorded a restriction, you can activate Break the Rule for that restriction at the moment it would affect you, requiring no action. You can do this even if the restriction itself would prevent you from taking Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions.

optionalfeature.name: The Rule Bends Both Ways
entries: A limitation defines more than what can't be done. It also reveals exactly where reality expects resistance. Once you understand that pressure, you can push in the opposite direction.

entries.name: Invert the Restriction
entries: While you are ignoring a recorded restriction with Break the Rule, once on each of your turns when that restriction would normally hinder, reduce, or prevent something you do, you can instead gain a benefit based on the nature of that restriction. The benefit must directly oppose the restriction and lasts only for that instance.

items: A restriction that would reduce your Speed can instead increase your Speed by the same amount.
Difficult Terrain that would cost additional movement can instead cost you no movement for the affected space.
An effect that would impose Disadvantage on one of your rolls can instead grant Advantage on that roll.
An effect that would reduce damage you deal can instead cause that damage to ignore the reduction and deal additional damage equal to your Charisma modifier.
An effect that would prevent you from taking a Reaction can instead allow you to take one additional Reaction before the start of your next turn.

An effect that would prevent you from regaining Hit Points can instead cause the next healing you receive before the start of your next turn to restore additional Hit Points equal to your Warlock level.

entries: The benefit must be a direct inversion of the specific restriction you recorded. It doesn't grant unrelated abilities.

entries.name: Level 11 — Turn the Pressure
entries: When Invert the Restriction grants you Advantage, additional movement, additional damage, additional healing, or an additional Reaction, you can grant that same benefit to one willing creature you can see within 30 feet instead of yourself.

entries.name: Level 17 — Reality Overcorrects
entries: The first time on each of your turns that you use Invert the Restriction, you can apply the inverted benefit at double its normal numerical value, if it has one. For example, a 10-foot Speed reduction could become a 20-foot Speed increase, and additional damage equal to your Charisma modifier would become twice your Charisma modifier.

optionalfeature.name: Your Rule, Not Mine
entries: A restriction doesn't vanish simply because you refuse to obey it. The rule still exists. You have merely decided who it applies to instead.

entries.name: Return the Restriction
entries: While you are ignoring a recorded restriction with Break the Rule, when a creature you can see causes that same restriction to apply to you, you can use your Reaction to force that creature to suffer an equivalent restriction until the start of your next turn. The reflected restriction must be one that can meaningfully apply to that creature.

items: If it prevents you from taking Reactions, that creature can't take Reactions.
If it reduces your Speed, its Speed is reduced by the same amount.
If it imposes Disadvantage on your attacks, its attacks have Disadvantage.
If it prevents you from regaining Hit Points, that creature can't regain Hit Points.
If its Resistance reduces damage you deal, it loses that Resistance against your damage for the duration.
If it prevents you from casting spells, it can't cast spells for the duration.

entries: You don't transfer the original effect itself. You impose only the specific recorded restriction you are currently ignoring.

entries.name: Level 13 — Same Rule for Everyone
entries: When you use Return the Restriction, you can affect up to a number of creatures equal to your Charisma modifier, provided each creature is contributing to or benefiting from the same recorded restriction and is within 30 feet of the original creature. Each affected creature suffers the reflected restriction until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Level 17 — The Exception Becomes the Rule
entries: When you use Return the Restriction, the reflected restriction lasts for 1 minute instead. An affected creature can repeat the saving throw, if any saving throw was originally associated with the restriction, at the end of each of its turns, ending the reflected restriction on itself on a success. If the original restriction had no saving throw, the reflected restriction lasts for the full duration unless ended by an effect that could normally remove an equivalent condition or limitation.

optionalfeature.name: Relentless Casting
entries: Once the spell begins, interruption only makes you force it through harder.

Whenever you cast a spell and one of the following causes that spell to fail or have no effect against at least one target, you can immediately attempt to force the same spell through again against one affected target:

items: The target succeeds on its Saving Throw.
Your Spell Attack misses.
The spell is Counterspelled.
The target's Resistance or Immunity causes the spell to deal reduced or no damage.

entries: You don't expend another Spell Slot or Material Component. Resolve the spell against that target again as though you had just cast it, including making another Spell Attack or forcing another Saving Throw as appropriate. You can continue doing this until the spell successfully affects that target or you choose to stop. Each additional attempt after the first causes you to take 1d12 Force damage after that attempt is resolved. This damage can't be reduced or prevented and can't reduce you below 1 Hit Point.

optionalfeature.name: Spellbreaker's Instinct
entries: Magic always reveals itself in the instant before it takes form. You have learned to recognize that fragile moment and strike directly into it. To you, a spell is not an inevitability—it is simply another thing that can be broken. Whenever a creature you can see within 60 feet casts a spell, you can immediately make one Spell Attack against that creature.

items: The attack requires no Reaction.
The attack happens before the spell resolves.
The attack uses your Charisma modifier for the attack roll.
On a hit, the attack deals 1d10 + your Charisma modifier Force damage.

entries: If the attack hits, the caster must make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC.
On a failed save, choose one:

items: The spell is Countered and has no effect.
If the spell requires Concentration, the caster begins it with Disadvantage on all Concentration saves until the end of its next turn.
The spell's damage ignores none of your Resistances or Immunities this casting.

entries.name: Break Through Resistance
entries: When this attack hits a creature that has Resistance to Force damage, you ignore that Resistance. If the creature has Immunity to Force damage, treat that Immunity as Resistance instead.

optionalfeature.name: Echoes Left Behind
entries: Every hand leaves something behind, even when no fingerprint remains. Places remember those who passed through them, and objects remember how they were used. You have learned how to make those silent memories answer. When you touch an object, structure, or section of terrain and concentrate on it for 1 minute, you can read fragments of impressions left upon it.
Choose one of the following questions:

items.name: Who Used This?
items.entry: Learn a general description of the most recent creature to meaningfully use or interact with it.

items.name: What Happened Here?
items.entry: Learn the most significant event involving it within the last 24 hours.

items.name: Where Did It Come From?
items.entry: Learn the general direction and approximate distance to the place where the object was created, last assembled, or last considered its home.

items.name: What Is Hidden?
items.entry: Learn whether it contains a hidden compartment, concealed mechanism, secret entrance, trap, or intentionally hidden feature.

items.name: How Does It Work?
items.entry: Learn the object's intended mundane or magical function and the basic method normally used to operate it.

items.name: Where Did They Go?
items.entry: If a creature interacted with the target within the last 24 hours, learn the direction that creature traveled immediately afterward.

entries: You receive the information as brief sensory impressions, emotions, images, sounds, or instinctive understanding, rather than a perfect recording.

entries.name: Dig Deeper
entries: After receiving an answer, you can immediately ask one additional question from the list about the same target. Doing so causes you to take 1d6 Psychic damage, which can't be reduced or prevented. You can continue asking additional questions in this way, taking an additional 1d6 Psychic damage for each question after the first.

entries.name: Old Memories Fade
entries: Normally, this Invocation can read impressions from only the last 24 hours. At Warlock level 7, this increases to 30 days. At Warlock level 13, it increases to 1 year. At Warlock level 17, you can read impressions from any point in the target's history, provided some meaningful trace still remains.

optionalfeature.name: Sovereign's Mark
entries: Those who stand before your authority don't simply leave your presence unchanged. Once the Crown has acknowledged someone, distance alone can't fully sever that connection. Your subjects may wander beyond sight, but the Crown remembers where its gaze has fallen.

entries.name: Mark a Subject
entries: Until you finish a Long Rest, dismiss the mark, or replace it. After you speak directly with a creature for at least 1 minute, you can mark that creature as one of your Subjects. You can have a number of Subjects equal to your Proficiency Bonus simultaneously. If you mark another creature while already at this maximum, choose one existing Subject; its mark immediately ends. You can dismiss a mark at any time. A creature doesn't automatically know that it has been marked.

entries.name: The Crown Knows Its Subjects
entries: While the creature remains your Subject. While a Subject is on the same plane as you, you instinctively know the general direction toward it; whether it is within 300 feet, 1 mile, 10 miles, or farther away; and whether it is conscious or unconscious. This feature doesn't reveal the Subject's exact location. Barriers, darkness, invisibility, and ordinary concealment don't prevent this awareness.

entries.name: Speak Across Distance
entries: For as long as you continue the communication. You can speak directly into the mind of any Subject on the same plane. Only that Subject hears your words unless you choose to speak normally as well. The Subject can mentally reply to you while the connection remains open. You don't need to share a language to communicate simple concepts, intentions, emotions, images, or commands. Complex conversation still requires a language both of you understand. Distance doesn't prevent this communication as long as you and the Subject remain on the same plane.

entries.name: Through the Eyes of a Subject
entries: Establishing the connection requires an Action; switching senses afterward requires no Action. Up to 10 minutes. Choose one of your Subjects on the same plane. For the duration, you can perceive through that Subject's senses instead of your own. You can use every sense the Subject normally possesses, including sight, hearing, smell, Darkvision, Blindsight, Tremorsense, Truesight, or another special sense naturally available to that Subject. You perceive what the Subject perceives from its position and perspective.

While using the Subject's senses, you are Blinded and Deafened with regard to your own surroundings. You can switch back to your own senses at any time. While the duration remains, you can return to the Subject's senses at any time. The Subject doesn't automatically know that you are perceiving through it. You can still use Speak Across Distance with that Subject while perceiving through its senses. This effect ends early if the Subject leaves your plane of existence, its mark ends, you become Incapacitated, or you choose to end the effect.

entries.name: Authority Finds You
entries: You can use Assume Command against one of your Subjects even if that creature is outside Assume Command's normal 60-foot range, can't physically hear you, or isn't currently visible to you. The Subject must still be on the same plane. Your command is transmitted directly through Speak Across Distance, so the Subject counts as hearing and understanding the command for the purpose of Assume Command. If the Subject is within 1 mile, Assume Command functions normally.
If the Subject is farther than 1 mile away, it has Advantage on its Saving Throw against Assume Command. All other rules and durations of Assume Command remain unchanged.

entries.name: Summoned Before the Crown
entries: Activating this feature requires a Bonus Action. Up to 1 minute. Choose one of your Subjects on the same plane. For the duration, you know its exact direction, you know its approximate distance from you, and the Subject instinctively knows the shortest reasonable direction toward you. If that Subject fails a Saving Throw against your Assume Command during this duration, you can include an instruction such as "Come to me" as part of the command without that portion counting toward the command's normal complexity.

The Subject still uses its own movement and abilities normally to reach you. This feature doesn't teleport the Subject or allow it to pass through obstacles it couldn't normally cross. You can end this effect at any time with no Action required.

optionalfeature.name: Imperishable Decree
entries: Some commands are meant to outlive battles, kingdoms, and even the voice that first pronounced them. Your authority no longer rests upon the mind alone; it is carved into flesh, will, and soul as an immutable law. Once the Crown has spoken its decree, neither time nor another master's hand can teach the subject to disobey.

entries.name: Inscribe a Decree
entries: Activating this feature takes 1 minute. Permanent until fulfilled, dismissed, or otherwise ended by this Invocation. Choose one creature you can see within 60 feet that can understand you. Speak a command, prohibition, duty, standing instruction, or conditional order to that creature.

The decree can be significantly more complex than Assume Command and can describe something the creature must do, something it must never do, someone it must protect, somewhere it must remain, a secret it must never reveal, a person or group it must obey, a condition that causes it to perform a specific task, a long-term responsibility, or a rule governing its future behavior.

Examples include: "Never reveal what happened in this chamber," "Protect this bloodline for as long as you exist," "Whenever this city is attacked, defend its people," "You will never willingly harm me or my companions," "When you find the man bearing this symbol, bring him before me," "Guard this door and permit entry only to those carrying my seal," or "If I die, deliver this letter to my successor."

entries.name: Willing Subjects
entries: Permanent. A willing creature automatically accepts the decree. No Saving Throw is required.

entries.name: Unwilling Subjects
entries: Permanent on a failed save. An unwilling creature makes a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the decree takes hold permanently. On a successful save, the decree fails to take hold. A creature that successfully saves against a particular decree can't be targeted by that same decree again until you finish a Long Rest. Once the decree takes hold, the creature receives no further Saving Throws merely because time passes.

entries.name: Bound in Body and Soul
entries: While the decree exists. An Imperishable Decree binds the creature's body, mind, will, and soul simultaneously. The creature can't willingly or unwillingly perform an action that directly violates the decree.

This remains true even if the creature is affected by another effect that would normally control or replace its actions, including being Charmed or Dominated, possession, magical or psionic mind control, direct control of its body, forced movement or forced actions, memory alteration, personality or alignment alteration, control or manipulation of its soul, another creature choosing its actions, transformation into another form, or unconscious or altered states in which another effect attempts to direct its behavior.

If another effect attempts to force the creature to violate your decree, the conflicting portion of that effect fails. For example, if your decree states "Never harm me" and another creature completely controls the Subject and commands it to attack you, the Subject can't make that attack. The controller may command it to perform other actions that don't violate the decree. An Imperishable Decree therefore takes precedence over other forms of control whenever their instructions conflict.

entries.name: The Body Obeys
entries: While the decree exists. If fulfilling the decree requires the creature to act, its body must cooperate with the decree even if its conscious mind resists. It must use its movement, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, speech, possessions, spells, features, and other available capabilities as reasonably necessary to obey.

A creature can't deliberately paralyze itself, surrender control of its body, render itself unconscious, alter its own memories, transform itself, or place itself under another creature's control for the purpose of escaping or violating the decree.

entries.name: The Soul Remembers
entries: While the decree exists. The decree is attached to the creature's identity and soul, not merely its current body. Changing bodies, possessing another body, transforming, being reincarnated, being resurrected, or otherwise continuing existence in another physical form doesn't remove the decree. If the creature temporarily ceases to possess a usable body, the decree remains dormant rather than ending and resumes functioning when the creature can act again.

entries.name: Bound to the Word
entries: While the decree remains active. The creature is compelled to act according to the decree's wording. If the decree prohibits something, the creature simply can't violate that prohibition. If obedience is temporarily impossible, the creature isn't required to accomplish the impossible. The decree remains active and resumes compelling obedience as soon as compliance becomes possible again.

entries.name: Conditional Decrees
entries: Its activation is defined when the decree is created. Permanent until triggered and completed, unless written to repeat. A decree can remain dormant until a condition you specify occurs. For example: "If anyone opens this vault without my permission, sound the alarm and attack them." You can also create a recurring decree. For example: "Whenever the bells ring three times, return to this fortress." A recurring decree continues to function whenever its condition occurs unless its wording states otherwise.

entries.name: The Crown Interprets
entries: While the decree exists. A decree follows the meaning and intent you held when you created it, rather than merely its most technically convenient interpretation. The creature can't escape through deliberate grammatical loopholes, technicalities, indirect actions, intermediaries, or intentional misinterpretation. If circumstances make the wording ambiguous, the decree follows the interpretation that most closely reflects your original intent.

entries.name: Command From Afar
entries: Instantaneous modification. If the affected creature is also one of your Subjects from Sovereign's Mark, you can modify an existing decree on that creature while both of you are on the same plane. You communicate the alteration through Speak Across Distance. The creature receives no new Saving Throw if the alteration remains within the original purpose of the decree. A fundamentally unrelated command counts as a new decree.

entries.name: Revoke the Law
entries: Instantaneous. You can permanently end any Imperishable Decree you created, provided you and the affected creature are on the same plane.

optionalfeature.name: Edict of the Unthinking
entries: Your Crown gives silent matter a will: weapons, relics, machines, and landscapes rise to obey, alone or as a colossal body.

entries.name: Authority Without a Mind
entries: Your Pact of the Crown features can affect eligible targets without a mind, hearing, language, life, or creature status. This permanent authority binds their physical form and any supernatural essence. Genuinely mindless targets automatically fail mental saving throws against your Crown features. Targets with independent will save normally, regardless of Intelligence or ability to communicate.

entries.name: Matter Answers the Crown
entries: This benefit is permanent. You can command nonliving natural or artificial matter, including discrete masses, as objects even if they weren't previously considered objects. Eligible materials include earth, soil, sand, stone, gravel, clay, mud, minerals, ore, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, rubble, ash, and glass. Use the Crown-Bound Object stat block appropriate to the mass's Size.

entries.name: Animate the Unthinking
entries: When you command an eligible object or mass of material that normally can't move or act independently, you can animate it as a Crown-Bound Object. Use the Crown-Bound Object stat block corresponding to its actual Size: {@creature Tiny Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Small Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Medium Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Large Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, {@creature Huge Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}, or {@creature Gargantuan Crown-Bound Object|FftForbiddenTome}.

You can animate any number of Crown-Bound Objects of any Size. Animation grants movement, action, and obedience without transforming the target. Use the summon entry matching its Size for quick selection.

For quick-play combat, you can use the dedicated Slashing, Piercing, or Bludgeoning Crown-Bound Object summon matching the animated object's Size when that damage type represents the object. These stat blocks are simplified attack variants of the normal Crown-Bound Object rules.

entries.name: The Object Remains Itself
entries: While animated, the target retains its existing Armor Class, Hit Points, Ability Scores, Saving Throws, Skills, Speeds, Resistances, Immunities, Vulnerabilities, senses, attacks, damage dice, weapon properties, magical properties, traits, actions, special functions, and other statistics. The Crown-Bound Object stat block supplies missing statistics and capabilities; use original values when better or more appropriate.

entries.name: Bound to the Crown
entries: While animated, Crown-Bound Objects understand your instructions and intent and obey absolutely, without becoming Sapient or gaining personalities or independent desires. A command continues until completed, replaced, permanently impossible, or the animation ends. No further Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction from you is required.

entries.name: Floating Servants
entries: While animated, every Crown-Bound Object gains its stat block's Fly Speed and can Hover, regardless of whether its shape permits natural flight. This doesn't reshape it.

entries.name: Initiative
entries: While animated, Crown-Bound Objects act immediately after your turn, in an order you choose. They can use their movement, Action, available Bonus Action, Reaction, native abilities, and Crown-Bound abilities without spending any of your actions.

entries.name: Crown Strike
entries: As an Action, a Crown-Bound Object can make a Crown Strike instead of using a native attack.
Attack Roll: d20 + the object's appropriate Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
Damage: {@damage 1d4} + the same Strength or Dexterity modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.

The damage type is determined by the object's actual form, normally Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing, or another appropriate damage type provided by the object's actual magical or physical properties. This formula applies to ordinary Crown-Bound Objects. Crownforged Titans use their own Titan Attack Formula instead.

entries.name: Native Attacks
entries: An object can use a native attack with its normal action economy, damage dice, modifiers, Reach, Range, riders, magical properties, additional damage, special effects, and ammunition rules. It needn't replace a superior native attack with Crown Strike.

entries.name: Purpose of Form
entries: While animated, an object can use any Crown-Bound Forms its actual construction supports: Edged, Piercing, Crushing, Guardian, Grasping, or Projectile. It can qualify for multiple Forms; none transform it.

entries.name: Independent Servants
entries: While animated, Crown-Bound Objects independently carry out complex combat or physical tasks, understanding your intended result without step-by-step instructions.

entries.name: The Crown Has Hands
entries: While animated, an object can precisely manipulate itself and nearby objects as needed to fulfill commands, without literal hands. On ability checks using a Skill or Tool with which you are proficient, it can add your Proficiency Bonus, or twice that bonus if you have Expertise.

entries.name: Eyes of the Crown
entries: You can perceive through any Crown-Bound Object you control, using its stat block's senses and the original target's additional sensory functions until you stop. You can switch freely between your senses and those of your objects without an Action. You remain aware of your surroundings unless you choose to focus entirely through an object.

entries.name: One Crown, Many Bodies
entries: While animated and on the same plane, Crown-Bound Objects understand each other's intended actions and coordinate movement, combat, and work without speech or obstructing each other.

entries.name: Combined Strength
entries: Any number of Crown-Bound Objects working on the same task can combine their capacities to carry, lift, push, drag, support, restrain, hold in place, construct, or dismantle.

entries.name: Command the Function
entries: While animated, an object can independently use its native functions, including Magic Item properties, built-in spells, charges, command words, weapon properties, siege functions, vehicle controls, mechanisms, traps, and magical or technological devices. It can serve as its own wielder, wearer, rider, driver, or operator, manipulating controls, aiming, and speaking command words as needed. Ammunition, charges, fuel, and consumable components are spent normally.

entries.name: No Operator Required
entries: While animated, an object needs no other creature to hold, wear, wield, ride, or operate it to use its own functions. It gains no functions it didn't possess.

entries.name: Endless Labor
entries: While a command remains active, Crown-Bound Objects can perform ordinary physical labor continuously without Exhaustion. They still require the necessary materials, fuel, tools, and other resources.

entries.name: Coordinated Command
entries: You can issue the same command to any number of Crown-Bound Objects simultaneously.

entries.name: Command the Mindless
entries: Assume Command can affect mindless creatures without hearing or language. Those without independent will automatically fail the save; those with independent will save normally. Commands can govern movement, Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, attacks, spells, supernatural abilities, targets, object interactions, and other capabilities.

entries.name: Decree Upon Matter
entries: Prerequisite: Imperishable Decree. Using its normal action economy, you can place a permanent Imperishable Decree on eligible nonthinking targets, including objects, natural matter, structures, mechanisms, Crown-Bound Objects, and mindless creatures. Genuinely mindless targets make no Wisdom saving throw. The decree binds the target's physical form and supernatural essence. An otherwise motionless target can animate as a Crown-Bound Object whenever compliance requires action, then become motionless again without ending the decree.

entries.name: Level 5: Awakened Instruments
entries: When you gain this Invocation, all its base abilities become permanently available: animate objects and natural matter, grant independent movement and action, enable native functions, coordinate servants, perceive through them, and command mindless beings.

entries.name: Command the Possessed
entries: Your Crown features can target objects that are worn, wielded, carried, held, mounted, installed, operated, or otherwise actively possessed. This includes weapons, armor, shields, Magic Items, Spellcasting Focuses, equipment, tools, containers, ammunition, and vehicles. If your command directly opposes a creature's physical control over the object, that creature makes a Strength or Dexterity Saving Throw of its choice against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the object obeys you.

entries.name: Rebellion of Property
entries: While its command remains active, an object can physically oppose its possessor, such as hindering attacks or movement. If it can separate from the possessor, it can animate and leave as a Crown-Bound Object.

entries.name: Level 9: The Crown Uses All Things
Sovereign Activation
entries: While animated or under your Crown authority, an object satisfies its own abilities' requirements for Attunement, class, species, Ability Scores, command words, wielders, wearers, and operators. Use each ability's normal action economy. This doesn't attune you personally to the object.

entries.name: The Crown Supplies the Wielder
entries: While Sovereign Activation applies.
If an object's ability requires a wielder's Attack Bonus or Save DC but doesn't provide one itself, use the following values:
Attack Bonus = the object's appropriate Ability modifier + your Proficiency Bonus.
Save DC = 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the object's appropriate Ability modifier.
If the object already has a superior fixed Attack Bonus or Save DC, it can use the superior value.

entries.name: Unerring Operation
entries: While under your Crown authority, an object automatically knows how to operate its own functions. You needn't understand them and don't gain that technical knowledge.

entries.name: Level 13: Ownership Is a Lesser Law
Override the Bond
entries: For the duration of the Crown command that established control. Your authority can contest supernatural effects determining who controls an object, owns it, commands it, can activate it, can recall it, or is permitted to use it. This includes Attunement bonds, magical ownership restrictions, creator-only controls, bonded weapons, summoned weapons, remote control, magical recall effects, curses governing an object's actions, controlled Constructs, and similar supernatural claims.

If another creature actively controls the object, make a contested check: you make a Charisma Check and add your Proficiency Bonus; the opposing controller uses the Ability modifier used by its controlling feature and adds its Proficiency Bonus, if any. If no creature can reasonably make the opposing check, use 10 + the effect's spell level, or 10 + its creator's Proficiency Bonus if no spell level exists and that Proficiency Bonus is known. On a success, your Crown takes precedence.

entries.name: The Object Chooses the Crown
entries: While Override the Bond succeeds, the former controller can't command the object, recall effects can't remove it from your control, others need your permission to activate it, and effects forcing it to violate your commands fail. The original bond is suppressed, not necessarily destroyed, and can resume when your control ends.

entries.name: Relics Must Kneel Too
entries: Override the Bond permanently applies to Magic Items and Artifacts regardless of rarity or power. An object's genuine independent sentient will can still resist normally.

entries.name: Mass Edict
entries: As an Action, choose a point you can perceive within 1 mile. For up to 1 hour, command any number of eligible objects, structures, or masses of nonliving matter within 1 mile of that point, regardless of Size. Chosen targets can immediately animate if necessary and receive a command. You can exclude any targets.

entries.name: One Voice, Countless Bodies
entries: While Mass Edict lasts, you can command every affected target throughout the area regardless of ordinary hearing distance. Give shared, group, or individual commands and replace instructions as needed.

entries.name: A Living Domain
entries: While Mass Edict lasts, affected objects can coordinate large-scale combat or physical work as one force.

entries.name: The Crown Does Not Tire
entries: Mass Edict requires no Concentration. Becoming Incapacitated doesn't automatically end existing commands, but you can't issue new ones while unable to act.

entries.name: Titan Convergence
entries: Activating this feature requires an Action. Up to 1 hour. Choose one point you can perceive within 1 mile. Choose any number of eligible targets within 1 mile of that point, including Crown-Bound Objects, ordinary objects, weapons, armor, vehicles, machinery, siege equipment, magical objects, statues, corpses, mindless Constructs, structures, sections of structures, rubble, earth, soil, stone, sand, clay, minerals, ore, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, and other eligible nonliving matter.

The selected material converges on the point, animating as needed. Once enough arrives, it forms one Crownforged Titan per use. Components can differ in material, origin, purpose, Size, shape, and magical nature. Use the summon entry matching the Titan's Size for quick selection.

entries.name: Crownforged Titan
entries: For the remainder of Titan Convergence. Choose whichever stat block is appropriate to the amount of material gathered: {@creature Huge Crownforged Titan|FftForbiddenTome} or {@creature Gargantuan Crownforged Titan|FftForbiddenTome}. Both are CR 24. The Titan uses its dedicated Crownforged Titan stat block and obeys your Crown absolutely.

entries.name: The Whole Remembers Its Parts
entries: While the Titan exists, its components retain functions that can reasonably operate: weapons, siege equipment, Magic Items, engines, machinery, restraining chains, and reinforcing armor. Natural matter provides mass and structure. Charges, ammunition, fuel, and other consumable resources are spent normally.

entries.name: Titan Attack Authority
entries: Crownforged Titans use this formula instead of Crown Strike: Attack Bonus = relevant Ability modifier + Titan's Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus. Damage = attack's damage dice + relevant Ability modifier + Titan's Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus. Save DC = 20 + your Proficiency Bonus, as specified in the Titan's stat block.

entries.name: When Titan Convergence Ends
entries: When the 1-hour duration ends or you voluntarily command the Titan to separate, its surviving components immediately detach into separate objects and materials. Components maintained by another Crown feature can immediately resume functioning under it. Actual damage suffered as a Titan can leave components damaged, broken, scattered, or destroyed as appropriate.

entries.name: Crown Summons
entries: Use the summon entry for the Size and form you need. These references grant no access to a servant before a feature allows you to create or animate it.

optionalfeature.name: Relic Assimilation
entries: The Arsenal doesn't merely preserve enchanted weapons. It learns them. Every relic placed within it becomes another principle of violence written into the whole armory. A single legendary edge can teach a thousand lesser weapons how to bite.

entries.name: Arsenal Relics
entries: When you finish a Long Rest, choose a number of eligible Magic Items stored within your Arsenal up to your Proficiency Bonus. The chosen items become your Arsenal Relics until you choose again when you finish a Long Rest. An eligible item must be a weapon, ammunition, or a Magic Item whose magical properties directly modify a weapon or weapon attack.

entries.name: Total Assimilation
entries: While you wield or make an attack with any weapon from your Arsenal, that weapon can use every applicable magical property of all your Arsenal Relics simultaneously. For those properties, the Arsenal weapon counts as each Arsenal Relic whenever a property refers to "this weapon," "the weapon," or otherwise requires the effect to originate from that relic.

entries.name: Relic Without Form
entries: A copied property isn't restricted by the Arsenal Relic's original weapon type, ammunition type, damage type, reach, or range unless the property would be impossible to resolve without that requirement. If a property requires a melee attack, ranged attack, thrown attack, Critical Hit, specific target, or another condition created by the attack itself, you must still satisfy that condition.

entries.name: Convergent Enchantments
entries: Properties from different Arsenal Relics can function on the same attack and their benefits are cumulative, including bonuses to attack rolls, damage rolls, additional damage, Critical Hit effects, and other effects triggered by an attack. A property with the same name from multiple Arsenal Relics doesn't stack with itself unless it explicitly says otherwise.

entries.name: Shared Activation
entries: If an Arsenal Relic has a property you can activate while holding, wielding, attacking with, or otherwise using that item, you can activate it through any weapon from your Arsenal as though you were using the Arsenal Relic. If the property creates an effect from the relic, you can have that effect originate from the Arsenal weapon you're currently using.

entries.name: One Relic, One Resource
entries: The Arsenal shares power, not resources. Charges, limited uses, Recharge, once-per-turn limits, once-per-round limits, and other usage limits remain tied to the original Arsenal Relic. Using that property through any Arsenal weapon expends or counts against the original Arsenal Relic's resource normally.

entries.name: Bound Requirements
entries: You must still satisfy an Arsenal Relic's Attunement requirement and any requirement based on the wielder, such as class, creature type, alignment, ability score, or another quality of the wielder. Once you satisfy those requirements, every weapon in your Arsenal is treated as satisfying that item's weapon-specific requirements for the copied property.

entries.name: Transcendent Attunement
entries: As your bond with the Arsenal deepens, the Arsenal learns to sustain relics in your place. At 7th level, one of your Arsenal Relics can function through this Invocation even if you are not Attuned to it. At 11th level, up to two of your Arsenal Relics can ignore their Attunement requirements this way. At 15th level, up to three of your Arsenal Relics can ignore their Attunement requirements this way. At 17th level, all of your Arsenal Relics can function through this Invocation without requiring Attunement.

Ignoring Attunement this way applies only while the item is one of your Arsenal Relics and only to properties used through Relic Assimilation. It doesn't make you Attuned to the item, grant its normal benefits outside the Arsenal, or increase your number of Attunement slots.

entries.name: Relic Remains Whole
entries: An Arsenal Relic isn't consumed, destroyed, stripped of its magic, or permanently altered by this Invocation. It remains a normal Magic Item and can still be summoned and used directly.

optionalfeature.name: Arsenal Instinct
entries: The Arsenal watches every clash. It learns what fails, what pierces, and what kind of weapon the next moment demands. Before long, you no longer choose the right weapon—the Arsenal does.

entries.name: Predatory Selection
entries: Whenever you miss a creature with a weapon from your Arsenal, or the creature reduces the damage of that attack through Resistance or Immunity, you can immediately return that weapon to the Arsenal and summon another stored weapon into the same hand. The replacement requires no action. Until the end of your turn, your first attack against that creature with the replacement weapon has Advantage.

entries.name: Learned Weakness
entries: Once you damage a creature with a weapon from your Arsenal, the Arsenal remembers that creature until the end of your next Long Rest. For a remembered creature, the Arsenal learns how that creature responds to damage dealt by your Arsenal, including any Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability revealed by those attacks.

entries.name: Adaptive Armament
entries: Whenever you make a weapon attack against a remembered creature using a weapon from your Arsenal, the Arsenal can alter that attack's damage type to the most effective damage type against that creature. If the creature has one or more Vulnerabilities, the attack becomes a damage type to which it is Vulnerable. If it has no Vulnerabilities, the Arsenal instead chooses a damage type that the creature neither Resists nor is Immune to, if one is available.

You don't need to know what damage type was chosen beforehand. The Arsenal determines the most effective option automatically when the attack hits. The available damage types are Acid, Bludgeoning, Cold, Fire, Force, Lightning, Necrotic, Piercing, Poison, Psychic, Radiant, Slashing, and Thunder.

entries.name: Perfect Answer
entries: Starting at 11th level, attacks altered by Adaptive Armament also ignore Resistance to the chosen damage type. Starting at 17th level, if the creature has no Vulnerability, the chosen damage type treats the creature as though it had Vulnerability to that damage for that attack.

optionalfeature.name: Adaptive Arsenal
entries: No weapon leaves the Arsenal unchanged. Each one is refined for the exact moment it is called. What you draw is not merely a stored weapon, but the version of it the battle demands.

entries.name: Mutable Armament
entries: Whenever you summon a weapon from your Arsenal, choose one of the following properties: Finesse, Light, Thrown (20/60), Reach, or Versatile (1d10). The weapon gains the chosen property until it returns to the Arsenal. If the weapon already has the chosen property, choose another.

entries.name: Greater Adaptation
entries: Starting at 7th level, choose two properties whenever you summon the weapon. Starting at 13th level, choose three properties whenever you summon the weapon.

entries.name: Perfect Form
entries: Starting at 17th level, when you summon a weapon, you can also change its normal weapon damage die to 1d12 if it would normally be lower. If the weapon normally rolls multiple weapon damage dice, you can instead change each of those dice to 1d8.

entries.name: Arsenal Mastery
entries: Whenever you summon a weapon from your Arsenal, you can choose which Weapon Mastery property you use with that weapon from among any Weapon Mastery properties you know. You can choose again each time the weapon is summoned.

optionalfeature.name: Echoed Form
entries: The Mirror studies not what you are, but how you act. A spell, a strike, a dash, a gesture—each leaves behind a perfect pattern. For a moment, that pattern can be called upon again.

entries.name: Reflected Action
entries: Once on each of your turns after you take an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, the Mirror records the form of that action until the start of your next turn. Before the reflection fades, you can use it once to repeat the same type of action without using its normal action cost. The repeated action must be one you could currently perform and must obey all of its normal requirements.

entries.name: Shared Expenditure
entries: Repeating an action this way doesn't duplicate resources. If the repeated action would expend a spell slot, class resource, item charge, limited-use feature, ammunition, Hit Die, or another expendable resource, you must expend that resource again normally.

entries.name: Mirrored Execution
entries: The repeated action doesn't need to target the same creature, point, or object. If it includes an attack, spell, movement, Grapple, Shove, item interaction, or another effect, you can choose new legal targets and resolve it normally.

entries.name: Perfect Echo
entries: Starting at 11th level, you can maintain two different recorded actions at once. Starting at 17th level, once on each of your turns, the first reflected action you repeat doesn't expend a limited-use class or subclass resource, though it still requires spell slots, item charges, ammunition, or other external resources normally.

optionalfeature.name: Unbroken Focus
entries: Your concentration has become something closer to a fixed state than an effort of will. Pain can shake your body, but the spell remains where you placed it.

items: You have Advantage on Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration.
You add your Proficiency Bonus to Constitution saving throws made to maintain Concentration, even if you already add your Proficiency Bonus to the save.
Whenever you make a Constitution saving throw to maintain Concentration and roll a 9 or lower on the d20, treat the roll as a 10.
Taking 20 damage or less from a single source doesn't require you to make a saving throw to maintain Concentration.
When you fail a saving throw to maintain Concentration, you can succeed instead. You can do this once per turn.
Your Concentration doesn't end solely because you become Incapacitated, Stunned, Unconscious, or are reduced to 0 Hit Points.
Death still ends your Concentration normally.

If an effect would end your Concentration without dealing damage and without allowing a saving throw, you can make a Constitution saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a success, you maintain Concentration.

optionalfeature.name: Reflex Casting
entries: Magic no longer waits for conscious thought. When danger appears, the spell is already forming.
When one of the following happens, you can take a Reaction to cast a spell you know or have prepared that normally has a casting time of an Action or Bonus Action:

items: A creature you can see damages you.
A creature you can see forces you to make a saving throw.
A creature you can see misses you with an attack.
A hostile creature enters your reach.

entries: The spell must satisfy at least one of the following:

items: Target the triggering creature.
Include the triggering creature in its Area of Effect.
Target only you.

entries: The spell otherwise follows its normal rules, including range, components, Spell Slots, and Concentration. Casting a spell through this Invocation changes its casting time to a Reaction for that casting. A spell cast this way doesn't prevent you from casting another leveled spell during the same turn.

optionalfeature.name: Split Spell
entries: You can divide a single magical effect without weakening either half. When you cast a spell that targets exactly one creature and has a range other than Self, you can choose a second creature within the spell's range that would also be a valid target. The spell affects both creatures independently.

items: Make separate attack rolls and saving throws for each target as normal.
Damage, healing, conditions, and all other effects apply fully to both targets.
If the spell requires Concentration, a single instance of Concentration maintains the spell on both creatures.
You expend only the spell's normal Spell Slot and components.
A spell that already targets more than one creature, creates an Area of Effect, or gains additional targets from being cast at a higher level can't benefit from this Invocation.

entries: You can use this Invocation on Cantrips without limit. For spells of 1st level or higher, you can use it a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

optionalfeature.name: Spell Reach
entries: Your magic no longer stops where ordinary spellcasting says it should.
Whenever you cast a spell, you can extend its reach as follows:

items: If the spell has a range expressed in feet, double its range.
If the spell has a range of Touch, its range becomes 30 feet.
If the spell has a range of Self that creates a Cone, Line, Emanation, or other Area of Effect measured from you, double every distance used to determine that area.
This Invocation doesn't increase a spell's duration or allow it to ignore Total Cover.
A spell with a range of Self that affects only you is unchanged.

entries: For example, a spell with a range of 60 feet becomes 120 feet, a Touch spell can target something within 30 feet, and a 15-foot Cone originating from you becomes a 30-foot Cone.

optionalfeature.name: Dual Concentration
entries: Your mind can hold more than one spell structure simultaneously. You can maintain Concentration on up to two spells at once.
When you are concentrating on two spells, the following rules apply:

items: If you make a saving throw to maintain Concentration because of damage or another effect, make one saving throw for each spell separately.
Failing the saving throw for one spell doesn't automatically end the other.
If an effect causes you to lose Concentration without a saving throw, you choose which one of the two spells ends.
Casting a third spell that requires Concentration forces you to choose one of your current Concentration spells to end before the new spell begins.
Any feature that modifies your Concentration saving throws applies to both spells normally.

optionalfeature.name: Moving Spell
entries: Your ongoing magic no longer has to remain where it was first cast. When you cast a spell with a duration longer than Instantaneous that creates an Area of Effect which normally remains in a fixed location, you can move that area while the spell lasts.
As a Bonus Action, choose one of the following:

items: Move the entire Area of Effect up to 30 feet in any direction.
If the spell creates a Line, Cone, Wall, or similar directional area, you can also rotate or change its direction as part of this movement.
If the spell consists of multiple connected sections, such as a wall, all sections move together and retain their original arrangement.

entries: The spell's size, duration, damage, saving throws, and other effects remain unchanged. You must be able to perceive at least part of the spell's area when you move it, but the new position doesn't need to remain within the spell's original casting range from you. If moving the spell causes a creature to enter its area, that creature is treated exactly as though it had entered the area normally. Moving an area over the same creature repeatedly during the same turn doesn't cause the spell to affect that creature more often than the spell normally allows.

optionalfeature.name: Selective Spell
entries: You decide exactly who your magic is allowed to affect. Whenever you cast a spell that can affect more than one creature or creates an Area of Effect, you can choose any number of creatures you can see when you cast the spell. The chosen creatures are unaffected by that spell for its entire duration.

items: They take no damage from it.
They automatically avoid any conditions, forced movement, or other harmful effects caused by it.
They ignore Difficult Terrain and other movement penalties created by the spell.
If the spell normally deals half damage or produces a reduced effect on a successful saving throw, the chosen creatures instead suffer no effect.
An ongoing spell continues to ignore those creatures even if they later leave and re-enter its area.

entries: If the spell lasts longer than Instantaneous, at the start of each of your turns, you can change which creatures are excluded from it without an action.

optionalfeature.name: Retarget Spell
entries: Your magic doesn't remain bound to the creature it first touched. While you are maintaining a spell with a duration longer than Instantaneous that currently affects exactly one creature, you can use a Bonus Action to choose another creature within the spell's normal range that would be a valid target for that spell. The spell immediately leaves the previous target and transfers to the new target.

items: The spell's remaining duration is unchanged.
If the spell normally requires a saving throw to establish its effect, the new target makes that saving throw against your Spell Save DC.
If it normally requires a spell attack, make a new spell attack against the new target.
On a failed save or successful attack, the new target becomes affected by the spell for its remaining duration.
On a successful save or missed attack, the transfer fails and the spell remains on its previous target.
Effects that occur only when the spell is initially cast aren't repeated by transferring it.
Concentration, if required, continues normally and isn't interrupted by transferring the spell.

entries: You can use this Invocation repeatedly on the same spell while that spell remains active.

optionalfeature.name: Overcast Spell
entries: Whenever you cast a spell of 1st level or higher using a spell slot, you can treat the spell as though it were cast using a spell slot one level higher than the slot you actually expended. For example, if you expend a 5th-level spell slot, the spell is treated as though it were cast using a 6th-level spell slot. This can increase a spell only up to 9th level. This benefit applies every time you cast an eligible spell and requires no additional action or resource.

optionalfeature.name: Perfect Casting
entries: Your spellcasting has been refined beyond ordinary limitations.
Whenever you cast a spell:

items: You can cast it without Verbal, Somatic, or Material components.
You don't need a Spellcasting Focus.
Material components with a listed cost or that are normally consumed are not required and aren't consumed.
You can cast while unable to speak, while your hands are occupied, while Restrained, Grappled, bound, submerged, or otherwise unable to perform the spell's normal components.
Your casting produces no perceptible sign that you are casting a spell before the spell takes effect.
A creature doesn't automatically know that you are the caster unless the spell itself clearly reveals its source.
Your casting can't be identified or interrupted by an effect that requires perceiving you cast the spell.
Your spells can't be Counterspelled or otherwise interrupted by an effect that requires detecting the casting.

entries: After the spell takes effect, its normal visible, audible, and other perceptible effects occur normally.

entries.name: Spellcasting Bonus
entries: You gain a bonus to your spell attack rolls and spell save DC based on your level:
This bonus applies to all spells you cast, regardless of which class, feature, item, or other source granted the spell.

optionalfeature.name: Unspent Spell
entries: When you cast a spell of 1st level or higher using a spell slot, the spell slot is not expended if the spell fails to affect anything.
This happens if, for example:

items: Every spell attack misses.
Every target succeeds on its saving throw and the spell has no effect on a successful save.
Every intended target becomes invalid before the spell resolves.
The spell is completely prevented before producing any effect.

entries: If the spell deals damage, applies a condition, moves a creature, creates or changes something, or otherwise produces any effect, the spell slot is expended normally. Material components and other resources used to cast the spell are still expended normally.

optionalfeature.name: Double Casting
entries: Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell of 1st through 5th level using a spell slot, you can immediately cast that spell a second time as part of the same casting.
The second casting:

items: Requires no action and expends no additional spell slot.
Is cast at the same level as the original spell.
Can choose completely different legal targets, areas, or points of origin.
Requires no additional Material components, including components that are normally consumed.
Doesn't prevent you from casting it because of a rule limiting how many spells you can cast during the turn.

entries: If the spell requires Concentration, one Concentration maintains both castings, and both end if that Concentration ends. The additional casting can't trigger Double Casting again.

optionalfeature.name: Unbounded Spell
entries: Distance no longer limits where your magic can take form. Whenever you cast a spell, you can choose any creature, object, or point you can see and cause the spell to originate from that location instead of from you. A location counts as something you can see even if you see it indirectly through another creature, a Familiar, a magical sensor, a spell, a Magic Item, or any other effect that allows you to see from another location.
When you use this Invocation:

items: The spell appears and takes effect directly at the chosen location. It doesn't travel from you to that location.
Distance between you and the chosen location doesn't matter.
Creatures, walls, Total Cover, and other barriers between you and the chosen location don't block the spell.
Any range, area, Line, Cone, Sphere, Cube, or other effect is measured from the chosen location.
You choose the spell's direction and orientation from that location.
After the spell originates there, it follows its normal rules for range, cover, targets, and clear paths from that location onward.

entries.name: Touch Spells
entries: When you cast a spell with a range of Touch, you can target a creature or object you can see through this Invocation as though you were physically touching it.

entries.name: Self Spells
entries: When you cast a spell with a range of Self:

items: If the spell creates an area, Line, Cone, emanation, or other effect originating from you, you can cause that effect to originate from the chosen location instead.
If the spell normally affects only you, you can instead choose one creature you can see at the chosen location. For that casting, the spell treats that creature as you and affects it instead of you.

entries: For example, while seeing through your Familiar inside a sealed room, you could cast a Touch spell on a creature beside the Familiar, create a Self-originating Cone inside the room, or cast a Self-only spell so that it affects a creature you can see there instead.

optionalfeature.name: Instant Casting
entries: You can compress even the longest spellcasting process into a single moment. Whenever you cast a spell with a casting time of 1 Action or longer, you can change its casting time to 1 Bonus Action.
This includes spells that normally require:

items: 1 Action.
Multiple rounds.
1 minute.
10 minutes.
1 hour.
8 hours.
24 hours.
Any longer casting time.

entries: When you use this Invocation:

items: The entire spell is completed during that Bonus Action.
You don't need to spend additional Actions, maintain the casting over multiple turns, or remain in place for the spell's normal casting time.
The casting can't be interrupted merely because the spell normally requires a long period of continuous casting.
You still expend any required spell slot.
Material components, including costly or consumed components, are still required normally.
Reducing the casting time doesn't change the spell's duration, targets, range, Concentration, or other effects.

entries: A spell with a casting time of 1 Reaction keeps its normal casting time. If you cast a spell as a Ritual, this Invocation can reduce the spell's entire Ritual casting time to 1 Action instead of 1 Bonus Action. The spell still counts as being cast as a Ritual and doesn't expend a spell slot.

optionalfeature.name: Self-Sustaining Spell
entries: Your spells no longer need your attention to remain stable. Whenever you cast a spell that requires Concentration, you can choose for that casting to require no Concentration, regardless of the spell's level.
When you do so:

items: The spell lasts for its normal duration.
Taking damage can't end the spell.
Becoming Incapacitated or Unconscious doesn't end the spell.
Starting Concentration on another spell doesn't end it.
You can have any number of spells sustained this way simultaneously.
Death doesn't automatically end the spell unless the spell itself says it ends when you die.
The spell can still be dispelled, suppressed, or otherwise ended by an effect that could normally end that spell.

entries: This benefit applies to all spells from 1st through 9th level.

optionalfeature.name: Maximum Casting
entries: Your spells no longer rely on favorable rolls for their raw power. Whenever you cast a spell, any dice rolled by that spell to determine damage, healing, Temporary Hit Points, or another numerical effect can use their maximum possible result instead of being rolled.
For example:

items: {@dice 8d6} damage becomes 48 damage.
{@dice 6d10} healing becomes 60 Hit Points.
{@dice 4d8} Temporary Hit Points becomes 32 Temporary Hit Points.

entries: This applies every time the spell produces that effect during its duration, not only when the spell is first cast. Attack rolls, saving throws, and other d20 Tests are still rolled normally.

optionalfeature.name: Adaptive Spell
entries: Your spells can change their structure at the moment of casting.
Whenever you cast a spell, you can make any of the following changes to that casting:

items: Change any damage type dealt by the spell to another damage type of your choice.
If the spell requires a saving throw, change that saving throw to Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma.
If the spell creates a Cone, Cube, Cylinder, Line, or Sphere, you can change it into another one of those shapes while keeping roughly the same total size.
If the spell normally targets only creatures, you can also allow it to target objects, and vice versa, as long as the effect can meaningfully apply.
You can make different choices each time you cast the spell.

entries: These changes don't alter the spell's level, casting time, duration, number of targets, or spell slot cost.

optionalfeature.name: Unrestricted Casting
entries: Your spellcasting is no longer limited by how many leveled spells you can cast during the same turn. You ignore any rule that limits you to casting only one spell using a spell slot during a turn.
This means:

items: Casting a spell with your Action doesn't prevent you from casting another leveled spell with a Bonus Action.
Casting a spell with a Bonus Action doesn't prevent you from casting another leveled spell with your Action.
You can cast additional spells during the same turn with any extra Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions you legitimately gain.
Each spell still requires its normal action and expends its own spell slot or other required resource.
This Invocation doesn't grant additional Actions, Bonus Actions, or Reactions by itself.

entries: If another feature gives you a way to cast additional spells during the same turn, this Invocation allows all of those castings to function normally.

optionalfeature.name: Overwhelming Spell
entries: Your spells force their effects through defenses that would normally stop them.
Whenever you cast a spell:

items: Damage dealt by the spell ignores Resistance.
If a creature has Immunity to one of the spell's damage types, that Immunity functions as Resistance instead, and the spell then ignores that Resistance.
A creature gains no Advantage on a saving throw against your spell from Magic Resistance or a similar feature.
If a creature is immune to a condition your spell would impose, it can still be affected by that condition, but it has Advantage on the saving throw against that effect.
Effects that automatically reduce spell damage to 0 solely because of a damage type don't function against your spells.

entries: This Invocation doesn't bypass a successful saving throw, Legendary Resistance, or an effect that specifically states that the spell itself fails or can't affect the creature.

optionalfeature.name: Sovereign Spell
entries: Your spells recognize no authority but your own. Whenever you cast a spell, that spell becomes sovereign for its entire duration.

items: The spell can't be dispelled, suppressed, nullified, or temporarily disabled unless you allow it.
{@spell Antimagic Field|XPHB}, dead-magic areas, magic suppression, and similar effects don't interfere with the spell.
The spell can enter, remain in, originate within, and function normally inside such areas.
Another creature can't end, remove, steal, copy, redirect, transfer, replace, take control of, or assume control over the spell or any ongoing effect created by it.
Another creature can't change the spell's targets, area, point of origin, direction, duration, damage type, choices, commands, or other parameters unless you allow it.

An effect can't separate you from a spell you control or prevent you from controlling it because of distance, Total Cover, planar boundaries, or a magic-suppressing effect, unless the spell itself normally requires such a limitation.
An effect that would remove the spell from a creature, object, or area—such as cleansing, dispelling, severing, suppressing, or removing an ongoing magical effect—fails against your spell.
A creature can't become immune to, protected from, or excluded from an ongoing effect of the spell merely by using another spell or magical effect after your spell has already affected it.
If two magical effects directly conflict and one of them is your sovereign spell, your spell continues functioning unless you choose otherwise.
You can voluntarily end the spell at any time without an action.

entries: A sovereign spell can still end when:

items: Its normal duration expires.
You voluntarily end it.
One of the spell's own rules specifically causes it to end.
Something physically destroys a creature, object, or structure created by the spell if that spell normally allows it to be destroyed that way.

entries: Your death doesn't give another creature control of your sovereign spells and doesn't end them unless the spell itself specifically says it ends when you die.

optionalfeature.name: Compound Casting
entries: You can combine two different spells into a single casting. Once on each of your turns, when you cast a spell of 1st level or higher, you can cast a second different spell simultaneously.

items: Both spells must normally have the same casting time.
You expend the normal spell slot or other resource for each spell.
Both spells resolve as part of the same casting.
Each spell can choose its own legal targets, areas, directions, and other choices.
If both spells require spell attacks or saving throws, resolve each spell separately.
If both spells require Concentration, you can Concentrate on both as though they were one spell. If that Concentration ends, both spells end.
Casting the second spell requires no additional Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction.
The second spell doesn't trigger Compound Casting again.

entries: For example, you could cast {@spell Disintegrate|XPHB} and {@spell Hold Monster|XPHB} together with the same Action, expending the appropriate spell slot for each spell.

optionalfeature.name: Focused Spell
entries: You can compress the full power of an area spell into a single target. Whenever you cast a spell that normally affects an area or can affect multiple creatures, you can choose one creature that could legally be affected by the spell and focus the entire casting on it.
When you do:

items: The spell affects only that creature.
Double all damage dice and healing dice of the spell against that creature.
The creature has Disadvantage on every saving throw it makes against that casting.
If the spell normally deals half damage on a successful save, it instead deals full damage on a successful save.
If the spell makes multiple spell attacks, all of them can target that creature even if the spell normally requires different targets.
Any condition, forced movement, or other effect that would normally apply to a creature affected by the spell applies normally.
The spell otherwise keeps its normal level, duration, Concentration, and spell slot cost.

entries: For example, you could compress a large {@spell Fireball|XPHB} into one creature, dealing twice its normal damage dice to that target instead of creating an area.

optionalfeature.name: Universal Targeting
entries: Your spells no longer care what kind of creature stands before you. Whenever you cast a spell, you can ignore restrictions based on a target's creature type, size, anatomy, or similar physical classification.
This means:

items: A spell that normally affects only Humanoids can affect any creature.
A spell that normally affects only Beasts, Undead, Constructs, Fiends, Celestials, Plants, or another creature type can affect any creature.
A spell that normally works only on creatures of a certain Size can affect creatures of any Size.

A spell can't fail solely because the target lacks a particular biological feature, such as blood, breath, flesh, bones, or a conventional body, as long as the spell's effect can still meaningfully apply.
The spell still follows its normal rules for range, saving throws, attack rolls, duration, and number of targets.
This Invocation doesn't ignore a requirement that the target be willing.

entries: For example, {@spell Hold Person|XPHB} could affect a Dragon, {@spell Dominate Beast|XPHB} could affect a Construct, and a spell limited to Large or smaller creatures could affect a Gargantuan creature.

optionalfeature.name: Locked Spell
entries: Once your spell takes hold, escaping it becomes extremely difficult.
Whenever a creature fails its first saving throw against a spell you cast, that creature automatically fails any later saving throw granted by the same spell specifically to:

items: End the spell's effect on itself.
Escape from the spell.
Remove a condition caused by the spell.
Break free from a restraint, control effect, transformation, or similar ongoing effect caused by the spell.
