entries: Saving throws caused by the spell for new damage or new effects are still rolled normally. This Invocation doesn't affect the spell's initial saving throw and doesn't prevent a creature from using Legendary Resistance on that initial save. For example, if a creature fails its initial save against {@spell Hold Monster|XPHB}, it can't later succeed on the repeated saves to end the Paralyzed condition from that casting.

optionalfeature.name: Unbound Form
entries: Your body is no longer a fixed thing. At the start of each of your turns, you can reshape yourself in any number of the following ways. The changes last until you change them again.

items: Change your Size to Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, or Huge. Your equipment changes with you.
Grow or remove limbs, eyes, mouths, wings, tails, gills, claws, or other ordinary body parts.
Gain a Climb Speed or Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
If you create wings, gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.
You can breathe air and water.
Your reach becomes 10 feet if your current form has limbs capable of reaching that distance.
You can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without Squeezing, provided your equipment can pass with you.
You can alter your voice, facial features, apparent age, sex, height, weight, skin, hair, and other physical details freely.
You can make your body appear to belong to any Humanoid species or other creature with a similar body plan, but this doesn't give you that creature's statistics or special abilities.
Missing nonessential body parts can be replaced instantly when you reshape yourself.

entries: These changes are not a spell, transformation spell, or illusion. They are your natural physical state. An effect that reveals your "true form" reveals only that your body has no single fixed form; it doesn't force you back into any previous appearance.

optionalfeature.name: Every Door Leads Somewhere
entries: Every doorway you pass through leaves a faint impression in your mind. When you later place your hand on another threshold, its interior darkens into an impossible depth, and for a moment the doorway opens somewhere else entirely. Whenever you pass through a doorway, gate, archway, hatch, window, or similar opening, you can remember that threshold. You can remember a number of thresholds equal to twice your Proficiency Bonus.

As an Action, while touching a doorway or similar opening large enough for you to pass through, choose one remembered threshold on the same plane. Until the start of your next turn, the opening leads directly to that threshold instead of to the space normally beyond it.

items: Anything that can physically fit through the opening can pass through.
Creatures, objects, attacks, spells, sound, and light can pass through normally.
Distance between the two thresholds doesn't matter.
You don't need to know the exact location of the destination, only which remembered threshold you are choosing.
The destination threshold doesn't need to be open, unlocked, or unobstructed on its original side.
You can see and hear through the connected opening.
Movement through it costs movement normally, but the two openings count as adjacent while connected.
A creature passing through chooses its exact unoccupied space immediately beyond the destination threshold.
You can end the connection at any time, requiring no Action.
If either threshold is destroyed, ceases to exist, or becomes too small for the thing attempting to pass through, that passage can't be used.

entries: When you would remember a new threshold beyond your limit, choose one existing memory to forget. This Invocation isn't teleportation and doesn't create a spell effect. For the brief time the connection exists, the two thresholds are simply the same doorway.

optionalfeature.name: Weight Is Optional
entries: Your body has stopped treating weight as an inherent property. Your steps can become too light to disturb dust, then impossibly heavy a heartbeat later, bending stone beneath your feet without changing your shape. You can change your effective weight at any time, requiring no Action or Reaction, even while falling, being moved, or during another creature's turn. Choose any weight from effectively weightless to 1,000,000 pounds. Your Size doesn't change, and your chosen weight never makes it harder for you to move or act.
You never take falling damage, regardless of your current weight, the distance fallen, or what surface you land on.

entries.name: Nearly Weightless
entries: While nearly weightless:

items: You gain a Fly Speed equal to your Speed and can hover.
You can stand and move across liquids, fragile surfaces, snow, leaves, ropes, and similar things without breaking or sinking through them.
Your jump distance has no normal limit from your Strength; you can jump up to your remaining movement.
You can stop yourself in midair at any time during a fall.

entries.name: Massively Heavy
entries: While massively heavy:

items: You can't be knocked Prone or moved against your will unless you allow it.
You can't be lifted, carried, dragged, thrown, or telekinetically moved unless the effect is capable of moving your current weight.
A creature Grappling you can't move you unless it could normally move your current weight.
Ordinary wind, currents, explosions, recoil, impacts, and collapsing terrain can't move you against your will.
You have Advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and you can use your current weight instead of your normal body weight whenever weight or mass would be beneficial.
Your weight doesn't prevent you from walking, climbing, jumping, swimming, flying, or otherwise using your movement normally.
A surface that can't support your chosen weight can crack, collapse, or give way beneath you as appropriate.

entries.name: Unstoppable Descent
entries: When you descend at least 10 feet before striking a creature, object, or surface, you can become massively heavy immediately before impact. You take no damage from the collision. Each creature of your choice within 15 feet of the point of impact must make a Dexterity saving throw against your Spell Save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 2d12} Bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet you descended, to a maximum of {@damage 20d12}, is knocked Prone, and is pushed up to 15 feet away from the impact.

On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and suffers no other effect. Unattended objects and structures automatically take the damage. If you strike a floor, roof, bridge, wall, vehicle, or other structure that can't withstand your chosen weight, you can continue falling or moving through it rather than stopping at the first surface.

entries.name: Immovable by Choice
entries: Whenever an effect would forcibly move, teleport, banish, launch, pull, push, or otherwise relocate you against your will, you can make yourself impossibly anchored. If the effect allows a saving throw or ability check, you automatically succeed. If it normally allows no roll, you instead remain where you are unless the effect is capable of moving at least 1,000,000 pounds or moves the entire region or plane containing you. Your weight returns to whatever value you choose immediately afterward.

optionalfeature.name: Everything Within Reach
entries: Distance no longer determines what your body can reach. When you extend a hand toward something far away, perspective folds around you; your arm appears to vanish into the intervening distance and emerge beside whatever you chose to touch. Anything you can see on the same plane is considered to be within your physical reach, regardless of the actual distance between you.

items: You can touch, grab, pick up, carry, open, close, press, pull, push, turn, drag, throw, or otherwise physically manipulate anything you can see.
You can make melee weapon attacks, Unarmed Strikes, Grapples, and Shoves against visible creatures at any distance.
A melee attack made this way remains a melee attack.
Your attacks don't suffer Disadvantage merely because of the distance involved.
You can make Opportunity Attacks against any creature you can see that would normally provoke one from you.
You can use Touch-range spells, class features, Magic Items, and other abilities on a visible target through this reach.
You can retrieve a visible unattended object directly into your hand.
You can place or throw an object you are holding into any visible space.
You can interact with objects behind transparent barriers as long as you can see them, though a magical effect that specifically prevents passage or interaction can still stop you.
Your normal Strength and carrying capacity still determine what you can physically lift or carry.

entries.name: Distant Grasp
entries: When you Grapple a creature using this Invocation, distance doesn't end the Grapple.
While you maintain it:

items: The creature can be any distance from you as long as you can still see it.
You can prevent it from moving in any direction you choose.
When you move the creature, you can move it toward you, away from you, sideways, upward, or downward rather than merely dragging it beside you.
You can move it up to your Speed whenever you would normally be able to move a Grappled creature.
Size doesn't prevent you from attempting the Grapple, though your normal Strength still determines whether you succeed.
If you can lift the creature, you can suspend it in the air while Grappling it.
If you stop being able to see it, the Grapple ends.

entries.name: Take It From There
entries: When you successfully hit a creature with a melee attack through this Invocation, you can immediately attempt one of the following against it without using an additional Action:

items: Grapple it.
Shove it.
Take one unattended object in its space.

Attempt to take one object it is holding. The creature makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw, its choice, against your Spell Save DC. On a failure, the object appears in your hand if you can carry it.

entries: You can use this benefit once on each of your turns.

entries.name: Nothing Is Too Far to Catch
entries: When a creature or object you can see begins falling, is thrown, is launched, or would move past a point you can see, you can use your Reaction to reach it instantly. If it is willing or unattended, you can catch it automatically. If it is an unwilling creature, make a Grapple attempt against it. On a success, its movement immediately stops and you hold it at that location. A creature or object you catch this way takes no falling damage from the distance it had fallen before you caught it.
For you, "out of reach" is no longer a meaningful distance.

optionalfeature.name: There Is No Between
entries: Distance no longer exists for you in the usual way. When you move, your body briefly stretches into an impossible line before appearing where you intended to be. Whenever you move, you can instead choose an unoccupied space you can perceive within 300 feet. You move directly there, spending only 5 feet of movement.

items: You don't pass through the intervening spaces.
This movement isn't teleportation.
Walls, terrain, creatures, hazards, and magical barriers such as {@spell Wall of Force|XPHB} or {@spell Forcecage|XPHB} don't prevent it.
You can move in any direction, including through empty air.
You don't provoke Opportunity Attacks from this movement.
You can remain standing in midair or on vertical or inverted surfaces without falling.
You can use this movement while Grappled, Restrained, Prone, bound, enclosed, or otherwise unable to move normally.
Using this movement immediately ends any Grapple affecting you, and frees you from any mundane restraint or confinement that can't continue to affect you at your destination.
You can bring one willing creature you are touching or one creature you are Grappling.

entries: Once on each of your turns, you can move to a location within 300 feet that you can't currently perceive, provided you have personally occupied that exact location before. For you, there is no path between two places—only where you are, and where you choose to be.

optionalfeature.name: Flat Against the World
entries: Your body can collapse into a living image upon any surface, becoming thinner than paper while remaining fully capable of acting. As a Bonus Action, you can flatten yourself onto a surface you touch. You can return to normal form at any time, requiring no Action.
While flattened:

items: Your Speed is doubled, and you can move across walls, floors, ceilings, creatures, objects, and other solid surfaces.
You can pass through cracks, beneath doors, and through openings as narrow as a hair.
You can't be Grappled, Restrained, Shoved, or knocked Prone by physical means.
You have Resistance to all damage except Force and Psychic.
You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws, and take no damage on a successful Dexterity save that would normally deal half damage.
You can still attack, cast spells, manipulate objects, and use your abilities normally. Range and reach are measured from your position on the surface.
You can move directly from one touching surface to another regardless of their angle.
You can move across the surface of a creature; if it moves, you move with it without spending movement.
You don't fall while attached to a surface, even if that surface is moving or upside down.

entries: If the surface beneath you is destroyed, you can immediately attach yourself to another surface within 30 feet. If none exists, you return to normal form in the nearest unoccupied space. You can remain flattened indefinitely.

optionalfeature.name: Wear the World
entries: Nonliving matter can become your body. When you touch an object or structure, your form sinks into it until only faint traces of you remain across its surface. As a Bonus Action, merge into one nonliving object or connected structure you touch. You can leave it at any time, requiring no Action.
While merged:

items: You occupy the object instead of your normal space and have Total Cover from outside it.
You can see, hear, speak, attack, cast spells, and use abilities from any point on its surface.
You move with it automatically and can control all of its movement, mechanisms, doors, limbs, weapons, controls, and other functional parts.
If it can't normally move, you can make it move with a Speed of 60 feet, including climbing surfaces.
When the object makes an attack, check, or saving throw, you can use your own attack bonus, ability modifier, or saving throw bonus if higher.
The object has Resistance to all damage while you inhabit it.
Damage dealt to the object doesn't damage you.
Once on each of your turns, you can move directly into another nonliving object or connected structure touching your current one, requiring no Action.
Magic that would normally target only a creature can't target you through the object unless it can also affect you despite Total Cover.

entries: If the object is destroyed, you immediately emerge in the nearest unoccupied space and take {@damage 2d10} Force damage. You can inhabit anything from a Tiny object to an entire connected structure.

optionalfeature.name: Borrowed Identity
entries: You can force reality to recognize you as someone you remember. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature whose identity you can clearly remember. You copy that creature's identity until you choose another.

items: You count as both yourself and that creature whenever identity matters.
Your appearance doesn't change, but other creatures perceive and recognize you as the copied creature.
Creatures remember encounters with you as encounters with the copied creature.
No matter how strange, impossible, or out of character your behavior is, creatures treat it as normal for that creature and instinctively rationalize it.
Your voice, scent, fingerprints, blood, magical signature, soul, name, species, creature type, bloodline, class, and similar identifiers can be treated as either yours or theirs, your choice.
Locks, wards, portals, contracts, Magic Items, divination, tracking, and similar effects recognize you as the copied creature.
You satisfy requirements based on that creature's identity.
Truesight and effects that reveal illusions don't expose you, because your appearance isn't being disguised.

entries: You don't gain the creature's statistics, memories, features, spells, or abilities.

optionalfeature.name: You Already Thought of That
entries: Preparation is only difficult when it has to happen before you need it. Whenever a need arises, you can declare that you already prepared for it at some point during the previous 7 days. Choose a time and place during that period where you were personally present. You establish that you spent up to 1 hour performing any actions you could genuinely have performed there.

items: Hidden, moved, planted, retrieved, purchased, carried, assembled, dismantled, or prepared objects.
Written messages, maps, instructions, passwords, warnings, or other information.
Opened, locked, blocked, altered, trapped, reinforced, or otherwise prepared part of the environment.
Cast spells, performed rituals, or activated Magic Items you possessed and could have used at that time.
Spent spell slots, charges, money, ammunition, components, Hit Dice, or other resources you actually possessed at that time.

entries: Reality immediately changes to reflect that this preparation already occurred. Any resource used becomes expended now, any object you left somewhere is considered to have remained there since then, and an effect with a duration measures that duration from the moment you retroactively created it. You can establish any number of connected preparatory actions within the chosen hour, provided you could physically have completed them.

You can use this Invocation any number of times. It has no usage limit, but every use must still obey its normal requirements and expend any resources the established preparation would have required. You can't use this Invocation to directly attack, damage, control, or otherwise affect an unwilling creature in the past, nor can you determine another creature's past choices.

Physical evidence, written records, surveillance, and the memories of creatures other than you adjust to the resulting history. You retain your original memories and immediately understand every change caused by your preparation. You don't travel through time. You simply reveal that you were prepared all along.

optionalfeature.name: Material Is a Choice
entries: Stone, steel, glass, and gold are only different answers to the same question. As a Bonus Action, choose nonliving matter you can see within 60 feet and any material or physical substance you have personally encountered before. You can transform any portions of the chosen matter contained within a 60-foot Cube into that substance.

items: You choose the transformation with perfect precision, including individual layers, internal sections, hollow spaces, mixtures, patterns, and microscopic components.
You can transform solids, liquids, gases, and other physical substances.
Shape and volume remain as you choose rather than being determined by the original material.

The transformed matter gains all ordinary physical properties of the chosen substance, including hardness, flexibility, density, conductivity, transparency, melting point, buoyancy, and similar properties.

You can freely redistribute the affected matter within the area while transforming it, allowing you to reshape structures, create openings, seal gaps, form tools, create supports, or completely rebuild the affected material.
Matter can be separated into multiple substances during the same use.
The transformation is permanent.

entries: You can affect unattended objects, terrain, buildings, vehicles, and objects being worn or carried. A creature holding or wearing an affected object doesn't prevent its transformation. Magic Items retain their magical properties even if their physical material and shape are completely changed. You can't create or duplicate a magical property merely by reproducing the material of a Magic Item. You can't directly transform a creature's body, but nonliving material inside, attached to, implanted within, or surrounding a creature can be affected normally.
Artifacts resist this Invocation unless their own properties allow their physical substance to be altered.

optionalfeature.name: What a Coincidence
entries: If something could go your way, somehow it does.

entries.name: Make It Happen
entries: As a Bonus Action, describe one physically possible mundane event involving something you can perceive within 120 feet. Before the start of your next turn, that event occurs through an extraordinary but possible coincidence. The event can't directly control another creature's decisions, contradict an established fact, or cause something physically impossible.

entries.name: Of Course
entries: Whenever a random or genuinely uncertain event you can perceive is about to be determined, you can choose one possible outcome instead.

entries.name: Convenient Reality
entries: Whenever an unestablished mundane fact becomes relevant, you can declare a favorable version of that fact, provided it was genuinely possible and doesn't contradict anything already established.

entries.name: Cheat the Roll
entries: When a creature you can perceive rolls a die, you can change one die to any result that die could normally roll. This can affect Attack Rolls, Saving Throws, Ability Checks, damage, healing, Recharge rolls, random tables, and any other die roll. A d20 can become a natural 20 or natural 1.

entries.name: Stack the Odds
entries: As an Action, choose one creature you can perceive within 120 feet. Until the start of your next turn, whenever that creature rolls dice, you choose the result of every die it rolls from among the results that die could normally produce.

entries.name: Fortune Is Yours
entries: Whenever genuine in-world chance determines an outcome, you can choose the result. This includes cards, dice, roulette, lotteries, coin flips, shuffled draws, random selections, and randomly determined targeting. If winning is one of the possible outcomes determined purely by chance, you can win.

entries.name: Impossible Luck
entries: You can't have Disadvantage on a d20 Test. Any effect that would impose Disadvantage on one of your d20 Tests fails to do so. Disadvantage can't cancel Advantage you have. Whenever you make a d20 Test with Advantage, roll one additional d20 and choose which result to use. Whenever an effect forces you to reroll a d20, you can choose whether to use the original roll or the reroll.

This Invocation can't directly control another creature's decisions, contradict an established fact, or make a physically impossible event occur. If reality contains even one favorable possibility, chance can find it for you.

optionalfeature.name: Down Is Wherever I Point
entries: Gravity is a direction, not a law. As a Bonus Action, choose a point you can see within 120 feet and a direction. Gravity within a 60-foot Cube centered on that point pulls in the chosen direction until you change or end it.

items: Floors, walls, and ceilings can become down.
Creatures and unsecured objects fall in that direction normally.
You can point gravity upward, sideways, diagonally, or toward a specific point.
Creatures can stand and move normally on whichever surface gravity presses them against.
Falling distance and falling damage use the new direction of gravity.
You can move the Cube or change its gravity direction as a Bonus Action.
You can exclude any creatures or objects you choose.

entries: You can also change your own personal gravity at any time without an Action, allowing you to walk on walls, ceilings, or simply fall toward whatever direction you choose. Down is wherever you say it is.

optionalfeature.name: Not Worth Noticing
entries: Being visible and being noticed are not the same thing. As a Bonus Action, choose any number of creatures, objects, or ongoing events you can perceive within 120 feet, up to your Proficiency Bonus. Each becomes perceptually irrelevant until you end the effect. Affected things remain completely visible and detectable, but creatures instinctively dismiss them as meaningless background.

items: Creatures don't willingly focus on, investigate, follow, approach, avoid, target, or react to it.
It can't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
Creatures won't deliberately include it as a target of an attack, spell, feature, command, alarm, or other chosen effect.

If a creature nevertheless attempts to directly interact with, investigate, manipulate, oppose, attack, or otherwise act against an affected thing, it has Disadvantage on every Attack Roll and Ability Check made as part of that attempt.
Creatures automatically overlook suspicious, unusual, dangerous, or blatantly impossible behavior involving it and rationalize what they perceive as unimportant.
Truesight, Blindsight, Tremorsense, magical detection, surveillance, recordings, and similar methods can perceive it normally, but don't overcome this Invocation.
Memories involving it remain, but creatures instinctively disregard their significance and rarely think to act upon them.
Explicitly warning another creature about the affected thing doesn't automatically make it important enough to notice.

entries: If an affected thing directly damages a creature, that creature can focus on and respond to it until the end of its next turn. Other creatures remain unaffected by that exception. You can affect yourself, your equipment, your allies, or actions and phenomena they create. You can end any individual effect at any time, requiring no Action. They can see you. They know you're there. Their mind simply refuses to treat that fact as important.

optionalfeature.name: The Truth Is in the Answer
entries: Anyone can stay silent. Speaking to you is the dangerous part. Whenever a creature you can perceive answers a question you asked, you immediately understand the complete truth as that creature actually knows and remembers it. This occurs regardless of what words it chooses to give you.
You learn:

items: Whether every part of its spoken answer is true, false, mistaken, incomplete, or deliberately misleading.
The truthful answer it could have given using its own knowledge and memories.
Any relevant information it intentionally omitted, concealed, minimized, or avoided mentioning.
The intended meaning behind ambiguous wording, coded language, euphemisms, technicalities, implications, or deliberate misdirection.
Whether it actually knows something it claims not to know or remember.
Which parts of its knowledge are uncertain, secondhand, assumed, or based on incomplete information.
Whether any relevant memory it possesses appears to have been magically altered, suppressed, fabricated, or removed.

entries: The creature doesn't realize what information you learned unless you reveal it. It can still refuse to answer or remain completely silent. However, any deliberate response to the question counts as answering, including a lie, partial answer, deflection, coded response, or claim of ignorance. Magic, features, or abilities that prevent lie detection or conceal whether a creature is truthful don't prevent this Invocation.

This Invocation reveals what the creature genuinely knows; it doesn't make incorrect beliefs true and doesn't restore information completely absent from its mind. Once they answer, you don't hear what they chose to tell you. You hear everything they tried not to.

optionalfeature.name: There Is Always a Way There
entries: You don't need a map. You need a destination. Choose any creature, object, or location on your current plane that you can identify by sight, memory, name, description, or previous encounter. You immediately know its exact direction, distance, and the best route to reach it. The route continuously updates as you move, the destination moves, or circumstances change.
You can choose the:

items: Shortest route.
Fastest route.
Safest route.
Least guarded route.
Least noticeable route.
Route requiring the fewest resources.
Best route for intercepting a moving destination.

entries: Your guidance accounts for everything that presently affects travel, including secret doors, hidden passages, traps, guards, hazards, locked areas, vertical routes, portals, vehicles, shifting terrain, illusions, magical mazes, extradimensional architecture, and your own abilities. You can't become lost, magically misdirected, or deceived about which direction leads toward your chosen destination.
You automatically know:

items: Every obstacle you must overcome before reaching it.
Approximately how long each available route will take.
Where a route branches and what each branch leads toward.
When a previously better route becomes unavailable or a new superior route appears.

entries: If no complete route currently exists, you instead know the smallest series of changes necessary to create one—such as opening a sealed door, breaking a wall, obtaining a key, activating a portal, moving an obstruction, repairing a bridge, or reaching a required intermediary location. If reaching the destination is presently impossible by any means available on your plane, you know exactly what makes it impossible. You can reproduce any route revealed by this Invocation as a perfectly accurate map.
There is always a way there. And if there isn't, you know what must change until there is.

optionalfeature.name: Your Body Has No Safe Limit
entries: The limits of the body exist to prevent it from destroying itself. Yours stopped caring. Your body continuously operates beyond its normal physical limits.

items: Your Speed is tripled.
You gain a Climb and Swim Speed equal to your Speed.
Difficult Terrain doesn't cost you extra movement.
Standing from Prone costs no movement.
Your jump distance is ten times normal, and you don't need a running start.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
You have Advantage on all Strength, Dexterity, and Constitution Ability Checks and Saving Throws.
You can't have Disadvantage on those checks or saving throws.
Whenever you roll a Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution Ability Check or Saving Throw, a d20 result of 9 or lower counts as 10.
Your Speed can't be reduced unless an effect reduces it to 0.
You can't gain Exhaustion from physical exertion, lack of sleep, forced marches, extreme physical activity, or similar bodily strain.
You can hold your breath indefinitely and can continue strenuous physical activity without needing to rest or pace yourself.
You have Resistance to Bludgeoning, Piercing, and Slashing damage.

entries: Whenever you make a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you can use Strength or Dexterity, regardless of the weapon's normal properties. Your body also reacts faster than conscious thought. You gain one additional Reaction each round, though you can't use more than one Reaction during the same turn. At the start of each of your turns, if you have at least 1 Hit Point, you regain Hit Points equal to your Proficiency Bonus + your Constitution modifier.

You can exert maximum physical force instantly without needing leverage, preparation, a running start, or proper footing. Your own body never limits how much of your available Strength you can apply. If an ordinary humanoid body could theoretically perform an action but would normally injure itself attempting it—such as striking at full force, landing from extreme movement, accelerating suddenly, or exerting itself beyond safe muscular limits—you suffer no harm merely from your own physical output.
Your body no longer survives what you demand of it. It was rebuilt around the assumption that you will demand more.

optionalfeature.name: The World Moves Too Slowly
entries: Everyone else is still reacting to a moment you already finished understanding. Your perception and reflexes operate at supernatural speed.

items: You can't be Surprised.
You are immune to the Blinded condition.
You have Advantage on Initiative rolls and add your Proficiency Bonus to Initiative.
A d20 roll of 14 or lower on Initiative counts as 15.
You have Truesight out to 300 feet and Blindsight out to 60 feet.
Being unable to see a creature doesn't grant that creature Advantage against you.
You don't have Disadvantage on attacks merely because you can't see your target.
Invisible, hidden, obscured, or disguised creatures gain no combat benefit against you merely from being unseen or visually concealed.
You have Advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
You can take Reactions before your first turn in combat.
At the start of every creature's turn, you regain one expended Reaction.

entries: Whenever a creature or effect you can perceive begins an attack, casts a spell, moves, teleports, activates an ability, produces an area of effect, or otherwise begins something that could affect you, you perceive what is happening before it resolves. Once per turn, before the triggering event resolves, you can immediately move up to your Speed.
This movement:

items: Requires no Action or Reaction.
Doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
Can occur regardless of how much you have already moved.
Can include climbing, swimming, flying, or any other movement mode you possess.
Can occur between individual attacks, movements, or effects of the same Action.
Can cause the triggering attack, spell, ability, or effect to fail against you if you leave its reach, range, line of effect, legal target conditions, or affected area.

entries: If your movement makes you an invalid target, the triggering creature doesn't get to choose a replacement target for that specific attack, spell, or effect unless it could normally do so after its target becomes invalid. You also can't be caught off guard by speed alone. Effects that claim to occur too quickly to react to, deny Reactions because of their speed, or resolve before a creature could normally respond don't prevent this Invocation from functioning. Your body isn't moving through stopped time.
You simply begin responding before everyone else has finished deciding what they are doing. By the time danger happens, you have already moved.

optionalfeature.name: Nothing in You Is Vital
entries: Your body still has organs. It simply stopped depending on any particular one. Your body has become impossibly redundant.

items: Critical Hits against you become normal hits.
You can't suffer additional harm or penalties merely because a specific limb, organ, artery, nerve, or other body part is struck or destroyed.

Losing limbs, eyes, lungs, your heart, your head, or other portions of your body doesn't by itself prevent you from moving, speaking, perceiving, breathing, thinking, attacking, casting spells, or using your abilities.
You can't be instantly killed by decapitation, destruction of the brain or heart, blood loss, suffocation, massive damage, or similar anatomical failure.
Effects that require particular anatomy can still affect you, but destroying that anatomy doesn't remove the functions it normally provides.
Severed body parts remain alive as parts of you and can be reattached simply by holding them against their original location for a moment.

entries: When you are reduced to 0 Hit Points, you don't fall Unconscious, fall Prone, or lose Concentration, and you can continue taking turns and acting normally.
While at 0 Hit Points:

items: You still make Death Saving Throws normally.
You have Advantage on Death Saving Throws.
A roll of 1 causes only one failure, rather than two.
Taking damage causes only one failed Death Saving Throw, regardless of whether the damage came from a Critical Hit.
Whenever you succeed on a Death Saving Throw, you immediately regain 1 Hit Point.
Becoming Stable also causes you to regain 1 Hit Point.

entries: If an effect would kill you outright without reducing you to 0 Hit Points, you instead drop to 0 Hit Points and suffer one failed Death Saving Throw, unless your body is completely destroyed or the effect explicitly prevents survival by any means. You die normally only if you accumulate three failed Death Saving Throws, your body is completely destroyed, or an effect explicitly prevents this Invocation from preserving you. There is no single part of you that the rest can't live without.

optionalfeature.name: The Weave Moves Too Slowly
entries: Magic begins forming long before lesser minds realize a spell has been cast. Your magical perception and spellcasting reflexes operate at supernatural speed.

items: You can't be Surprised.
You have Advantage on Initiative rolls and add your Proficiency Bonus to Initiative.
A d20 roll of 14 or lower on Initiative counts as 15.
You have Truesight out to 300 feet.
You continuously perceive the presence of magic within 300 feet of you.
Within that range, you know the location of magical creatures, active spells, magical effects, portals, wards, and Magic Items that aren't behind Total Cover.
Whenever you perceive a spell being cast, you immediately know the spell, its level, targets or area, and whether it requires Concentration before it resolves.
You automatically recognize the nature and function of active spells and magical effects you can perceive.
You have Advantage on saving throws against spells and magical effects.
You can take Reactions before your first turn in combat.
At the start of every creature's turn other than your own, you regain one expended Reaction.

entries.name: Unrestricted Reactions
entries: Your Reaction spellcasting is no longer restricted by the normal limits on casting multiple spells during the same turn. Whenever the trigger for a spell with a Casting Time of 1 Reaction occurs, you can cast that spell normally if you have a Reaction available.
Casting a spell using your Reaction:

items: Doesn't prevent you from casting another spell using a Spell Slot during the same turn.
Isn't prevented because you already cast one or more spells using Spell Slots during that turn.
Can be done repeatedly during the same round as long as you continue regaining Reactions and have the required Spell Slots or other resources.
Can include multiple leveled spells cast during the same creature's turn if you legitimately gain enough Reactions to do so.
Ignores any rule that would otherwise limit how many spells using Spell Slots you can cast during that turn.

entries: Each spell still expends its Spell Slot and other required resources normally. If you have another Reaction, you have another spell.

optionalfeature.name: The Fight Does Not Wait for Your Turn
entries: Turns are an abstraction. Violence isn't. Your combat reflexes no longer obey the normal rhythm of battle.

items: You can't be Surprised.
You have Advantage on Initiative rolls and add your Proficiency Bonus to Initiative.
A d20 roll of 14 or lower on Initiative counts as 15.
You can take Reactions before your first turn in combat.
At the start of every creature's turn other than your own, you regain one expended Reaction.
Making an attack as a Reaction doesn't prevent you from making other attacks during that turn.

entries: Whenever a creature you can perceive begins an attack, casts a spell, moves, teleports, activates an ability, draws or uses an object, or otherwise commits to an action, you can use your Reaction before that event resolves. When you do, you can immediately take the Attack action.
This Attack action:

items: Can use weapons, Unarmed Strikes, or any combination normally available to you.
Includes every additional attack you would normally make when taking the Attack action, including Extra Attack.
Can use Weapon Mastery and other features that normally apply to your attacks.
Can occur even if you already took the Attack action during that turn.
Can interrupt the triggering event if your attacks make it impossible to complete.
Resolves completely before the triggering event continues.

entries: Before making these attacks, you can also move up to half your Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Effects that claim to occur too quickly to react to don't prevent this Invocation from functioning. If someone else gets a turn, you get a fight.

optionalfeature.name: Combat Is One Motion
entries: To you, attacking, guarding, moving, and acting are all parts of the same motion. Whenever you take the Attack action, you can replace any attack you would make as part of that action with one nonmagical Action or Bonus Action you could normally take.

items: The replacement requires no additional Action or Bonus Action.
It can't be the Attack action or Magic action.

You can use Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide, Influence, Ready, Search, Study, Utilize, or activate a nonmagical class feature, feat, item, or ability that normally requires an Action or Bonus Action.
You can choose the same option multiple times during the same Attack action if its effect can meaningfully occur more than once.
You can freely alternate attacks, movement, and replacement actions in any order.
Taking one of these replacement actions doesn't prevent you from taking that same Action or Bonus Action again normally during the turn.

A restriction that normally allows a particular nonmagical Action or Bonus Action only once during your turn doesn't prevent you from taking it again through this Invocation unless the feature itself has a limited number of uses.
If you replace an attack with Dash, you immediately gain additional movement equal to your Speed.
If you replace an attack with Dodge, its benefits begin immediately rather than waiting for the Attack action to finish.
If you replace an attack with Ready, the readied action doesn't require your Reaction when its trigger occurs, though you can have only one such readied action waiting at a time.

entries: In addition, whenever another feature grants you additional attacks as part of the Attack action, each of those attacks can also be replaced through this Invocation. So if you can make four attacks, you effectively possess four interchangeable pieces of martial action economy every time you take the Attack action. You don't divide six seconds into actions. You simply use all six seconds.

optionalfeature.name: Perfect Opening
entries: Armor doesn't stop your attacks. It only tells you how precise the strike needs to be. Whenever you make a weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, compare the total attack roll to the target's AC.

items: If the attack roll exceeds the target's AC by 5 or more, the attack is a Critical Hit.
If it exceeds the target's AC by 10 or more, maximize all damage dice rolled for that attack instead of rolling them.
If it exceeds the target's AC by 15 or more, the attack also deals one additional set of the weapon's or Unarmed Strike's normal damage dice, maximized.
A natural 20 is treated as exceeding the target's AC by at least 10 for this Invocation.
If another feature expands your Critical Hit range, those Critical Hits also receive the maximized damage benefit if the attack roll exceeds the target's AC by 10 or more.
Bonuses and penalties to the attack roll or the target's AC apply normally when determining these thresholds.
An effect that would normally turn a Critical Hit into a normal hit doesn't prevent this Invocation from treating an attack that exceeds AC by 5 or more as a Critical Hit.

entries: The additional normal damage dice from exceeding AC by 15 are part of the attack, but aren't doubled again by the Critical Hit. The farther your attack passes their defense, the less of them is left afterward.

optionalfeature.name: Sweeping Assault
entries: Whenever you make a melee weapon attack or {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB}, you can attack every creature and object of your choice within your reach with that attack. Make a separate attack roll against each target.

items: Each hit deals the attack's full normal damage.
Each hit can independently trigger Weapon Mastery, Critical Hits, and other on-hit effects.
Effects that add damage to an attack apply to every qualifying hit unless they explicitly state they can affect only one creature or one hit.
Creatures don't provide Cover to other targets of the same attack.
You can choose different damage types, Mastery effects, or other attack-by-attack choices separately for each target when normally allowed.
If the attack pushes, pulls, knocks Prone, Grapples, disarms, or otherwise affects its target, you can apply that effect independently to every creature hit.
Missing one target has no effect on the attacks against the others.

entries: This applies to every melee attack you make, including attacks from Extra Attack, Bonus Actions, Reactions, Opportunity Attacks, and attacks granted by other features. If an effect lets one melee attack strike from an unusual location or with an increased reach, Sweeping Assault uses that attack's actual reach for determining every eligible target. A melee attack is no longer one strike against one enemy. It is everything within reach being struck at once.

optionalfeature.name: Parry the Impossible
entries: {@i If an effect can reach you, there is a moment in which it can be struck.}
Whenever an effect forces you to make a Saving Throw, you can use your Reaction to make one weapon attack or Unarmed Strike instead. Use the effect's Saving Throw DC as the AC for this attack.

items: On a hit, you count as succeeding on the Saving Throw.
On a miss, you fail the Saving Throw.
Advantage or Disadvantage on the Saving Throw instead applies to this attack roll.
Normal bonuses to your weapon attack or Unarmed Strike apply, but bonuses that apply specifically to Saving Throws don't.
You can use features that modify the attack roll, but effects that require actually hitting a creature don't trigger.
If the attack is a Critical Hit, and the effect would normally deal half damage or impose a reduced effect on a successful save, you instead suffer no damage and no additional effect.

entries: This can be used against spells, breath weapons, explosions, supernatural abilities, traps, and other effects that allow a Saving Throw. It doesn't work against effects that provide no Saving Throw, and it doesn't automatically negate an effect merely because you succeed; unless you score a Critical Hit, use the effect's normal result for a successful save.
{@i You aren't immune to magic. You're simply allowed to fight it.}

optionalfeature.name: Bleed the Weave
entries: {@i Spellcasting becomes difficult when every wound tears at the magic holding it together.}
Whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, that creature becomes unstable until the start of your next turn.
While unstable, whenever it casts a spell using a Spell Slot, it must choose one:

items: Expend an additional Spell Slot of the same level or higher.
Cast the spell normally, but immediately take damage equal to twice the damage dealt by your triggering attack after the spell resolves.

entries: If it has no additional Spell Slot it can expend, it must take the damage. If you hit the same creature multiple times, each hit creates another separate cost. The next spell it casts must satisfy all of those costs. For example, if you hit a Wizard three times before it casts Disintegrate, it must either expend three additional qualifying Spell Slots, take the stored damage from any costs it doesn't pay, or combine the two. This doesn't prevent spellcasting, Counterspell the spell, or remove existing magic.
{@i You don't silence a mage. You make every spell hurt enough to matter.}

optionalfeature.name: Break Their Rhythm
entries: {@i Every hit takes something out of the next few seconds.}
Whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, choose one of the following effects:

items: Its Speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
It can't take Reactions until the start of your next turn.
It can't take Bonus Actions until the start of your next turn.
The next time it takes the Attack action or Multiattack before the start of your next turn, it makes one fewer attack.
The next attack roll it makes before the start of your next turn has Disadvantage.

entries: Different effects from this Invocation can affect the same creature simultaneously. If you hit it multiple times, you can choose an effect for every hit. The Speed reduction and reduction to the number of attacks are cumulative. If the number of attacks it could make is reduced to 0, it can still take the Attack action or Multiattack, but makes no attacks as part of it.
{@i You don't need to defeat someone in one blow. You can take their turn apart piece by piece.}

optionalfeature.name: Strike the Attempt
entries: {@i Anything someone tries to do has a moment where it can be interrupted.}

Whenever a creature you can perceive within your weapon's reach or range makes a d20 Test, you can use your Reaction to make one weapon attack or Unarmed Strike against that creature. Resolve your attack roll before the triggering d20 Test is resolved.

items: If your attack roll is lower than the creature's d20 Test total, nothing changes.
If your attack roll equals or exceeds that total, the creature's d20 Test fails, regardless of whether it would normally have succeeded.
Your attack still deals damage normally if it hits the creature's AC.
The attack can interfere with an Attack Roll, Ability Check, or Saving Throw.
Advantage, Disadvantage, Critical Hits, Weapon Mastery, and other effects that modify your attack function normally.
Effects that modify the triggering creature's d20 Test still apply before the totals are compared.
Legendary Resistance can still turn a failed Saving Throw into a success normally.

entries: You don't need to damage the creature for the interruption to work; you only need your attack roll to meet or exceed its result.
{@i A perfect attack, a desperate save, a flawless maneuver—it only has to be disrupted once.}

optionalfeature.name: Wounds Stay Open
entries: {@i Your attacks leave injuries that refuse to close while the fight is still happening.}
Whenever you damage a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, until the start of your next turn:

items: It can't regain Hit Points.
It can't gain Temporary Hit Points.
Any Regeneration or similar feature it possesses is suppressed.
Effects that would restore Hit Points are still used or expended normally, but restore 0 Hit Points.
If an effect would return it from 0 Hit Points without actually resurrecting it from death, that effect fails.
Healing, regeneration, transformation, changing form, or replacing its body can't remove damage you dealt during this period.

entries: Hitting the creature again refreshes the duration. This works regardless of whether the recovery comes from magic, medicine, biology, items, class features, monster traits, or another creature.
{@i Once you make a wound, it stays a wound until you give it time to close.}

optionalfeature.name: Cut It Loose
entries: {@i If something is holding a creature, then that something can be cut.}

Whenever you make a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you can target one effect currently affecting a creature within your reach or weapon range instead of targeting the creature itself. Make the attack against the effect's Saving Throw DC as AC. If it has no DC, its AC is 18.
On a hit, choose one of the following affecting that creature and end it:

items: Grappled or Restrained.
Charmed, Frightened, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, or Stunned.
A curse, possession, forced transformation, or mind-control effect.
A magical or supernatural restraint, binding, seal, or similar effect.
A nonmagical restraint such as chains, manacles, ropes, webs, or another physical binding.

entries: The attack deals no damage to the creature unless you choose otherwise. If the effect normally can't be ended early, doesn't allow repeated Saving Throws, or says it can be removed only by a particular method, this Invocation can still end it. On a Critical Hit, you can end every qualifying effect from the same source affecting that creature.
{@i If it can hold someone, you can find the part that needs cutting.}

optionalfeature.name: Break Their Foundation
entries: {@i Every fighter depends on something. Strength, speed, endurance, focus—you can break whichever part matters most.}

Whenever you hit a creature with a weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, choose Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma. The chosen Ability Score is reduced by 2 until the start of your next turn, to a minimum of 1.

items: Multiple hits can reduce the same Ability Score, and the reductions are cumulative.
You can choose a different Ability Score for each hit.
Any Attack Roll, Ability Check, Saving Throw, save DC, AC, damage modifier, spellcasting modifier, feature, or other calculation that uses the reduced score uses its current reduced value.
If reducing Dexterity lowers a creature's AC, its AC changes immediately.
If reducing an Ability Score causes the creature to stop meeting a requirement for one of its own features, that feature is suppressed until it meets the requirement again.
Hitting the creature again refreshes the duration of all reductions you have inflicted on it.

entries: The reductions end together at the start of your next turn.
{@i You don't have to overcome what someone is good at. You can make them worse at it.}

optionalfeature.name: If It Exists, You Can Stand on It
entries: {@i Your body no longer recognizes "nothing" as a valid excuse for falling.}

For you, anything that occupies, crosses, affects, or meaningfully exists within a space can function as solid terrain, regardless of whether it possesses matter, weight, permanence, or a physical surface.
You can walk, run, climb, stand, or balance on things such as:

items: Air, water, smoke, mist, clouds, fire, light, darkness, shadows, sound, or magical energy.
Walls, ceilings, vertical surfaces, and empty space.
Beams, barriers, portals, magical fields, spell effects, and other supernatural phenomena.
Falling rain, flying debris, explosions, shockwaves, moving currents, and similar transient phenomena.
Weapons, ammunition, projectiles, creatures, vehicles, or other moving things.

entries: You can change the direction you consider down whenever you move, allowing you to travel freely in three dimensions using your normal Speed without gaining a Fly Speed.
In addition:

items: You can stop in empty space at any moment and remain there indefinitely.
If the thing supporting you moves, you can allow it to carry you without spending your movement.
You can step onto a projectile, beam, wave, or similar moving effect and travel with it until you step away.
If your current support disappears, expires, is destroyed, or moves away, you can simply continue standing on the space where it was.
You can instantly stop any fall by treating the air beneath you as ground.
Forced movement can't make you fall simply because there is no surface beneath you.
Creatures and objects you are carrying or dragging are supported along with you and don't fall merely because your path has no conventional ground.
You can stand upon something even if it is normally incorporeal, intangible, immaterial, or incapable of supporting weight.
Your weight and movement don't damage or disturb the thing you are standing on unless you deliberately interact with it normally.

entries: This doesn't make the chosen surface solid for anyone else.
{@i To you, "there's nothing there" stopped meaning anything.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Flame
entries: {@i Every flame is part of the same fire—and fire answers when you call.}

Whenever you touch or enter a flame, you can connect to any other flame you know exists on the same plane. Through connected fire, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the shared fire, and use another flame to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect. As a Bonus Action, you can ignite a flame at a point you can see within 120 feet. The flame can occupy up to a 10-foot Cube, lasts until you dismiss it, and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Fire damage.
You can transform into living flame.
While transformed, you can pass through creatures, tiny openings, flames, smoke, and burning spaces.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Whenever you emerge from a connected flame, creatures of your choice within 10 feet make a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC, taking {@damage 6d8} Fire damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. Flammable unattended objects in the area ignite.
{@b Level 17.} Flames on other planes are also connected.
{@i You don't travel through fire. Fire burns wherever you choose to arrive.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Water
entries: {@i Every drop is part of the same sea—and the sea moves with you.}

Whenever you touch or enter water, you can connect to any other water you know exists on the same plane. Through connected water, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the shared water, and use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect. As a Bonus Action, you can create water at a point you can see within 120 feet, filling up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You can breathe air and water.
You gain a Swim Speed equal to twice your Speed.
You can transform into living water.
While transformed, you can flow through creatures, tiny openings, pipes, cracks, and other spaces liquid could pass through.
Pressure, currents, and depth don't harm or hinder you.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected water, you can release a violent surge. Creatures of your choice within 10 feet make a Strength Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Bludgeoning damage, are pushed up to 20 feet, and are knocked Prone. On a success, they take half damage only.
{@b Level 17.} Water on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't cross the sea. The sea carries you wherever you decide to surface.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Earth
entries: {@i Every stone is part of the same earth—and the earth has no walls for you.}

Whenever you touch earth, stone, sand, clay, crystal, or natural metal, you can connect to any other such material you know exists on the same plane. Through connected earth, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the connected earth, and use another surface to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

As a Bonus Action, you can cause earth, stone, or crystal to grow at a point you can see within 120 feet, occupying up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You can move through earth and stone as though they were open space.
You can transform into living stone, sand, or earth.
You don't need to breathe while inside solid material.
Pressure, crushing, burial, and lack of space don't harm you while traveling this way.
You can't be knocked Prone or forcibly moved while touching the ground unless you choose to be.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected earth, the ground within 10 feet erupts. Creatures of your choice there make a Strength Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Bludgeoning damage, are knocked Prone, and their Speed becomes 0 until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half damage only.
{@b Level 17.} Earth and stone on other planes are also connected.
{@i You don't pass through the mountain. The mountain simply stops being an obstacle.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Wind
entries: {@i Every breath and breeze belongs to the same sky—and the sky carries you wherever you wish.}

Whenever you are in contact with air or wind, you can connect to any other air or wind you know exists on the same plane. Through connected air, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the connected sky, and use another area of air to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

As a Bonus Action, you can create a powerful current of air at a point you can see within 120 feet, occupying up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You gain a Fly Speed equal to twice your Speed and can Hover.
You can transform into living wind.
While transformed, you can pass through creatures, tiny openings, cracks, and any space air can enter.
Wind, storms, altitude, and atmospheric pressure don't hinder you.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected air, you can unleash a blast of wind. Creatures of your choice within 15 feet make a Strength Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Thunder damage and are pushed up to 30 feet. On a success, they take half damage and aren't pushed.
{@b Level 17.} Air on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't fly through the sky. The sky moves you.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Lightning
entries: {@i Every spark is part of the same storm—and so are you.}

You can create electricity from your body at will. As a Bonus Action, you can call down or create a bolt of lightning at any point you can see within 120 feet. Creatures within 5 feet of that point make a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC, taking {@damage 6d10} Lightning damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. The lightning counts as an electrical source for this Invocation until the start of your next turn.
Whenever you touch or enter lightning, electricity, or an electrical charge, you can connect to any other electrical source you know exists on the same plane.
Through connected electricity, you can:

items: See, hear, speak, reach, attack, and interact as though the two sources were beside each other.
Pass objects through one source and retrieve them from another.
Enter one source and emerge from another, bringing willing creatures touching you.
Use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.
Remain within the current and emerge elsewhere later.

entries: You can also transform completely into living lightning. While transformed, you can move through creatures, tiny openings, wires, metal, and conductive material, or travel through open air using your normal Speed. You can't be Grappled, Restrained, or knocked Prone, your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks, and you are Immune to Lightning damage. Natural lightning, static electricity, electrical devices, magical lightning, and lightning you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Electrical sources on other planes are also connected.
{@i You don't wait for the storm. You make one.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Frost
entries: {@i Every frost is part of the same winter—and winter follows wherever you go.}
Whenever you touch ice, frost, snow, or supernatural cold, you can connect to any other such source you know exists on the same plane.
Through connected winter, you can:

items: See, hear, speak, reach, attack, and interact as though the two sources were beside each other.
Pass objects through one source and retrieve them from another.
Enter one source and emerge from another, bringing willing creatures touching you.
Remain within the connected winter and emerge elsewhere later.
Use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

entries: As a Bonus Action, you can cause frost, snow, or solid ice to appear at a point you can see within 120 feet, covering a surface or space up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Cold damage.
Snow, ice, extreme cold, and blizzards never hinder your movement or vision.
You can move through ice and snow as though they were open space.
You can transform into living frost or drifting snow while traveling through the connected winter, allowing you to pass through tiny openings and spaces creatures normally couldn't occupy.

entries: Whenever you emerge from a connected source, you can instantly freeze the area within 10 feet of you. Creatures of your choice there make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC, taking {@damage 6d8} Cold damage on a failed save, or half as much on a success. On a failed save, their Speed also becomes 0 until the start of your next turn. Cold, snow, ice, blizzards, magical ice, supernatural freezing, and frost you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Frozen sources on other planes are also connected.
{@i You don't travel through winter. Winter opens wherever you choose to arrive.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Light
entries: {@i Every ray belongs to the same light—and for a moment, so do you.}

Whenever you touch or stand within Bright Light or Dim Light, you can connect to any other source of light you know exists on the same plane. Through connected light, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the connected light, and use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.
As a Bonus Action, you can create a source of brilliant light at a point you can see within 120 feet. It fills a 10-foot Cube, lasts until you dismiss it, and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Radiant damage.
You can transform completely into living light.
While transformed, you can move through creatures, transparent objects, tiny openings, and any path light could physically pass through.
Your Speed becomes four times your normal Speed, you gain a Fly Speed equal to it, and you can Hover.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
Mirrors and reflective surfaces can redirect your movement without costing additional movement.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected light, creatures of your choice within 15 feet make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take 6d8 Radiant damage and are Blinded until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half damage and aren't Blinded. Sunlight, moonlight, magical light, reflected light, and light you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Light on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't move at the speed of light. You become the light that was already there.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Darkness
entries: {@i Every shadow belongs to the same darkness—and darkness is never truly empty.}
Whenever you touch or enter darkness or a shadow, you can connect to any other darkness or shadow you know exists on the same plane.
Through connected darkness, you can:

items: See, hear, speak, reach, attack, and interact as though the two sources were beside each other.
Pass objects through one source and retrieve them from another.
Enter one source and emerge from another, bringing willing creatures touching you.
Remain within the connected darkness and emerge elsewhere later.
Use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

entries: As a Bonus Action, you can create supernatural darkness at a point you can see within 120 feet, filling up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it, extinguishes nonmagical light inside it, and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Necrotic damage.
You can see normally through Darkness, magical or otherwise.
You can transform into living darkness.
While transformed, you can pass through creatures, tiny openings, shadows, and any unlit space.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
Even the smallest shadow can momentarily expand enough for you to enter or emerge from it.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected darkness, creatures of your choice within 15 feet make a Wisdom Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Necrotic damage and are {@condition Frightened|XPHB} of you until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half damage and aren't Frightened. Ordinary darkness, shadows, magical Darkness, and darkness you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Darkness on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't hide in darkness. Darkness is where you exist.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Acid
entries: {@i Every corrosive drop is part of the same dissolution—and eventually, everything gives way.}

Whenever you touch acid or another strongly corrosive liquid, you can connect to any other such source you know exists on the same plane. Through connected acid, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the connected acid, and use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

As a {@b Bonus Action}, you can create a pool or torrent of supernatural acid at a point you can see within 120 feet, occupying up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Acid damage.
You can transform completely into living acid.
While transformed, you can flow through creatures, tiny openings, cracks, pipes, and other spaces liquid could pass through.
You can move through nonmagical objects and structures as though they were Difficult Terrain, dissolving a passage through them as you move.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected acid, creatures of your choice within 10 feet make a Dexterity Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Acid damage, and their AC is reduced by 2 until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half damage and suffer no AC reduction. Unattended objects and structures affected by this acid take maximum damage, and the damage ignores Damage Thresholds and ordinary material hardness.
Natural acid, alchemical acid, digestive acid, magical acid, and acid you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Acid on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't find a way through. You dissolve one.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Poison
entries: {@i Every venom, toxin, and poisoned breath is part of the same corruption.}

Whenever you touch poison, venom, toxin, toxic gas, or a creature suffering the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition, you can connect to any other such source you know exists on the same plane. Through connected poison, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the connected poison, and use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

As a Bonus Action, you can create supernatural poison at a point you can see within 120 feet, as liquid, vapor, or mist filling up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Poison damage and the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.
You can transform completely into living poison.
While transformed, you can flow as liquid or vapor through creatures, tiny openings, cracks, pipes, vents, and any space gas or liquid could enter.
A creature suffering the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition itself counts as an entrance and exit for your connected poison.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected poison, creatures of your choice within 15 feet make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Poison damage and become {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half damage and aren't Poisoned. A creature Poisoned by this Invocation immediately becomes a valid source for it, allowing the connected poison to spread from creature to creature.
Natural venom, alchemical poison, poisonous plants, toxic gas, magical poison, and poison you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Poison on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't carry poison. Wherever poison exists, part of you is already there.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Thunder
entries: {@i Every sound is only matter remembering how to shake.}

Whenever you touch or enter a sound, vibration, shockwave, or thunderous impact, you can connect to any other sound or vibration you know exists on the same plane. Through connected resonance, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the resonance, and use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

As a Bonus Action, you can create a thunderous vibration at a point you can see within 120 feet, filling up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Thunder damage and the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition.
You can transform completely into living vibration.
While transformed, you can move through air, water, creatures, walls, floors, metal, stone, and any other material capable of carrying vibration.
You can pass through tiny openings and solid objects without damaging them.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.
You have Blindsight 120 feet while any sound or vibration exists within that range.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected resonance, creatures of your choice within 15 feet make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Thunder damage, are pushed up to 20 feet, and are {@condition Deafened|XPHB} until the start of your next turn. On a success, they take half damage and suffer no other effect. Unattended objects and structures in the area take maximum Thunder damage, and this damage ignores Damage Thresholds.
Voices, footsteps, weapon impacts, explosions, music, tremors, magical sound, and thunder you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Sound and vibration on other planes are also connected.
{@i You don't travel with the sound. You are the vibration passing through the world.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Force
entries: {@i Every impact, pressure, barrier, and invisible push is only force taking a different shape.}

Whenever you touch a magical force, force field, shock of kinetic energy, or effect that deals Force damage, you can connect to any other such source you know exists on the same plane. Through connected force, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the connected force, and use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.

As a Bonus Action, you can create a visible or invisible knot of pure force at a point you can see within 120 feet, occupying up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source for this Invocation.
While using this Invocation:

items: You are Immune to Force damage.
You can transform completely into living force.
While transformed, you gain a Fly Speed equal to twice your Speed and can Hover.
You can move through creatures, objects, walls, magical barriers, and other solid matter as though they were Difficult Terrain.
Effects that would push, pull, knock you Prone, or forcibly move you have no effect unless you allow them.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected force, creatures of your choice within 15 feet make a Strength Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Force damage, are knocked {@condition Prone|XPHB}, and you move them up to 30 feet in any direction. On a success, they take half damage and aren't moved or knocked Prone. Force fields, magical barriers, telekinetic force, impacts, magical pressure, and effects that deal Force damage all count.
{@b Level 17.} Force on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't push against the world. You become the force that decides where the world moves.}

optionalfeature.name: Avatar of Blood
entries: {@i Blood is not separate simply because it flows through different bodies.}

Any creature with blood, any exposed blood, and any effect that creates or manipulates blood counts as a source for this Invocation. You can connect to any such source you know exists on the same plane. Through connected blood, you can see, hear, speak, reach, attack, interact, pass objects, travel with willing creatures touching you, remain within the connected blood, and use another source to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect.
As a Bonus Action, you can create supernatural blood at a point you can see within 120 feet, filling up to a 10-foot Cube. It lasts until you dismiss it and counts as a source.
While using this Invocation:

items: You can transform completely into living blood.
While transformed, you can flow through creatures, wounds, tiny openings, pipes, cracks, and any space liquid could enter.
A creature with blood counts as an entrance and exit even if it isn't wounded.
You can remain inside a creature's bloodstream without occupying its space.
You don't need to breathe while transformed.
Your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks.

entries: Whenever you emerge from connected blood, creatures of your choice within 10 feet make a Constitution Saving Throw against your Invocation Save DC. On a failure, they take {@damage 6d8} Necrotic damage, and until the start of your next turn, whenever they move, make an attack, or cast a spell, they take an additional {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage. On a success, they take half the initial damage and suffer no additional effect. Natural blood, magical blood, blood inside living creatures, and blood you create all count.
{@b Level 17.} Blood on other planes is also connected.
{@i You don't move through their veins. For a moment, their veins are part of you.}

optionalfeature.name: Be Somewhere Else When It Happens
entries: {@i Sometimes the easiest way to survive a moment is simply not to be part of it.}

When an attack, spell, trap, Area of Effect, or other effect would affect you, you can use your Reaction to step outside the current moment before that effect resolves. You cease to exist until the start of your next turn.
While absent:

items: You can't be targeted, damaged, perceived, moved, or affected by anything.
The triggering effect can't affect you, even if it normally ignores cover, crosses planes, or affects an entire area.
You don't occupy a space.
You don't experience time, and durations affecting you don't decrease.
You can't take Actions, Bonus Actions, Reactions, or movement.
Grapples, restraints, and other effects requiring something to physically hold or contain you immediately end.

entries: At the start of your next turn, you return to the space you left. If that space is occupied or no longer exists, you appear in the nearest unoccupied space you choose. Anything you were wearing or carrying leaves the moment with you.
