{@b Level 17.} When you leave the moment, you can return at the start of any later turn you can perceive, rather than necessarily your next turn.
{@i You weren't fast enough to dodge it. You simply weren't there when it happened.}

optionalfeature.name: Cross It Out
entries: {@i Reality is surprisingly willing to accept corrections.}

As an Action, write one short sentence describing a fact you can currently perceive about a creature, object, or location within 120 feet. The sentence must be true when written. You can then cross out one word or short phrase and replace it with another. Reality immediately changes to make the corrected sentence true.
For example:

items: "The door is locked." → "The door is open."
"The sword is in his hand." → "The sword is on the floor."
"The bridge is broken." → "The bridge is intact."
"The torch is burning." → "The torch is extinguished."
"The creature is standing." → "The creature is Prone."
"The wall is whole." → "The wall is shattered."

entries: If the correction directly alters an unwilling creature or something it is wearing or carrying, that creature makes a Charisma Saving Throw against a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the modifier of the ability score you use for this Invocation. On a success, that correction fails. The correction can't directly declare a creature dead, nonexistent, change its identity, create a creature from nothing, or grant resources or abilities it didn't possess.
{@b Level 17.} You can correct facts about anything you can perceive on the same plane, regardless of distance.
{@i You don't change reality. You correct the sentence describing it.}

optionalfeature.name: Solid to Whom?
entries: {@i Being solid does not mean being solid to everyone.}

As a Bonus Action, choose any amount of nonliving solid matter you can perceive within 120 feet, contained within a 60-foot Cube. You decide exactly what that matter is solid or intangible to. Your choices can distinguish between creatures, objects, attacks, projectiles, spells, and other effects individually.
For example:

items: You and your allies can walk through walls while enemies can't.
A floor can support everyone except one creature.
Your attacks can pass through walls, shields, armor, or other barriers before striking normally.
Enemy projectiles can pass harmlessly through the floor or a chosen barrier instead of striking their targets.
A prison can remain solid to its prisoners while everyone else walks through it.
Objects can be placed inside or removed through sealed containers without opening them.
A creature can fall through several floors while those floors remain solid to everyone else.

entries: The affected matter remains physically unchanged and can still support, block, contain, or interact with anything you haven't excluded. You can change any of these permissions at any time without an Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction, including immediately before something would touch or pass through the affected matter. Magical objects and magical structures can be affected normally. Artifacts are unaffected unless they allow their physical state to be altered.

If something is inside affected matter when you make that matter solid to it, you choose whether it is pushed to the nearest open space on either side or remains harmlessly embedded until you allow it to pass out.

{@b Level 17.} Range is no longer relevant. You can alter the solidity of any nonliving solid matter you can perceive or whose location you know on the same plane, and different portions of the same object or structure can obey entirely different permissions simultaneously.
{@i The wall is real. Who it is real to is your decision.}

optionalfeature.name: Say My Name
entries: {@i Speaking of you is dangerously close to inviting you in.}

Whenever a creature knowingly speaks any name, nickname, title, or designation that refers to you, you immediately know it happened. You learn the speaker's identity, exact location, and plane of existence, provided you have encountered that creature before. Otherwise, you learn its exact location and plane.
For the next 1 minute, the speaker becomes an anchor for you. Through that creature, you can:

items: See and hear from its space while still perceiving normally from your own.
Speak from its space in your own voice.
Use its space to determine your range, reach, line of sight, and line of effect for attacks, spells, Invocations, and other abilities.
Interact with unattended objects within your normal reach of it as though you were standing there.
Pass an object you are holding through the anchor, causing it to appear in an unoccupied space within 5 feet of the speaker.
Target the speaker itself through the anchor regardless of distance or Total Cover.

entries: Distance and physical barriers between you and the anchor don't interfere with any of these benefits. If a name, nickname, title, or designation referring to you is written, that writing becomes an anchor instead and remains one for as long as it is legible. Writing copied, carved, printed, painted, engraved, magically produced, or displayed electronically all qualify. Through a written anchor, you gain all the same benefits, using the writing's location instead of a speaker's space.

You can perceive through any number of your anchors simultaneously, and whenever you make an attack, cast a spell, or use an ability, you can choose which anchor it originates from. You immediately know whenever one of your anchors is moved, destroyed, erased, concealed, or made unreadable. This Invocation functions across planar boundaries.
{@i They didn't summon you. They just made the mistake of referring to you.}

optionalfeature.name: Stay There
entries: {@i Putting something somewhere can be more permanent than gravity expects.}
Whenever you release an object you are touching, you can choose for it to become fixed exactly where and how you left it.
While fixed:

items: The object can't be moved, rotated, pushed, pulled, lifted, dropped, or knocked away unless you allow it.
Gravity, wind, water, impacts, explosions, forced movement, teleportation, and magical effects can't change its position.
It can remain suspended in midair at any angle.
It can support any amount of weight, though the object itself can still break if it isn't durable enough.
A fixed rope, chain, weapon, pole, shield, door, lever, wheel, or similar object can function as an immovable anchor.
If something is attached to the object, moving that thing doesn't move the fixed object.
If the surrounding floor, wall, vehicle, building, or terrain moves or disappears, the object remains exactly where it was.

entries: You can release any object you fixed at any time without an action. You can also move one of your fixed objects normally while touching it; the moment you stop moving it, it becomes fixed again wherever you left it.

{@b Level 7.} You can fix an object regardless of its size or weight. You can also touch an object being worn or carried by another creature and attempt to fix it. An unwilling creature makes a Strength Saving Throw against a DC equal to 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the modifier of the ability score you use for this Invocation. On a failure, the object becomes fixed, potentially pinning the creature in place until it releases the object, escapes it normally, or the object is destroyed.
{@i You didn't make it heavy. You told its position to stop changing.}

optionalfeature.name: Your Voice Has No Location
entries: {@i Sound only comes from somewhere because most people let it.}

Whenever you or anything you are wearing or carrying produces a sound, you decide where that sound originates. It can originate from you, from any point you know within 120 feet, from several such points simultaneously, or from nowhere at all.
You gain the following benefits:

items: You can perfectly reproduce any voice or nonmagical sound you have ever heard, including its volume, accent, rhythm, pitch, and other audible qualities.
You can make different creatures hear the same sound from different directions.
You can make a sound audible only to creatures you choose, provided they are within 120 feet of you or one of its chosen origins.
You can whisper directly beside a creature's ear without anyone else hearing it.
You can make your footsteps, breathing, armor, weapons, clothing, carried objects, and other sounds you cause completely silent.
You can make a tiny sound as loud as a shout, or reduce a deafening sound you personally produce to a whisper.
You can make your speech come from behind walls, beneath floors, inside containers, from the ceiling, or from another location you know even if no open path exists between you and that point.
You can reproduce several different remembered sounds simultaneously, placing each at a different location.
You can continuously move the apparent origin of a sound while it is being produced, up to any location within range.
You can leave a repeated sound at a point you know. It continues repeating exactly as you produced it until you dismiss it, move more than 1 mile away, or create another repeated sound this way.
When a creature within 120 feet produces a nonmagical sound you can hear, you can immediately copy that sound and reproduce it from any location allowed by this Invocation.

entries: If you provide a Verbal component for a spell, you can relocate the sound of that component normally. This doesn't change the spell's actual point of origin, range, or target. A magical effect that prevents you from producing sound entirely still prevents you from supplying a Verbal component, but ordinary Silence around your body doesn't suppress sounds whose chosen origin lies outside that silenced area.
{@i Your lips moved. That is the only evidence the sound ever belonged to you.}

optionalfeature.name: You Can Eat That
entries: {@i Food is just matter with better marketing.}
You can bite, chew, swallow, and digest any nonliving substance, regardless of its hardness, composition, toxicity, temperature, or whether it would normally be edible.

items: Stone, metal, glass, wood, bone, ice, poison, acid, and similar materials can be eaten safely.
Anything you swallow this way can't harm you merely from being consumed.
Your teeth and digestive system aren't damaged by the material.
As an Action, you can bite away and destroy up to a 1-foot Cube of unattended nonmagical material you can reach.
This ignores the object's AC, Damage Threshold, and damage Resistances or Immunities.
You can use this to chew through walls, doors, chains, locks, bars, weapons, or similar objects.
Material you completely digest is destroyed and leaves no usable remains.
You can survive indefinitely by consuming otherwise inedible matter; it provides whatever ordinary nutrition and hydration your body requires.

entries: {@b Level 7.} You can also consume magical objects and magically created matter. A Magic Item loses a portion of its physical substance normally when bitten, though an Artifact can't be destroyed by this Invocation unless it can normally be destroyed that way.
{@i Eventually, everything is bite-sized.}

optionalfeature.name: Carry Yourself
entries: {@i You are perfectly capable of lifting yourself.}
As long as you have at least one free hand, you can grab your own body, clothing, armor, or equipment and lift yourself as though you were carrying another creature.
While doing so:

items: You can move yourself through the air using your Speed, in any direction.
You can stop in midair and remain there without falling.
You can pull yourself straight upward without a surface, ladder, rope, or handhold.
You can immediately stop a fall by grabbing yourself; you take no falling damage from that fall.
You can carry yourself across gaps, over hazards, or along ceilings simply by moving yourself there.
Your own weight doesn't count against the amount you can lift for this Invocation.
Creatures or objects you are actually carrying still count against your normal carrying capacity.

entries: If both of your hands become unable to hold yourself, you fall normally.
{@b Level 5.} You no longer need a free hand; you can move yourself this way simply by deciding where your body should be carried.
{@i Everyone else needs something to stand on. You already brought yourself.}

optionalfeature.name: Sleepwalker
entries: {@i Your body sleeps. Your mind refuses.}
Whenever you sleep or take a Long Rest, you can remain fully conscious, aware, and in control of your body while still receiving every benefit of sleep.
While resting this way:

items: You see, hear, speak, and perceive normally, and your Passive Perception is unaffected.
You aren't Unconscious merely because you're sleeping and can't be caught unaware for that reason.
You can take Reactions normally and roll Initiative normally if danger appears.
You can stand, sit, walk slowly, keep watch, read, write, eat, drink, talk, use tools, and perform other light activity throughout the entire rest.
You can maintain Concentration while sleeping or resting.
You can choose which parts of your body actually sleep; parts that aren't needed can rest while the rest of you continues functioning normally.
Magical sleep can make your body sleep, but it can't make your consciousness shut down. You remain aware and can wake your body whenever you choose.
Effects that depend specifically on you being unaware or Unconscious because you're asleep treat you as awake instead.

entries: {@b Level 7.} Rest no longer requires you to remain stationary. You can travel using your normal Speeds, ride, climb, swim, or be carried for the entire duration of a Long Rest without interrupting it, provided you aren't performing strenuous activity such as fighting. You can also keep watch for the entire Long Rest without reducing or interfering with the benefits you gain from it.
{@i Your body can have the night off. Someone still has to watch it.}

optionalfeature.name: Drink the Light
entries: {@i Light is only difficult to hold if you insist on using your hands.}
As a Bonus Action, choose a point you can see within 60 feet and swallow the light from a 20-foot-radius Sphere centered there.
While you hold that light:

items: The area becomes Darkness, regardless of how much nonmagical light enters it.
Nonmagical flames, lanterns, sunlight, glowing objects, and similar sources continue to exist but produce no illumination inside the area.
You can see normally through Darkness created by this Invocation.
You can move the darkened area up to 60 feet at any time on your turn, requiring no action.
The Darkness can move through walls and other barriers with you directing its center.
You can reshape it into any contiguous form that fits within its original volume, such as a corridor, curtain, dome, narrow trail, or several connected chambers.
You can exempt any creatures, objects, or spaces you choose, allowing light to function normally for them.
You can swallow the light emitted by a specific unattended source instead of creating an area, causing that source to emit no light until you release it.
If you enter an area of ordinary Bright Light or Dim Light, you can swallow that illumination around yourself automatically without using an action.

entries: You can keep swallowed light for as long as you wish. When you release it, choose any point you can see within 120 feet. The stored illumination erupts there, and you decide its shape and brightness, up to Bright Light in a 60-foot radius and Dim Light for another 60 feet.

You can instead release it in an instant flash. Creatures of your choice within 20 feet of the point that can see the flash make a Constitution Saving Throw against 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the modifier of the ability score you use for this Invocation. On a failed save, a creature is Blinded until the start of your next turn. You can freely dim, brighten, extinguish, relocate, divide, or recombine light you have swallowed.

{@b Level 7.} You can swallow magical illumination as easily as ordinary light. If a spell or magical effect creates light, you can remove only its illumination without ending its other effects. You can also swallow sunlight itself from the affected area. The area no longer counts as being in sunlight until you release it.
{@i The sun is still shining. You simply haven't given its light back yet.}

optionalfeature.name: Liquids Go Where You Pour Them
entries: {@i "Down" is only a suggestion.}
Whenever you touch a nonliving, nonmagical liquid, you can control up to a 10-foot Cube of that liquid while it remains within 60 feet of you.

items: On each of your turns, you can move it up to 60 feet in any direction, requiring no action.
You can stop, reverse, redirect, divide, gather, suspend, or reshape it into simple forms.
The liquid can flow across walls, ceilings, through the air, or through any opening it could physically fit through.
Gravity, currents, pressure, buoyancy, and momentum affect it only when you allow them to.
You can separate different liquids from a mixture and control them independently.
Briefly touching acid, poison, boiling liquid, molten material, or similar hazardous liquid to establish control doesn't harm you merely from that contact.

entries: This Invocation can't create liquid or directly control liquid inside a creature.

{@b Level 5.} Your range becomes 120 feet, and you can control up to a 30-foot Cube. Controlled liquid can become rigid enough to form platforms, bridges, barriers, or carry creatures and objects. An unwilling creature carried this way can make a Strength Saving Throw against 8 + your Proficiency Bonus + the modifier of the ability score you use for this Invocation to escape your control.
{@b Level 9.} You can also control magical and magically created liquids, and established control no longer ends because of distance while the liquid remains on the same plane.
{@i You don't control where liquid falls. You decide where it goes.}

monster.name: Crown-Bound Object

ac.special: 15 or the object's original AC, whichever is higher or more appropriate

hp.special: 5 + three times your level, or the object's original Hit Points if higher or more appropriate

languages: understands your commands but can't speak unless its physical form permits it

trait.name: Animated Object
entries: {@b Original Object.} Animation doesn't reshape the object. It retains its original physical form, material, Armor Class, Hit Points, ability scores, saving throws, skills, movement speeds, resistances, immunities, vulnerabilities, senses, weapon properties, magical properties, traits, attacks, damage dice, special actions, and other existing abilities. If the original object has an Armor Class higher than 15, use the original Armor Class. Use the original Hit Points or other statistics when higher or more appropriate; this stat block supplies missing statistics without weakening superior native statistics.

{@b Object Nature.} The object doesn't need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep. While animated, it counts as a Construct and remains an object for effects concerning objects, structures, materials, weapons, armor, or similar things.

{@b Native Attacks.} The object can use a native attack instead of Crown Strike, retaining its normal damage dice, modifiers, range, reach, additional damage, magical properties, riders, and special effects. Use the Strength or Dexterity Crown Strike appropriate to its actual form; these are alternative rolls for the same attack. Retained superior ability scores still apply.

trait.name: Crowned Servant
entries: {@b Bound to the Crown.} The object understands and obeys your commands and intent, despite lacking ordinary intelligence, without further actions from you. It gains neither sapience nor an independent personality.

{@b Initiative.} The object takes its turn immediately after yours. If multiple Crown-Bound Objects act simultaneously, you determine their order. The object doesn't require your Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction to take its turn or continue following an existing command.
{@b Floating Servant.} The object has a flying speed of 40 feet and can hover, regardless of its original shape. It can retain a faster appropriate original speed.

trait.name: Object Forms
entries: Forms reflect the object's existing shape and don't transform it. It can use multiple Forms if its construction supports them.

{@b Edged Form.} Crown Strike deals slashing damage when this Form is used. Once per turn when the object hits with an attack, it deals an extra {@damage PB} Slashing damage. When it scores a Critical Hit, roll one additional normal damage die of the attack.

{@b Piercing Form.} Crown Strike deals piercing damage when this Form is used. The object's melee reach increases by 5 feet while using a piercing portion of its form. Once per turn when it hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, that creature can't willingly move farther away from the object until the start of the object's next turn.

{@b Crushing Form.} Crown Strike deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used. Once per turn when the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, choose one: push the creature 5 feet, knock it prone, or move it up to 5 feet to an unoccupied space within the object's reach.
{@b Guardian Form.} Crown Strike normally deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used unless the object's actual form suggests otherwise.

{@b Grasping Form.} When the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, it can immediately attempt to grapple the target as part of the same attack. The escape DC is {@dc 7 + PB} when using Strength or {@dc 12 + PB} when Dexterity better represents how the object binds the target. These use the object's listed ability scores; retained superior scores still apply. The object can continue attacking while maintaining the grapple if its physical form permits it.

{@b Projectile Form.} The object retains its actual range, ammunition requirements, weapon properties, damage, and magical properties. When making a native ranged attack, the object can use {@hit 4 + PB} as the attack bonus (use retained superior Dexterity if applicable) instead of its normal attack bonus. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on its ranged attacks.

action.name: Crown Strike
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit -1 + PB} to hit, reach determined by the object's actual form, one target. {@h}{@damage 1d4 + -1 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as appropriate to the object's actual physical form. If another damage type is more appropriate because of its original magical or physical properties, use that type instead.

action.name: Crown Strike (Dexterity)
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 4 + PB} to hit, reach determined by the object's actual form, one target. {@h}{@damage 1d4 + 4 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage, as appropriate to the object's actual physical form. If another damage type is more appropriate because of its original magical or physical properties, use that type instead.

reaction.name: Interpose (Guardian Form Only)
entries: When another creature within the object's reach is hit by an attack, the object can move up to half its flying speed toward that creature without provoking opportunity attacks from the attacker and interpose itself. Reduce the triggering attack's damage by {@dice 1 + PB} (use retained superior Constitution if applicable). If this reduces the damage to 0, the protected creature takes no damage from the attack.

trait.name: Crowned Servant

trait.name: Object Forms
entries: Forms reflect the object's existing shape and don't transform it. It can use multiple Forms if its construction supports them.

{@b Edged Form.} Crown Strike deals slashing damage when this Form is used. Once per turn when the object hits with an attack, it deals an extra {@damage PB} Slashing damage. When it scores a Critical Hit, roll one additional normal damage die of the attack.

{@b Piercing Form.} Crown Strike deals piercing damage when this Form is used. The object's melee reach increases by 10 feet while using a piercing portion of its form. Once per turn when it hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, that creature can't willingly move farther away from the object until the start of the object's next turn.

{@b Crushing Form.} Crown Strike deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used. Once per turn when the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, choose one: push the creature 10 feet, knock it prone, or move it up to 10 feet to an unoccupied space within the object's reach.
{@b Guardian Form.} Crown Strike normally deals bludgeoning damage when this Form is used unless the object's actual form suggests otherwise.

{@b Grasping Form.} When the object hits a creature no more than one size larger than itself, it can immediately attempt to grapple the target as part of the same attack. The escape DC is {@dc 14 + PB} when using Strength or {@dc 8 + PB} when Dexterity better represents how the object binds the target. These use the object's listed ability scores; retained superior scores still apply. The object can continue attacking while maintaining the grapple if its physical form permits it.

{@b Projectile Form.} The object retains its actual range, ammunition requirements, weapon properties, damage, and magical properties. When making a native ranged attack, the object can use {@hit 0 + PB} as the attack bonus (use retained superior Dexterity if applicable) instead of its normal attack bonus. Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on its ranged attacks.

monster.name: Crownforged Titan

hp.special: 200 + fifteen times your level

languages: understands your commands; can't speak unless incorporated components allow it

trait.name: Crown Authority
entries: {@b Absolute Servitor.} The Titan obeys your commands absolutely. It acts immediately after your turn and requires no Action, Bonus Action, or Reaction from you to continue carrying out an existing command. It understands the meaning and intent of your commands and can independently determine how to fulfill them. It doesn't become Sapient or develop an independent will.
{@b Titan Save DC.} Whenever a Crownforged Titan ability requires a Saving Throw, the save DC is {@dc 20 + PB} (20 + your Proficiency Bonus) unless that ability explicitly states otherwise.

{@b Titan Attack Formula.} This formula applies only to Crownforged Titans. Whenever the Titan makes an attack, its Attack Bonus equals the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + its Proficiency Bonus (+6) + your Proficiency Bonus. Its attack damage equals the attack's damage dice + the Titan's relevant Ability modifier + its Proficiency Bonus + your Proficiency Bonus. Use the ability relevant to the incorporated component's attack. The Titan Strike entries are alternative rolls for the same attack, not additional attacks. In War Titan Configuration, the Titan can replace one attack of its Multiattack with a Titan Strike.

{@b The Whole Remembers Its Parts.} The Titan retains usable properties of incorporated components whenever those functions can still reasonably operate. This can include Magic Item properties, magical weapons, built-in spells, command-word abilities, siege weapons, firearms, launchers, engines, machinery, vehicles, armor, shields, chains, restraints, magical devices, technological systems, special materials, traps, and other functional components. The Titan can operate these components itself. Charges, ammunition, fuel, consumable components, and similar resources are still consumed normally.

trait.name: Sovereign Defenses
entries: {@b Sovereign Magic Immunity.} The Titan is immune to spells and magical effects unless you choose for that specific effect to affect it. This immunity doesn't interfere with your Crown features, the Titan's own abilities, magic belonging to incorporated components, or effects you voluntarily permit. If an effect would normally have a reduced effect on a successful Saving Throw, it instead has no effect on the Titan unless you allow it.

{@b Sovereign Adamantine Body.} The Titan is immune to all damage caused by nonmagical attacks, regardless of the damage type dealt by that attack. An attack must be magical or otherwise supernatural to bypass this immunity. After bypassing it, the Titan's other Damage Resistances and Damage Immunities still apply.

{@b Immutable Sovereign Form.} Unless you allow it, the Titan can't be transformed, polymorphed, petrified, forcibly changed in Size, merged into another creature or object, magically disassembled, forced to rearrange its components, partially teleported apart, or reshaped by another effect. Only your Crown authority can voluntarily reconfigure or separate it.

{@b Absolute Mass.} Unless you allow it, the Titan can't be Grappled, knocked Prone, Shoved, forcibly moved, forcibly teleported, carried, dragged, lifted, or physically Restrained. An effect that moves the entire surrounding region, plane, or structure can still move the Titan as part of that larger movement.

trait.name: Reconstruction
entries: {@b Indestructible Convergence.} At the start of each of the Titan's turns, it regains 120 Hit Points. This regeneration functions even while the Titan has 0 Hit Points. If it starts its turn at 0 Hit Points and eligible material remains available to constitute it, it regains Hit Points and reforms. Reducing the Titan to 0 Hit Points doesn't automatically destroy it.

{@b Matter Feeds the Titan.} Whenever the Titan regenerates, it can draw eligible unattended nonliving matter within 120 feet into itself. Eligible matter includes earth, soil, stone, sand, clay, rubble, minerals, raw metal, crystal, ice, snow, bone, dead wood, destroyed objects, damaged machinery, broken weapons, and other suitable nonliving matter. The material moves toward the Titan and becomes part of its body. The Titan doesn't require its original components to continue rebuilding itself.

{@b Reconstruction at 0 Hit Points.} Reaching 0 Hit Points doesn't automatically end Titan Convergence. Because of Indestructible Convergence, the Titan can reconstruct itself at the start of its next turn if sufficient eligible material remains. If Titan Convergence ends or the Titan can no longer reconstruct itself, its remaining components collapse into the spaces it occupied.

trait.name: Titan Configuration
entries: The Titan can change Configuration as a Bonus Action; it lasts until changed or the Titan ends. {@b War Titan.} Multiattack: the Titan makes 3 Titan Strikes. (or greater if granted by an incorporated component), one target. {@h}{@damage 6d12 + 7 + PB} Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage according to the incorporated component, or another justified damage type supplied by an incorporated magical component.

action.name: World-Crushing Trample
entries: The Titan can use this as part of its movement. Limit: Once per turn per creature. The Titan can move through the spaces of creatures smaller than itself. The first time it enters a creature's space on a turn, that creature must succeed on a {@dc 20 + PB} Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 12d12 + 17 + PB} Bludgeoning damage, be knocked Prone, and either be pushed to an unoccupied space adjacent to the Titan's path or carried beneath or within the Titan's moving mass until the movement ends.
On a successful save, the creature takes half damage and is moved to the nearest available space outside the Titan's path.

action.name: Sovereign Breach
entries: The Titan can replace one attack of its Multiattack with this action. The Titan can directly attack a magical barrier, ward, boundary, or supernatural obstruction within its Reach, including magical walls, walls of force, magical cages, magical domes, sealed magical doors, supernatural shields, wards preventing passage, barriers preventing teleportation, dimensional boundaries, magical prison walls, and similar effects.

For Sovereign Breach, such a barrier counts as something the Titan can physically attack even if its rules state that it can't be damaged, has no Hit Points, is immune to damage, can't be physically interacted with, can only be removed by a particular spell, or normally can't be destroyed by attacks. Make an attack using the Titan Attack Formula. Choose the relevant ability: {@hit 17 + PB|Strength}, {@hit 8 + PB|Dexterity}, {@hit 17 + PB|Constitution}, {@hit 3 + PB|Intelligence}, {@hit 11 + PB|Wisdom}, {@hit 7 + PB|Charisma}. If the effect has an AC, use it. Otherwise its AC is 10 + the spell or effect's level, or 20 if it has no meaningful level. On a hit, the magical barrier is shattered.

If it is a single continuous barrier, the entire barrier ends. If it is an exceptionally large magical structure, the Titan destroys a section up to a 30-foot Cube with each successful Breach Attack. Sovereign Breach ignores Damage Resistance, Damage Immunity, damage reduction, immunity to physical interaction, and requirements that only a particular spell can remove the barrier. The attack counts as both magical and physical for this purpose.

If a boundary prevents entering, leaving, teleporting, crossing dimensions, or passing through a region without physically manifesting, the Titan can attack the boundary itself. A successful Sovereign Breach destroys the restriction in the breached area.

action.name: Siege Barrage (Siege Titan Only)
entries: Choose a point within 300 feet. Each creature in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered there must make a {@dc 20 + PB} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d12 + 17 + PB} damage. Choose a damage type appropriate to the incorporated components, such as Bludgeoning, Piercing, Slashing, Fire, or another justified damage type. On a successful save, the creature takes half damage.

action.name: Seize (Grasping Titan Only)
entries: {@actSave str} {@dc 20 + PB}, any number of creatures within the Titan's Reach up to its remaining Grapple capacity. Each target chooses Strength or Dexterity and makes only that saving throw; use the corresponding Seize roll. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions until the Grapple ends.

action.name: Seize (Dexterity; Grasping Titan Only)
entries: {@actSave dex} {@dc 20 + PB}, any number of creatures within the Titan's Reach up to its remaining Grapple capacity. Each target chooses Strength or Dexterity and makes only that saving throw; use the corresponding Seize roll. {@actSaveFail} The target has the {@condition Grappled|XPHB} and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions until the Grapple ends.

bonus.name: Crush the Captive (Grasping Titan Only)
entries: Each creature currently Grappled by the Titan takes {@damage 4d12 + 17 + PB} Bludgeoning damage.

bonus.name: Reconfigure
entries: This configuration lasts until it is changed again or the Titan ends. Choose War Titan, Fortress Titan, Siege Titan, Grasping Titan, or Devouring Titan. The Titan rearranges its components accordingly and retains its current Hit Points.

reaction.name: Interpose the Fortress (Fortress Titan Only)
entries: When a creature within 30 feet takes damage, the Titan can move up to half its Speed toward that creature and interpose itself. Reduce the damage by {@dice 3d12 + 17 + PB}. The Titan takes damage equal to the amount prevented.

trait.name: Draconic Nature
entries: {@b Young Mind, Ancient Blood.} The wyrmling is fully sapient but is still a child. It can speak, reason, learn, negotiate, deceive, understand consequences, and make deliberate plans, but it normally lacks the experience, restraint, knowledge, and long-term judgment of older dragons. A wyrmling isn't automatically a scholar, mastermind, or expert spellcaster.

{@b Draconic Magical Instinct.} The dragon is proficient in Intelligence ({@skill Arcana}). It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, and supernatural creatures. This instinct doesn't automatically reveal complete information.
{@b Keen Senses.} The dragon has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) checks that rely on sight or smell.
{@b No Change Shape.} The wyrmling doesn't possess Change Shape. True dragons of this variant first gain Change Shape at the Young age category.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Fire Affinity.} When the dragon casts a spell that deals Fire damage, it ignores Resistance to Fire damage. A creature with Immunity to Fire damage remains immune.
{@b Innate Elemental Casting.} When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Fire, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed its Proficiency Bonus. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows every spell in the Red Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 1. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast its Innate Draconic Spellcasting At Will spells without spell slots or usage limits. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell burning hands|XPHB}.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: Each spell listed as Draconic High Magic can be cast once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. Draconic High Magic requires Material components only if costly or consumed. Draconic High Magic: {@spell burning hands|XPHB}.

trait.name: Sovereignty of the Burning Hoard
entries: To a red dragon, possession is not a legal concept but a fact of nature. What it claims becomes part of its identity, and resistance to its authority is treated as a personal insult. With age, the distinction between its treasure, its territory, and the world it believes it deserves begins to disappear.

entries.name: Claimed Treasure
entries: The dragon must touch the object for 1 minute to use this feature. The claim lasts until the dragon willingly releases it. The dragon can mystically mark up to PB × 10 objects as Claimed Treasure. While a Claimed object is on the same plane and within 1 mile, the dragon knows its direction, approximate distance, and whether it is moving. This doesn't reveal who carries the object or grant supernatural vision through it.

entries: Green dragons understand that controlling what someone believes is often more useful than controlling their body. trait.name: Draconic Nature
entries: {@b Growing Draconic Mind.} A Young Dragon is fully sapient and has developed considerably beyond the impulsive reasoning of a wyrmling. It can plan ahead, understand politics and social structures, deliberately manipulate others, study magic, manage servants or territory, and pursue long-term goals. It is still substantially less experienced than an Adult or Ancient Dragon.

It can make Arcana checks concerning spells, magical effects, Magic Items, curses, wards, magical creatures, and supernatural phenomena. Its greater experience allows it to recognize and analyze magic much more reliably than a wyrmling, but this feature doesn't grant automatic knowledge.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. trait.name: Sovereignty of the Burning Hoard

entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity. Tracks, scents, wounds, habits, and escape routes become parts of a living map in the dragon's mind. Once an elder white dragon decides something is prey, distance becomes a temporary inconvenience.

entries.name: Chosen Prey
entries: The dragon must spend 1 minute observing a creature, its scent, or its tracks to use this feature. The effect lasts until replaced. The dragon marks one creature as its Chosen Prey. It has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to locate or track that creature. While within 1 mile, if there is a physical trail or scent the dragon could reasonably detect, it knows the trail's general direction.

entries.name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the Chosen Prey, and snow and ice don't cost the dragon extra movement during it.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting
headerEntries: The dragon is a 7th-level spellcaster. Its spellcasting ability is Charisma. Its spell save DC is 15, and it has +7 to hit with spell attacks. It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body. It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The dragon makes three attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. The dragon can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action. The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 9} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 3d10 + 5} Piercing damage plus {@damage 3d8} Cold damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 9} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 3d6 + 5} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 9} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 3d8 + 5} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 9} to hit, reach 10 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 3d6 + 5} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Cold Breath
entries: Recharge 5–6. The dragon exhales its breath weapon in a 30-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 17} Constitution Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 12d8} Cold damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage.

action.name: Frost Shard
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 7} to hit, range 120 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 5d10} Cold damage. The target's Speed is reduced by 20 feet until the start of the dragon's next turn. This attack is magical. It counts as a spell attack but isn't itself a spell and doesn't expend a spell slot.

monster.name: Adult Red Dragon

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (3/Day)
entries: If the dragon fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The dragon can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the dragon ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. The dragon magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 19 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body. It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.

It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The dragon can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The dragon can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell disintegrate|XPHB}, {@spell incendiary cloud|XPHB}, and {@spell meteor swarm|XPHB}. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the dragon from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. Draconic High Magic requires Material components only if costly or consumed.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Innate Elemental Casting.} When the dragon casts a spell whose primary damage type is Fire, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.
{@b Superior Fire Affinity.} The dragon's spells ignore Fire Resistance. For the dragon's spells, Fire Immunity is treated as Fire Resistance instead.
{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the dragon can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 6. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows every spell in the Red Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 9. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast its Innate Draconic Spellcasting At Will spells without spell slots or usage limits. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack. Leveled At-Will Magic at this age: {@spell detect magic|XPHB}, {@spell burning hands|XPHB}, {@spell scorching ray|XPHB}, {@spell see invisibility|XPHB}, {@spell fireball|XPHB}, {@spell dispel magic|XPHB}.

trait.name: Sovereignty of the Burning Hoard
entries: To a red dragon, possession is not a legal concept but a fact of nature. What it claims becomes part of its identity, and resistance to its authority is treated as a personal insult. With age, the distinction between its treasure, its territory, and the world it believes it deserves begins to disappear.

entries.name: Claimed Treasure
entries: The dragon must touch the object for 1 minute to use this feature. The claim lasts until the dragon willingly releases it. The dragon can mystically mark up to PB × 10 objects as Claimed Treasure. While a Claimed object is on the same plane and within 1 mile, the dragon knows its direction, approximate distance, and whether it is moving. This doesn't reveal who carries the object or grant supernatural vision through it.

entries.name: Tyrant's Challenge
entries: The dragon can use this feature as a Bonus Action. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. The dragon chooses one creature within 60 feet. The target must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC. On a failed save, the target has Disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than the dragon, and the first time on each of its turns that it damages another creature, it takes {@damage 2d8} Fire damage. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

entries.name: Burning Dominion
entries: The dragon emits a 60-foot aura. A hostile creature that starts its turn in the aura while Frightened of the dragon takes Fire damage equal to the dragon's PB + Charisma modifier. Until the start of that creature's next turn, it can't become Invisible and treats movement that carries it farther from the dragon as Difficult Terrain.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its presence commands the fear earned by centuries of survival. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

trait.name: Web of the Verdant Lie
entries: Green dragons understand that controlling what someone believes is often more useful than controlling their body. They collect promises, weaknesses, fears, alliances, and secrets with the same appetite other dragons reserve for gold. At great age, simply dealing with one becomes dangerous long before initiative is rolled.

entries.name: Borrowed Voice
entries: Reproducing a learned voice or sound requires an Action. The dragon remembers the learned voice or sound indefinitely. After hearing a voice or sound for at least 1 minute, the dragon can reproduce it. A creature suspicious of the imitation can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC. This doesn't provide perfect supernatural identity copying.

entries.name: Venomous Bargain
entries: This effect lasts for 24 hours. When a creature willingly makes an explicit promise to the dragon, the dragon can mystically mark that promise. If the dragon later actually learns that the creature knowingly broke the promise during the duration, it can trigger the mark. The creature takes {@damage 4d8} Poison plus {@damage 4d8} Psychic damage, and the dragon knows its direction for 1 hour while both remain on the same plane. This isn't perfect lie detection; the dragon must genuinely learn that the promise was broken.

entries.name: Web of Influence
entries: After speaking with a creature for at least 1 minute, the dragon can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check opposed by the creature's Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check. On a success, the dragon learns one broad current reasonably exposed by the creature's behavior: a fear, desire, important loyalty, or immediate goal. This doesn't reveal memories or perfectly hidden truths.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its presence commands the fear earned by centuries of survival. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 120 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition.

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (7/Day)
entries: If the wyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Wyrm Magic Resistance.} The wyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
{@b Perfect Concentration.} The wyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.
{@b Innate Elemental Casting.} When the wyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Cold, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

{@b Wyrm Cold Supremacy.} The wyrm's Cold damage ignores Cold Resistance. When the wyrm deals Cold damage to a creature with Cold Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Cold Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance. As a result, the wyrm's Cold damage affects creatures with Cold Resistance or Cold Immunity without reducing the damage.

{@b Apex High Magic Recovery.} At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic for a spell of 8th level or lower. A 9th-level Draconic High Magic use still requires a Long Rest to recover.
{@b Arcane Reclamation.} At the end of a Short Rest, the wyrm can recover expended spell slots whose combined spell levels don't exceed 24. It can't recover uses of Draconic High Magic this way.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows every spell in the White Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 9. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast its Innate Draconic Spellcasting At Will spells without spell slots or usage limits. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack. trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 25 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body. It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.

It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The wyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The wyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell cone of cold|XPHB}, {@spell wall of ice|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell shapechange|XPHB}, and {@spell wish|XPHB}. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the wyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. Draconic High Magic requires Material components only if costly or consumed.

trait.name: World-Heart Reignition (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious. Instead, it regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Breath Weapon; regains 3 expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains one expended use of Draconic High Magic, including a 9th-level spell; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions.

trait.name: Memory of the Endless Hunt
entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity. Tracks, scents, wounds, habits, and escape routes become parts of a living map in the dragon's mind. Once an elder white dragon decides something is prey, distance becomes a temporary inconvenience.

entries.name: Chosen Prey
entries: The wyrm must spend 1 minute observing a creature, its scent, or its tracks to use this feature. The effect lasts until replaced. The dragon marks one creature as its Chosen Prey. It has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to locate or track that creature. While within 1 mile, if there is a physical trail or scent the dragon could reasonably detect, it knows the trail's general direction.

entries.name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the Chosen Prey, and snow and ice don't cost the dragon extra movement during it.

entries.name: Learn the Prey's Pattern
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. This effect lasts until the end of the dragon's next turn. After its Chosen Prey hits the dragon with an attack or causes the dragon to fail a Saving Throw, the dragon gains a bonus equal to its PB to AC or Saving Throws, as appropriate, against subsequent uses of that same attack or effect by that prey until the end of the dragon's next turn.

entries.name: Frozen Quarry
entries: This effect lasts while the creature remains the dragon's Chosen Prey. A Chosen Prey within 120 feet gains no benefit from being Invisible against the dragon and can't Hide from the dragon using snow, fog, or ice alone. Whenever the dragon deals Cold damage to that creature, its Speed becomes 0 until the start of the dragon's next turn.

entries.name: There Is No Escape
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When the Chosen Prey within 1 mile teleports or magically moves away, the wyrm immediately knows its direction, distance, and whether it changed planes. If the prey remains on the same plane, the wyrm can immediately move up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its presence commands the fear earned by centuries of survival. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition. a creature that fails its initial Saving Throw can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. This additional effect occurs only on the initial failed save.

trait.name: Web of the Verdant Lie
entries: Green dragons understand that controlling what someone believes is often more useful than controlling their body. They collect promises, weaknesses, fears, alliances, and secrets with the same appetite other dragons reserve for gold. At great age, simply dealing with one becomes dangerous long before initiative is rolled.

entries.name: Borrowed Voice
entries: Reproducing a learned voice or sound requires an Action. The dragon remembers the learned voice or sound indefinitely. After hearing a voice or sound for at least 1 minute, the dragon can reproduce it. A creature suspicious of the imitation can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC. This doesn't provide perfect supernatural identity copying.

entries.name: Venomous Bargain
entries: This effect lasts for 24 hours. When a creature willingly makes an explicit promise to the dragon, the dragon can mystically mark that promise. If the dragon later actually learns that the creature knowingly broke the promise during the duration, it can trigger the mark. The creature takes {@damage 4d8} Poison plus {@damage 4d8} Psychic damage, and the dragon knows its direction for 1 hour while both remain on the same plane. This isn't perfect lie detection; the dragon must genuinely learn that the promise was broken.

entries.name: Web of Influence
entries: After speaking with a creature for at least 1 minute, the dragon can make a Wisdom ({@skill Insight}) check opposed by the creature's Charisma ({@skill Deception}) check. On a success, the dragon learns one broad current reasonably exposed by the creature's behavior: a fear, desire, important loyalty, or immediate goal. This doesn't reveal memories or perfectly hidden truths.

entries.name: Forest of False Paths
entries: In natural vegetation, forest, swamp, or jungle, the dragon leaves no trail unless it chooses, can't be tracked nonmagically, and can move through nonmagical plants without slowing. A creature tracking the dragon can be deliberately led onto a false route unless it succeeds on a Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) check against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

entries.name: Every Promise Has Teeth
entries: Once per turn, when a creature affected by one of the wyrm's Enchantment spells, Illusion spells, Charmed effects, or Venomous Bargains damages the wyrm or knowingly acts directly against an instruction it accepted, that creature takes {@damage 8d10} Poison or Psychic damage (the wyrm's choice). The creature also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the dragon more than size. Its presence commands the fear earned by centuries of survival. Those who stand before it can feel that history pressing against their courage. At the start of its turn, the dragon can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the dragon's choice within 300 feet that can see or hear it must make a Wisdom Saving Throw against the dragon's Spell Save DC.

On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the dragon for 1 minute. The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that dragon's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition. a creature that fails its initial Saving Throw can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. This additional effect occurs only on the initial failed save.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting
headerEntries: The wyrm's spellcasting ability is Charisma. Its spell save DC is 25, and it has +17 to hit with spell attacks. It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body. It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The wyrm makes five attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. The wyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a casting time of 1 Action. The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d10 + 10} Piercing damage plus {@damage 8d8} Poison damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 20 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d6 + 10} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 35 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d8 + 10} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 18} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 8d6 + 10} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Poison Breath {@recharge 4}
entries: The wyrm exhales its breath weapon in a 120-foot Cone. Each creature in that area must make a {@dc 26} Constitution Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 32d6} Poison damage. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Wyrm Poison Supremacy applies to this Poison damage.

action.name: Sovereign Toxin
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 17} to hit, range 400 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 16d12} Poison damage. The target must succeed on a {@dc 25} Constitution Saving Throw or, until the end of its next turn, have Disadvantage on Attack Rolls, Ability Checks, and Saving Throws, can't take Reactions, and have its Speed halved. This attack is magical and counts as a spell attack, but isn't itself a spell.

legendaryHeader: The wyrm can take 7 Legendary Actions, choosing from the options below. Only one Legendary Action option can be used at a time and only at the end of another creature's turn. The wyrm regains spent Legendary Actions at the start of its turn.

legendary.name: Detect
entries: The wyrm makes a Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) check.

legendary.name: Claw Attack
entries: The wyrm makes one Claw attack.

legendary.name: Tail Attack
entries: The wyrm makes one Tail attack.

legendary.name: Cast Cantrip
entries: The wyrm casts one cantrip.

legendary.name: Wing Attack (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: Each creature within 25 feet of the wyrm must make a {@dc 26} Dexterity Saving Throw. On a failed save, a creature takes {@damage 8d6 + 10} Bludgeoning damage and falls Prone. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage and doesn't fall Prone. The wyrm can then fly up to half its Fly Speed.

legendary.name: Cataclysmic Movement (Costs 2 Actions)
entries: The wyrm moves up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks. Each creature the wyrm passes within 20 feet of during this movement must succeed on a {@dc 26} Dexterity Saving Throw or fall Prone.

legendary.name: Cast Spell (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell of 7th level or lower that normally has a casting time of 1 Action, expending a spell slot or use as normal.

legendary.name: Breath Surge (Costs 3 Actions)
entries: The wyrm rolls one additional d6 to recharge Poison Breath. If Poison Breath is already available, the wyrm can instead immediately use Poison Breath.

legendary.name: High Magic (Costs 5 Actions)
entries: The wyrm casts one spell from Draconic High Magic whose use is still available.

monster.name: Blue Wyrm

conditionImmune.note: from effects other than being reduced to 0 Hit Points

trait.name: Legendary Resistance (7/Day)
entries: If the wyrm fails a Saving Throw, it can choose to succeed instead.

trait.name: Draconic Magic
entries: {@b Wyrm Magic Resistance.} The wyrm has Advantage on Saving Throws against spells and other magical effects.
{@b Perfect Concentration.} The wyrm automatically succeeds on Constitution Saving Throws made to maintain Concentration as a result of taking damage.
{@b Innate Elemental Casting.} When the wyrm casts a spell whose primary damage type is Lightning, it can cast that spell without Verbal, Somatic, or non-costly Material components.

{@b Wyrm Lightning Supremacy.} The wyrm's Lightning damage ignores Lightning Resistance. When the wyrm deals Lightning damage to a creature with Lightning Immunity, that Immunity is treated as Lightning Resistance, and the wyrm then ignores that Resistance. As a result, the wyrm's Lightning damage affects creatures with Lightning Resistance or Lightning Immunity without reducing the damage.

{@b Draconic Spell List.} Draconic magic grows from instinct and experience. The dragon knows every spell in the Blue Dragon Spell List of a level no higher than 9. Those spells are presented in its Innate Draconic Spellcasting trait.

{@b Draconic At-Will Magic.} The dragon can cast its Innate Draconic Spellcasting At Will spells without spell slots or usage limits. A leveled spell cast this way is cast at its lowest spell level. The dragon can instead expend a spell slot to cast that spell normally, including to upcast it when applicable. An At-Will spell with a Casting Time of 1 Action can replace the dragon's one permitted spell replacement in Multiattack, if that dragon has Multiattack. trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the wyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. The wyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 28 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body. It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.

It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The wyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

entries: When the wyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious. trait.name: Throne of the Storm

entries.name: Mirage of the Wastes
entries: The wyrm can use this feature as an Action. This effect lasts for up to 1 hour. The dragon creates a harmless visual or auditory mirage within 60 feet occupying no more than a 10-foot Cube. Physical interaction reveals that it isn't real. The dragon also ignores natural penalties caused by extreme heat and blowing sand.

entries.name: Static Step

If this movement changes whether the attack can legally reach it, the attack is resolved using the dragon's new position. The dragon can use this Reaction a number of times equal to its PB per Long Rest.

entries.name: Storm Dominion

entries: The wyrm must touch the object for 1 minute to use this feature. The claim lasts until the dragon willingly releases it. trait.name: Change Shape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as an Action. The transformation lasts until the greatwyrm ends it, uses this feature again, or dies. The greatwyrm magically assumes the form of a Humanoid or Beast whose Challenge Rating is 33 or lower, or returns to its true form.

While transformed, it retains its Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma scores; Hit Points and Hit Dice; Saving Throw and Skill proficiencies; languages; personality and memories; Innate Draconic Spellcasting; Legendary Resistance; and other mental or magical traits that don't specifically require its true draconic body. It otherwise gains the assumed form's physical characteristics.

It doesn't gain the assumed form's Spellcasting, Legendary Actions, Lair Actions, Mythic Actions, Legendary Resistance, class levels, or class features. The greatwyrm can continue using its own draconic spellcasting while transformed.

trait.name: Draconic High Magic
entries: The greatwyrm can cast each of the following spells once per Long Rest without expending a spell slot: {@spell cone of cold|XPHB}, {@spell wall of ice|XPHB}, {@spell forcecage|XPHB}, {@spell control weather|XPHB}, {@spell foresight|XPHB}, {@spell time stop|XPHB}, {@spell shapechange|XPHB}, and {@spell wish|XPHB}. Casting a spell this way doesn't prevent the greatwyrm from casting the same spell again using a spell slot. Draconic High Magic requires Material components only if costly or consumed.

trait.name: The Last Winter (1/Long Rest)
entries: When the greatwyrm would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, it doesn't die or fall Unconscious. Instead, it regains all of its Hit Points; ends any conditions or ongoing effects on itself that it chooses; recharges its Cold Breath; regains all expended uses of Legendary Resistance; regains all expended uses of Draconic High Magic; and immediately regains its full allotment of Legendary Actions. For 1 hour, the greatwyrm enters The Last Winter.

A supernatural freezing storm extends 300 feet from the greatwyrm and moves with it. The area is Difficult Terrain for creatures of the greatwyrm's choice. At the start of each creature's turn within the area, the greatwyrm can choose for that creature to take {@damage 6d10} Cold damage. Greatwyrm Cold Supremacy applies to this damage. Nonmagical flames within the area are extinguished. At the start of each of the greatwyrm's turns, its Cold Breath automatically recharges. While The Last Winter is active, the greatwyrm can use its Mythic Actions.

trait.name: Memory of the Endless Hunt
entries: White dragons may be less scholarly than their kin, but the hunt is a language they understand with terrifying clarity. Tracks, scents, wounds, habits, and escape routes become parts of a living map in the dragon's mind. Once an elder white dragon decides something is prey, distance becomes a temporary inconvenience.

entries.name: Chosen Prey
entries: The greatwyrm must spend 1 minute observing a creature, its scent, or its tracks to use this feature. The effect lasts until replaced. The dragon marks one creature as its Chosen Prey. It has Advantage on Wisdom ({@skill Perception}) and Wisdom ({@skill Survival}) checks made to locate or track that creature. While within 1 mile, if there is a physical trail or scent the dragon could reasonably detect, it knows the trail's general direction.

entries.name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Bonus Action. The dragon moves up to half its Speed toward its Chosen Prey. This movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks from the Chosen Prey, and snow and ice don't cost the dragon extra movement during it.

entries.name: Learn the Prey's Pattern
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. This effect lasts until the end of the dragon's next turn. After its Chosen Prey hits the dragon with an attack or causes the dragon to fail a Saving Throw, the dragon gains a bonus equal to its PB to AC or Saving Throws, as appropriate, against subsequent uses of that same attack or effect by that prey until the end of the dragon's next turn.

entries.name: Frozen Quarry
entries: This effect lasts while the creature remains the dragon's Chosen Prey. A Chosen Prey within 120 feet gains no benefit from being Invisible against the dragon and can't Hide from the dragon using snow, fog, or ice alone. Whenever the dragon deals Cold damage to that creature, its Speed becomes 0 until the start of the dragon's next turn.

entries.name: There Is No Escape
entries: The greatwyrm can use this feature as a Reaction. When the Chosen Prey within 1 mile teleports or magically moves away, the greatwyrm immediately knows its direction, distance, and whether it changed planes. If the prey remains on the same plane, the greatwyrm can immediately move up to its Fly Speed without provoking Opportunity Attacks.

entries.name: Nowhere Is Far Enough
entries: While its Chosen Prey is on the same plane, the greatwyrm always knows its direction and distance. This knowledge doesn't require sight, sound, scent, a physical trail, or line of effect. The Chosen Prey can't become Hidden from the greatwyrm, and being Invisible grants it no benefit against the greatwyrm. Whenever the Chosen Prey teleports, is magically transported, or leaves its current plane of existence, the greatwyrm immediately knows what occurred and the plane to which the prey traveled.

When the Chosen Prey teleports or is magically transported, the greatwyrm can use its Reaction to follow. The greatwyrm appears in an unoccupied space of its choice within 60 feet of the prey's destination, even if the destination is on another plane of existence. Running farther merely tells the greatwyrm where to hunt next.

trait.name: Frightful Presence
entries: Age has given the greatwyrm more than size. Its presence carries the authority of a creature older than empires. At the start of its turn, the greatwyrm can activate this feature. This effect lasts for up to 1 minute. Each creature of the greatwyrm's choice within 500 feet that can see or hear it must make a {@dc 26} Wisdom Saving Throw. On a failed save, the creature is Frightened of the greatwyrm for 1 minute.

The creature repeats the Saving Throw at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature that succeeds on the save, or for which the effect ends, is immune to that greatwyrm's Frightful Presence for 24 hours. This feature doesn't bypass immunity to the Frightened condition. A creature that fails its initial Saving Throw also can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn.

spellcasting.name: Innate Draconic Spellcasting
headerEntries: The greatwyrm's spellcasting ability is Charisma. Its spell save DC is 26, and it has +18 to hit with spell attacks. It requires no Spellcasting Focus. It can perform Somatic components using its draconic body. It doesn't require Material components that have no listed cost and aren't consumed.

action.name: Multiattack
entries: The greatwyrm makes six attacks using any combination of its Bite, Claw, and Tail. The greatwyrm can replace only one of these attacks with the casting of a spell that normally has a Casting Time of 1 Action. The spell is resolved normally and expends a spell slot or use as normal. A spell cast through Draconic High Magic can also replace that one attack.

action.name: Bite
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 21} to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 10d10 + 11} Piercing damage plus {@damage 10d8} Cold damage.

action.name: Claw
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 21} to hit, reach 25 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 10d6 + 11} Slashing damage.

action.name: Tail
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 21} to hit, reach 40 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 10d8 + 11} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Wing
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 21} to hit, reach 30 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 10d6 + 11} Bludgeoning damage.

action.name: Cold Breath {@recharge 3}

A creature that fails the save also has its Speed reduced to 0 until the end of its next turn. Greatwyrm Cold Supremacy applies to this Cold damage.

action.name: Absolute Zero
entries: {@atk rs} {@hit 18} to hit, range 600 ft., one target. {@h}{@damage 20d12} Cold damage.
